roles.description: Assist a preschool, elementary, middle, or secondary school teacher with instructional duties. Serve in a position for which a teacher has primary responsibility for the design and implementation of educational programs and services.
roles.sector: Educational instruction and library

tasks.label: Supervise students in classrooms, halls, cafeterias, school yards, and gymnasiums, or on field trips.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classroom supervision: monitoring 20-30 K-12 students during teacher-led instruction, independent work, testing, or the teacher's brief absence — scanning for off-task or unsafe behavior, redirecting students verbally and by proximity, separating disputes, noticing a student in distress, escorting a student to the office or nurse, keeping hands/objects/furniture safe.

Cafeteria/lunch duty: overseeing 100-300 students in a noisy lunchroom — enforcing seating and line rules, opening containers and helping young children with trays, wiping spills, watching for allergy exposure or choking, intervening in food-throwing or scuffles, dismissing tables and checking tables are cleared.

Recess/school-yard duty: outdoor supervision of running, climbing children on playground equipment and blacktop — maintaining sightlines over a dispersed group, spotting risky play, giving first aid for scrapes and bumps, resolving conflicts, headcounts, whistle/line-up and return indoors, in varying weather.

Hallway, stairwell, restroom-door, gymnasium/assembly and arrival/dismissal-bus-line duty: standing post or escorting a class through crowded transitions, keeping students moving and out of restricted areas, checking passes, monitoring bus and car loading and verifying children leave with the correct adult.

Field trips: accompanying a small group off-site (museum, zoo, park, theater, public transit/bus) — repeated headcounts, keeping the group together in public crowds, restroom escorts, managing behavior away from school routines, handling a lost child, motion sickness or injury.

sources.system: Team 1st Technologies / SMP-based autonomous security robot
sources.title: Santa Fe rolls out robot to help keep schools safe
sources.claim: An autonomous security robot from Team 1st Technologies patrols Santa Fe High School's campus, learning the layout and reporting unusual or aggressive behavior to human security staff; it is positioned as extra 'eyes,' not a replacement for human patrollers, and its responses are limited to movement, prerecorded messages, or two-way audio guided by security personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: campus security patrol. It shares the setting (school grounds, halls, yards) and the perceptual element of supervision, so it bounds what robots do there today: navigate and alert. It does not transfer to student supervision because it cannot manage behavior, give first aid, physically separate students, or hold custodial responsibility for minors.

sources.title: Knightscope K5 Upgrade Expands Market Reach
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot is a commercial product deployed at schools, hospitals and campuses, performing autonomous patrol and remote monitoring of large areas; its function is surveillance and alerting to human operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous premises patrol in institution-controlled facilities. Same class of environment as school corridors and yards, but the accepted output is video/alerts to a remote human, not the intervention, assistance and custody a supervising aide provides.

sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom
sources.claim: In a high school classroom trial, the Pepper social robot connected to an LLM presented learning content to student groups; social robots assisting teachers in schools remain rare and the work is a research trial of content presentation, not supervision of a class.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-classroom robot assistance. Nearest available system to classroom supervision; it establishes that current classroom robots deliver content in a researcher-supervised trial and do not monitor, redirect, or physically manage a class.

sources.developer: Realbotix / Salamanca City Central School District
sources.title: New York school district to deploy humanoid robot in classrooms this fall
sources.claim: A humanoid robot piloted in a New York school ... for fall 2026 is a seated conversational unit with facial expressions and upper-body motion — it does not move about the room or supervise students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid classroom assistant. Directly relevant setting, but a stationary talking head cannot patrol, intervene, escort or provide physical aid, so it cannot substantiate supervision.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: As of late 2025, leading consumer humanoids such as 1X's NEO cannot complete whole everyday tasks autonomously in unstructured human settings; teleoperation is the practical mode, and humanoid autonomy is confined to structured industrial environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose mobile manipulation among people. Supervising children requires mobile, contact-capable, judgment-laden response; this source shows such capability is still teleoperated, bounding what any humanoid could do on hall, yard or field-trip duty.

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Preschool/K-2 classroom: aide shows a table group of 4-8 young children how to hold and carry scissors, squeeze glue bottles, use crayons/markers, stack blocks and put lids and caps back on; gives hand-over-hand correction, takes items away from a child using them unsafely, and supervises cleanup into bins while other children move about the room.

Elementary/middle general classroom with 1:1 devices and shared supplies: aide instructs students on carrying Chromebooks/iPads with two hands, plugging into charging carts, handling headphones, calculators and math manipulatives; circulates during the period, catches rough handling or misuse, corrects it verbally and physically, and checks equipment back in undamaged.

Science lab, art room or makerspace (grades 4-12): aide demonstrates correct use of microscopes, hot plates/burners, glassware, hot glue guns, clay tools or a kiln; enforces goggles/aprons; walks the benches watching several stations at once, stops unsafe actions (loose hair near flame, mishandled glassware), and oversees cleaning and storage of equipment.

PE class, gym or playground recess: aide explains safe use of balls, jump ropes, scooters, mats and climbing structures; spots students on equipment, physically redirects or blocks unsafe play, retrieves and racks equipment, and monitors a mixed, fast-moving group outdoors or in a noisy gym.

Secondary CTE / shop / family-and-consumer-science lab: aide reinforces the teacher's safety demonstration on sewing machines, drill press, hand tools, ovens and knives; verifies guards, PPE and machine settings before use, stands by while students operate the equipment, and intervenes or shuts a machine down when a student handles it unsafely.

Music room, library/media center and AV or cart-based equipment: aide instructs students in handling band instruments, laminators, projectors, book carts and lab carts moved between rooms; monitors handling in hallways and shared spaces and checks items for damage on return.

sources.system: Social robots in education (206 documented deployments, 43 models incl. NAO, Pepper)
sources.developer: various (survey by Aymerich-Franch, Dubai Future Labs)
sources.title: Social robots for education: a global analysis of deployments in real scenarios
sources.claim: The largest documented survey of real-world social-robot deployments in education (206 cases, 28 countries, 43 robot models, in kindergartens through secondary schools) finds their functions are edutainment, entertainment, teaching programming and psychological support - none reported as instructing or supervising students in the safe handling of classroom equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: social robots working alongside teachers in K-12 classrooms. The survey shows the deployed repertoire is verbal/social interaction, with no case of monitoring students' equipment handling or intervening to prevent injury or damage, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom (arXiv:2508.05646)
sources.claim: A humanoid social robot (Pepper linked to an LLM) was trialled as a classroom teaching assistant, but its role was limited to presenting learning content verbally to student groups; the paper notes such classroom robots remain rare.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acting as a teaching assistant in a live classroom. It substantiates only spoken content delivery to a seated group; the robot does not handle classroom equipment, watch multiple students' hands, or intervene physically, so it cannot carry over to equipment-safety instruction and monitoring.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid + Optio AI teacher's assistant
sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: The first US school-district deployment of a humanoid 'teacher's assistant' provides conversational engagement and avatar-based tutoring; the M-Series humanoid is a stationary expressive conversational robot with no role in handling equipment or supervising student safety.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: embodied teaching-assistant duties in a working school district. The deployed capability is conversation and engagement only - no locomotion among students, no object manipulation, no safety monitoring - so it cannot complete instruction and monitoring of equipment use.

sources.title: Florida School Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)
sources.claim: Autonomous security robots patrol school campuses, but their function is limited to driving fixed routes and recording/alerting on vehicle and pedestrian traffic; they do not instruct students, handle equipment, or physically intervene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring of an institution-controlled school property. It shows only perimeter patrol with camera recording and alerting to human staff; it provides no instruction in equipment use and no physical intervention, so it does not substantiate completing this task.

tasks.label: Clean classrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-K/kindergarten room after snack and center time: aide sanitizes and wipes tables, sweeps crumbs and sand from under tables, returns blocks, manipulatives, art supplies and toys to labeled bins and shelves, wipes mouthed toys — floor and tables cluttered with dozens of small mixed objects, children present or just departed.

Elementary/middle classroom end-of-day tidy: pick up papers, pencils, crayons, books and jackets from floor and desktops, return them to cubbies/bins, straighten desks and push in chairs, tidy the classroom library shelf, erase and clean the whiteboard, empty small trash can.

Routine floor care in the classroom: vacuuming the carpet/rug area and sweeping or dust-mopping the hard floor after an activity, with chairs stacked or pushed in; open floor, standard school flooring.

Spot cleanup of a mess: spilled paint, glue, glitter, juice or water on a table and floor, sand from the sensory table, occasionally a bodily-fluid accident — aide fetches paper towels/spray/mop, cleans the specific soiled spot and disinfects it.

Disinfecting high-touch classroom surfaces during illness season or at day's end: desks and tabletops, doorknobs, light switches, shared supplies and keyboards, wiped down with district-approved disinfectant to the school's sanitation standard.

sources.title: Trusted, Integrated Commercial Robotic Solutions for Schools — SoftBank Robotics America
sources.claim: SoftBank's Whiz autonomous commercial vacuum is deployed in a US school district (Wicomico County Schools) where it has vacuumed millions of square feet of school floor space; vendor materials state Whiz vacuums classrooms as well as libraries and lunchrooms.

sources.title: Neo™ Autonomous floor cleaning machine for Educational Facilities
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robots are marketed and sold to educational facilities from pre-schools to universities and clean without human intervention.

sources.title: Brain Corp: School Cleaning Services Get a Boost From Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile cleaning robots running Brain Corp's autonomy stack are in service in K-12 schools and operate inside classrooms and gyms as well as hallways during school hours.

sources.title: UVD Robots Deploys Nation’s Largest Fleet of Autonomous Disinfection Robots to a School District
sources.claim: A New Mexico school district deployed 37 fully autonomous UV-C disinfection robots that disinfect surfaces and air in classrooms as part of the district's routine sanitation process.

sources.title: Business Talk AI: Let's talk about Artificial Intelligence for recycling with AMP Robotics
sources.claim: AMP's Cortex robotic sorting cells autonomously identify, pick and place highly varied, never-before-seen small objects from a presented stream into designated destinations at 99% accuracy and 80–120 picks ... in production facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting mixed novel objects into destination bins. If classroom items were presented to the machine as a purpose-built cell would present them (singulated on a belt with bins alongside), the object size, variability and placement precision are comparable to returning crayons, blocks and papers to labeled bins.

sources.title: Car Body Cleaning – Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's EcoRS Clean F is a production cleaning robot that wipes dust and dirt off varied car-body surfaces with feather rollers in automotive paint shops, running unattended in the line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wiping of a presented, fixtured surface to an accepted cleanliness standard. It substantiates that when the surface is brought to the machine (E1 presentation), autonomous contact wiping of contoured surfaces is a production-grade, deployed capability.

sources.system: Everyday Robots mobile manipulator (RL table-wiping framework)
sources.title: Robotic Table Wiping via Reinforcement Learning and Whole-body Trajectory Optimization
sources.claim: Google Research/Everyday Robots demonstrated a mobile manipulator that autonomously wipes tables to clean spills and ..., validated on hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the wiping component of classroom table cleanup (crumbs and liquid spills); it is a research demonstration on staged tables, so it supports the skill under machine-friendly presentation rather than unattended classroom-quality service.

sources.system: π0.5 VLA on mobile bimanual robots
sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 autonomously performs household cleaning behaviors — wiping spills, putting items away, picking clothing off floors — in homes not seen in training, but does not reliably succeed on the first try.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ tidying and spill wiping in a lived-in room. Objects and motions match classroom tidying, but the reported first-try failures and slow speed show the capability is not yet at worker quality in an as-found room.

sources.system: survey of π0.5, Figure 03, Galaxea R1 Lite and others
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: An independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capabilities classifies room tidying as only 'validated in lab' with imperfect first-try reliability and demonstrations sped up as much as 10×, and kitchen cleaning as having significant limits in lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying a lived-in room (bedroom) and cleaning a kitchen. It is the closest surveyed analogue to tidying a classroom and establishes that no such system is deployed at accepted-service reliability.

sources.title: Roborock Saros Z70 Review: The arm isn't quite there
sources.claim: The only commercially sold mobile robot with an arm for picking objects off floors, Roborock's Saros Z70, picks up only a narrow set of light items and is unreliable in testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking loose objects off a room floor and depositing them in a designated place — the core of classroom tidying. Its measured unreliability shows the in-situ version is not achievable at worker quality.

tasks.label: Organize and label materials and display students' work in a manner appropriate for their eye levels and perceptual skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary classroom: sorting and organizing instructional supplies and manipulatives (crayons, scissors, glue sticks, counters, leveled readers, math kits) into tubs, baskets, cubbies and shelves at child height, with the room partly occupied by furniture and sometimes children.

Preschool/early elementary: making and affixing labels (picture + word) onto bins, shelf edges, hooks, cubbies, supply drawers and center signs so young children can find and return materials; relabeling when contents change.

Mounting student work on a classroom bulletin board at students' eye level: trimming/backing papers, arranging them in a layout, stapling or pinning them, adding border strips and cut-out title letters.

Hallway or common-area display boards: putting up a new seasonal/unit display, then taking down the previous one (removing staples/tape), sorting the returned papers back to individual students' folders or cubbies.

Middle/secondary: organizing lab kits, textbook sets, art or shop supplies in cabinets and carts, labeling shelves and kit trays, and mounting posters/anchor charts and student project displays on walls.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout – GeekWire
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow autonomously picks individual, diverse products out of containers and places them into specific totes inside fenced workcells in fulfillment centers; deployed and being rolled out more widely.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level sortation of heterogeneous small goods into designated totes. Classroom 'organizing materials' is the same operation on comparable objects (small, mixed-shape consumer-type items) into designated bins, at lower precision and speed requirements, when the items are presented to the machine.

sources.system: Danfoss automated kitting cell with Roboception rc_viscore 3D vision
sources.title: Case Studies: Automated Kitting Solution with 3D Robot Vision | Roboception GmbH
sources.claim: A production kitting cell at Danfoss Drives uses a 3D-vision-guided robot to pick an assortment of different parts from supplier pallets and place them into different trays, with sub-millimetre detection of parts as small as 1.5 x 5.5 cm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting. Sorting assorted small parts into designated tray compartments is the same pick-place-and-arrange operation as grouping assorted classroom materials into labelled bins or kit trays; object sizes and required precision are comparable or tighter.

sources.system: REA LABEL DS / REA LABEL Robotic Labeler
sources.title: Automatic labeling: easier, faster, more reliable | REA JET
sources.claim: Robotic print-and-apply labelling systems automatically print a paper label, pick it up with a vacuum plate on a robot arm and apply it to a defined location on the target object; sold as fully automatic industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers making and applying labels. Also transfers to mounting student work: picking a flat printed paper sheet with a vacuum end-effector and affixing it, adhesive-backed, at a planned location on a presented surface is the same manipulation as sticking artwork onto a display board.

sources.title: Robotic Labeling - Motion Controls Robotics - Certified FANUC System Integrator
sources.claim: FANUC-integrated robotic labelling cells apply printed labels at complex positions and angles onto cases, pallets, rolls and individual products, including unique per-item labels verified by scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated label application. Applying a unique printed label at a taught position on a container is the same physical act as labelling a supply bin or shelf edge; content selection is a planning step, not a manipulation constraint.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is deployed in hundreds of Japanese convenience stores where it autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with bottled and ..., with remote operators taking over only when automatic restocking fails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stocking shelves inside a human-use facility (E2). It bounds what is deployed at E2 today: a rail-mounted arm at a fixed cooler station handling uniform bottles and cans, not a mobile robot organizing heterogeneous classroom materials across a room.

sources.system: π0.5 (pi-0.5) vision-language-action model on mobile manipulators
sources.title: π0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization | Physical Intelligence
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 model controls a mobile manipulator to perform long-horizon tidying tasks such as cleaning a kitchen ...; it is a research model, not a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying and putting objects away in rooms taken as found. It is the closest work to organizing a classroom in situ, but is a research demonstration with partial success rates and no deployment, so it does not establish worker-quality completion in an occupied classroom.

tasks.label: Organize and supervise games and other recreational activities to promote physical, mental, and social development.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor recess duty on an elementary school playground: the TA takes out a bin of balls, jump ropes and chalk, starts informal games (tag, four square, kickball) for children who want them, scans 40-100 running children across blacktop, field and climbing structures, enforces safety rules, mediates disputes and exclusion, responds to scrapes and collisions, then whistles the class in and collects equipment.

Leading a structured group game or PE-style activity for a class in the gym or on the field: setting out cones, hoops, parachute or bases, explaining and demonstrating rules, forming teams, refereeing scoring and fouls, adjusting the game for younger or less able children, keeping non-participants engaged, and packing equipment away.

Preschool/kindergarten free-play and learning-center time indoors: setting up play centers (blocks, dramatic play, sand/water table, ride-on toys), joining in play, modeling turn-taking and sharing, redirecting rough or unsafe behavior, spotting children on climbers, toileting/accident interruptions, and leading cleanup.

Indoor recess or classroom brain-break games (rainy day): distributing board games, cards, puzzles or running a whole-class game such as charades, Simon Says or a dance video; teaching the rules, keeping noise and movement within limits, resolving rule disputes and cheating claims, and restoring the room afterwards.

Small-group game session with 2-6 students in a quiet corner, breakout room or hallway table, chosen to build social skills or reinforce academics (cooperative board game, math bingo, memory/card game): setting up materials, teaching rules, prompting turn-taking and good sportsmanship, keeping reluctant students engaged, and returning students to class.

Off-site or special-event recreation: field day stations on a public park field, a class trip to a park/museum play area, or an after-school club on grounds shared with the public - crowded, unfamiliar layout, head counts, weather and stranger traffic, plus setup and teardown of activity stations.

sources.developer: Oregon State University Colleges of Engineering and Health (Naomi Fitter, Samuel Logan)
sources.title: Toddlers show increased physical activity with a robot playmate moving around the room | Newsroom | Oregon State University
sources.claim: GoBot, a custom wheeled foam-padded robot, autonomously played keep-away with individual toddlers in a playroom and raised their physical activity; researchers stress it is not aimed at replacing caregivers, and sessions were one child at a time with adults present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led active play with a young child to promote physical development. Same population and purpose as the preschool play instance, but it engages one toddler in an instrumented playroom and performs no group organization, rule enforcement or safety supervision.

sources.system: NAO 6 socially assistive robot (KIT daycare deployment)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Rixen, Gerling, Bruno) / Aldebaran NAO
sources.title: Long-Term Integration of a Robot in an Inclusive Daycare: An Ethnographic Study Focused on Children and Caregivers
sources.claim: A four-month deployment of a NAO 6 in an inclusive daycare represents the state of the art for robots in childcare settings: the robot sat in a corner recognizing communication cards and speaking pre-recorded intents, needed a researcher to carry it out, boot it and run a laptop each day, and had robustness problems.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting and population as the preschool/free-play instance. The deployed robot is a stationary interaction partner requiring daily human setup, showing no capability to organize activities or supervise a group of children.

sources.title: Andromeda raises AUD $23m to launch robots for aged care
sources.claim: Genesis Abi, a companion robot deployed in Australian aged-care homes and rolling out to US assisted living, is described by its developer as fully autonomous, navigating the facility on a schedule and supporting staff who lead group activities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading/participating in group recreational activities inside a structured care facility (E2). It is the closest deployed analogue, but it assists human staff with cooperative adults, handles no equipment, and takes no responsibility for supervising or physically intervening with participants.

sources.developer: Bristol Robotics Laboratory / UWE Bristol (Katie Winkle, Séverin Lemaignan et al.)
sources.title: World's first robotic personal trainer guides gym-goers through exercise programme | UWE Bristol
sources.claim: A Pepper robot at Bristol Robotics Laboratory acted as an autonomous socially intelligent fitness coach, guiding ten participants through a Couch-to-5k treadmill programme three times a week for three months in a university gym.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a physical-activity session and motivating participants. Transfer is limited: it coaches one cooperative adult fixed on a treadmill, does not set up equipment, referee, manage groups, or supervise safety.

sources.developer: ATR Intelligent Robotics and Communication Laboratories (Kanda et al.)
sources.title: A Two-Month Field Trial in an Elementary School for Long-Term Human–Robot Interaction
sources.claim: The Robovie humanoid operated autonomously in a Japanese elementary school for a two-month field trial, interacting and playing with children at the classroom perimeter, but as a play partner rather than an organizer or supervisor of children's activities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained recreational interaction with school children inside a school (E2). It shows robots can be present and engage children, but it never organized games for a group or supervised their safety and behaviour.

sources.system: AI-driven school security patrol robot (Santa Fe High School pilot)

sources.claim: A school security robot patrolled Santa Fe High School's campus to survey for threats and let a remote security team speak to intruders - monitoring of school grounds with human operators in the loop, not supervision of children's activities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patrolling and monitoring school grounds. It shows only camera-on-wheels surveillance with remote humans deciding and acting; it cannot start a game, judge child behaviour, or physically intervene, so it cannot substantiate recess supervision.

tasks.label: Use computers, audio-visual aids, and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Running the presentation technology live during a lesson in a K-12 classroom: waking the interactive whiteboard/projector, launching the teacher's slide deck or video, advancing slides on the teacher's verbal cue, switching between laptop and document camera, adjusting volume/captions, and pausing on request while 20-30 students watch.

Pre-lesson setup of AV equipment in the classroom or a shared space: wheeling out a projector/speaker cart, connecting the laptop by HDMI/USB-C, powering on projector, screen and speakers, loading the file, focusing and checking picture and sound, and clearing a 'no signal' or audio-input problem before class starts.

Handing out a class set of supplementary equipment or materials during the lesson: bringing Chromebooks/tablets from the charging cart, headphone sets, science-kit trays, or printed graphic organizers to each table group so the activity accompanying the teacher's presentation can begin.

Collecting and restocking at the end of the activity: gathering the tablets/headphones and printed materials, returning each device to its numbered slot in the charging cart and plugging in the chargers, and putting kit items and visual aids back in the storage cabinet.

Helping individual students or a small group with the technology while the teacher presents: getting a student logged in, resetting a frozen app, seating headphones on a young child, connecting an assistive listening or captioning device, or re-orienting a student to the right screen or page.

Producing the supplementary materials ahead of time in the school workroom: printing and photocopying handouts, collating packets, cutting and laminating vocabulary/manipulative cards, and mounting or posting visual aids for the lesson.

sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom (arXiv:2508.05646)
sources.claim: A Pepper humanoid connected to an LLM was used as a teaching assistant delivering learning content to student groups in a real high school classroom; the author reports current robots are not robust enough for autonomous continuous use in ....
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: a robot acting as a classroom teaching assistant presenting learning content; establishes that live in-class instructional-technology support is not yet reliably autonomous.

sources.title: The use of social robots in classrooms: A review of field-based studies
sources.claim: Review of field studies of social robots in classrooms finds autonomous deployments are rare and short-lived, and personalization in real classrooms is difficult.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting and role (robots operating in K-12 classrooms alongside teachers); supports the negative judgment for live in-class equipment operation and individual student technology support.

sources.title: Robotic gripper with soft, sensitive fingers can handle cables with unprecedented dexterity
sources.claim: A robot arm with tactile-sensing grippers autonomously followed a free earbud cable, localized the plug and inserted it into a phone's headphone jack on a lab bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cable plug insertion. The AV-setup instance is the same physical act (mating an HDMI/USB-C/audio plug with a socket) on comparable objects and tolerances, performed at a fixtured bench.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: connector insertion in a purpose-built cell; transfers to plugging laptop/projector/charger cables when the equipment is presented fixtured, which is the E1 counterfactual for AV setup and for recharging a device cart.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously carrying trays of items to seated people at tables in a busy human facility and bussing items back; comparable to bringing a class set of devices or handouts to table groups and collecting them, with recipients lifting items off the tray.

tasks.label: Prepare lesson materials, bulletin board displays, exhibits, equipment, and demonstrations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Copy/print run for a lesson: TA takes a master or file, runs 25-120 copies of worksheets, reading packets, quizzes or homework on the school workroom copier, collates and staples sets, three-hole punches, then stacks them by class period and carries them back to the classroom.

Making hands-on materials: printing and cutting out flashcards, word cards, number tiles, game pieces and center activities; running them through a laminator; trimming the laminated sheets; sorting complete sets into labeled bags, bins or trays for each table group, plus assembling per-student craft packets.

Bulletin board / display work: cutting butcher paper backing and border strips, cutting or die-cutting letters, stapling backing and border to a corkboard wall or hallway display case, mounting student work and captions in an arranged layout, and taking the old display down.

Equipment setup before a lesson: positioning and connecting a projector or document camera, wheeling in and distributing charged laptops/tablets from a cart, setting up an art or science station, or putting out PE gear (cones, mats, balls) in the gym, then breaking it down afterward.

Preparing a demonstration: measuring and mixing science demo solutions, portioning paint, sand, water, baking soda or seeds into cups/trays for each group, and laying out the demo apparatus on the teacher's table in the order the teacher will use it.

tasks.label: Conduct demonstrations to teach skills, such as sports, dancing, and handicrafts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Preschool/early-elementary movement and dance: the aide leads a class through action songs, simple dance steps, or warm-up calisthenics in a classroom or multipurpose room, performing each move so children imitate, repeating and cueing as needed.

PE or recess sports skill: in a school gym or on a school field, the aide models dribbling, throwing/catching, jump rope, or batting technique for a class, then supervises practice and re-demonstrates to correct form.

Art/handicraft project: at classroom tables, the aide demonstrates step-by-step how to cut, fold, glue, bead, weave, or mold clay with ordinary classroom materials for a small group or whole class, then helps children copy the steps.

One-on-one or small-group fine-motor and practical skill: showing pencil grip and letter formation on paper, scissors technique, shoe tying, or use of a ruler/compass, seated beside the student and repeating the motion slowly.

Secondary elective, lab, or CTE demonstration: threading and running a sewing machine, a kitchen technique, a shop tool, lab glassware handling, or an instrument fingering, shown to older students at a bench or station.

tasks.label: Distribute teaching materials, such as textbooks, workbooks, papers, and pencils, to students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary classroom: hand one worksheet/handout (sometimes differentiated by group) to each of ~20-25 children seated at desks, walking narrow aisles past backpacks, chair legs and moving kids, finishing in a minute or two so the lesson can start.
Middle/secondary classroom: pass out textbooks, lab packets, or graded papers to students in rows or at lab benches, often returning named papers to the right student, between bells.

Preschool/kindergarten: put out crayons, pencils, scissors, glue sticks and construction paper at each table or floor center while young children move freely around the room, adjusting counts as children shift groups.
Standardized testing day: distribute secure test booklets, answer sheets and sharpened pencils to specific assigned seats, counting and tracking booklet numbers under a strict protocol.
Bulk set-up: bring class sets from the supply closet or cart into the room and drop stacks of textbooks, supply bins, whiteboards or device-cart items at each table group for students to take one.

sources.system: Durst P5 Robotics (Kuka arms); Zund/RobotFactory cobot sheet loading
sources.title: The Rise of Robotics: Automating Wide Format Print Production (FESPA)
sources.claim: Kuka robotic arms in Durst's P5 Robotics print cells autonomously pick individual sheets, including thin materials such as foil paper, off a stack and register them precisely before placing them; a commercially sold, fenced print-production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sheet loading in print production. The core physical difficulty of handing out papers — separating one thin sheet from a stack and placing it accurately — is the same object class and precision, though here in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm picks individual, varied items out of containers and places them into specific totes inside fulfillment centers, deployed in production operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse item picking. Books, workbooks, pencils and glue sticks fall inside the size/weight class Sparrow singulates from bins, so picking one item per recipient at a fixtured station transfers.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' AI-Driven Robot ADAM Surpasses 16,000 Drinks Served at Flagship Las Vegas Location
sources.claim: Richtech's dual-arm ADAM robot prepares and serves drinks to walk-up customers at a commercial Las Vegas café, having served over 16,000 drinks since opening, i.e. a purpose-built robotic station that delivers items to individual people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic beverage kiosk service. It substantiates the hand-off half of distribution at E1 — a robot at a fixed station repeatedly delivering an item to each person who steps up, at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Figure AI humanoids sort 28,000 packages in 24-hour autonomous test
sources.claim: Figure's humanoids running Helix-02 sorted more than 28,000 packages over a 24-hour continuous run, fully autonomously with no teleoperation, detecting barcodes and placing packages at near-human speed in a warehouse-style facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel singulation and sorting. Shows sustained autonomous pick-and-place of flat, book/packet-sized items with identity checking, comparable to counting and routing test booklets or packets presented at a station.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi family are commercially deployed autonomous mobile service robots that run food, drinks and bussing to tables in restaurants and hotels, navigating 18-inch aisles among seated guests and moving staff, carrying up to 88 pounds per trip.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restaurant food running. Delivering loaded trays to designated tables where seated people take items off is the same physical act as wheeling class sets to table groups for students to take, in a comparably dynamic institution-run room.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator operates autonomously in more than 25 US ..., having completed over 1.25 million deliveries of supplies, medications and lab samples through corridors and elevators shared with staff and patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery by a mobile manipulator. Establishes autonomous fetch-and-deliver of material payloads inside a people-filled, institution-run facility at production reliability.

sources.developer: ATR / Osaka University (Shi, Satake, Kanda, Ishiguro)
sources.title: A Robot that Distributes Flyers to Pedestrians in a Shopping Mall (Int J Soc Robotics)
sources.claim: A humanoid research robot was built to hand paper flyers to passing pedestrians in a real shopping mall, using a learned approach-and-extend behavior model validated in a field experiment; the in-situ person-by-person handout of paper remains at research field-trial level.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous task: giving a sheet of paper to each of many people in a shared human space. Autonomy and acceptance rates are not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Type, file, and duplicate materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine duplicating: TA takes a teacher's master worksheet to the school workroom multifunction copier and runs a class set (20-90 copies), often double-sided and collated, sometimes stapled; loads paper, selects settings on the panel, clears jams, retrieves master and stacks.

Typing: keying up a worksheet, quiz, word list, labels, or parent letter from the teacher's handwritten or marked-up draft at a school computer; or entering grades, attendance, and reading-log data into a form or spreadsheet.

Filing: sorting graded and returned papers into student folders, cubbies, or mailboxes by name; alphabetizing; filing permission slips, assessment records, and forms into classroom or office cabinets and portfolios.
Finishing assembled materials: collating multi-page packets from separate stacks, stapling, hole-punching for binders, and trimming sheets on the paper cutter.

Laminating and cutting out classroom display and manipulative materials: running card stock and bulletin-board letters through the laminator, then cutting irregular shapes out by hand with scissors or a trimmer.

Office errand under time pressure: pulling a student file or a master copy from the front-office cabinet, duplicating it on the shared office copier while staff and visitors come and go, then refiling the original.

sources.title: Ripcord raises $45 million to digitize paper records with robotics and AI
sources.claim: Ripcord operates purpose-built robotic workcells whose robots autonomously handle loose and stapled paper records — removing fasteners, singulating and feeding sheets, scanning, indexing and categorizing them — at commercial scale (over a billion pages per year for named enterprise customers).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk document digitization. Transfer to filing/typing: same objects (loose and stapled office paper), same precision requirement (damage-free sheet-level singulation), and the machine's output — de-stapled, read, indexed and categorized records — is the sorting/keying product a clerk would produce.

sources.title: Digitize Your Documents with Ripcord
sources.claim: Ripcord's robots use air-lift end effectors and computer vision to pick and separate individual delicate sheets and remove fasteners without damaging them, inside the company's own robotic scanning facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic paper handling for scanning. Transfer: the hardest physical element of filing and duplicating is picking one thin sheet off a stack and de-stapling sets without tearing; this system does exactly that on arbitrary office paper.

sources.title: Espresso Machine in NYC's SoHo Brews not Coffee but Print-on-Demand Books
sources.claim: The Espresso Book Machine is a deployed, machine-controlled print-and-finish unit built around a Xerox copier/printer that takes a digital master and produces a complete, collated, bound and trimmed multi-page paper document without human handling of the sheets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: print-on-demand book production. Transfer to duplicating/collating: identical objects (letter/A4 sheets from a copier engine) and identical output form (a collated, fastened, trimmed multi-page set), at volumes and page counts far exceeding a classroom packet.

sources.title: The Future of the Espresso Book Machine
sources.claim: The EBM has been in commercial service in bookstores and libraries for over a decade, producing a several-hundred-page collated and bound document in about three minutes per copy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand book printing/binding. Transfer: establishes throughput and reliability of unattended collate-and-fasten finishing of paper sets, the finishing half of duplicating class packets.

sources.title: Automated Delivery Unit Sorter (ADUS) - U.S. Postal Facts
sources.claim: USPS operates deployed automated sorters that route paper mail pieces and bundles into destination bins by machine-read identifiers at 3,400 pieces per hour with 99.95 percent sort accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: postal sorting. Transfer to filing: sorting flat paper items into named destination bins by a machine-read identifier is the same operation as distributing graded papers into student mailboxes, at accuracy above a human aide's.

sources.system: Automatic mail sorting machines (transport + OCR address reader + mechanical sorter)
sources.developer: Postal automation vendors (e.g., Siemens, Solystic) as described in the literature

sources.claim: Automatic mail sorting machines in routine postal service transport and sort tens of thousands of letters per hour, using a scanner and OCR address reader to route each sheet-like item to a mechanical sorter destination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: letter sorting. Transfer to filing papers by student name: the machine singulates flat paper items, reads printed and handwritten identifiers optically, and deposits each in the correct bin — the same perception and placement problem.

sources.title: Scaling Helix: a New State of the Art in Humanoid Logistics
sources.claim: Figure's Helix policy lets a humanoid autonomously sort mixed parcels, including flat envelopes and deformable poly bags, at roughly one item every four seconds in an hour of uninterrupted running at a purpose-built sorting station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel induction. Partial transfer: shows autonomous handling of flat, deformable mailers, but at a fixtured induct station with items presented by conveyor, not loose sheets in a school workroom.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial deployment of mobile manipulators inside human-standard institutional buildings, Diligent's Moxi, performs point-to-point fetch-and-deliver of supplies and pharmacy items in hospitals; it transports payloads rather than manipulating documents, operating copiers, or filing paper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery. Cited to characterize what autonomous mobile manipulation actually achieves in E2 facilities — transport of bins and totes — which does not cover copier operation or sheet-level paper handling.

tasks.label: Laminate teaching materials to increase their durability under repeated use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School workroom/copy room: TA takes a stack of freshly printed letter-size worksheets, charts and reference sheets, runs them through the building's heated roll laminator (film on both sides), then separates the run and trims each sheet with the guillotine/rotary trimmer, leaving a small sealed margin. Interruptions from other staff sharing the room are common.

Pouch laminating small individual items — student name tags, desk labels, word/sight-word cards, cubby signs. TA centers each item in a pouch (sometimes several small items per pouch, spaced), feeds it into the pouch laminator, lets it cool flat, then cuts the pieces apart with rounded corners and a sealed border.

Wide-format work: anchor charts, posters, bulletin-board borders and die-cut letters/shapes run through the 25-27 inch roll laminator, then the irregular shapes are cut out by hand with scissors along their outlines while keeping a laminate margin so pieces don't peel.

Class-set batch job: laminating a full set of manipulatives or task cards (e.g., 30 sets of 12 cards, math game pieces, matching cards), then cutting the sheets apart into hundreds of individual pieces, sorting them into 30 labeled bags/envelopes, and returning them to the teacher before the lesson.

sources.system: Rollem Cardistry card pack production slitter
sources.title: Card Pack Slitting Production Machines - Rollem USA
sources.claim: Rollem's Cardistry system converts full laminated/printed press sheets into finished cards with automated two-directional cutting, collating and corner punching in one automatic system, used in production by major card manufacturers.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting laminated sheets apart into many small cards, punching corners and collating them into sets is the cut-and-sort half of the TA's card/manipulative laminating job, on the same object class (small coated cards).

sources.title: Automatic cutting system - Bograma - die / for cardboard / for packaging
sources.claim: Bograma sells an automated card production system that die-cuts, collates and stacks playing and game cards inline.
sources.transferJustification: Die-cutting laminated card stock into individual pieces with a margin and collating them into sets matches the trimming/sorting portion of laminating class sets of task cards.

sources.system: Zünd G3/D3 cutter with Over Cutter Camera (OCC)
sources.title: Over Cutter Camera | OCC | Zünd
sources.claim: Zünd's Over Cutter Camera performs fully automated optical capture of register marks on printed material so a Zünd flatbed cutter can contour-cut irregular shapes in printed/laminated sheets without manual alignment.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting laminated posters and die-cut shapes out along their printed outlines is the scissors step of the TA's task; the OCC-equipped cutter does the same contour cutting on laminated graphics automatically.

sources.system: Zünd cutter with BHS Board Handling System
sources.title: Digital Cutting at an Industrial Level | Zünd
sources.claim: Zünd cutters with the BHS Board Handling System load and advance sheet material fully automatically, enabling unattended production runs, including transport of printed films from the loading table.
sources.transferJustification: Supplies the automatic material presentation (feed and off-load) that makes the contour-cutting step of the laminating task a whole, hands-off operation rather than a hand-fed sub-step.

tasks.label: Requisition and stock teaching materials and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary classroom, between or during lessons: refilling table caddies and bins with pencils, crayons, markers, glue sticks and scissors, restocking the paper tray, tissues and wipes from the classroom cabinet, with students and their furniture in the room.

Receiving a delivered supply order at the school: opening and unpacking cartons, checking contents against the packing slip, shelving reams of paper, boxes of markers, workbooks and cleaning supplies in the classroom cabinet or the school supply closet, and breaking down the boxes.

Preparing and stocking instructional material sets for upcoming lessons: collating and stapling worksheet packets, assembling per-table kits of manipulatives, art or lab materials, and laying the sets out at student stations or in labeled bins.

Inventory walk-through of the classroom and supply closet: checking what is depleted or expiring, listing items, and completing/submitting a paper requisition form or the district's online supply order for teacher/office approval.

Preschool/kindergarten room with children present: restocking art and play materials (paint cups, paper, playdough, snack supplies) and re-sorting manipulatives into low open bins and shelves amid floor clutter and moving toddlers.

Fetching supplies from the central school stockroom or main office and moving them by cart through corridors and stairwells/elevator to the classroom, signing out or logging what was taken and putting the load away.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robots autonomously stow assorted small consumer items into and pick them from fabric storage pods at stow/pick stations in fulfillment centers, handling ~75% of stored item types at human-comparable speed, escalating items it cannot handle to a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stowing. Stowing miscellaneous small goods (pens, boxed items, soft packages) into crowded fabric bins involves the same object classes, grasp variety and placement precision as filling supply caddies and stocking bins, but occurs in a caged robotic workcell where the pod is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Staples deployed RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking arms across North American fulfillment centers to pick office- and school-supply items of varying shape, size, weight and packaging into totes/order containers; RightHand markets the same cells for kitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking/kitting of office and school supplies. The items are precisely those a teaching assistant stocks (pencils, markers, glue, notebooks); assembling repeatable kits from bulk feeds is the fixtured-cell analogue of filling caddies and per-table material kits.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics' Stretch Available for Commercial Purchase
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is a commercially sold mobile robot that autonomously unloads floor-loaded trailers and containers of mixed cases up to 50 lb; a human drives it into position and then it completes the unload on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carton handling at a receiving dock. Moving and placing mixed delivered cartons is the same handling problem as taking in a school supply delivery, but Stretch works at a dock/conveyor built around it rather than shelving contents in a closet.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots were mass-deployed to 300 FamilyMart convenience stores in ... to autonomously restock refrigerated beverage shelves from crates, running 24/7 with remote human help only on exceptions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment. Shows autonomous placement of uniform stock onto shelves, but the robot rides a rail behind a fixed-geometry cooler installed for it, i.e. the shelf is presented to the machine rather than found as a classroom cabinet would be.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi / Meet Moxi: Why We Invested in Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously travels hospital corridors, uses elevators and doors with its arm, and picks up and delivers supplies, medications and lab items; the fleet has passed one million deliveries across 25+ US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply runs. Fetching supplies from a stockroom and carrying them through busy corridors and elevators to a work area is the same errand as a school stockroom run; hospital corridors are at least as dynamic as school hallways.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously scans store shelves during business hours, capturing product availability, price and placement data used to flag out-of-stocks and drive replenishment; it is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores after a five-store rollout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf inventory auditing. Walking labeled shelving to record what is depleted and generating the resulting reorder list is the physical half of a supply requisition; the ordering step itself is clerical software.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator (ORB) automated operating-room supply retrieval and restocking, reporting 80% success in retrieval and 96% in restocking operations in evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level restocking of a supply room in a human facility; shows the capability exists only at research-demo reliability, below the error rate an employer would accept for a teaching assistant's stocking work.
