tasks.label: Assist in bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary school morning arrival: the aide stands in the outdoor bus loop as buses pull in, opens/holds the door area, steadies young children stepping down, hands down dropped backpacks and lunchboxes, keeps the line back from moving buses, greets each child by name, and walks the group into the building.

Afternoon dismissal at an elementary/middle school: the aide holds the bus roster, calls bus numbers, sorts 100+ milling students into the correct bus lines, physically redirects a child heading to the wrong bus, coaxes a crying or refusing kindergartner aboard, confirms counts with the driver, and stays until the last bus clears.

Preschool/pre-K loading and unloading: the aide lifts or steadies 3-5 year olds up and down the high bus steps, fastens or unfastens child safety harnesses/seats, checks name tags and hand-to-hand release to the bus attendant or waiting parent, and carries the child's bag and folder.

Field trip loading/unloading off-site: the aide counts students in a museum or park parking lot or at a curb on a public street, loads bags and equipment into the bus bay, holds the group back from passing traffic, boards last after a head count, and repeats the process at the return.

Adverse conditions or special assistance at the bus zone: rain, snow or ice on the loading pad; the aide holds umbrellas, keeps footing for students, assists a student on crutches or with a large instrument case or wheelchair lift, and manages a behavioral incident or a near-miss with a car passing the stop arm.

sources.title: Schools & Higher Education | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots are deployed on school campuses, where they patrol grounds and act as a mobile call box; their function is observation and communication, with no manipulation of objects or physical assistance to people.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot operating on school grounds during student movement; cited to show the state of the art there is autonomous patrol and video/audio relay, not escorting or physically assisting children boarding buses, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Terminal 3 porter robots; LG CLOi GuideBot
sources.developer: Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport / LG Electronics
sources.title: How Robotics Are Changing Airport Operations | Aviation Week
sources.claim: Airport porter/guide robots autonomously guide passengers through terminals and carry small amounts of baggage, i.e. person-guiding in a controlled institutional facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guiding cooperative adults through a structured facility. It does not transfer to bus loading duty, which requires supervising and physically handling non-compliant young children beside moving vehicles, with responsibility for their safety.

sources.developer: school-bus safety education vendor (used by Mobile County and Columbia County school districts)
sources.title: Buster – Transportation – Columbia County Schools
sources.claim: The only robot actually used at school-bus safety work is 'Buster', a remote-controlled animated bus prop used to teach children bus-safety lessons; it is operated by a human and does not perform loading or unloading duties.
sources.transferJustification: Directly at the bus loading zone context, but it is a teleoperated instructional prop; under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment and shows no robotic system performs the aide's loading duties.

sources.developer: University of Toronto / TU Munich field deployment
sources.title: Deploying SICNav in the Field: Safe and Interactive Crowd Navigation using MPC and Bilevel Optimization
sources.claim: Autonomous social navigation among pedestrians on a university campus is still a research field-test activity, with robots navigating hallways and courtyards among people rather than managing or assisting them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving safely among crowds of people. Shows that even bare navigation near pedestrians is at field-test maturity; no capability for crowd control, child handling, or safety intervention transfers to bus loading duty.

tasks.label: Maintain computers in classrooms and laboratories, and assist students with hardware and software use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During a lesson, the aide moves among desks helping individual students use the computer: log-in failures, finding the right app or assignment, a frozen window, plugging in headphones, printing; mostly verbal coaching with frequent hands-on reaching over to the child's mouse/keyboard, in a classroom of 20-30 children.

Chromebook/tablet cart logistics: hand out ~30 numbered devices to students, collect them at period's end, seat each in its slot and plug it into the cart's charging cable, verify counts against the roster, wheel the cart to the next classroom.

Simple peripheral fixes at a classroom or lab station: reseat a loose USB/HDMI/headphone cable, plug in a dead power adapter, swap a non-working mouse or keyboard for a spare, press-and-hold to restart a frozen machine.

In-situ diagnose-and-fix of a varied fault on installed equipment: projector or interactive whiteboard showing no signal, printer paper jam, network drop at one station, ceiling-mounted or under-desk cabling, unknown symptom requiring judgment about what is wrong and whether to escalate to district IT.

Routine upkeep of a ~30-station computer lab before a testing session: wipe screens and keyboards, tidy cables, wake each machine and confirm it logs in and that updates/test software are current, tag and set aside broken units.

Start-of-year or refresh intake in a school workroom/library: unbox devices, apply asset labels, plug each in for imaging/enrollment, record serial numbers in the inventory system, load charged units into carts.

sources.system: Breezy AI-powered robotic grading and refurbishment line (DECANT station + 18 robotic workstations)
sources.title: Breezy launches AI-powered robotic line in Poland for grading and upgrading pre-owned smartphones - ASBIS
sources.claim: Breezy (ASBIS) operates a commercial robotic line in Poland that automatically identifies device model/IMEI/serial, erases data, charges the battery, uploads a diagnostic app, connects the device to the network, then cleans, inspects and functionally tests devices with only 4 human operators per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intake, charging, imaging and functional grading of portable computing devices. Same object class (handheld/portable computers), same operations a school aide performs on a device fleet (charge, image, inventory, verify, flag faulty), at equal or finer precision, in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: HIL-SERL (Franka arm, wrist cameras, fixtured workcell)
sources.title: Precise and Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: HIL-SERL trains policies that run autonomously on a fixtured bench and achieve 100% success on precise computer-hardware tasks including USB connector grasp-and-insertion, RAM insertion, SSD assembly and USB cable clipping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting USB connectors and computer components into their sockets. Reseating a classroom USB/charging cable and plugging a device into a charger require the same connector geometry, tolerances and force control, on the same object class.

sources.date: 2012 (mechanism described); kiosks commercially deployed since, thousands in US retail
sources.title: New 'ATM' takes old phones and gives back green - Research & Development World
sources.claim: ecoATM retail kiosks autonomously inspect a device placed in the chamber, identify its model by machine vision, robotically select and attach the correct connector cable from 23 options, and run electronic diagnostics to grade the device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recognizing an unlabeled consumer device and connecting the right cable to it for diagnostics. Matches the aide's charging/imaging cable work on mixed device models, with the workpiece presented in a fixtured chamber.

sources.system: Rocsys M1 / RCS-2 autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M - Electrek
sources.claim: Rocsys' rail-mounted robotic arm autonomously detects an arriving vehicle, opens the charge port, plugs the connector in and disconnects after charging, deployed for fleet and port charging operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided autonomous plugging of a charging connector at production reliability. Demonstrates that repeated plug-in/unplug cycles of a charging fleet can be automated; the connector is larger and coarser than USB-C, so it supports the operation type rather than the fine tolerance.

sources.system: MATT (Standard / Extended) device test automation robot
sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: Adapta Robotics' MATT is a commercial testing robot that physically presses buttons and drives touchscreens to execute device commissioning, refurbishment and end-of-line test scenarios continuously for many hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically operating a device's keys and screen to run a scripted functional check. This is the same act as waking a lab machine, entering a test login and confirming software state, on presented devices at a fixtured station.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is an autonomous cleaning robot leased to office buildings and commercial facilities that cleans fixtures and floors during normal facility operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wiping/washing of hard surfaces in an institutional building. Supports the surface-cleaning element of lab upkeep; it does not itself handle delicate electronics, so the fine cleaning of screens/keyboards rests on the refurbishment-line evidence.

sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: Realbotix is piloting an Optio AI teaching assistant plus an M-Series humanoid in a New York school ... for fall 2026; the offering is conversational tutoring and homework help, not physical servicing of classroom computers.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 25 ... and has completed over a million autonomous deliveries, but its work is point-to-point transport of supplies, labs and pharmacy items rather than servicing or repairing equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the ceiling of deployed mobile manipulation inside institutional human facilities (E2): fetch-and-carry between fixed pickup/dropoff points, not per-device manipulation among seated occupants.

tasks.label: Grade homework and tests, and compute and record results, using answer sheets or electronic marking devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Plan, prepare, and develop various teaching aids, such as bibliographies, charts, and graphs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School copy/work room: TA produces class sets of printed teaching aids from a teacher's master or file — worksheets, reading lists/bibliographies, data tables and graphs — printing/copying, collating, stapling and sorting into class-set piles for distribution.

School print/media center or classroom: TA prepares laminated card sets and paper manipulatives — printing or copying flashcards, number lines, sorting cards; running sheets through the laminator; trimming/cutting into individual pieces; grouping into labeled sets or baggies for centers.

Elementary/middle classroom or workroom: TA develops a large visual aid — a math reference chart, word wall, labeled diagram or anchor chart — laying out the content and producing it at poster size (hand-lettered chart paper or printed on the school's poster maker) for classroom display.

Desk/computer work in classroom or staff area: TA compiles a bibliography or reading list, builds a chart or graph in a spreadsheet, or assembles a slide deck of visuals, delivered to the teacher/students electronically with no printed output.

Classroom: TA assembles hands-on aid kits for a lesson — counting/measuring manipulatives, science lab items, art materials — gathered from classroom cabinets and bulk supply bins and portioned into per-group trays or bags.

sources.system: Ricoh Booklet Finisher SR4160 / Ricoh production MFP finishing options
sources.date: 2023-05 (product page); finishing option in current production
sources.title: Booklet Finisher SR4160 | Ricoh Latin America
sources.claim: Networked office/production printers with booklet and multi-position finishers automatically collate, staple, fold and saddle-stitch printed sets from a submitted digital job, producing finished class-set style document packets without an operator handling each sheet.
sources.transferJustification: Same output as the TA's copy-room instance: printed, collated, stapled sets of instructional documents produced from a master file.

sources.title: Duplo System 5000 Dynamic 20-Bin Booklet Maker | Boggs Equipment
sources.claim: Multi-bin collating/booklet-making systems automatically collate printed sheets into sets and stitch and trim them at production rates, replicating the manual collate-and-staple step for large numbers of sets.
sources.transferJustification: Print-shop collating/stitching is the same physical operation as assembling stapled class sets of worksheets and handouts.

sources.title: Duplo DC-618 Slitter Cutter Creaser | All-in-One Print Finishing
sources.claim: A fully automated slitter/cutter/creaser reads registration marks/barcodes on printed sheets and slits, cuts and creases them into finished small pieces (cards, tickets) in a single pass — the trimming step for card-sized teaching aids.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting printed sheets into card-sized pieces is the same physical operation as trimming flashcard/manipulative sheets after printing or laminating.

sources.date: Product page current as of 2026; product shipping since 2019
sources.title: GBC Foton 30 Automated Pouch-Free Laminator | GBC
sources.claim: An automatic pouch-free laminator feeds a stack of sheets, laminates and trims them unattended after a single start command — the laminating step of preparing durable classroom cards and charts.

sources.system: VariQuest Cutout Maker 1800 / 2800 digital die-cut system
sources.title: Die-Cut Machines for Schools | Letter & Shape Cutters | VariQuest
sources.claim: A digital die-cut system sold to and installed in schools automatically cuts letters, numbers, shapes and manipulatives (including laminated construction paper) from stock loaded into the machine, producing the paper teaching aids TAs otherwise cut by hand.

sources.system: VariQuest Perfecta Q36 poster design and print system
sources.title: School Poster Maker Machines & Design Software | VariQuest
sources.claim: A poster/banner printing system built for schools produces full-color classroom visual aids from a design-software template library, deployed in school buildings for teachers and staff.

sources.system: Autobag Kit-Veyor counting and bagging system
sources.title: Autobag Kit-Veyor Packaging Conveyor System – Pyramid Packaging
sources.claim: An automated counting-and-bagging kit line collates assorted small parts into packaged kits ... at production rates, matching the physical operation of portioning assorted small items into per-group sets.
sources.transferJustification: Bagging mixed small-parts kits is the same physical operation as portioning counters, cards and small science/art items into per-group bags for a lesson.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: AI-driven piece-picking robot cells autonomously pick assorted individual items from bins and place them into totes/bags for kitting workflows in fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Kitting of varied small consumer-sized items from presented bins into containers matches assembling classroom manipulative/science kits when the supplies are presented in bins to the cell.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: The most capable general-purpose humanoids in commercial operation are working in logistics facilities moving totes, loading conveyors and stacking containers — not performing multi-step material preparation inside schools.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the ceiling of current mobile-manipulator capability in human work facilities; the repertoire (tote moves) does not cover operating copiers, laminators and cutters or assembling paper aids in a school workroom.

tasks.label: Operate and maintain audio-visual equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-class setup of the classroom projector or interactive flat panel: wake/power on the display, retrieve the HDMI/USB-C cable from the cart or wall plate and plug it into the teacher's laptop, select the correct input, lower the screen, verify image and sound, adjust volume. Done in an occupied K-12 classroom minutes before the lesson.

Operating AV live during instruction at the teacher's cue: cueing and starting/pausing a video, advancing slides, sliding a worksheet under the document camera and adjusting zoom/focus, passing and adjusting the wireless mic/classroom amplification, fixing an audio dropout or blank screen mid-lesson without stopping the class.

End-of-use device-cart handling: returning 25-30 Chromebooks/tablets to the charging cart, plugging each into its own charging cable, untangling and routing cords, checking charge indicators, closing and locking the cart in the classroom or storage room.

Routine upkeep and first-line troubleshooting: swapping AA batteries in a remote or wireless mic, wiping the projector lens and panel screen, replacing a projector filter or lamp module, reseating a loose connector, power-cycling a frozen device, coiling and storing cables, flagging the rest for IT.

AV for an assembly, guest speaker or event outside the home classroom: wheeling the AV cart down the hall to the gym, library or auditorium, positioning speakers and screen, running and taping down cables, patching into the house sound system, running a mic check and setting levels for the room, then packing up.

sources.system: Sanctuary AI Physical AI on industrial robot arm
sources.title: New robot plugs moving wires with 99.5% accuracy in factory test (Interesting Engineering)
sources.claim: Sanctuary AI's Physical AI system autonomously detects, tracks and inserts flexible wire connectors into moving targets on a live production conveyor at >99.5% success and 2.54 s cycle time — production-grade connector mating in a fenced industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive wire-harness plug insertion. Transfers to plugging an HDMI/USB-C/charger cable because both require grasping a limp cable end, visually locating a small keyed socket and inserting under force limits; the factory version is harder (moving target, production tempo).

sources.title: Precise and Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning (arXiv 2410.21845)
sources.claim: A vision-based RL policy autonomously grasps a USB cable lying freely on a bench and inserts it into the port on a motherboard, reaching near-perfect success rates after 1-2.5 h of real-world training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: USB connector grasp-and-insert on a motherboard assembly bench. Same object class (consumer data/charging connectors), same sub-millimetre insertion tolerance, and the cable start pose is unfixtured, matching plugging a laptop or charging cable at a bench.

sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs (Apple Newsroom)
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously takes in consumer electronic devices on a conveyor, identifies the model, and disassembles them — removing batteries, screws and modules — at 200 units per hour inside a dedicated fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated device disassembly and battery/module removal. Transfers to AV upkeep such as swapping batteries, pulling a lamp or filter module and re-seating parts: comparable small fasteners and components, comparable precision, with each device presented to the machine on a conveyor.

sources.system: FANUC CRX mobile cobot machine-tending cell
sources.title: Solving Labor Shortages with Mobile Machine Tending (FANUC CRX Collaborative Robot)
sources.claim: Commercial mobile machine-tending cobots autonomously operate machine controls — reading the stack light and physically pressing the cycle-start button — as part of an unattended work cycle in an industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pressing physical controls and verifying an indicator on production equipment. Transfers to powering on a projector/display and selecting an input, then confirming from the status light or image that the device responded.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid 'Sally' with Optio AI assistant
sources.title: US Firm's Humanoid Robot Teaching Assistant to Support 500 Students in 2026 (eWeek)
sources.claim: The humanoid robot actually being placed in US K-12 classrooms is a conversational/engagement system; the pilot covers tutoring and interaction with students, not manipulation, setup or maintenance of classroom audio-visual equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of robotics actually operating in the E2 classroom setting: it establishes that deployed classroom robots converse rather than handle cables, remotes, carts or projectors.

sources.title: Robots now wipe tables, sort trash, open doors at Google offices (The Tribune)
sources.claim: A fleet of over 100 ... mobile manipulators performed coarse autonomous chores — wiping tables, sorting trash, opening doors — inside Google's office buildings, the closest institutional-building precedent for autonomous mobile manipulation; the program was later shut down and never handled fine connector or equipment work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside a structured human facility (E2). It marks the ceiling of demonstrated E2 manipulation — bulk objects and surface wiping — and shows nothing at the precision of cable plugging, remote/battery work or AV setup.

tasks.label: Distribute tests and homework assignments and collect them when they are completed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary classroom (K-5), ~20-25 students at desks/tables: the TA walks the rows handing each child a worksheet or homework packet (sometimes passing stacks down rows), then at the end of ... activity walks back around collecting the completed sheets from desks and hands, checking names are on them and stacking them for the teacher. Children are moving, dropping papers, and asking questions.

Middle/high school class period: TA distributes test booklets and answer sheets (often one specific numbered/named copy per student, face down) at the start of a period, then collects and counts every booklet and answer sheet at the end, verifying none are missing before students leave; standardized-test security rules apply.

Preschool/kindergarten: TA places activity sheets, tracing pages or take-home folders at each child's spot at small tables or in cubbies, assists 3-5 year olds during the activity, then gathers finished and unfinished sheets from tables and floor, sorting them into each child's folder.

Homework collection at the start of class: TA stands at the door or circulates with a bin/tray as middle or high school students turn in loose papers of varying size and condition; TA checks each has a name, sorts into a class-period stack, notes who did not submit, and delivers the stack to the teacher.

Prep/workroom paper work: TA retrieves copies from the copy room, collates multi-page assignment packets, counts sets per class, places sets in class trays or student mailboxes, and later files collected work into the teacher's grading bin or returns graded work into individual folders.

Distributing and collecting devices and materials used for the assignment (Chromebooks/tablets from a cart, calculators, whiteboards) — issuing the numbered device to each student, then checking each item back in, verifying nothing is missing or damaged, and returning them to the cart to charge.

sources.title: Ballot on Demand - Election Systems & Software
sources.claim: Ballot-on-Demand systems automatically receive a per-person request from an electronic pollbook and print and dispense the correct individualized paper document for that person, at scale in US polling places.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing an individualized paper form to a specific named person who presents at a station. Objects (single letter/legal sheets), precision (right form to the right person), and accountability requirements match distributing a named test or worksheet when the work is brought to the machine (E1 presentation).

sources.title: Voting Equipment Database – ES&S DS200 | Verified Voting
sources.claim: Precinct scanners take a completed paper form directly from a person's hand, pull it in with a motorized feed, verify it, and deposit it into a secured collection box; deployed nationwide with attendant supervision only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting a completed paper form from each person and securing it in an accountable stack. Same object class (single completed sheets), same acceptance criterion (every form accounted for), performed with the work brought to the machine.

sources.system: LaptopsAnytime automated dispensing kiosks (e.g., Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library laptop kiosks)
sources.developer: LaptopsAnytime / Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library
sources.title: Laptop Kiosks | Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library
sources.claim: Automated laptop/tablet dispensing kiosks deployed in libraries and schools issue a device to an authenticated user and accept, secure, recharge and re-provision the returned device without staff handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing a numbered device to a named user and checking it back in. This is the device-distribution variant of the task, performed with users coming to a purpose-built machine bay.

sources.system: FANUC robots for paper & printing automation
sources.title: Automation for Paper & Printing Industries | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial robots are used in commercial paper and print operations to transfer paper stacks and individual printed sheets between presses, cutters and finishing ... in purpose-built cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of loose sheets and stacks in a fixtured cell, which is the collating/sorting/filing half of distributing packets and stacking collected work when the paper is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Schmalz vacuum grippers with sheet-separation (piston) cups
sources.title: Vacuum grippers: definition, types & applications | Schmalz
sources.claim: Vacuum gripper technology used on industrial robots reliably separates and lifts a single sheet of paper from a stack, a standard automation solution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking exactly one sheet off a stack — the core manipulation in dealing out worksheets or tests — demonstrated as routine in fixtured industrial handling.

sources.title: Scantron System Basics (Rutgers-Camden Information Technology)
sources.claim: Desktop OMR scanners used in K-12 schools ingest stacks of completed answer sheets from an automatic hopper at thousands of sheets per hour without continual operator attention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically taking in and ordering completed test sheets in a school, i.e. the processing end of collecting completed tests once the papers are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator is deployed at scale in hospitals doing point-to-point delivery of supplies and pharmacy items between fixed stations, but its manipulation is limited to grasping designated totes/bags at stations rather than handing individual documents to seated people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous item delivery inside a structured human facility (E2). It marks the current E2 frontier — station-to-station transport of bagged items — and shows no capability for per-person handout and retrieval of loose paper.

sources.title: Gemini Robotics: Google DeepMind's New AI Models for Robots - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: A general-purpose vision-language-action model drove a bi-arm robot to perform fine manipulation of a sheet of paper (folding an origami fox) autonomously from a natural-language instruction, in a lab tabletop setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous manipulation of a single limp sheet of paper. It shows sheet handling is feasible for a fixed-base robot in a controlled tabletop workspace, not in a moving classroom.

tasks.label: Collect money from students for school-related projects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary classroom: TA collects field-trip / class-photo money over several mornings — students hand over crumpled envelopes, folded bills, checks and permission forms from backpacks and desks; TA opens each, verifies the amount against the form, checks names off a roster, chases students who forgot, and walks the sealed collection to the front office.

Fundraiser (candy/cookie dough/read-a-thon): TA receives order forms with mixed bills and loose coins from students across a class over one to two weeks, counts each student's payment, reconciles totals against order forms, notes shortfalls, and turns in the counted money with a tally sheet to the bookkeeper.

Fixed sales point inside the school (book fair table, school store, concession/ticket table at a school event): TA staffs a counter, rings up small purchases for a line of students, takes cash, makes change from a cash box or POS drawer, and balances the drawer at the end.

Preschool/kindergarten: money arrives in envelopes tucked in backpacks and cubbies or handed over by parents at drop-off; TA retrieves and identifies envelopes (often mislabeled), matches payments to the right child, records them, and secures the cash.

Middle/high school: TA collects class dues, yearbook, athletics or field-trip payments — mostly checks plus some cash — handed over between classes or in homeroom, logs each payer in a spreadsheet or receipt book, issues receipts, and delivers the batch to the school treasurer.

sources.system: Newton/MSB Cash Kiosk (MCS Software / MySchoolBucks cafeteria POS)
sources.developer: MCS Software (Newton cafeteria management, MySchoolBucks integration)
sources.date: 2016-06 (vendor documentation, product in continuing district use)
sources.title: Cash Kiosk - Newton (Cafeteria Management & Point of Sale) - Confluence
sources.claim: Self-service cash kiosks are sold to and installed in K-12 schools so that students themselves feed bills and coins into an acceptor, are identified by a scanned ID/barcode, and have the money credited to their school account immediately, with the collected cash counted and reconciled against the system's expected total at day's end.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting lunch money from students. Same payers (K-12 students), same objects (bills and coins presented by hand), same output (money secured plus a per-student record of who paid) as collecting money for a trip or project; only the fee code differs.

sources.date: 2026 (page retrieved 2026-07; kiosks deployed nationwide for years)
sources.title: Get cash for your coins at Coinstar
sources.claim: Unattended coin-counting kiosks in supermarkets accept a poured handful of mixed, dirty loose change from a member of the public, sort and count it automatically, reject non-coins, and issue a redeemable voucher for the total.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counting and tallying collected coin. Fundraiser collections are exactly loose mixed coin and small bills that must be counted and totaled accurately; the kiosk performs that count unattended to an auditable total.

sources.system: NCR self-checkout with cash automation (NCR FastLane family)
sources.title: 4 misconceptions about accepting cash at self-service checkouts | NCR Atleos
sources.claim: Cash-automation modules on retail self-checkouts accept banknote and coin payment from shoppers and dispense the correct change without staff involvement, removing manual cash handling from the lane.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staffing a cash register. A book-fair or concession table is the same transaction — take cash from a customer at a counter, make change, record the sale, balance the drawer.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-10X back-office cash recycler
sources.date: 2025 (current product pages; family deployed globally for years)
sources.title: CI-10X - compact back office cash recycler | Glory Global
sources.claim: Compact back-office cash recyclers count, validate and reconcile mixed banknote and coin takings in retail and food-service sites, replacing staff counting and till balancing and producing the deposit record.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-collection counting and reconciliation. The TA's final step — count the collected bills and coins, produce a tally that matches the expected total, and hand over a deposit — is what the recycler automates.

sources.title: Dartmouth deploys new AI-enabled POS kiosks for self-checkout - CampusIDNews
sources.claim: AI self-checkout kiosks are deployed in school and campus dining facilities and other high-traffic venues: the customer sets items on a tray, cameras identify them automatically, and the customer pays at the kiosk with no cashier present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running the sales counter at a school store/book fair. Same setting type (school food-service/retail point inside an institution), same customers (students), same output (items rung up, payment taken, sale recorded).

sources.developer: JPMorgan Chase (ATM hardware from NCR/Diebold Nixdorf)
sources.date: 2023-02 (bank guidance page); technology deployed for over a decade
sources.title: Can You Deposit Cash at an ATM? | Chase
sources.claim: Modern bank ATMs take loose cash and checks without envelopes at an unattended machine, imaging and counting the deposit and crediting the account.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: accepting checks and cash and recording them to an account. The secondary-school variant is mostly checks handed over for logging; ATM check imaging shows unattended machines capturing, reading and posting checks reliably.

roles.title: Teaching Assistants, Special Education
aliases: Basic Skills Improvement Program Instructional Aide (BSIP Instructional Aide)
Early Childhood SPED PARA (Early Childhood Special Education Paraprofessional)
Specialized Programs TA (Specialized Programs Teacher Assistant)
SPED Classroom Aide (Special Education Classroom Aide)
