instances.label: Science teaching-lab TA preparing for a section: gathers reagents, glassware, specimens, probes and consumables from a shared departmental prep room/stockroom, checks quantities against the lab manual, loads a cart, wheels it to the teaching lab, and sets out per-bench kits for 20-24 student stations. Items are varied, some fragile or hazardous; the prep room is crowded and its contents shift week to week.

TA picks up a completed print job (handouts, problem sets, exam packets, course readers) from the campus copy center or the department office mail counter, verifies the count, and carries the boxes/stacks through corridors and elevators to the classroom or instructor's office before class.

TA runs copies themselves at the departmental copier/printer: loads originals and paper, selects duplex/collate/staple settings, clears jams, sorts output into per-section sets, and assembles exam packets.

TA submits an electronic requisition or supplier order (lab consumables, art or shop supplies, desk copies, clicker batteries) through the university procurement system or by email; when the cartons arrive at the department office or dock, opens them, checks contents against the packing slip, resolves shortages, and shelves the items in the supply cabinet or prep room.

TA checks out instructional or AV equipment (projector, laptop, adapters, clickers, anatomical models, art or PE gear) from media services or a storage closet, transports it to the assigned room, and sets it up/connects it before class, returning it afterward.

TA makes a procurement run off-campus or across campus: walks or drives to the bookstore, hardware/craft store, or campus mailroom, selects and purchases or collects the items, and carries them back to the department in whatever weather, over sidewalks, streets and building entrances.

instances.label: Chemistry/biochemistry teaching lab: the TA works through the week's experiment at a student bench before the section - weighs and dissolves reagents, runs the titration/synthesis/extraction, takes spectrometer or melting-point readings, times each step against the 3-hour period, and notes yield problems, ambiguous handout wording and reagent-quantity fixes.

Biology/microbiology/molecular-biology teaching lab: TA pre-runs the protocol - pours plates or prepares media, pipettes reactions, sets up PCR and pours/runs a gel, stains and views slides on the scope - to confirm the samples give visible results for students and to adjust volumes, incubation times or specimen quality.

Physics/electronics/mechanical engineering teaching lab with human-scale apparatus: TA builds the breadboard circuit or clamps the mechanics rig, wires the DMM/oscilloscope/photogates or power supply, runs the trials, and checks that the equipment at each of ~12 stations produces data within tolerance; flags broken leads, bad calibration and unclear wiring diagrams.

Instrument-centred physical-science/engineering lab: TA runs the experiment on a dedicated instrument bench - an optics table setup (beam profiling, interferometer), a tensile/flexure test on a materials testing machine, or an instrumental-analysis run - and checks that the measured curves match expected values before assigning it.

Computational lab: TA works the CS programming assignment, statistics/simulation lab or data-analysis notebook end to end on a computer, checks the starter code and test cases, times how long it takes, and revises the write-up. No physical specimen or apparatus is handled.

Other applied labs and field/clinical exercises: geology or ecology field exercise walked in advance, surveying traverse, psychology human-subject procedure piloted on a volunteer, nursing/clinical simulation scenario rehearsed with a manikin, anatomy dissection prosection prepared - done at varying, uncontrolled sites or with people as subjects.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to faculty members or staff with laboratory or field research.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine, protocol-driven wet-bench support in a faculty research lab: weighing and mixing reagents/buffers, serial dilutions, aliquoting, running standardized assays (PCR, ELISA, titrations, plate cultures), loading samples onto benchtop analyzers and logging results into the lab notebook/LIMS. Standard labware, institution-controlled premises.

Non-routine bench and apparatus support: one-off or newly written protocols, dissecting or preparing specimens, assembling/repairing custom rigs (optics, electronics, flow setups), troubleshooting a misbehaving instrument, and setting up and running human-subject or behavioral sessions for the faculty member's study.

Preparing the instructional laboratory used for the course and faculty's research-linked exercises: making up and labeling stock solutions, assembling per-bench kits and trays, setting out glassware, reagents, specimens and instruments at 15-24 student stations, then collecting, washing and restocking afterwards.

Lab upkeep and logistics: washing and autoclaving glassware, sterilizing media, maintaining cell cultures / plant or animal stocks, calibrating balances and probes, stocking and inventorying consumables, moving samples to freezers/storage, and handling chemical and biohazard waste.

Field data collection at accessible, mappable sites using instrument platforms: gridded soil sampling in research plots, transect/bathymetric/acoustic survey lines on water, deploying and servicing loggers and sensors, and returning georeferenced data or bagged samples to the lab.

Field research support in varied terrain: hauling gear to streams, forests, wetlands, outcrops or dig sites; hand-collecting and labeling specimens; running quadrats, cores and transect measurements; setting camera traps and repairing gear in weather, mud and dense vegetation.

tasks.label: Demonstrate use of laboratory equipment and enforce laboratory rules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-lab demonstration to a section of ~20 undergraduates in a university wet teaching lab (intro chemistry/biology): the TA sets up the day's apparatus on the front bench and shows the standard technique — micropipetting, weighing on an analytical balance, running a titration, loading a spectrophotometer/gel — narrating hazards and common errors, holding items up, and answering questions before students start.

Circulating supervision during a 3-hour lab session: walking the aisles, checking goggles/gloves/closed shoes, stopping eating or phone use, telling students to work in the fume hood, catching improper chemical or sharps handling, directing waste into the right container, and verifying benches are cleaned and equipment shut down before dismissal.

Bench-side one-on-one re-demonstration and troubleshooting: a student's instrument or setup is not working or is being used wrongly (microscope out of focus / oil objective misuse, unbalanced centrifuge, miscalibrated pH meter, oscilloscope trigger set wrong, leaking burette), and the TA diagnoses the problem at that bench, re-shows the correct handling, and watches the student repeat it.

Engineering/physics/shop or instrumentation lab: demonstrating operation of a machine or instrument (lathe, drill press, 3D printer, soldering station, laser or optics bench, ultrasonic tester) and then running the safety checkout — enforcing PPE, guarding, tie-back and laser-eyewear rules, and signing off that each student may operate the machine.

Responding to a rule violation or safety incident during a session: a chemical spill or broken glassware, a small flame or fume release, a student ignoring instructions or doing an unauthorized procedure — the TA halts the work, isolates the hazard, applies spill/eyewash procedure, corrects or removes the student, and reports the incident.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA mobile robot platform)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A KUKA mobile manipulator ('mobile robotic chemist') autonomously operated analytical instruments and performed multi-step wet-chemistry procedures in a chemistry laboratory over eight days without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running lab procedures with standard lab instruments. It transfers to the physical half of 'demonstrate use of laboratory equipment' — same instrument types (solid dispensing, liquid handling, photolysis, chromatography) and comparable precision — but the stations were pre-engineered and calibrated for the robot and no students or teaching interaction were involved.

sources.developer: University of Toronto / Vector Institute / NVIDIA
sources.title: ORGANA: A robotic assistant for automated chemistry experimentation and characterization (Matter)
sources.claim: ORGANA, a Franka-arm benchtop robotic chemistry assistant, autonomously executes standard undergraduate-style chemistry procedures (solubility screening, recrystallization, pH measurement, electrochemistry including electrode polishing) and interacts with chemists in natural language.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing bench chemistry procedures. These are the very procedures a TA demonstrates in a teaching lab, with the same glassware, pH meters and electrodes; the system runs them autonomously from a fixtured benchtop cell and reports in natural language, covering the physical execution part of a demonstration.

sources.title: Donation of Opentrons OT-2 Liquid Handling Robots to UCL Chemical Engineering
sources.claim: Opentrons OT-2 and Flex liquid-handling robots are commercially deployed inside university teaching laboratories, where they autonomously execute pipetting protocols (DNA assembly, PCR screening, cell viability assays) during student lab sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: executing a pipetting protocol. Transfers to the physical execution of a standard teaching-lab technique demonstration — same pipettes, tips and labware, same volumetric precision — but only with labware fixtured in known deck positions, i.e. work brought to the machine.

sources.developer: Institute of Science Tokyo (Maholo LabDroid by Yaskawa/Robotic Biology Institute)
sources.title: Tokyo Unmanned Lab Opens With Robots At Work, No Human Staff
sources.claim: An unmanned robotic laboratory with 10 robots including the dual-arm Maholo LabDroid runs medical/biology experiments with no on-site human staff, performing reagent transfers, opening temperature-controlled equipment and automated cell ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous execution of laboratory protocols with standard labware. Shows purpose-built robotic lab cells can perform the manipulations a demonstration would show, but the facility explicitly operates without people present, so it says nothing about supervising or instructing students.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) framework socially assistive robot
sources.title: Socially Assistive Robot as Laboratory Safety Assistant for Science Students (IEEE Xplore)
sources.claim: A socially assistive 'Laboratory Safety Assistant' robot framework is a research prototype aimed at detecting student behaviours that could cause lab accidents; it is a detection/alerting framework, not a deployed system that enforces lab rules on students.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published work to 'enforce laboratory rules'; cited to document that only behaviour detection has been prototyped, with no evidence of autonomous, worker-quality enforcement of rules on students, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Humanoid robots and lab machines attract researchers at SLAS (C&EN)
sources.claim: Humanoid robots presented for laboratory work at the 2026 SLAS lab-automation conference were being driven by human operators rather than running autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish that general-purpose humanoid lab robots able to move around a human lab and handle arbitrary equipment remain teleoperated as of 2026, so they cannot support positive judgments at E2.

tasks.label: Provide instructors with assistance in the use of audiovisual equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pre-class setup at a standard classroom/lecture-hall lectern: wake the podium AV system, connect the instructor's own laptop via the podium HDMI/USB-C cable (often with a dongle), power the projector, lower the screen, select the input, confirm image/resolution, set audio level, and check the wireless mic battery before the class starts.

Live troubleshooting when the AV fails, usually with a class waiting: no signal after connecting, wrong input, mirroring/resolution problem, no sound, dead lapel mic battery, wireless presentation system won't pair, Zoom/Teams audio routed to the wrong device. Requires diagnosis across laptop, cable, switcher, projector and the instructor's own settings.

Running lecture capture / hybrid streaming for a class: starting the recording, keeping the instructor framed as they move across the stage and write on the board, capturing the content feed, and delivering a usable recording/stream to remote students.

Hands-on media operation during class: advancing slides on the instructor's cue, cueing and playing video clips, swapping between podium PC and document camera, adjusting volume, and carrying the handheld mic to students asking questions in the seats.

Transporting and setting up portable AV in a seminar room, teaching lab or off-site session with no built-in equipment: wheeling a cart with projector, laptop and powered speaker, erecting a tripod screen, running and taping cables, finding wall power, aligning and focusing the projection, then striking it afterwards.

Coaching the instructor in using the equipment: walking them through the lectern touch panel, showing how to start the recording software or share a screen, clipping on and testing a lapel mic, and answering questions during a pre-semester room orientation.

sources.title: EC20 PTZ Camera for Lecture Capture | 4K, AI Tracking | Epiphan
sources.claim: Epiphan EC20 is a commercial AI auto-tracking PTZ camera built for classroom lecture capture; on-camera AI performs presenter tracking, focus and exposure autonomously and it records natively to Panopto.

sources.developer: SHaRe-RL research group (Stranghöner, Hartmann et al.)
sources.title: SHaRe-RL: Structured, Interactive Reinforcement Learning for Contact-Rich Industrial Assembly Tasks
sources.claim: A UR3e arm with wrist force/torque sensing and a wrist camera autonomously inserts industrial Harting connectors with 0.2-0.4 mm tolerance in a fixtured cell, reported at 95% success and 5.4 s cycle time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic mating of electrical connectors in a fixtured cell. The crux of the TA's setup instance is mating a small signal connector (HDMI/USB-C) at sub-millimetre tolerance; demonstrated tolerances and contact forces are comparable, but only with the workpiece fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Behavioral Cloning for Robotic Connector Assembly: An Empirical Study
sources.claim: A learned vision+force policy inserts five different connector geometries autonomously with 92.8% average success using only a grayscale camera and force-torque sensing, without pose information.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-geometry connector insertion. Shows one fixtured cell can handle several connector types, as a lectern robot would face HDMI, USB-C and DisplayPort; success rates remain below what an employer would accept for a live class and parts are presented in a purpose-built rig.

sources.title: Rocsys unveils next version of its robotic charging solution - electrive.com
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic charging systems autonomously locate a vehicle's charging port, open the flap and insert and remove the charging connector without human intervention, in port and depot operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plug insertion into a port whose pose varies inside a working facility. It supports connector-mating capability generally, but EV inlets are large, mechanically guided and standardised, unlike a small port on an arbitrary laptop, so it does not carry over to an untouched lectern.

sources.title: 3E8 Robotics introduces Elly delivery robot that can detect and press elevator buttons - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: 3E8 Robotics' Elly delivery robot uses an on-device AI-driven actuator to locate and physically press buttons on elevator panels and keypads in ordinary multi-floor buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided pressing of wall/panel buttons. Powering a projector and selecting an input on a lectern control panel is the same class of action (locate a labelled button, press it), supporting that sub-step of AV setup.

tasks.label: Select materials for use based on strength, color, texture, balance, weight, size, malleability and other characteristics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Studio potter/ceramicist choosing materials for a piece: opening clay bags and wedging a lump to judge moisture, plasticity and grog, comparing test tiles to pick glazes for color, surface texture and fit to the clay body. Cluttered small studio, dusty, idiosyncratic storage.

Fiber/needlecraft artist (weaver, knitter, quilter) pulling yarns and fabrics from stash bins or supplier shelves: checking fiber content, yarn weight/gauge, fabric weight and drape by hand, and matching colors and textures for the planned piece.

Jewelry maker / welded-metal sculptor selecting stock from racks and bins: sheet gauge, wire alloy and temper, tube and bar sizes; checking straightness, soundness, malleability (annealed vs work-hardened) and weight/heft for the intended piece. Small owner-run metal shop.

Woodworker, leatherworker or glass artist picking sheet goods at a supplier or from shop racks: sorting boards for grain, color match, knots, warp and stiffness; hides for defect-free usable zones; sheet stock for thickness and weight. Lumberyard/supplier with standard racking.

Mixed-media artist sourcing found and natural materials: beach, roadside, salvage yard or flea market, picking driftwood, stones, rusted hardware, vintage textiles and cast-offs judged for their look, heft, soundness and potential in a future piece.

sources.developer: Valvan Baling Systems / Fibersort Consortium (Wieland Textiles)
sources.title: Fibersort - Wieland Textiles
sources.claim: Fibersort is a commercial, fully automatic conveyor-based installation that optically scans post-consumer textiles and sorts them into categories by fiber composition, color and structure at about 900 kg/hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated textile sorting. It performs the same discrimination a fiber craft artist makes when choosing stock - fiber content, color and fabric structure - on material presented to the machine, at commercial throughput and accuracy.

sources.title: AMP Robotics Launches Material Characterization Solution to Improve Recycling
sources.claim: AMP's Cortex robotic sorting systems, deployed at scale in material recovery facilities, identify materials by color, texture, shape, size and label and then robotically pick and place them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting of mixed material streams. It selects individual pieces of heterogeneous material by exactly the perceptual criteria in this task (color, texture, shape, size) and physically picks the chosen piece off a conveyor.

sources.title: WEINIG Experience: EasyScan Smart C
sources.claim: Weinig Luxscan EasyScan Smart C is a commercial wood scanner that detects knots, wane, holes and color variation on each board and drives optimizing cross-cut saws and sorting at production speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grading and sorting of lumber. It makes the same board-by-board judgment a woodworker makes when picking stock - defects, grain, color match - on boards presented by a feed line, and routes each board accordingly.

sources.title: Lectra Aims to Disrupt Auto Leather Value Chain with New Technology
sources.claim: Lectra's Versalis leather line scans each hide as it is loaded to map quality zones and defects, then automatically nests the order over a sequence of ... before cutting; used commercially in automotive and furniture leather cutting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hide quality assessment for cutting. Judging which regions of a natural, variable material are strong and defect-free enough for a part is the same selection judgment a leather or wood craft artist makes on presented stock.

sources.title: Introducing Helix 02: Full-Body Autonomy
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 humanoid autonomously extracts small metal components from a cluttered pile using visual grasp selection with tactile ..., running on real parts at Figure's BotQ manufacturing facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving specified metal stock from a jumbled supply bin. Comparable objects (small metal parts), comparable clutter, and the tactile/visual confirmation step matches a metalsmith checking a piece of stock before taking it.

sources.title: Inbolt provides vision guidance in real time for new bin-picking system
sources.claim: Inbolt's vision-guided bin-picking system locates and picks parts autonomously from unstructured bins and is running in production at more than five factories, with the company serving over 70 factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identifying and retrieving a specified part from mixed stock. Selecting the right gauge/size piece of metal stock from a bin is the same perception-and-pick problem on comparable rigid metal objects.

sources.system: Finger-shaped tactile sensor with robotic sliding
sources.title: Fabric Classification Using a Finger-Shaped Tactile Sensor via Robotic Sliding
sources.claim: A finger-shaped tactile sensor on a robot performing sliding exploration classified everyday fabrics by their fine texture with up to 96% accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tactile discrimination of fabrics. It substantiates the hand/texture judgment a fiber artist makes by touch, on the same class of materials, with the fabric presented to the robot.

sources.title: e-David: A Painting Robot That Can Even Sign Its Own Name
sources.claim: The e-David painting robot uses visual feedback of the evolving canvas to choose brushes and colors from a fixed repository of 24 colors and five brushes in a purpose-built painting rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous art-making. It shows a machine choosing among presented art materials by color for a specific artwork - the aesthetic side of material selection - though only within a fixed, purpose-built palette station.

tasks.label: Create functional or decorative objects by hand, using a variety of methods and materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Studio potter makes a repeat batch of an established functional design (e.g., 24 stoneware mugs or bowls): wedging clay, throwing/forming, trimming, attaching handles, bisque firing, glazing, glaze firing, in the artist's own small studio with a wheel, damp shelves and an electric kiln.

Fiber craft artist produces a repeat run of textile goods for sale — knitted hats/scarves, sewn tote bags or plush items, machine- or hand-embroidered decorated blanks — working from an established pattern at a home studio table with yarn, cloth, a domestic sewing machine and hand tools.

Jeweler/small metalworker fabricates earrings, pendants or rings: cutting and forming wire and sheet, torch soldering, bezel or prong stone setting, beadwork, filing, tumbling and polishing at a bench in a home or rented studio, often in small runs with slight variations per piece.

Carved, turned or welded decorative object in wood, stone or metal: roughing out and detail-carving a sculpture or relief, turning a bowl, or welding a metal garden sculpture from an established model or design, in the artist's shop with saws, chisels, lathe, grinder or MIG welder.

Molded or poured small-batch goods: pouring scented candles into vessels, cutting/stamping cold-process soap, casting resin or plaster ornaments, slumping or casting small glass pieces — repeatable recipes and molds worked in a home kitchen-studio or small workshop.

One-off, improvised handwork piece for exhibition or commission: hand-built ceramic sculpture with carved/slip-decorated surface, crocheted or hand-embroidered art textile, tapestry woven on a floor loom, or mixed-media assemblage combining found objects, where form and materials are decided while making.

sources.title: Meet ROBOTOR, the Robotic Sculptor of Marble Statues - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: Robotor/TorArt operate multi-axis robotic milling cells in Carrara that carve marble sculptures and reproductions end to end; software generates the machining program from a 3D file and the robot executes all carving steps, with replicas delivered without hand finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stone sculpture carving/reproduction. It is the same class of output craft artists make (carved decorative objects), at the same or finer precision, and the source states the machine performs all carving steps from the 3D model, with the replica left unfinished by hand.

sources.system: Delta WASP 40100 Clay Production printer (Continuous Feeding System + Automated Production System)

sources.claim: Commercial clay/ceramic 3D printers form vases, sculptures and other ceramic objects unattended; with the automated production system that swaps print trays the machine runs as a continuous 24/7 production cell for identical or customized clay objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: additive forming of ceramic ware. Same material (clay/porcelain) and same object class (vessels, decorative ceramics) as a studio potter's repeat production; substitutes for the forming stage of the instance in a purpose-built machine setting.

sources.system: Yutai automatic ceramic forming line / automatic pottery glazing machine
sources.title: Automatic Ceramic Forming Line for Plates, Cups, Mugs Making Machine | Yutai Machine
sources.claim: Fully automatic ceramic tableware lines form, dry, demould and trim cups, bowls and plates in one continuous workflow and connect directly to an automatic glazing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial forming and glazing of tableware. The finished object (glazed, fired mug or bowl) is the same functional object a production potter makes in repeat batches, at equal or better dimensional consistency, but produced with the work presented to fixed machinery.

sources.system: Rollon gantry glazing line with ABB FlexPicker

sources.claim: Automated pottery glazing lines use robots to pick cups and bowls from pallets onto conveyors and dip them through glaze, replacing hand-dipping in ceramic ware production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic glazing of pottery. Glazing is the decisive finishing step of the ceramics instance; the robot handles the same fragile greenware/bisque cups and bowls and applies glaze to production quality in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: I ♡ WHOLEGARMENT® | SHIMA SEIKI
sources.claim: Computerized flat knitting machines knit complete three-dimensional garments (sweaters, hats, accessories) in one piece directly off the machine with no cutting or sewing, from a digital design and loaded yarn.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial whole-garment knitting. The output (a finished knitted hat, scarf or sweater) is the same object a craft knitter produces in repeat runs, with equal or better stitch consistency, produced from a digital pattern with only yarn loading by a human.

sources.title: Sewbots® - Softwear Automation
sources.claim: SoftWear Automation's Sewbot worklines use machine vision and robotics to steer limp fabric through sewing stations and sew finished T-shirts automatically, deployed in dedicated automated sewing factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic sewing of limp fabric. Sewn craft goods (tote bags, simple soft goods) involve the same deformable material handling and stitching precision; the cited line completes whole sewn articles rather than a sub-step.

sources.system: Automatic rotating tealight candle production line

sources.title: Supply Auto Tealight Production Line Wholesale Factory - LIAONING GAOGE NEW MATERIAL CO.,LTD
sources.claim: Fully automatic candle production lines carry out the whole candle-making sequence — wax handling, wicking, pressing/pouring, cooling and demoulding — without human intervention between load and finished product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial candle manufacturing. The finished object (a poured/pressed wax candle with wick) is the same product a craft chandler makes from a fixed recipe and mold, and the line completes it end to end in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: G3DP / G3DP2 molten glass printing platform

sources.claim: MIT's G3DP platform deposits molten glass through a heated nozzle from a kiln cartridge into annealed, optically transparent glass vessels and decorative objects that have been exhibited as artworks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine forming of hot glass objects. It produces the same class of decorative glass vessels a glass craft artist makes, autonomously within a purpose-built heated enclosure, supporting the glass portion of the molded/poured instance.

sources.developer: Christian Tse Design & Manufacturing with FRE
sources.title: Christian Tse on the Future of Jewelry Manufacturing - JCK
sources.claim: Automation in fine jewelry manufacturing is concentrated on finishing: Christian Tse introduced two-arm robots adapted from automotive work for polishing jewelry, not for fabricating, soldering or setting whole pieces.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to scope jewelry automation: it substantiates only a finishing sub-step (polishing), not fabrication, soldering or stone setting, so it cannot support completion of the whole jewelry instance.

sources.title: RoPotter: Toward Robotic Pottery and Deformable Object Manipulation with Structural Priors
sources.claim: Robotic pottery remains a research problem: the RoPotter system studies wheel-based clay shaping with a robot arm, using a human-held game controller to drive the arm while cameras capture the clay state, and addresses only basic shaping primitives.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (wheel pottery) but teleoperated data collection at research scale; cited only to support the negative judgment that improvised hand-forming of clay is not yet done autonomously at worker quality.

instances.label: Studio potter glazes a small batch of handmade ware (mugs, bowls, vases) with a single uniform glaze: dips or sprays the glaze, wipes the foot clean, sets pieces on a rack for kiln loading. Own or rented studio, pieces of varying but related shapes.

Ceramic artist applies an artistic multi-layer surface treatment to one-off pieces: wax resist on rims and feet, brushed overglaze/oxide washes, slip trailing or sponged accents on irregular sculptural forms, judging coverage by eye piece-by-piece.

Woodcraft artist finishes turned bowls, carvings, or small furniture: applies oil/wax/varnish/lacquer, sands between coats, wipes back and buffs, adapting to grain, end grain and figure on each unique piece. Home or small shop with a rudimentary spray area.

Metalsmith/jewelry maker finishes small irregular metal pieces: buffs and polishes, applies a chemical patina or plating, then a protective lacquer or wax; pieces are small, delicate, and each is slightly different. Bench studio with a buffing motor and small fume area.

Craft artist applies a protective clear coat or sealant to painted or mixed-media decorative objects (painted gourds, signs, resin/wood assemblages, glass-mosaic pieces) — spray or brush, one or two coats, small batches, in a garage or studio spray area.

Fiber/textile artist finishes woven, felted or needlecraft pieces: wet-blocking and pinning a knit or woven panel to shape, applying stiffener or sizing to baskets/lace, or spraying fabric protector on a limp, deformable finished piece.

sources.title: Automated Production Line in Ceramic Manufacturing | KUKA Global

Same finish material (glaze) on fired-clay bodies of complex curved shape, same quality criterion (even, defect-free coat), so it transfers to a craft potter's uniform glaze coat when the piece is presented in a glazing booth.

sources.title: Çanakcilar Seramik starts up the second Gaiotto glazing system | Ceramic World Web

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic glaze spraying of sanitaryware. The robot is programmed by a glazer hand-guiding it, then executes autonomously — the same mode a small-batch craft glazing job would use, with comparable glaze material and coverage tolerances.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dip-glazing of tableware. Dipping is the dominant studio-pottery glazing method; the objects (saucers, cups) are the same scale and fragility as craft ware, so the demonstrated grip-dip-swirl motion transfers when parts are presented in a cell.

sources.title: Cefla Finishing Lab Adds Cartesian Spray Robot | IWF Atlanta
sources.claim: A commercially sold cartesian spray robot scans workpieces of varying shape ... on the line and then sprays coating on them, installed in a finishing lab and sold for wood/panel finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated spray coating of wood panels and shaped components (lacquer, varnish, stain). Same finish materials and film-quality standard as craft wood finishing; scanning removes the need for per-piece programming, which matters for one-off craft shapes.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated clear-coat/varnish spraying of irregularly shaped products (flower pots, appliance parts, doors). Craft sealing of painted or mixed-media objects uses the same sprayed coatings and the same acceptance criterion of an even, run-free film.

Craft metal finishing (buffing and polishing before patina/lacquer) uses the same abrasive and buffing media and force-control demands; scanning handles part-to-part variation typical of handmade pieces.

sources.system: Cohesive Robotics woodworking finishing workcell (Argus OS)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding of wood parts. Sanding between finish coats and final buffing are integral steps of applying a wood finish; force-controlled sanding on scanned, non-CAD parts covers the shape variation of craft pieces.

tasks.label: Cut, shape, fit, join, mold, or otherwise process materials, using hand tools, power tools, or machinery.

instances.label: Ceramics: in a home or rented studio, the artist wedges clay and forms vessels and ware (wheel-thrown mugs and bowls, press-molded or slab-built planters and tiles), trims them, and readies the greenware for drying and firing; small repeat batches for shows and wholesale orders.

Fiber and textile craft: in a home studio, cutting fabric/felt/yarn goods to pattern and machine-sewing, quilting, weaving, or knitting them into finished pieces (bags, quilts, scarves, wall hangings), often in small repeat runs.

Woodcraft: in a garage or small shop, ripping and crosscutting stock on table saw/bandsaw, shaping and carving (router, chisels, lathe), sanding, and fitting and gluing joints for boxes, bowls, small furniture and carved objects.

Metal and stone work: in a fabrication-style shop with standard equipment (welder, grinder, plasma cutter, anvil/forge, pneumatic carving tools), cutting plate and bar, welding or forging sculptural and functional pieces, and grinding/finishing welds and carved surfaces.

Fine jewelry bench work: at a jeweler's bench in a small private studio, piercing and sawing sheet and wire, forming and forging small parts, torch-soldering bezels, findings and joints, setting stones, and filing/polishing the finished piece.

Sheet and mixed-media craft: scoring and cutting glass for stained/fused panels, cutting leather, paper, acrylic and mosaic tesserae to pattern, grinding or edge-finishing pieces, and joining them (foiling and soldering, stitching, gluing) in a home studio.

sources.title: Robotic Sculpture Change Marble Carving Art - Inside Telecom

sources.transferJustification: Robotic carving of one-off sculpture is the shaping half of this task performed on art-grade workpieces inside a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: The Technology - Path Robotics

sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics Unveils 100,000-Square-Foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson | RoboticsTomorrow

sources.transferJustification: Sanding, grinding and polishing shaped workpieces is the surface-shaping/finishing element of "otherwise process materials" in wood and metal craft work, on comparably sized parts.

Woodworker, glass or metal craft artist builds a scale model or full-size mockup of a piece (chair, cabinet, sculptural form, lamp) in wood, foam, board or a test-blown/cast material to check proportion and joinery before the finished object.

instances.label: Weekend outdoor juried art/craft festival in a park or on a closed street: research and apply to the show, produce/pack inventory, drive a loaded van, unload with a dolly, erect a 10x10 canopy with weights, set up grid walls/tables/lighting, arrange fragile handmade work (pottery, glass, jewelry), staff the booth two days in wind, heat or rain, talk technique and pricing with browsers, take card/cash payments, wrap and bag purchases, then tear down and reload.

Indoor community holiday craft fair in a school gym, church hall, VFW or community center: haul totes in from a parking lot, dress a rented 6-ft table, build a small display, staff the booth for a day, engage shoppers, sell and package items, restock from under-table stock, pack out at closing.

Large indoor juried show or wholesale gift/trade show at a convention center or armory: dock load-in with crates and dollies, build a pipe-and-drape or modular booth to show rules, stage inventory and signage, staff a multi-day booth, converse with retail buyers and consumers, write orders/take payments, break down and ship out.

Recurring weekly outdoor artisan/farmers market stall in a parking lot, plaza or street: quick canopy and table setup, cash box and card reader, sell small handmade goods to passersby for 4-6 hours, handle weather and neighboring vendors, strike the stall.

Planning-weighted episode with a light in-person component: from home studio, research show calendars, prepare juried applications with booth and product photos, pay fees, plan inventory and travel, promote appearances; then a short physical errand such as scouting the venue, delivering a display fixture or consignment case to a shop-hosted trunk show, and setting it up.

sources.title: IntBot to Debut First-Ever Unmanned CES Booth Run by a Robot; Humanoid "Nylo" Takes the Floor Solo
sources.claim: IntBot announced that its CES 2026 exhibit would be staffed for the opening day solely by its Nylo humanoid social robot, greeting visitors and conversing on the trade show floor; the robot performs conversational booth-greeting only and does not build the booth, handle merchandise, or transact sales.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staffing an exhibit booth and engaging visitors. It covers only the conversational sub-step of attending a craft show; it is a vendor press announcement about a single show day, with no merchandise handling, payment taking, setup or teardown, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.title: Galbot G1: The Humanoid Robot Revolutionizing Retail with Award-Winning Precision
sources.claim: Galbot's G1 wheeled humanoid is deployed in unmanned stores and pharmacies in Beijing, autonomously locating and retrieving packaged products for customers in a purpose-built unmanned retail space stocked and maintained by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: serving customers at an unmanned retail point. It shows item retrieval and vending of standardized packaged goods in a fixed, purpose-built store; it does not transport inventory to a venue, erect or dress a booth, arrange fragile one-off handmade work, or strike a display, so it covers only part of the sell-at-a-booth sub-step.

sources.title: A Humanoid Robot Is About to Run a 24-Hour Store in Hong Kong
sources.claim: A Galbot G1 unit ('Xiao Gai') is reported as running a 24-hour store in Hong Kong performing restocking, product retrieval, inventory and checkout — all inside a fixed, standardized convenience-store format rather than a temporary event booth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended retail clerking. Transfer is limited: the goods are uniform packaged SKUs on fixed shelving in an institution-controlled store, whereas a craft show requires vehicle transport, canopy/booth erection on unprepared ground, arranging unique fragile handmade pieces, persuasive maker-to-buyer selling, and teardown.

Works on paper at a studio desk: original pen-and-ink, charcoal, graphite or watercolor drawings and illustrations — sketching from life, photo reference or imagination, blending/erasing charcoal, inking line work, washing watercolor, on paper of varying size taped or clipped to a board.

Digital artwork: illustrator creates original images with computer software (Photoshop, Procreate, Illustrator, 3D tools) using a stylus and tablet at a desk; the deliverable is a file, with layers, revisions and client-directed changes.

Sculpture and three-dimensional work in a studio/workshop: modeling clay, carving stone or wood, welding or assembling mixed media, moldmaking and finishing — heavy, irregular material handled with hand and power tools in a cluttered shop.

On-location work: plein-air watercolor or sketching outdoors or at a live event — carrying and setting up an easel or sketchbook, working from direct observation in changing light, wind and passers-by, finishing a small piece in one sitting.

sources.claim: CoFRIDA, the successor system, paints and draws on real paper/canvas in a lab setup and won the ICRA 2024 best paper award for human-robot interaction, showing the painting/drawing pipeline is a peer-reviewed, reproducible robotic capability rather than a one-off stunt.

sources.title: The e-David project – Rediscovering Art and Artisanship Through Robotic Painting
sources.claim: e-David, a long-running robotic painting project at the University of Konstanz, paints with real brushes and paint at a fixed easel, observing its own canvas with a camera and adapting strokes in a feedback loop to build up a painting in layers; its outputs are exhibited as artworks.

sources.developer: Aidan Meller / Engineered Arts / Oxford and Leeds engineering teams
sources.title: AI Robot Artist Strikes Gold By Selling Painting Of Alan Turing For $1.3 Million
sources.claim: Ai-Da, a humanoid robot with cameras in its eyes and a KUKA robotic arm, physically applied acrylic and oil paint to canvas, producing 15 individual portrait paintings of Alan Turing at roughly six to eight hours each; human studio assistants and a 3D texture printer were used to assemble and finish the final large polyptych panel.

sources.title: Artwork Made by Humanoid Robot Ai-Da Using AI Algorithms Sells for $1 M. at Sotheby's
sources.claim: The resulting robot-made painting was accepted and sold on the fine-art market at Sotheby's for $1.08 million, evidence that output produced by a robot at a painting station can be accepted as a finished original artwork.

sources.developer: Engineered Arts / University of Oxford algorithms / Leeds arm team
sources.title: Meet the Robot Artist Who Just Became the First to Stage a Solo Exhibition
sources.claim: Ai-Da draws and paints from what its eye camera sees, with algorithms converting the captured image into arm trajectories; its drawings and self-portraits have been exhibited at museums such as London's Design Museum.

sources.title: Montreal's Acrylic Robotics mixes paint and robots to produce fine art
sources.claim: Acrylic Robotics runs a commercial robot painting cell in which an arm dips a brush into paint wells and lays down brushstrokes on canvas from stroke-level data, producing painted (not printed) fine-art canvases; demonstrated live at AWS re:Invent 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: brushstroke-level execution of a painting on canvas. It shows a purpose-built painting cell can produce gallery-grade painted surfaces with the same media, tools and precision as the studio painting instance, though the composition is supplied rather than invented.

sources.developer: Robotor (Giacomo Massari, Filippo Tincolini), with KUKA and HSD
sources.title: Meet ROBOTOR, the Robotic Sculptor of Marble Statues
sources.claim: ROBOTOR multi-axis robots in the TorArt workshop in Carrara autonomously carve marble sculptures from digital models for contemporary artists and designers, producing large finished stone works in a purpose-built robotic stone-milling cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sculptural fabrication in stone. It demonstrates robotic execution of an original three-dimensional artwork to exhibition finish when the block is fixtured and the form is presented digitally, matching the E1 counterfactual for the sculpture instance.

tasks.label: Integrate and develop visual elements, such as line, space, mass, color, and perspective, to produce desired effects, such as the illustration of ideas, emotions, or moods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Studio painter develops an original oil or acrylic painting on stretched canvas in their own or a shared rented studio: blocks in the composition, mixes colors on a palette, adjusts value, edges and perspective across several sessions, stepping back to judge the effect. Canvas size, subject and support vary from work to work.

Illustrator executes a commissioned image to a client brief (book cover, editorial spread, poster, album art) at a desk in a home office or studio — usually digitally on a tablet, sometimes ink, gouache or watercolor on paper — composing figures, color and depth to carry a specified mood, then revising after art-director feedback.

Sculptor develops a three-dimensional work — modeling clay or plaster, carving stone or wood, welding steel, assembling mixed media — in a private studio or shared fabrication shop, resolving mass, silhouette and negative space in the round and finishing surfaces to the intended effect.

Preparatory work: thumbnails, value studies, perspective layouts, color roughs or small maquettes made in the studio or on location (plein air, life drawing session) to settle composition, light and mood before committing to the final piece.

Site-specific or public-facing production inside an institution: painting or drawing during a gallery/museum residency, a live demonstration at an art fair or festival booth, or a commissioned mural in a venue-controlled lobby or wall, with staff, visitors and fixed schedules around the work.

sources.system: FRIDA (Framework and Robotics Initiative for Developing Arts)
sources.title: Carnegie Mellon's AI-Powered FRIDA Robot Collaborates with Humans To Create Art
sources.claim: FRIDA, a robot arm with a brush at CMU's Robotics Institute, takes a high-level goal (text, image or audio), plans a painting in simulation using vision-language models, and executes it on canvas with camera feedback in a lab rig where a human mixes and presents the paint.

sources.title: Painting Robot e-David | Research | Visual Computing
sources.claim: e-David decomposes an image into shapes, chooses a style for each region, plans strokes, and paints acrylic/ink/gouache on canvas while a camera supervises and iteratively corrects errors; it has produced realistic portraits and abstract compositions shown in exhibitions.

sources.title: Painting Robot e-David | Research | Visual Computing
sources.claim: e-David's painting robots are fixed installations in a robotics lab, with a smaller ABB arm and a paper-feed rig that can be transported to exhibitions; the workpiece is always presented to the machine on its own rig.

sources.developer: Aidan Meller / Engineered Arts (arm by Salah Al Abd and Ziad Abass)
sources.title: Artwork Made by Humanoid Robot Ai-Da Using AI Algorithms Sells for $1 M. at Sotheby's
sources.claim: Ai-Da, a humanoid robot with cameras and a robotic painting arm, produced 'A.I. God. Portrait of Alan ...', which sold at Sotheby's for $1,084,800 — evidence that robot-made paintings can reach an art market that accepts them as finished works.

sources.title: AI-Powered Robots in the Art World: Applications in Contemporary Art and Museums
sources.claim: Analysis of AI robots in galleries and museums reports that Ai-Da's artworks depend on a surrounding human team, i.e. the robot does not complete works with only limited intervention.

sources.title: King Charles III Gets A New Portrait — Painted By A Humanoid Robot
sources.claim: Ai-Da painted 'Algorithm King', an oil-on-canvas portrait of King Charles III made from photographs rather than a sitting, unveiled at the UK Mission in Geneva for the 2025 UN AI for Good Summit; press reviews were lukewarm about its quality.

sources.system: cloudpainter / Van Arman AI painting robots
sources.title: Inside the Studio With an AI-Guided Painting Robot
sources.claim: TIME commissioned Pindar Van Arman's AI painting robot to make artwork illustrating a cover story; the robot painted for 22 hours and about 13,940 brush strokes in his studio rig, making many aesthetic decisions itself under the artist's guidance.

sources.system: artonomous (ST Robotics R17 HS painting robot)
sources.title: Artist Pindar Van Arman Develops ST Robotics' Collaborative Robot into the World's Most Evocative Painting Robot
sources.claim: An ST Robotics R17 arm with a brush in its gripper and a camera on the arm, running more than two dozen AI algorithms, was integrated by Van Arman to paint curated portraits autonomously at a fixed painting station.

sources.title: ROBOTOR: the robot-sculptor that carves Carrara marble!
sources.claim: Robotor/TorArt run robotic carving cells in Carrara that machine finished marble sculptures for name artists from scans and 3D models — the robot realizes a form supplied to it, it does not originate the composition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stone carving. It shows a machine can shape mass and surface in stone to museum standards, but the three-dimensional design is supplied as a digital model by the artist, so it does not transfer to developing the sculptural form itself.

sources.title: AI robots can already carve stone statues. Entire buildings are next
sources.claim: Monumental Labs uses seven-axis robotic arms in a New York factory to carve museum-grade marble sculptures and facade ornament, but the robot-cut pieces are finished by hand by trained stone carvers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic carving of sculpture and ornament. It demonstrates machine shaping of stone in a fixtured factory cell, but the design comes from a digital model and human carvers complete the piece, so the whole artistic task is not machine-completed.

sources.title: RobotSculptor: Artist-Directed Robotic Sculpting of Clay
sources.claim: RobotSculptor lets a user create stylized clay sculptures with a standard 6-axis arm: the system generates tool paths from a base mesh the user supplies and applies algorithmic sculpting styles while the arm removes clay in a lab cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic clay sculpting. It shows an arm can shape clay to a style, but the base form is authored by the human, so it substantiates execution rather than developing the three-dimensional composition.
