tasks.label: Study different techniques to learn how to apply them to artistic endeavors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A studio painter researching a technique (e.g., glazing, underpainting, encaustic layering) by reading books, articles, and technical manuals, and watching recorded demonstrations online, in order to understand how the method works and whether it suits a planned piece.

An illustrator studying digital and hybrid techniques — brush engines, layer/blend workflows, new software or AI-assisted tools — through tutorials, forums, and observation of other illustrators' process breakdowns, to add the method to their repertoire.

A fine artist examining original works in a museum, gallery, or collection — studying surface, mark-making, palette, and construction of pieces by other artists — and taking notes or sketching to deduce how the effects were achieved.

A sculptor or mixed-media artist attending a workshop, class, residency demonstration, or peer studio visit where a technique (e.g., mold-making, patination, welding, kiln work) is shown and discussed, learning its steps, materials, and hazards.

An artist doing exploratory hands-on trials in their own studio — test panels, maquettes, sample swatches — to internalize a technique read about or observed, where the artifacts are discarded and only the acquired understanding matters.

tasks.label: Monitor events, trends, and other circumstances, research specific subject areas, attend art exhibitions, and read art publications to develop ideas and keep current on art world activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Photograph objects, places, or scenes for reference material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-location reference shoot of a place or scene: the artist travels to a landscape, streetscape, park, farm building or piece of architecture and photographs it from several vantage points, working with available light, weather and passers-by, to build reference images for a painting.

Opportunistic and close-range reference capture while out: snapshots of details and textures encountered on the street or in nature (bark, rust, lichen, drapery on a chair, a shop window, hands, sky, a passing dog), taken handheld as the subject presents itself.

Studio still-life shoot: the artist arranges objects, props, fabric, skulls or plants on a table in their own (often cluttered, idiosyncratic) studio, sets lamps or window light, and shoots the arrangement from several angles and distances for later painting reference.

Live-subject session: a model, family member or pet posed in the studio (or a person in motion outdoors) is photographed for figure, portrait or gesture reference; the artist directs poses, adjusts lighting and shoots many frames at eye level.

Reference shoot inside an institution: photographing artworks, artifacts, taxidermy or period interiors in a museum, historic house, zoo or botanical garden, working within the venue's rules and fixed layout, often without flash.

sources.title: How to use 3D Capture with Skydio X10 – Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan lets Skydio drones autonomously plan and fly adaptive scan patterns around a designated outdoor structure or scene, photographing it from every angle to produce a comprehensive image set; sold and used commercially for inspection and documentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous photographic documentation of structures/scenes for inspection and 3D reconstruction. It transfers to shooting reference material of a place because the subjects (buildings, terrain, machinery), the working distances and the output (a multi-viewpoint high-resolution photo set of a real scene) are the same; only the downstream use differs.

sources.title: SpotWalk comes to construction in HoloBuilder, Boston Dynamics teamup
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped, running HoloBuilder's SpotWalk app, walks construction job sites on its own and captures 360-degree images documenting the site over time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous progress-documentation photography of an unstructured site. It transfers to photographing places/scenes for reference because the robot navigates a site taken as found and returns usable wide-scene imagery, though its route is taught by a human first.

sources.title: Automated Inspections Made Simple | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot robots run recorded Autowalk inspection missions autonomously in industrial plants, stopping at checkpoints to photograph specified objects such as analog gauges and equipment; deployed commercially for routine rounds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous image capture of designated objects inside a human work facility. It transfers to reference photography of objects in an institutional venue because the robot positions itself and frames a specified subject at close range, producing documentation-quality images.

sources.title: PhotoBench 280 - 360 Photography Lightbox and Software
sources.claim: Ortery PhotoBench product-photography systems are purpose-built rigs in which software drives the lights, camera and motorized turntable to capture multi-angle, evenly lit image sets of an object placed inside; a standard commercial product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-angle product photography. It transfers to shooting objects for artistic reference because the objects (small to mid-sized props), the lighting control and the deliverable (sharp, well-exposed images of the object from many angles) match what an artist collects as reference.

sources.title: Google Art Camera uses robotic system to take gigapixel photos of museum paintings: DPReview
sources.claim: Google's Art Camera is a robotic ... mount that, once positioned and calibrated against a work in a museum gallery, automatically shoots hundreds of focused close-ups of the painting and stitches them into a gigapixel image; used across partner museums worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic photographic digitization of artworks in museums. It transfers to an artist's institutional reference shoot: same venue type, same subjects (paintings and flat works), and an output of detailed images captured without a human framing each frame.

sources.title: Pilot project takes automated inventory management to the next level | DC Velocity
sources.claim: Verity's indoor drones fly warehouse aisles without a pilot, positioning themselves over pallet locations and photographing labels and goods; more than 150 commercial deployments including Maersk warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-facility photographic capture of designated objects. It transfers to photographing objects inside an institution-controlled building because the machine navigates a human-built interior unaided and frames specified subjects to produce usable images.

sources.system: BOTSCAN NEO / VTX full-body photogrammetry scanners
sources.title: How Body Measurement Technologies Are Advancing - botspot
sources.claim: botspot builds commercial photogrammetric capture studios (BOTSCAN full-body scanners) in which a person stands inside a purpose-built enclosure and synchronized high-resolution cameras with controlled lighting capture them automatically in one workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-view photographic capture of a posed human under controlled light. It transfers to figure/portrait reference capture: same subject, same need for even lighting and all-round coverage, and an image set an artist can draw from.

sources.title: The Best Follow Me Drone In 2022 | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 2+ is a commercially sold self-flying camera whose onboard autonomy tracks a designated moving subject outdoors and keeps it framed and exposed while shooting stills and 4K video.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cinematography of a live subject in the open. It transfers partially to reference capture of people and outdoor scenes, since the machine picks its own viewpoints and exposure and returns usable stills, but only at aerial standoff distances.

tasks.label: Model substances such as clay or wax, using fingers and small hand tools to form objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Artist's own studio: modeling an original figurative or portrait sculpture in oil-based or water clay over a wire/pipe armature, built up in multiple sessions with fingers, loop and rake tools, working from a live sitter or reference and continually re-judging proportion, anatomy and surface; output is a finished clay model accepted for mold-making.

Home or shared ceramics studio: hand-building/sculpting an original stoneware or earthenware piece — coiling, pinching, slabbing, scoring and slipping joins, carving and stamping surface texture with small ribs and loop tools — while managing clay moisture and leather-hard timing so the piece survives drying and firing.

Art foundry wax room (institution-controlled facility, standard benches, heated tools): modeling a small wax maquette and chasing wax positives pulled from rubber molds — filling flaws, re-cutting lost detail, blending seams with heated spatulas and dental-type tools before investment for lost-wax bronze.

Commissioned model work at a client's or fabricator's studio/shop: sculpting a detailed maquette or presentation model in clay or wax (character/creature maquette, figure model for enlargement, architectural ornament study) at a shared bench with standard tools, to a brief and a deadline, with review and revision cycles.

Serial/editioned modeling in the studio: producing multiples of an already-established modeled design — relief tiles, ornamental clay elements, repeated small forms for a series — where fidelity to the approved master form and surface texture matters more than fresh invention.

Public or teaching setting: modeling clay in front of an audience at a workshop, school, art fair, museum demonstration or residency — variable table, lighting and clay supplied on site, interruptions and questions, finishing a demonstration piece within the session.

sources.title: Visual Sculpting: Visually-Aligned Planning Representations for Long-Horizon Robot Clay Sculpting
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robotic clay sculpting: a CMU system plans and executes >100 pokes with a single-contact end-effector to produce clay relief sculptures on a fixed lab tabletop rig with calibrated cameras; results are coarse reliefs, not finished artwork.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Bartsch, Oh et al.)
sources.title: SculptDiff: Diffusion Policy for Robotic Sculpting
sources.claim: SculptDiff learns real-world clay sculpting policies from human kinesthetic demonstrations, but the target forms are elementary shapes ('X', 'Line', 'Cone') made with a parallel gripper on a fixed lab robot; it is presented as the first real-world learned policy for 3D deformable objects.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (shaping modeling clay with a robot end-effector); shows the achievable complexity ceiling is single elementary shapes, far below a modeled figurative sculpture.

sources.title: Robots play with play dough — MIT CSAIL
sources.claim: RoboCraft autonomously plans pinch-and-release actions with a two-finger gripper to shape play dough into letters on a lab bench — the closest autonomous analogue to hand-modeling deformable material, and limited to crude letterforms.
sources.transferJustification: Direct analogue of modeling clay by hand: an elasto-plastic medium deformed by an end-effector; establishes that autonomous free-form shaping is at the level of block letters.

sources.title: RobotSculptor: Artist-Directed Robotic Sculpting of Clay — Disney Research
sources.claim: RobotSculptor uses a standard 6-axis arm with a customized loop tool to fabricate stylized clay models in water-based clay from a user-supplied mesh, executing planned toolpaths in a fixed robot workcell with a motorized turntable; the artistic design and style parameters are authored by the human beforehand.
sources.transferJustification: Forming clay objects with a hand-type loop tool under machine control; supports realizing an already-defined modeled form in clay, not originating one from observation.

sources.system: Studio RAP robotic clay-printing cell (KUKA arm + clay extruder)
sources.title: Studio RAP to 3D Print Ceramic Columns for Student Housing — 3D Printing Industry
sources.claim: Studio RAP commercially produces hundreds of unique relief-textured ceramic clay elements per commission with a custom clay extrusion head on a KUKA robot arm in its own workshop, at quality accepted for permanent architectural installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forming clay objects with relief/texture to accepted client quality under machine control. It substitutes for serial hand-modeling of an already-designed element, though the form is authored digitally rather than by hand tools.

sources.title: 3D-Printed Ceramic Tiles Shape Studio RAP's New 'Powerwall' in the Netherlands
sources.claim: Deployment record of the same robotic clay cell: 322 ceramic tiles for a public art installation fabricated in the studio's workshop by robotic clay printing, with the robot's own tool marks left as the finished surface.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: machine forming of clay elements to an accepted standard in a robot production cell, standing in for serial hand-modeled elements.

sources.title: Ai-Da (robot) — Wikipedia
sources.claim: The best-known 'robot artist' does not model sculpture physically: Ai-Da's sculptures are made by a human artist from her drawings and then 3D printed and cast, confirming no marketed robot performs artistic clay/wax modeling.

tasks.label: Create sculptures, statues, and other three-dimensional artwork by using abrasives and tools to shape, carve, and fabricate materials such as clay, stone, wood, or metal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modeling a figurative or abstract form in oil-based clay, plasticine or wax over an armature in the artist's own studio — building up and cutting back with loop tools, rasps and rakes, working by eye to a finished surface ready for moldmaking or firing.

Carving a stone piece (marble, limestone, alabaster, soapstone) from a rough block in a studio bay or outdoor yard: roughing with pneumatic hammer/point chisel and angle grinder, refining with claw and flat chisels, then rasping, wet sanding and polishing to final surface.

Carving wood — a log, timber baulk or laminated blank — with chainsaw, mallet and gouges, rotary burrs and abrasives, either in a studio/shop or on site at a carving event or public commission, finishing with sanding, texturing and oil/wax.

Fabricating a welded/assembled metal sculpture in the artist's shop: cutting plate, bar and tube (plasma, torch, bandsaw), forming and fitting parts on a welding table, MIG/TIG welding a one-off geometry, then grinding, sanding and finishing/patinating the welds.

Building a mixed-media or found-object work — assemblage of salvaged objects, fiber, plaster, resin and hardware joined by improvised means, plus installation-scale pieces assembled and finished in a gallery or on site, where composition decisions are made while handling irregular, unique objects.

sources.system: ROBOTOR (Both One) marble carving robot, TorArt
sources.developer: Robotor / TorArt (Italy), with KUKA and HSD
sources.title: ROBOTOR: the robot-sculptor that carves Carrara marble! (IFR case study)
sources.claim: Robotor/TorArt in Carrara run KUKA-based 7-axis robotic sculpting cells that carve Carrara marble statues up to 3.5 m from a digital model; cloud software generates and simulates toolpaths and the robot executes the carving autonomously. The workshop produces works for fine artists including Jeff Koons, Maurizio Cattelan, Barry X Ball and Giuseppe Penone.

sources.title: Meet ROBOTOR, the Robotic Sculptor of Marble Statues - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: Robotor's OR-OS software converts a 3D file directly into milling toolpaths without operator intervention, and the systems are marketed and sold for continuous unattended stone sculpting production.

sources.system: Monumental Labs robotic stone carving cells (KUKA arms)
sources.title: Monumental Labs Turns to Automation and Robots to Revive the Art of Stone Carving | Architectural Record
sources.claim: Monumental Labs operates seven-axis KUKA robotic arms with diamond mill bits carving marble, limestone and granite statuary and ornament at plants in Mount Vernon and Greenpoint, NY; robots do the carving and human carvers do the final hand finishing.

sources.system: KUKA KR 210 R3100 milling robot (SEMATEK / Datentechnik Reitz integration)
sources.title: KUKA milling robot produces sculptures at Studio Babelsberg | KUKA Global
sources.claim: A KUKA KR QUANTEC ultra milling robot at Art Department Studio Babelsberg has produced three-dimensional sculptures and props from hard foam since 2016, running as a machine tool that carries out all work steps itself from a CAD/CAM model.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (shaping 3-D sculptural form by subtractive machining) in a purpose-built robotic cell; demonstrates full-form sculpture milling to accepted commercial quality, transferring to wood/clay blanks machined by identical spindle-and-toolpath means.

sources.system: KUKA robotic milling arm at UAP workshop
sources.title: Workshop - Manufacturing - UAP - Urban Art Projects
sources.claim: UAP, a fine-art fabricator that manufactures artworks for leading artists and galleries, uses a KUKA robotic arm in its workshop to mill and shape sculptural patterns and moulds in timber, foam, wax and sand.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the rated task (shaping wood and wax into sculptural form with machine tools) performed inside a fine-art fabrication workshop for artists' works, so material, scale and accepted quality match.

sources.system: Kolb design milling machines / Wenzel DesignTec DT Mill and DT Robot clay mills
sources.title: Kolb Design Technology | Using digital tools to cut cycle times in clay modelling | Autodesk
sources.claim: Five-axis clay milling machines (Kolb, Wenzel DesignTec) are standard equipment in automotive design studios, cutting full-size modelling clay and foam forms directly from a CNC file at surface quality accepted for final design sign-off.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sculpting modelling clay to a finished three-dimensional form. Same material (plasticine-type clay over armature), same subtractive tooling and comparable surface-finish demands as an artist's clay sculpture; the machine performs the shaping unattended in a purpose-built milling bay.

sources.title: Dragon Bench - MX3D
sources.claim: MX3D's robotic wire-arc additive manufacturing cells fabricated Joris Laarman Lab's large-scale sculptural Dragon Bench works in stainless steel, printing free-form self-supporting metal geometry with an industrial robot and welding machine; pieces were delivered as finished artworks (Nike Oregon campus, 2024 Doha Design Biennial).

sources.system: Path Robotics AI-2 / Obsidian autonomous welding cells
sources.title: The Technology - Path Robotics
sources.claim: Path Robotics sells intelligent welding cells whose AI scans each part, builds a weld plan on ... welds one-off, imperfectly fitting assemblies without teach-pendant programming or dedicated fixtures; the cells are deployed in US job shops and shipbuilding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining cut metal parts into a one-off welded structure. Steel plate/tube welding on unique, non-repeating assemblies is the same operation an artist performs when welding a fabricated sculpture, at equal or greater weld-quality demands.

tasks.label: Set up exhibitions of artwork for display or sale.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solo or group show in a commercial gallery, co-op, or arts center: unpack crates/boxes, lay work out, decide and measure a hanging line, install picture hooks/nails or cleats in drywall, hang and level 15-40 framed or stretched 2D works, patch and touch up walls, apply wall labels/vinyl title text, aim track lighting.

Outdoor art fair or street festival booth: unload van at a curb or grass lot, erect a 10x10 pop-up canopy, attach mesh/grid or ProPanel walls, weight or stake against wind, hang framed and unframed work, set up print bins, pedestals, signage and card reader, all in variable weather and crowded aisles.

Indoor art/craft fair or convention-center booth with venue-supplied pipe-and-drape or panel walls: hang framed work on provided hardware, set up tables, bins, pedestals and price tags within a marked 8x10 footprint on a loading-dock schedule.

Sculpture and 3D work install in a gallery or museum-style space: move and position plinths and vitrines, lift and set ceramics, castings, and mixed-media pieces (a few pounds up to rigging-weight), shim and level, secure pieces against tipping, mount wall-hung 3D work.

Alternative venue hang: cafe, restaurant, library, hospital corridor, church hall, or office lobby, using existing rails/hooks or ad-hoc hardware, working around furniture, patrons and staff, with varied wall construction and lighting; 8-20 pieces plus a signage card and price list.

Open studio, home show, or pop-up in a raw rented space: build or roll in temporary display walls/panels, clear and stage the room, hang and arrange work, set up plinths and lighting; layout differs every time.

sources.system: Arnold Machine automotive windshield glass assembly cell (4 robots, 3D vision)
sources.title: Automotive Windshield Glass Assembly - Arnold Machine
sources.claim: A commercial multi-robot cell picks large, fragile formed windshield glass from racks, squares and re-picks it for edge positioning, applies primer, uses 3D vision to place a bracket, and places the glass into fixtures - i.e. precise, gentle handling and placement of a large rigid fragile panel inside a fenced industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive glazing assembly. Hanging framed 2D artwork at E1 is placement of a large, rigid, fragile flat panel to millimetre accuracy onto a presented, fixtured surface - the same object class (glass/framed panel), the same precision, and the same fixtured-cell presentation.

sources.system: MWES Robotic Paint Line Tending Cell (FANUC R-2000iB/185L, vacuum/magnetic grippers)
sources.title: Robotic Paint Line Tending Cell | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: Six FANUC robot cells autonomously load 4-12 ft steel beams weighing up to 80 lb onto paint-line carriers (hanging carriage hooks) and unload and stack them, at 15 s/beam with only replenishment and banding by operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: paint-line racking. Hanging a work onto a hook, cleat or rail at a known position with a heavy but delicate payload is mechanically the same placement problem; this system does it repeatedly and unattended in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: REA LABEL Robotic Labeler
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic print-and-apply system prints and applies labels to products and pallets fully automatically, with flexible label positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial print-and-apply labeling. Exhibition wall labels and price tags are printed adhesive labels placed at specified positions next to each work; at E1 the surface is presented fixtured, matching the labeler's operating conditions.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor Robotic Sheathing / Robotic Sub-Assembly System
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: A configurable two-to-five robot factory system autonomously sheathes and assembles prefabricated wall panels, including sawing, gluing, sheet handling and stud sub-assembly, from digital plans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: panelized wall manufacture. Building the temporary display walls/panels used in pop-up and open-studio shows is panel fabrication and assembly from a plan, which this fixtured factory system performs on comparable materials and dimensions.

sources.title: Automated Trailer Unloading | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Stretch autonomously detects, grasps and places boxes of varying size, weight and surface finish while unloading trailers, deployed at DHL sites (10 robots across three countries as of June 2025), recovering from dropped boxes with minimal human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mixed-case unloading. Setting 3D works and plinths requires perceiving, grasping and placing varied, previously unseen objects of substantial weight; Stretch does this autonomously at commercial reliability, and at E1 the objects are additionally presented in known poses.

sources.system: Jacobi Robotics motion planning with Photoneo MotionCam 3D vision, mixed-case palletizing cell
sources.title: Mixed-Case Palletizing Puzzle: Solved With Jacobi Robotics
sources.claim: A 3D-vision-guided mixed-case palletizing system builds pallets from random case sequences, handling cases of different weights and ..., demonstrated at ProMat 2025 with ~500 cases across ~20 SKUs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mixed-SKU palletizing. Placing varied, fragile objects at planned positions on a stack is the same perception-plan-place loop needed to set sculptures and plinths at planned positions in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids autonomously performed a coordinated bedroom tidy-up - organizing items, hanging a coat, closing a laptop, ... making a bed - in a mock domestic room; the demonstrated manipulation is coarse household object handling, not precision wall mounting or levelling.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound, not support, capability in human-occupied settings: the closest autonomous whole-room manipulation in an unstructured setting handles soft, forgiving objects and does not include measuring, drilling/nailing hardware, or levelling framed work on a wall.

tasks.label: Render drawings, illustrations, and sketches of buildings, manufactured products, or models, working from sketches, blueprints, memory, models, or reference materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freelance illustrator at a studio desk or workstation renders an exterior or interior illustration of a proposed building, working from an architect's blueprints, CAD files, and site photos; delivered as a digital image file (Photoshop/Procreate/rendering software) to the client for review and revision.

Product/technical illustrator renders a manufactured product (appliance, tool, vehicle component) for a catalog, patent, instruction manual, or marketing piece, working from engineering drawings, reference photographs, or the physical product on the desk; output is a line drawing or shaded rendering supplied as a file.

Artist makes preliminary pencil, charcoal, or pen-and-ink sketches on paper of a scale model, maquette, or object in front of them (or from memory), as studies feeding a later painting, sculpture, or commissioned piece; sketches are working documents, often scanned or photographed.

Concept/visualization artist produces quick perspective sketches and iterations of a building or product concept during or after a client meeting, working from rough thumbnails, mood boards, and verbal direction, under short turnaround for presentation slides or a pitch deck.

Fine artist executes a finished rendering in traditional media (ink wash, watercolor, graphite on illustration board) of a building or product for sale, exhibition, or a client wanting an original physical artwork, working from reference photos and earlier sketches.

tasks.label: Shade and fill in sketch outlines and backgrounds, using a variety of media such as water colors, markers, and transparent washes, labeling designated colors when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solo fine artist/illustrator in a private home studio lays transparent watercolour washes and graded shading over a pencil or ink sketch on paper taped to a board or easel; wet-in-wet blending, judgment about wash density, work paced to drying time.

Illustrator working for a publisher, animation/design studio or agency fills flats and adds shading to line art with markers, inks and washes on bristol or overlays, and hand-letters designated colour codes/notes for the printer or colourist; desk in a shared studio room.
Artist blocks in and shades large background areas of a big canvas or panel in a studio - acrylic/oil glazes and transparent washes over a charcoal or pencil layout on an easel or flat table.

Plein-air or on-location work: artist finishes a sketch on site (landscape, street, event, fair booth) with watercolour washes and shading, judging colour against the live subject under changing light and wind.

Mural or scenic-backdrop work inside an institution-run building (library, school, theatre, hotel lobby): filling and shading large background areas of a chalked/projected outline from scaffolding or a lift.
Exterior mural: filling in and shading the background areas of a large wall design on a building facade, working from a lift, ropes or scaffold in outdoor weather.

sources.system: FRIDA (Framework and Robotics Initiative for Developing Arts)
sources.title: Carnegie Mellon's AI-Powered FRIDA Robot Collaborates with Humans To Create Art
sources.claim: FRIDA, a CMU robot arm holding a paintbrush or Sharpie, autonomously plans and executes brush strokes on a canvas in its workspace, using an overhead camera to check its progress and re-plan - i.e. it lays in tone and colour over an evolving image.
sources.transferJustification: FRIDA paints an image with brush/marker strokes rather than shading a given sketch; the media (brush, paint, Sharpie), the flat substrate and the stroke precision are the same as filling and shading a sketch.

sources.title: RI Research Brings Together Humans, Robots and Generative AI To Create Art
sources.claim: CoFRIDA extends FRIDA to co-painting: the robot observes what a human has already drawn on the canvas and takes turns adding its own strokes toward the stated goal - directly the case of a machine filling in and completing a human-started sketch.

sources.title: Recent Developments Regarding Painting Robots for Research in Automatic Painting, Artificial Creativity, and Machine Learning (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: e-David is an industrial robot arm wielding paintbrushes that paints on a mounted canvas with an optical feedback loop, choosing where to add the next stroke to build up shading; it swaps among five brushes and 24 colours in fixed positions.
sources.transferJustification: e-David renders a whole image rather than shading a supplied outline, but its feedback loop exists precisely to add strokes where tone is missing - the same act as shading and filling areas with a brush.

sources.developer: University of Trieste / University of Udine (Scalera, Seriani, Gasparetto, Gallina)
sources.title: Watercolour Robotic Painting: a Novel Automatic System for Artistic Rendering (Journal of Intelligent & Robotic Systems)
sources.claim: Busker Robot is a peer-reviewed automatic watercolour painting system: a 6-DOF collaborative arm with brushes that lays transparent watercolour washes on paper in the robot's workspace, exhibited publicly and awarded at RobotArt.
sources.transferJustification: The system renders an input image in watercolour rather than colouring an artist's own outline, but the medium (transparent watercolour washes on paper), the brush handling and the fixtured flat substrate match the task.

sources.title: Evil Mad Scientist AxiDraw User Manual
sources.claim: The AxiDraw is a commercially sold pen plotter that draws and writes with fountain pens and permanent markers on any flat surface, with software that fills selected shapes with adjustable hatch shading and plots text - covering marker fills, hatched shading and hand-written colour labels.
sources.transferJustification: A plotter executes marker/pen fills and hatched shading on flat artwork and can letter colour designations; that is the mechanical content of filling and shading line art in marker.

sources.title: AI-backed robot painting aims to boost artist income (AFP / Digital Journal)
sources.claim: Acrylic Robotics runs a commercial service in which a robotic arm dips a brush in paint pots and lays down an artist's work stroke by stroke on canvas; the collaborating artist judged the robot-painted result as looking like one of her own works.
sources.transferJustification: The robot executes a painting's strokes, including its shaded and filled passages, on a fixtured canvas at a quality the artist accepted commercially; that speaks to the output quality of robotic brush shading and filling.

sources.title: Architectural-Scale Artistic Brush Painting with a Hybrid Cable Robot (arXiv 2403.12214)
sources.claim: A hybrid cable-driven parallel robot with a serial wrist brush-painted a 27 m x 3.7 m artist-designed mural on the windows of Georgia Tech's Price Gilbert Library over 7 days on site, executing planned strokes with on-site calibration while human operators only swapped paint colours.
sources.transferJustification: The robot painted an artist's design, filling its areas with brush strokes; that is the same act as filling in and shading the background areas of a mural layout, at mural scale and inside a working human facility.

sources.title: New Spray-painting Robot Creates 98-Foot-Tall Mural in Estonia (Hyperallergic)
sources.claim: SprayPrinter's mural robot climbed a chimney in Tartu and sprayed a 98-foot full-colour mural from G-code instructions, using five spray cans on board and no manual painting labour.
sources.transferJustification: The robot lays down the full colour field of a mural, i.e. the filling and shading of the design, on an as-found outdoor wall; that is the mural-scale version of filling in backgrounds.

sources.title: Robot Paints Two-Story Mural In Downtown San Jose (CBS San Francisco)
sources.claim: RoboPrint/Vibot's ARTBOT, a computer-controlled painting rig, produced a two-storey mural on the exterior wall of a building in downtown ... as a commercial mural service, in about two and a half days.
sources.transferJustification: Applying the colour and tonal fill of a mural design onto an outdoor building wall is the mural-scale form of shading and filling in backgrounds; the substrate is as-found masonry outdoors.

tasks.label: Frame and mat artwork for display or sale.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Artist's studio/home workroom: mat and frame one standard rectangular work on paper (watercolor, drawing, etching, photo print, roughly 8x10 to 24x36 in). Measure the image, cut a beveled window mat and backing board, position and hinge/mount the piece square in the opening, clean the glazing, assemble mat-glass-art-backing into a ready-made or custom-cut moulding frame, secure with points, add dust cover, D-rings and wire.

Batch preparation of many similar pieces for a gallery show, art fair booth or online orders: 10-40 prints/photos cut to a handful of standard sizes, matted with identical mats and foam-core backing, then either sleeved with backing board or fitted into identical ready-made frames with hardware. Repetitive, standardized, deadline-driven.

Canvas painting: stretch the finished/primed canvas over stretcher bars (or re-stretch a rolled painting) and build/fit a simple wood floater or gallery frame - cut moulding to miter, join the corners, fit the stretched canvas into the frame and fasten it, attach hanging hardware.

Custom or conservation framing of non-standard work: shadow box or deep-spacer frame for a relief, collage, textile or small 3D object; float mounting a deckle-edged or irregular sheet on rag board; multi-opening, oval or V-grooved mats with fillets; hand-finished, gilded or artist-built ornamental frames.

Oversized or heavy work: canvases and works on paper larger than about 4 feet, heavy mouldings, acrylic glazing sheets that require two-person handling, or fitting/repairing frames on site at the gallery just before installation (broken glass, popped corner, re-fitting a warped backing).

sources.title: Gunnar AG | advanced cutting solutions | the aiox
sources.claim: GUNNAR AiOX computerized mat cutter cuts complete mat boards - window openings, bevels, V-grooves, double mats, edge trimming - fully automatically from a digital job, with clamping and automatic blade-depth control and no manual manipulation during the cutting process; a commercial product sold to frame shops and production framers.
sources.transferJustification: Same task step (cutting the window mat and backing for artwork) on the same materials (rag/conservation matboard) to the same bevel-cut quality a framer would accept.

sources.system: MWES vision-guided four-FANUC-robot picture frame assembly line
sources.developer: Midwest Engineered Systems (MWES) for a picture frame manufacturer
sources.title: Flexibility & Production Speed with Robotic Vision | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: A picture-frame manufacturer runs a four-robot, vision-guided assembly line built by Midwest Engineered Systems that feeds blank frames, applies glue, inserts glass, aligns and places paper mats and back panels in each frame, and presses the assembly closed - 900 finished frames in two hours across seven frame styles with recipe-driven changeover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is factory framing rather than an artist framing an original, but the objects (moulding, glass, matboard, backing), the alignment precision (a visibly square mat opening) and the fitting sequence are the same as the studio job's assembly step.

sources.system: AMP / Alfamacchine AF-500 Frame Joining Robot
sources.developer: A-Plus Automation s.r.l. (Alfamacchine/AMP), distributed by Fletcher Business Group
sources.title: AMP AF-500 Frame Joining Robot :: Fletcher Business Group
sources.claim: The AMP/Alfamacchine AF-500 frame joining robot automatically feeds moulding lengths from a magazine, positions them in four joining stations and V-nails all four corners in 4-6 seconds, auto-adjusting between frame sizes; rated 720-900 joined frames per hour for picture moulding and canvas stretcher bars up to 30 x 47 in.
sources.transferJustification: Same step as the artist building a frame from moulding or assembling stretcher bars: mitred corners joined with V-nails to a saleable finish.

sources.title: MHP Ultra | fully automatic | MH+P Technology GmbH | canvas production
sources.claim: The MHP Ultra is a fully automatic canvas stretching machine that stretches, folds the corners and staples canvas onto stretcher frames at up to 350 frames per ..., with an optional loading module that allows production to run with no operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is stretching printed canvas rather than an artist's painted canvas; the material, the stretcher bars and the required even tension and clean corner folds are the same, and the manufacturer states its machines serve artist canvas as well as digital prints.

sources.title: Picture Framing Equipment – Craft Inc.
sources.claim: Craft Inc's AHM-1X automatic hanger machine applies coil-fed hangers to picture and photo frame backs at about 40 hangers per minute behind a safety-interlocked guard, automating the hanging-hardware step of framing.
sources.transferJustification: Same final step of the framing job - attaching hangers/hardware to the frame back so the work can be displayed or sold.

tasks.label: Submit artwork to shows or galleries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Submit preliminary or finished artwork or project plans to clients for approval, incorporating changes as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freelance illustrator/concept artist working digitally in a home or small rented studio: exports preliminary sketches or renders, emails/uploads them to a commercial client (art director, publisher, game studio), reads written mark-ups, revises the file on screen, prints or exports a proof, and resubmits until approved.

Commissioned painter showing preliminary studies and then the in-progress/finished canvas to a private client in the studio or the client's home: takes verbal, often vague feedback ('warmer light, change the pose, lighten the background'), then physically repaints, glazes, or reworks areas of the wet/dry painting and presents it again.

Sculptor or public-art muralist presenting a scale maquette, material samples, and site renderings to a client committee (city arts board, architect, developer) in a meeting room, then modifying the physical maquette and the enlargement/fabrication plan per the committee's conditions before final approval.

Illustrator producing traditional media (ink, gouache, watercolor board) for a publisher: scans or photographs the piece, submits the file, then makes requested corrections physically on the original (repainting, opaque white, re-inking) or re-doing a spot element, and ships or hand-delivers the original artwork.

Artist delivering a finished framed/mounted work to a gallery, corporate lobby, or private client for final approval: transporting and unpacking the piece, hanging or positioning it, and making on-the-spot adjustments requested at hand-off (reframing, varnish, touch-up, repositioning).

sources.title: Ai-Da: Robot Artist - Interalia Magazine
sources.claim: Ai-Da, a humanoid robot artist, uses cameras and AI algorithms with a robotic drawing arm to make pencil portraits and derived paintings; the work is curated, exhibited, and sold by a human team rather than produced through a client revision loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically producing a drawing/painting. It is cited only to test transfer; it shows mark-making on paper in a controlled studio/exhibition setting, but nothing about presenting work to a paying client, interpreting revision notes, or reworking an existing piece to a client's satisfaction.

sources.title: AI-backed robot painting aims to boost artist income - Digital Journal
sources.claim: Acrylic Robotics uses a robotic arm to replay an artist's recorded brushstroke data in real paint on canvas, producing reproductions of an artwork the human artist has already designed and finished.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replicating a finished painting. Transfer fails for this task because the machine replays stroke data captured from a human artist; it does not generate preliminary work for approval, nor revise a piece in response to client feedback.

sources.title: Meet ROBOTOR, the Robotic Sculptor of Marble Statues - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: Robotor's multi-axis robotic cells in Carrara carve marble sculptures autonomously from a human-supplied 3D digital model, in a purpose-built industrial workshop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabricating a sculpture from a fixed digital file in a fenced robotic cell (E1). It substantiates only the execution step; the client presentation, the reading of committee feedback, and the artistic decision about what to change remain with the human sculptor.

sources.system: FRIDA (Framework and Robotics Initiative for Developing Arts)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Bot Intelligence Group
sources.title: Carnegie Mellon engineers made an AI-powered robot that manually paints pictures from text, audio, and visual prompts - TechSpot
sources.claim: CMU's FRIDA robotic arm plans and physically paints on canvas from text, audio and image prompts, using visual feedback to adapt strokes; it is a university research demonstration, not a commissioned-work service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous painting from a prompt in a lab. Output is loose and impressionistic and there is no evidence of iterating with a paying client to an accepted commissioned result, so it does not transfer to submitting work for approval and incorporating changes.

sources.title: Precision Meets Art: Autonomous Multi-UAV System for Large Scale Mural Drawing (arXiv:2601.06508)
sources.claim: A multi-drone system executed large-scale mural drawing outdoors from a supplied design, showing robotic execution of artwork in an unstructured outdoor setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: painting a pre-specified mural design outdoors. It substantiates robotic mark-making at scale outside a factory, but the design, the client approval, and any requested revisions are produced by humans upstream of the drones.

tasks.label: Collaborate with engineers, mechanics, and other technical experts as necessary to build and install creations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Cut, bend, laminate, arrange, and fasten individual or mixed raw and manufactured materials and products to form works of art.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Studio sculptor in a private or shared warehouse/garage studio builds a sculpture from wood, steel, or plastic stock: measuring and cutting parts with saw, grinder or torch, bending or forming them, then welding, screwing or gluing them together, adjusting proportions by eye as the piece develops. Layout is idiosyncratic, floor cluttered, materials stored loose.

Mixed-media artist works flat at a table making collage/laminated works: cutting paper, card, prints, fabric and thin sheet by hand or blade to planned shapes, layering and laminating, and gluing pieces in a composed arrangement onto a board or panel. Small scale, delicate, registration judged visually.

Assemblage artist joins heterogeneous found objects and ephemera (scrap metal, wire, toys, driftwood, textiles, hardware) into a three-dimensional work in the studio: trimming and bending odd parts, improvising joins with glue, screws, wire, nails or stitching, and rearranging repeatedly until the composition reads.

Artist has components fabricated with shop equipment at a makerspace, university shop, or professional art-fabrication studio (CNC router, laser/waterjet, robotic mill, press brake), then the parts are assembled and fastened into the finished work; includes monumental stone, metal, or composite commissions produced from the artist's model or digital file.

Site-specific installation assembled indoors at a gallery, museum, or interior public space: elements trimmed to fit the room, arranged in relation to walls and sightlines, and fastened or anchored in place over an install period, with on-the-spot adjustment to the site.

Large outdoor work in stone or earth built on site (dry-stone wall, cairn, land-art arrangement): irregular found boulders and debris selected, moved, and stacked/arranged to a planned form in the open, exposed to weather and uneven ground.

sources.title: Robots chisel out the future of sculpture as some artists embrace change and others push back - CBS News (60 Minutes transcript)
sources.claim: Robotor's multi-axis robotic milling machines commercially carve marble sculptures for artists in workshops in Carrara; the CEO states the robots perform 99% of the carving, with skilled artisans doing the final 1% by hand.

sources.title: Monumental Labs Turns to Automation and Robots to Revive the Art of Stone Carving | Architectural Record
sources.claim: Monumental Labs operates a plant of seven-axis KUKA robotic arms with diamond-tip mills that carve marble sculpture and ornament from digital models, with hand finishing afterward.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Gramazio Kohler Research / NCCR Digital Fabrication with Erne AG Holzbau
sources.title: Robotic collaboration in timber construction | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: In ETH Zurich's Robotic Fabrication Laboratory, two industrial robots cut 487 timber beams to size, drill the connection holes, and position each beam in the spatial arrangement given by a CAD model, with collision-free path replanning; workers then bolt the beams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic prefabrication of a geometrically unique timber structure. It is the same sequence of cutting stock to size, drilling, and positioning elements to a designer's digital model, at comparable member scale and millimetre precision, that a sculptor performs when building a constructed wood or metal work.

sources.system: Automatic mosaic ceramic art image tiling system (Link Hou robotic arms, U+I conveyors)
sources.title: Automatic tiling method for mosaic ceramic art images based on subpixel edge fitting localization and collaborative operation of multiple manipulators | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: A physical multi-manipulator cell with conveyors, CCD cameras and suction nozzles automatically selects, picks and lays multi-colour mosaic tesserae onto tiling boards to reproduce artists' mosaic art images, at 95.45% success and sub-millimetre positioning error.

sources.system: Acieta Robotically Integrated Bending Solutions (press brake tending cells)
sources.title: Press Brake Tending | Acieta
sources.claim: Commercially integrated robotic press-brake cells load, position and bend sheet-metal parts, including high-mix small parts, running complex multi-bend sequences with automatic gripper changes and no operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sheet-metal bending in a fabrication cell. Bending sheet and plate to a specified geometry is the same physical operation an artist performs on metal stock for a sculpture, at equal or finer precision, with the blank presented to the machine.

sources.title: G3 digital cutter | Flatbed CNC Cutter | Zünd
sources.claim: Zünd flatbed CNC cutting systems cut and route sheet materials held on a zoned vacuum table - cardboard, foam-core, display board, textiles, composites - up to 110 mm thick, using automatically changed knives, router bits and creasing ... driven from a digital file.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: digital cutting of sheet stock for graphics, packaging and display. The materials (paper, board, foam, textile, thin composite) and the blade/rout operations are the same as an artist cutting collage and laminated sheet elements, at tighter tolerance than hand cutting.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Gramazio Kohler Research, Robotic Systems Lab, Vision for Robotics Lab, with Eberhard AG
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a six-metre-high dry-stone wall | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: The HEAP autonomous excavator mapped an outdoor site, scanned and grasped irregular multi-tonne boulders and demolition debris, computed a placement for each, and built a 6 m high, 65 m long dry-stone wall itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dry-stone walling from on-site material. Selecting, orienting and stacking irregular found stones to a computed design on open ground is the same operation as an artist building a land-art stone wall or cairn, at the same coarse tolerance.

sources.system: MX3D M1 wire-arc robotic metal printing
sources.developer: MX3D with Joris Laarman Lab and Arup
sources.title: Long-awaited 3D-printed stainless steel bridge opens in Amsterdam | Dezeen
sources.claim: Six-axis robotic arms fitted with welding gear at MX3D fabricated a 12-metre stainless-steel pedestrian bridge to designer-artist Joris Laarman's form, depositing metal along programmed paths in the company's workshop before installation in Amsterdam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wire-arc fabrication of a large artist-designed metal object. It substantiates robotic joining of metal to build a sculptural form to an artist's digital design in a purpose-built robot workshop.

tasks.label: Provide entertainment at special events by performing activities such as drawing cartoons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Caricature artist stationed at a wedding, bar mitzvah, or holiday party in a hotel ballroom or banquet hall: draws individual guests and couples in roughly 4-6 minutes each on marker paper, banters with the line, hands each guest a signed keepsake, works a 2-3 hour reception.

Live cartoon/caricature artist working a corporate trade-show booth, conference, or brand activation in a convention center: high-volume branded drawings for attendees over a 6-8 hour show day, logo on the paper, digital copies for social sharing, long queues.

Caricature stand at a county fair midway, festival, theme park, or family entertainment center: pay-per-drawing walk-up customers, continuous crowds, sometimes outdoors under a tent with variable light and weather, cash/card handling.

Artist hired for a kids' birthday, graduation, or house party at a private residence: sets up in a living room, driveway, or backyard with whatever table and outlet is available, draws children and family members, deals with cramped space and unsupervised kids.

Live-drawing performance where the show itself is the product: a cartoonist doing rapid gag cartoons or roast caricatures on an easel projected to a crowd, or an event painter capturing the reception/ceremony scene on a large canvas as it unfolds, finishing one big artwork by the end of the night.

sources.title: Ai SketchBot - The Original Ai Robotic Sketch Artist
sources.claim: Ai SketchBot (Picture Mosaics) is a commercial robotic sketch artist: a guest photo is analyzed by AI and drawn by a robot arm with a real pen on branded paper in about 60 seconds, in caricature or portrait styles, sold for trade shows, conferences, corporate events and parties.

sources.title: Ai SketchBot Pro - The Robot that Draws and Delivers
sources.claim: The SketchBot Pro model runs as a full self-service kiosk: it autonomously swaps tools, draws the sketch, and hands the finished sketch directly to the guest, with optional tap-to-pay; the vendor sells it for high-volume unattended deployments.

sources.title: SketchBot: Turning Fun Into Profit at Fat Cats Fun Center - Picture Mosaics Blog
sources.claim: SketchBot kiosks operate as paid attractions in family entertainment centers, museums and attractions (Fat Cats fun center, Crayola Experience locations, Questacon, Science Museum of Virginia), charging guests $5-9 per sketch with turnkey operation.

sources.title: AI Sketch Robot for Corporate Events: The NYC Activation Guests Line Up For
sources.claim: An NYC event company runs twin sketch-robot activations on corporate floors and at Javits Convention Center trade shows; guests take a selfie on an iPad, AI makes a portrait or caricature, and a robot arm draws it on branded paper in 1-2 minutes, serving 60+ guests per hour versus 10-15 for a human caricature artist.

sources.title: Draw Me Bot Caricature Robot | Easy Breezy Bash Rentals
sources.claim: A Milwaukee/Chicago event-rental company rents a 'Draw Me Bot' caricature robot for weddings, birthday parties, private celebrations, school functions and trade shows, with optional delivery/setup; the robot arm draws stylized caricatures live and guests also get digital copies.

sources.system: Sketch Robot Booth (fleet with automatic queueing)
sources.title: Sketch Robot Booth | CEG Interactive
sources.claim: Sketch-robot event fleets need only an 8x8 setup area and a wall outlet, and can run off a silent ... outdoor or remote events; guests sit in front of the robot, its camera captures them, and the arm sketches the keepsake.

sources.title: SketchBot Wins Best New Product Award at IAAPA - Picture Mosaics Blog
sources.claim: At the IAAPA attractions expo the SketchBot robots sketched over 4,000 attendees across four days of show floor operation and the booth won IAAPA's 1st Place Brass Ring Best New Product award.

tasks.label: Develop project budgets for approval, estimating time lines and material costs.

tasks.label: Create and prepare sketches and model drawings of cartoon characters, providing details from memory, live models, manufactured products, or reference materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Animation or games studio: artist develops character model sheets and turnaround/expression sketches for a cartoon character, working from a director's notes, reference photos, and prior designs, delivered digitally (tablet) or on paper for scanning.

Licensing/merchandise or toy design work: artist prepares style-guide sketches and model drawings of an existing cartoon character based on a manufactured product or prototype in hand, matching an established brand model.
Freelance illustrator/cartoonist working from memory and imagination to rough out character sketches for a comic, children's book, or editorial cartoon, iterating quickly in a home studio.
Artist sketching a cartoon/caricature character from a live model or live subject (life-drawing session, caricature booth, on-location observation), capturing gesture and likeness in stylized form.

Advertising/marketing or theme-park design context: artist prepares character sketches and model drawings for a client presentation from a brief and reference materials, revising to client feedback under deadline.

tasks.label: Create finished art work as decoration, or to elucidate or substitute for spoken or written messages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Studio easel painting: an original acrylic or oil painting on stretched canvas or panel (portrait, landscape, abstract) made in the artist's own or a shared studio from a client brief or the artist's own concept - priming/stretching, mixing color, layering over several sessions, drying, varnishing and signing - sold or hung as decoration.

Hand-media illustration on paper: pen-and-ink, watercolor or gouache artwork for a book, magazine, poster, card or signage that carries a message, drawn at a desk or drafting table in a studio or home workspace, then scanned or delivered as a finished original.

Digital illustration: finished artwork drawn on a tablet or computer for a client (editorial, book, packaging, game or commercial art) and delivered as a file; no physical medium is worked and the deliverable is the digital image itself.

Sculpture or three-dimensional decorative work: modeling clay, carving stone or wood, or welding/assembling metal in a studio or fabrication shop, including surface finishing, polishing or patina and mounting, for a gallery, architectural client or private buyer.

Site-specific mural or large decorative wall work: designing and executing a painted image on an interior or exterior wall at a customer's building or public site, working from scaffolding, ladders or a lift, with wall prep, variable surfaces, weather and passersby.

sources.system: FRIDA (Framework and Robotics Initiative for Developing Arts)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute (Schaldenbrand, McCann, Oh)
sources.title: FRIDA: A Collaborative Robot Painter with a Differentiable, Real2Sim2Real Planning Environment
sources.claim: FRIDA, a robot-arm painter from CMU's Robotics Institute, plans and executes brush strokes on a canvas from a language description or reference image, continually re-planning from camera observation of the evolving canvas; the canvas and paint palette sit in the robot's calibrated workspace.

tasks.label: Create sketches, profiles, or likenesses of posed subjects or photographs, using any combination of freehand drawing, mechanical assembly kits, and computer imaging.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick portrait or caricature of a live sitter at an outdoor street fair, boardwalk, festival, or farmers-market booth: a canopy and folding chair on a public street, 5-15 minutes per sitter in charcoal/pastel on paper, wind, sun glare, passersby, restless children and group/pet requests, cash handled on the spot.

Live likeness sketches for a queue of guests at an indoor corporate event, trade show, convention, or wedding reception in a hotel ballroom or exhibit hall: standard tables and power, guests seated or photographed one at a time, dozens of takeaway portraits per hour.

Commissioned likeness worked up in the artist's studio from client-supplied photographs: graphite, charcoal, pastel or oil on paper/canvas, high fidelity to the subject, revisions to client feedback, delivered finished/framed over days or weeks.

Observational portrait and figure sketches of a posed live model in a studio, atelier, or life-drawing session: the model holds a pose, the artist works from direct observation to produce studies or exhibition-quality drawings.

Digital likeness produced with computer imaging at a desk (tablet and stylus, photo-reference portrait illustration, or 3D likeness) for an editorial, licensing, or private client; output delivered as a file or print.

Composite/forensic likeness at a law-enforcement facility: sketch built from a witness's description through cognitive interview and iterative revision, or assembled from a feature kit / composite software, verified against the witness before release.

sources.title: Patrick Tresset creates paintings, drawings and theatrical installations of robots with human traits using AI and computational systems
sources.claim: Patrick Tresset's 'Paul' / 'Human Study' robotic drawing installations seat a live human sitter and produce observational portrait sketches that the exhibitors describe as autonomous rather than pre-programmed, shown in galleries and museums.

tasks.label: Trace drawings onto clear acetate for painting or coloring, or trace them with ink to make final copies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freelance illustrator/comic artist in a home or small rented studio inks a finished pencil drawing at a drafting table: technical pens and brush on bristol board or vellum, varying line weight, producing the final ink copy for reproduction.

Animation/cel artist in a small animation studio traces pencil drawings onto clear acetate cels held on peg bars over a light table, laying a clean ink outline that will later be painted on the reverse; dozens of registered cels per sequence.

Fine artist in a private studio transfers a preliminary sketch/cartoon onto the final support (watercolor paper, illustration board, panel or stretched canvas) with tracing paper or graphite transfer, then goes over the transferred lines in ink; supports vary in size and texture.

Artist or studio assistant at a design/print shop traces artwork onto clear acetate or mylar overlays for production use - color separations, screen-print positives, sign patterns, registration overlays - working flat on a drafting table with technical pens.

Scenic artist/muralist scales up and traces a cartoon onto a large surface on site (a building wall, a scenic backdrop, a large panel), then outlines it in ink or paint marker before painting; surface condition and access vary by site.

sources.system: AxiDraw V3 (Evil Mad Scientist / Bantam Tools)

sources.title: AxiDraw V3 - Evil Mad Scientist
sources.claim: AxiDraw is a commercially sold pen plotter that holds ordinary pens, markers and fountain pens and draws or writes on almost any flat surface, executing a supplied vector drawing without human guidance of the pen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-plotting a line drawing in real ink on flat media. It is the same physical act as tracing a drawing with ink to make a final copy - same media (paper, film), same instrument (technical pen/marker), same sub-millimetre line precision - once the source drawing is scanned and vectorized.

sources.title: Bantam Tools
sources.claim: The current-production successor line of large-format pen plotters is sold to and used by professional artists for pen plots up to A1 / 22x34 inches.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the plotter class is a current commercial product at illustration-board and cel sizes, so the ink-tracing instances can be run at the sizes artists actually work at.

sources.system: UUNA TEK iDraw 3.0 pen plotter + Inkscape/Illustrator image trace
sources.title: How to Convert Any Photo to SVG and Draw It with the UUNA TEK 3.0 Pen Plotter
sources.claim: A standard commercial workflow converts a scanned raster image into vector outlines (image trace) and has a pen plotter physically redraw it in ink - i.e. machine tracing of an existing image to a final pen copy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reproducing a supplied image as a pen-drawn line copy. Tracing a drawing to make a final ink copy is the same operation with a scan of the artist's pencils as the input image.

sources.system: Pen plotters on double-matte mylar drafting film
sources.title: Mylar Drafting Film | Mylar Paper Film | Freedom Paper
sources.claim: Clear drafting film (mylar/acetate), the material used for ink tracing and overlays, is sold explicitly for use with pen plotters as well as hand drawing pens.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes media compatibility: the transparent film substrate named in the task ('clear acetate') is a routine pen-plotter substrate, so the ink-on-film tracing instance is within the machine's demonstrated materials.

sources.title: Handwriting Robots - Handwrytten
sources.claim: A fleet of roughly 175 pen-holding writing robots runs in a production facility and in third-party logistics facilities, writing with real ballpoint pens, feeding and handling its own cards and envelopes, and operating autonomously without a human at the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production-scale reproduction of specified pen strokes on sheet media. It substantiates reliability, media loading/unloading and unattended running of pen-on-paper machines - the operational requirements of turning out final ink copies at worker quality.

sources.system: Artistic Robotic Arm (Seung-Joon Yi, Pusan National University)
sources.title: Artistic Robotic Arm: Drawing Portraits on Physical Canvas under 80 Seconds
sources.claim: A robotic arm autonomously converts a captured image into a line drawing and draws it on a physical canvas with a variable-line-width calligraphy pen; it drew portraits of more than ... members of the public at a robotics exhibition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-to-ink-line reproduction by a general robot arm, including modulated line width - the expressive element of hand inking - on a fixed canvas presented to the machine.

sources.title: Carnegie Mellon's AI-Powered FRIDA Robot Collaborates with Humans To Create Art
sources.claim: A robot arm with a brush plans strokes from an image or text goal and uses an overhead camera to check the physical result and revise its plan, painting on a canvas mounted in front of it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop mark-making on an artist's support (canvas on an easel). Supports transferring a planned design onto a prepared painting support, the second half of the sketch-transfer instance.

sources.system: iDraw H A1 vertical pen plotter / hanging plotters
sources.title: Hanging Plotter Alternative: Create Vertical Art with iDraw H A1
sources.claim: Cable/hanging and large-format vertical plotters are sold and used to redraw supplied vector files as line art on wall-sized surfaces, including murals and wall illustrations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring a design onto a large prepared surface as line art - the scale-up-and-outline step of the mural/scenic instance - by a machine rigged to that surface.

tasks.label: Apply solvents and cleaning agents to clean surfaces of paintings, and to remove accretions, discolorations, and deteriorated varnish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Removing aged, discolored natural-resin varnish from an oil-on-canvas easel painting in a studio/conservation lab: solvent testing in small trial areas, choosing and adjusting solvent/gel systems, rolling swabs area by area under raking light and magnification, stopping short of original glazes and thin passages, and clearing residues.

Cleaning surface grime, smoke film and dust from an unvarnished or acrylic/modern painting on the studio bench using aqueous solutions, chelators, emulsions or dry-cleaning sponges, adapting pressure and formulation to water-sensitive, matte or friable passages.

Localized removal of accretions and discolorations - fly specks, drips, adhesive/tape residue, plaster splashes, discolored old retouches - under a stereomicroscope with solvent-charged micro-swabs and scalpel work, without disturbing surrounding original paint.

An artist cleaning their own recent works in their studio before varnishing, photographing, exhibition or sale: wiping studio dust, fingerprints and oil/medium residue from a batch of canvases and panels with mild solvents or cleaning agents.

In-situ cleaning of a large mural, ceiling canvas or architectural painting at a church, lobby or historic building, worked from scaffold or ladder with variable lighting, dust and access, and with public or building activity nearby.

sources.title: SwRI's laser coating removal robot wins R&D 100 Award
sources.claim: SwRI's Laser Coating Removal robot autonomously strips selected coating layers from aircraft in hangars using closed-loop color recognition, i.e. selective removal of a degraded coating without damaging the substrate - the closest industrial analogue to varnish removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective coating/varnish removal down to a chosen layer. Transfer fails for fine-art cleaning: aircraft carry standardized, documented coating stacks on rigid substrates with color-coded layers, whereas each painting has a unique, undocumented, heterogeneous and fragile paint/varnish stratigraphy where acceptable error is essentially zero, so this system cannot substantiate conservator-quality cleaning of a painting.

sources.system: IESL-FORTH KrF excimer laser cleaning workstation
sources.developer: IESL-FORTH (Institute of Electronic Structure and Laser, Crete)
sources.title: Laser cleaning of paintings: in situ optimization of operative parameters through non-invasive assessment by OCT, reflection FT-IR spectroscopy and LIF
sources.claim: The state of the art for machine-delivered varnish removal from a real easel painting is a custom laser workstation in which the painting is fixtured and the beam is scanned by galvanometric mirrors, but fluence and stopping points are set by researchers and evaluated between successive cleaning tests with OCT and FT-IR.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (removal of aged varnish and weathered accretions from a painting), but delivered as operator-parameterized test areas with human assessment between irradiations rather than autonomous completion of a painting's cleaning, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: 3M Finesse-It Robotic Paint Repair System Fixes Paint Defects on Assembly Lines
sources.claim: Deployed automotive robots autonomously find and repair paint-surface defects by sanding and polishing on the assembly line, showing machine-controlled, force-regulated material removal from a painted surface inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: controlled removal of a thin surface layer from a coated surface using liquids/abrasives under force control. Transfer fails because the workpiece is an identical, robust, freshly cured factory clearcoat of known thickness, not a unique fragile artwork with impasto, glazes and unknown solubility, and the acceptance standard is uniform gloss rather than a conservator's judgment about how much original surface to expose.

sources.system: Cultural relics protection robot (electron-beam irradiation, Dunhuang Academy project)
sources.developer: China Academy of Space Technology / Dunhuang Academy
sources.title: China develops robot for cultural relics protection - Xinhua
sources.claim: The heritage robot deployed on murals in China is remotely operated and delivers electron-beam sterilization rather than solvent cleaning, indicating in-situ mural work by machines remains teleoperated and does not cover accretion or varnish removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine intervention on painted heritage surfaces in situ. It is teleoperated and performs irradiation, not solvent cleaning or accretion removal, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.
