tasks.label: Brush or spray protective or decorative finishes on completed background panels, informational legends, exhibit accessories, or finished paintings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solo studio: artist brushes or sprays a clear protective varnish over a completed flat painting (stretched canvas, cradled panel, illustration board) after cure; must produce an even, drip-free film of uniform sheen, keeping dust and lint off a textured, one-of-a-kind, irreplaceable surface. Done in the artist's own studio/home workspace.

Studio or small fabrication shop: spraying a clear protective/UV sealer over a three-dimensional sculpture or exhibit accessory (irregular geometry, undercuts, multiple faces), rotating or repositioning the piece to reach all surfaces without runs or missed spots.

Museum or exhibit-fabrication shop: spraying protective clear coat or sealer on completed exhibit background panels and printed informational legend panels (large flat rigid sheets), in the shop's spray booth or curtained-off area, to a defect-free display standard.

Hand-applied decorative finishes requiring aesthetic judgment: antiquing glaze brushed on and rubbed back into recesses, chemical patina on a metal sculpture, metal-leaf gilding, or faux/textured finishes on exhibit accessories, judged and adjusted piece by piece.

Selective coating on a finished piece: masking or otherwise keeping the finish off designated areas (mounting surfaces, labels, passages that must stay matte) and applying the protective or decorative coat only to the intended regions of a flat work.

sources.title: iGiotto: anthropomorphic spraying robot | Cefla Finishing
sources.claim: Cefla's iGiotto anthropomorphic spray-coating robot applies coatings to large flat and complex-shaped workpieces (doors, window frames, chairs, musical instruments) inside an in-line spray booth, running the whole cycle automatically and optionally using a 3D C-Vision scanner to select/generate the program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial spray application of clear lacquers/topcoats to wood panels, doors and appearance-critical items such as musical instruments. Same operation as the task (spraying a protective/decorative finish), comparable flat and complex substrates, and the same visual-defect standard (uniform film, no runs), performed in a booth.

sources.system: CMA Robotics spray robot with 3D scanning / inverted shuttle spray system
sources.title: Woodworking Network Attends 2025 Live Automation Review
sources.claim: A CMA Robotics six-axis spraying robot with 3D scanning autogenerates its finishing program for each part as it passes the scanner, spraying one-off parts of differing size and configuration with no human programming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: batch-of-one spray finishing of wood components. Fine-art and exhibit finishing is likewise one-off work; the scan-and-generate approach removes the need for per-piece programming, and the coatings (lacquer/clear topcoat) and finish-quality standard match the task.

sources.system: Ventherm spray painting robot with PoseFitter / Automatic Programmer
sources.title: Spray Painting Robot – Automated Heavy Industry Solutions
sources.claim: Ventherm's spray painting robots scan each unpainted component, match the point cloud to CAD, and automatically generate the spray program, so parts of varying type can be coated in the booth without dedicated robot programmers and without high-precision placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray coating of varied industrial parts in a booth. It shows the perception-to-path capability needed when each workpiece differs, which is the main gap between mass-production coating and coating a finished artwork or exhibit panel.

sources.title: Çanakcilar Seramik starts up the second Gaiotto glazing system | Ceramic World Web
sources.claim: A Gaiotto GA 2000 self-learning glazing robot line spraying glaze onto complex three-dimensional sanitaryware has been in production at Çanakcilar Seramik, praised for the precision and repeatability of the finished coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of a protective/decorative glaze over the whole surface of complex three-dimensional ceramic bodies. Same act (spraying a finish coat), comparable sculptural geometry with undercuts, and a surface-appearance acceptance standard.

sources.title: EcoPaintJet Pro – Efficient and sustainable two-tone painting
sources.claim: Dürr's EcoPaintJet Pro robot system applies paint automatically with sharply defined edges and no overspray, eliminating manual masking for two-tone and decorative areas on car bodies in series painting lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a coating to only a designated region of a workpiece without masking. This is the capability at issue in selective finishing of an artwork or exhibit piece — a clean boundary between coated and uncoated areas at decorative-finish quality.

tasks.label: Teach artistic techniques to children or adults.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fine artist leads a weekly children's art class at a community center or after-school program: explains and demonstrates techniques (brush handling, color mixing, clay coil-building), circulates to give verbal feedback and correction, and manages a group of 8-15 kids.

Artist runs an adult workshop in their own studio or a rented arts-center room (e.g., watercolor, life drawing, printmaking, welding-based sculpture): presents a demonstration, explains materials and process, critiques work in progress, answers questions.

One-on-one private lessons or mentorship in the artist's studio or the student's home: diagnoses the student's habits, explains and shows corrections, assigns exercises, and reviews progress over sessions.

Visiting-artist residency, school workshop, or museum/gallery class: a one-off or short series where the artist explains their technique to a class or public audience and guides participants through a project.
Online or recorded instruction: livestreamed or pre-recorded technique tutorials, virtual classes, and written/illustrated step-by-step lessons for paying students or a subscriber audience.

tasks.label: Assemble, typeset, scan, and produce digital camera-ready art or film negatives and printer's proofs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-house studio/agency art department: artist assembles and typesets a digital camera-ready art file (title card, key art, packaging or ad mechanical) to spec, then outputs a hard proof on the department's proofing printer, checks color/type/trim, and releases it for approval. Setting is a controlled studio office with standard equipment.

Studio scanning station: artist scans physical source material — hand-drawn animation drawings, painted backgrounds, storyboard boards, logo slicks, photo prints — on a flatbed or feed scanner, batches and cleans the captures, and assembles them into the camera-ready digital file. Originals vary in size and condition but arrive stacked at the station.

Post-production/film lab variant: scanning motion-picture camera negative into a digital pipeline, and/or recording finished digital frames back out to 35mm film negative (film-out) on a film recorder, then handing off for processing and check print. Setting is a post facility or film lab with dedicated transport machinery.

Hand-off to a commercial printer/prepress house: the assembled file is RIPed, a contract proof is produced and verified against the standard, plates or film negatives are imaged, and a press proof is pulled and matched before the run. Setting is a printing plant prepress department and pressroom.

Freelance/home-studio or client-site variant: the same camera-ready art assembly, scanning of whatever originals the client supplies, and proofing on a consumer desktop scanner/inkjet in an ad hoc workspace with no standard layout or equipment.

sources.title: This robot scans rare library books at 2,500 pages per hour | Popular Science
sources.claim: The Treventus ScanRobot 2.0 MDS autonomously turns and scans book/manuscript pages (up to ~2,500 pages/hour) and is deployed in an institutional library digitization operation at the University of Tulsa's ..., substantiating machine-run scanning of physical originals in a human work facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library/archive digitization. It is the same physical act as the 'scan' step here — presenting paper originals to an imaging head and capturing calibrated high-resolution images — with comparable object handling (fragile flat paper) and precision, performed in an institution-controlled workroom.

sources.title: Document Imaging Solutions for Faster Digitization | OPEX
sources.claim: OPEX Velo 8000 production scanners run continuous, multi-shift batch scanning with automatic feeding, media handling, sorting and output handling, i.e. digitizing stacks of loose sheets with minimal operator intervention in scanning-service facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume document digitization. Loose animation drawings, storyboards and photo originals are the same class of flat paper stock, and the machine performs the feed-capture-sort cycle that a worker would perform by hand at a studio scanning station.

sources.title: GMG ProofControl - Color Management Group
sources.claim: GMG ProofControl Inline drives an Epson proofer with an integrated measuring device to produce a contract-quality proof and then measure and verify its control strip automatically against reference values, i.e. producing and accepting a printer's proof without an operator.

sources.system: Kodak MAGNUS Q800 platesetter with Multi-Cassette / Multi-Pallet Loader
sources.title: Continuing the success story: Innovative Kodak CTP solutions | Kodak
sources.claim: Kodak's CTP automation options (single/multi-cassette units, single/multi-pallet loaders) for MAGNUS platesetters handle plate media loading and unloading mechanically, giving essentially unattended imaging of press-ready output in a prepress department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: computer-to-plate imaging. Film-negative output (imagesetting) uses the same device class and prepress room — a laser imaging engine fed from a light-tight media cassette into an online processor — so machine handling of the sensitized media transfers directly to producing film negatives.

sources.system: Nela automated plate handling / plate logistics system

sources.claim: The AxiDraw (Evil Mad Scientist / Bantam Tools NextDraw line) is a commercially sold pen plotter that autonomously executes a supplied vector file, drawing with ordinary pens, markers and fountain pens on paper placed on its bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-plotting line art. Transfer covers only the physical act of this task — laying accurate pen strokes on a sheet of paper at line-art precision, the same medium and tolerance as an artist's scanned drawing — but the plotter supplies no image content of its own, so it substantiates completion only where the required content is algorithmic (texture/pattern passes).

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pen-on-paper handwriting at commercial scale. Transfer: it establishes that machine-driven pens produce paper output at production reliability and accepted quality in a purpose-built facility, i.e. the physical mark-making half of creating pen-and-paper artwork; it says nothing about generating pictorial content.

sources.title: Patrick Tresset creates paintings, drawings and theatrical installations of robots — Streaming Museum

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous observational portrait sketching on paper. Transfer is partial: it shows a robot originating and drawing an image, but the accepted output is a stylized gallery artwork, not an on-model, on-brief production drawing, so it does not substantiate the animator's content standard.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-house fit session in a design studio/sample room: the first proto or sample is put on a live fit model; the designer watches the model stand, walk and raise arms, assesses drape, balance and proportion, then pins, chalks and slashes the garment directly on the body and dictates the corrections to the patternmaker.

Examining the sample off the body — on a dress form or flat on the worktable: turning seams and linings out, feeling fabric hand and weight, checking hems, closures and topstitching against the sketch, re-draping and repinning on the form, and marking the changes on the garment/pattern.

Sample review against the tech pack in a vendor showroom, factory sample room or sourcing trip: measuring points of measure with a tape, comparing to spec and to the previous round, checking trims and construction, marking corrections on the sample and annotating fit comments for the maker.

Specialized or non-woven-apparel samples (knitwear, tailored outerwear, swim/activewear, handbags, footwear): handling the sample, working zippers/hardware, testing stretch, recovery or stiffness, checking it worn on a model or foot form, and deciding construction or material modifications.

Pre-show or photoshoot fitting backstage in a temporary venue: last-minute assessment of the sample on the runway/photo model under time pressure in a crowded, cluttered ad-hoc space — taping, pinning, re-hemming and restyling to get the intended silhouette on camera.

sources.title: Euveka Launches Morphable Robot Mannequins
sources.claim: Euveka's robot-mannequin is the most fit-focused robotic product in fashion: an actuated, digitally controlled form that morphs to reproduce many body morphologies so designers can try samples on different shapes. It presents the garment; the human designer still performs the examination, aesthetic judgment and design modification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: presenting/holding a sample garment at a chosen body shape during fit development. It is cited to bound the frontier — the robotic element replaces the dress form, not the designer's examination of the sample or the decision to modify the design.

sources.claim: Autonomous robotic manipulation of everyday garments (grasping and unfolding a hanging piece of clothing) remains an open research problem, with a large gap between lab results and independent out-of-the-lab evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous handling of limp garments — the physical substrate of examining a sample on and off a form. Even this sub-step is not yet reliable outside the lab, so it cannot support completion of the fuller evaluate-and-modify task.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating a garment onto a body form (the 'on models' half of the instance). Cited to bound the frontier: even in a lab with a rigid mannequin, the system only dresses; no evaluation or modification of the garment design is performed.

sources.title: Sewbots® - Softwear Automation
sources.claim: Commercial apparel robotics operates in purpose-built, fixtured worklines that sew simple sewn goods under machine vision; the work is fabricating panels to a fixed program, with no examination of a sample for aesthetic effect or modification of the design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated garment construction in a purpose-built cell — the E1 counterfactual for apparel work. It shows what a machine-built apparel environment can do (fixtured, pre-programmed sewing) and that sample evaluation/design revision is outside it.

sources.title: AI Humanoid Robots 2026: Technology, Builders & Future
sources.claim: As of 2026 humanoid robots in apparel-related settings are doing logistics — moving totes between AMRs and conveyors in an apparel distribution center — not studio or sample-room design work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose mobile manipulation inside an apparel company's facility. Cited to show the deployed humanoid envelope is rigid-tote handling, far from handling, judging and altering limp sample garments.

Output is a written/spec decision.

Designer sources at a textile trade show or mill/vendor showroom (e.g., Première Vision, supplier appointments), examining hanger sets and mini-rolls, discussing minimums, dye and finishing capabilities with reps, and choosing which qualities to develop for the collection.

Independent, bridal or couture designer selects yardage at a jobber or fabric supplier and tests candidate cloths by draping on a dress form or sewing a test seam, then decides the fabrication and the sewing/production techniques (e.g., French seams, fusing, hand finishing) for the garment.

Designer works with the technical designer and pattern maker to choose interfacings, closures, elastics, labels and trims and to fix production methods that suit the factory's machinery and the target cost, resolving substitutions when a first-choice material fails testing or is unavailable.

Designer selects materials and production techniques largely from digital libraries and 3D sampling tools (digital material scans, CLO/Browzwear), plus vendor PDFs and lab test reports, without physically handling the goods.

Designer attends a large textile trade fair (Première Vision, Munich Fabric Start, Texworld NYC, Kingpins): navigates a crowded convention hall of hundreds of mill booths, touches and compares hundreds of qualities, photographs/notes trend directions, collects swatch cards and business cards, and assembles a seasonal fabric-direction board.

Vendor/mill rep brings hanger books and seasonal offerings to the design studio (or the designer works through mailed swatch packages and sample cuts): designer handles each quality, drapes it on a dress form, checks against color standards and previous-season references, files selected swatches into the in-house fabric library and requests sample yardage.

Designer walks a jobber's / deadstock warehouse or fabric-district retail stockroom looking for what is actually available: pulls and unrolls bolts from stacked shelving, feels hand and checks flaws and available yardage, negotiates on the spot, and buys or reserves cuts.

Independent or small-brand designer sources on the road in unstructured settings: a regional mill floor, an artisan weaving/printing workshop, or an open-air fabric market abroad — variable layouts, no fixed presentation of goods, handling rolls and samples in situ to find novel materials.

sources.title: Ultimate Guide To Fabric Swatches For Fashion Designers – TradeUNO Fabrics
sources.claim: Industry sources describe the task as inherently tactile and in-person: designers request swatches from fabric showrooms ... specifically so they can physically feel the material before committing.
sources.transferJustification: Characterizes the task's physical requirements (in-person handling and tactile evaluation of fabric); not a robotic system and supports no positive judgment.

sources.title: How and Why to Swatch Fabrics - Threads Magazine
sources.claim: Evaluating a fabric requires judging color, opacity, weight, sheen and ... from a physical sample and comparing it against other candidate fabrics — perceptual and aesthetic judgment on handled material.
sources.transferJustification: Describes what the worker's output depends on; not a robotic system and supports no positive judgment.

sources.title: 3D digital technologies: Material focus – Innovation in Textiles
sources.claim: The closest machine to fabric 'assessment' is a bench material scanner that digitizes a swatch placed on it into PBR texture maps; it does not travel to showrooms, select fabrics, or judge commercial suitability, and samples are loaded by a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = fabric digitization. It handles the same objects (swatches) but only captures appearance of a swatch a human already chose and placed; it performs none of the visiting, discovery, tactile judgment, or selection that constitutes this task, so capability does not transfer.

sources.title: Sewbot Technology Drives SoftWear Automation, Raises 20 Million Dollars
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic handling of limp fabric exists only inside purpose-built sewing lines, where machine vision tracks fabric between fixed sewing stations; it is a manufacturing operation, not fabric discovery or evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated sewing of known, pre-cut fabric panels in a fenced production cell. Same material class, but the work is fixtured, single-quality, and pre-specified; it demonstrates no ability to survey unfamiliar new fabrics, judge hand/drape against a design direction, or select and collect swatches.

sources.title: Technology and the Future Of Trade Shows – Display Wizard
sources.claim: Robots that 'attend' trade shows are telepresence platforms driven remotely by a human attendee, not autonomous agents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = remote attendance at an exhibition. It is continuous human teleoperation with no manipulation or tactile evaluation of fabric, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

instances.label: Independent designer/small brand develops a seasonal capsule group (10-20 SKUs) in her own studio: selects fabrics and trims by hand, drapes and sews samples, fits them on a model, edits the assortment, then shows the physical samples with line sheets to boutique buyers at market week and writes wholesale orders.

In-house designer at a mid-size apparel/accessories brand develops a product group with an internal sample room and overseas vendors: reviews and marks physical prototypes in fit sessions, approves materials and colorways, then works with merchandising/sales to present the finished group in the showroom and place it in the catalog/e-commerce assortment.

Designer-owner of a micro-brand working out of a home studio makes small batches of the product group by hand, photographs and styles the pieces for a mail-order/online catalog, writes listings and pricing, then packs and ships individual customer orders.

Designer physically merchandises the new group at a boutique or pop-up: delivers the pieces, steams and hangs them, dresses mannequins, arranges racks and accessory displays to a look, and briefs store staff on the story of the line.

Designer develops an accessories group with an outside manufacturer: handles and corrects sample prototypes at the factory sample room, approves hardware/leather quality, then directs a product photo shoot and assembles the mail-order catalog pages and pricing.

sources.title: Sewbots® - Softwear Automation
sources.claim: SoftWear Automation's Sewbots autonomously sew a complete T-shirt from pre-cut pieces on a purpose-built, machine-vision-guided production line — a fixed, pre-specified product, not the development or marketing of a designer's product group.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated garment sewing. It substantiates only the manufacture of one already-designed style in a purpose-built cell; it does not create an assortment, make and edit samples, or sell to boutique/catalog channels, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: From Custom-Fit Jeans to Sustainable Fashion: Unspun's 3D Weaving Solution
sources.claim: unspun's Vega 3D weaving machine produces a finished pair of pants directly from yarn in about ten minutes, showing robotic garment production of a pre-specified digital design but not product-line development or marketing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand garment manufacture from a digital pattern. It shows machine execution of a finished design, not the designer's work of developing an assortment and bringing it to boutique or catalog channels.

sources.title: Retail automation: robots on the shop floor and behind the scenes
sources.claim: Autonomous in-store retail robots deployed in 2025 navigate aisles to scan shelves and report inventory data; their demonstrated capability is data capture, not merchandising, styling displays, or selling a collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store robotic operations. It shows what robots reliably do on a retail floor (scan and report) and thereby marks the absence of any system that stages a boutique display or presents a line to buyers.

sources.title: Robot folds laundry with remote human help
sources.claim: State-of-the-art home garment-handling robots still rely on remote human operators for clothes folding, indicating that dexterous fabric manipulation outside fixtured settings is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general garment manipulation in an unstructured studio/home. Teleoperation-dependent performance cannot support a positive judgment for sample making or product handling in this task.

tasks.label: Draw patterns for articles designed, cut patterns, and cut material according to patterns, using measuring instruments and scissors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-style first pattern: in a design studio or sample room (or the designer's own studio), the designer works from a sketch and a base block to draft pattern pieces on pattern paper with rulers, curves and measuring tape, trues seam lines, adds seam allowances, notches and grainlines, then cuts the paper pattern pieces with shears.

Draping-based development: muslin is pinned and marked on a dress form, style lines are drawn, the cloth is removed, trued and transferred into flat paper pattern pieces which are then cut; the muslin toile pieces are cut from the fabric.

Fit-correction round: after a fitting on a model or form, the designer measures the discrepancies, redraws the affected pattern pieces (adds/removes ease, moves darts, reshapes armholes) and recuts the corrected paper pattern.

Cutting the first sample/toile fabric from a finished pattern: yardage spread on a cutting table, pattern pieces placed to grainline and nap, weighted or pinned, then cut with shears/rotary cutter and notched, in a sample room or cutting room.

Cutting additional sample garments, colorways, size-set samples or a short production run from finalized patterns, including matching plaids, stripes and engineered prints and handling slippery or delicate fabrics, in a sample/cutting room.

Producing the pattern output from an approved master pattern: drawing/plotting the full-scale pattern set including graded sizes and the marker, and cutting duplicate hard patterns (oaktag/card) or marker paper for production.

sources.title: Vector Fashion | Automatic Fabric Cutter for Fashion & Apparel Manufacturing - Lectra

sources.title: ITMA 2023 – digital expertise for single-ply cutting | Zünd
sources.claim: Zünd single-ply digital cutters are sold and used for garment cutting rooms, cutting one-off, made-to-measure and small-batch garment pieces from digital patterns — the sample-room / short-run case rather than mass production.

sources.claim: Zünd cutters use an Over-Cutter Camera to register printed and patterned fabric before cutting, so pieces are cut in alignment with the print — the machine equivalent of a cutter matching plaids, stripes and engineered prints by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Print/plaid registration is the same requirement as the human step of aligning pattern pieces to a fabric's stripe or motif before cutting.

sources.transferJustification: Automatic grading/measurement-driven modification is the rule-based part of 'drawing patterns'; it feeds the plotter that performs the physical drawing and pattern cutting.

tasks.label: Sew together sections of material to form mockups or samples of garments or articles, using sewing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First-pattern muslin toile of a new structured style (dress bodice, jacket, tailored trouser): designer cuts muslin from a fresh paper/CAD pattern, then machine-bastes darts, curved princess seams, armholes and eased set-in sleeves on an industrial single-needle machine in the in-house design studio/sample room, often altering seam lines mid-sew.

Simple flat-panel sample built from cut pieces in the sample room: jersey tee, tank, hoodie body, simple skirt/shorts, tote or cushion-type accessory. Straight and gently curved seams, hems and binding on standard studio machines; small quantity (1-3 pieces) of a new but conventional style.

Presentation/showroom sample sewn in the actual fashion fabric with full construction: linings, facings, invisible zippers, plackets, collars, set-in sleeves, topstitching, delicate fabrics (chiffon, leather, sequins) and hand-finishing, produced in the studio/sample room to a standard buyers or the runway will see.

Reworking a sample after a fit session: unpicking and re-sewing side seams, moving darts, re-setting a sleeve, shortening/re-hemming, adding trims or pockets to an already-assembled mockup on the studio machine, working from pinned/chalked corrections marked on the garment.

Independent or freelance designer sewing mockups and small sample runs in a home studio or shared makerspace: domestic/semi-industrial machine and serger on a household table, mixed and unpredictable equipment and layout, garments ranging from simple tops to bridal and costume pieces.

sources.claim: Siemens/Sewbo/Levi's/Bluewater Defense robotic sewing workcell assembled denim shorts subassemblies and 3D garment-shaping seams (front rise, back rise, side seam) on a factory floor, using a UR5e with suction gripper, conventional sewing machines, suction table and welding station, with 90% trial success.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (production jeans assembly) shares the physical act of joining cut garment sections by machine seam; it does not cover one-off mockups of novel patterns, and only about half the garment's operations were automated.

instances.label: Retail flower shop workroom: one-off custom or "designer's choice" order (birthday, get-well, anniversary). Designer selects from whatever is in the cooler, strips and trims mixed stems and foliage to varying lengths, sets them in a vase or soaked foam, adds filler, ribbon, picks and wire, and finishes to a unique shape.

Retail shop or wholesale design room: standardized catalog product made repeatedly to a fixed recipe (a dozen roses in a vase, wire-service standard designs, a holiday run of dozens of identical arrangements). Same stems, same counts, same container each time.

Sympathy and funeral work: wreaths, standing/easel sprays and casket pieces. Designer covers a foam-filled cage or wire wreath frame with greens and blooms, wires and picks heavy-headed flowers, tapes and pins ribbon and banners, works to large scale on a stand under same-day deadline.

Wedding and event work: bridal and bridesmaid bouquets, boutonnieres and corsages. Individual stems wired, taped, and bound; stems trimmed and wrapped with ribbon and pearl pins; plus matching centerpieces. High finish quality, each order unique to the client.

Supermarket floral department or mass-market bouquet production room: high-volume wrapped mixed bouquets and mono bunches built to a fixed recipe from bulk stems — count out stems, remove lower leaves, cut to uniform length, band/tie, add food sachet, sleeve and place in buckets.

Non-fresh goods: silk/artificial arrangements and wreaths, dried designs, and planted terrariums or dish gardens (glass vessel, gravel, moss, soil, small plants), assembled with foam, hot glue, wire and picks in the shop workroom.

instances.label: Retail flower shop: a finished vase/container arrangement is sleeved or wrapped in a cellophane/cello cone (sometimes stapled at the top), a care card is added and a printed price sticker or hang tag is attached before the piece goes to the cooler, display case, or delivery rack.

Retail flower shop, walk-in or gift order: a completed hand-tied bouquet is wrapped by hand in tissue and decorative kraft/printed paper, corners folded, the stems bound and a ribbon bow tied, then priced (tag written/printed and attached or rung at POS).

Supermarket / mass-market floral department: designer sleeves finished bunches and mixed bouquets into pre-printed plastic or paper sleeves, adds flower-food sachet, and applies the UPC/price scan label before setting them out in buckets — high volume, standardized SKUs.

High-volume bouquet production or e-commerce fulfillment facility (grocery bouquet supplier, wire-service/online florist): completed bouquets move down a processing line to be sleeved, labelled with barcode/price and date, and packed for shipment.

Event/wedding and delivery packaging in the shop workroom: bridal bouquets, corsages and boutonnieres are boxed with tissue and cellophane, arrangements are braced and wrapped for transport, with pricing carried on the contract/invoice rather than a shelf tag.

sources.title: SleevR: a new fully automatic sleeving machine

tasks.label: Deliver arrangements to customers, or oversee employees responsible for deliveries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential delivery run: designer/driver loads 8-15 finished vase arrangements, plants and balloons into a van at the shop, drives a multi-stop route across a metro area, parks at private houses and apartment complexes, carries the water-filled arrangement up walkways and steps, hands it to the recipient or places it safely out of sun/wind when nobody answers, and reports non-deliveries back to the shop.

Business/office delivery: arrangement taken into a commercial building or office park, through lobby doors and elevators, signed in at a reception desk or handed to a receptionist for a named recipient, with card attached and packaging removed.

Hospital, nursing home or assisted-living delivery: arrangement carried to the facility's front desk, gift shop, or nursing station (occasionally a patient room), complying with visitor check-in and unit restrictions (e.g., no flowers in ICU), often with a wheeled cart for several pieces.

Funeral home, church, cemetery or event-venue delivery: standing sprays on easels, casket pieces, large sympathy baskets and reception centerpieces transported upright in a van, carried into a chapel or hall, assembled on easels/stands and positioned per the director's or client's instructions, on a hard deadline before the service starts.

Overseeing delivery staff: shop owner/lead designer batches orders by zone, builds driver routes and time windows, checks arrangements onto the truck for correct card/recipient, tracks drivers by phone, handles re-delivery of missed or damaged orders and customer complaints on peak holidays.

sources.title: Starship Technologies surpasses 8M autonomous deliveries - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Starship's sidewalk robots perform autonomous last-mile deliveries at commercial scale (8M+ deliveries, 10M+ miles) on campuses and in neighborhoods, but the cargo box is small (~400 x 320 x 340 mm, 10-22 lb) and the customer must come to the robot and unlock the lid to retrieve the goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous last-mile delivery of food/grocery parcels. Transfers partially to floral delivery (same routes, same recipients), but the sealed 13-inch-tall bin and customer-unlock handoff do not match carrying a water-filled vase arrangement to a doorstep.

sources.system: Starship delivery robot (Cal Poly campus deployment)
sources.title: Starship Robots Coming to Cal Poly Campus Dining
sources.claim: Starship robots are loaded by shop staff, carry up to 22 lb in a locked compartment, and the lid opens only when the customer prompts it on arrival - i.e., the recipient must be present, app-enabled and retrieve the item themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: campus/neighborhood parcel and food delivery. Establishes the size envelope and handoff model that a floral delivery would have to fit, on an institution-controlled campus (E2).

sources.title: Serve Robotics Rolls Out Third-Generation Autonomous Delivery Robot
sources.claim: Serve Robotics operates Level 4 autonomous sidewalk delivery robots commercially in Los Angeles and other US cities for Uber Eats; the Gen3 bin is sized for flat food orders (four 16-inch pizzas) with a 50 lb payload.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: public-sidewalk food delivery. Shows commercial E3 sidewalk autonomy exists but with a low, flat cargo bin unsuited to tall, top-heavy vase arrangements, and with curbside customer-retrieval rather than doorstep placement.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Releases New Hotel Delivery Robot That Offers Double the Capacity of Its Predecessor - Robotics 24/7

Same essential act as delivering an arrangement to a recipient inside a structured facility: loaded at a service point, transported autonomously among people and elevators, recipient opens the compartment; 41 L compartment accommodates a modest arrangement.

sources.title: Mercy Hospital Install their fleet of hospital delivery robots - Aethon

sources.title: Servi Plus: Bear Robotics' Flagship AI Service Robot for Hospitality and Beyond
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots are commercially deployed in restaurants, senior living, hotels and casinos, autonomously carrying open trays of food and drinks among seated guests with active suspension for stable liquid transport.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting open, top-heavy, liquid-filled items (glasses, plated food) across a people-filled human facility to a specific destination. Directly comparable to wheeling an unboxed vase arrangement across a lobby or ward without spilling or tipping.

sources.title: Greater Houston kicks off Walmart and Wing's biggest expansion year yet
sources.claim: Wing's autonomous drones deliver to homes at commercial scale with Walmart, but the tether-and-winch system is limited to packages of about 2.5 pounds lowered onto an open spot on the customer's property.

Grooming/cleaning product already in storage: removing yellowed leaves, bruised guard petals and debris, wiping foliage, culling spent stems from cooler buckets, dumping and refreshing bucket water with fresh preservative solution.

High-volume batch prep (wholesale/e-commerce fulfillment or large event order): hundreds of stems of one variety cut to uniform length, deleafed, bunched and placed into hydration buckets to a fixed spec.

sources.title: Twister | Automated hand bouquet line | HAVATEC
sources.claim: Havatec's Twister is a commercially sold bouquet line that automatically builds twisted (spiral) bouquets of 10-35 stems from multiple flower types presented on turntables inside a purpose-built flower-processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-variety bouquet composition. It handles the same objects (cut stems and greens) and produces the same accepted output (a saleable mixed bouquet), so it bears on whether a machine can put selected flora together at commercial quality.

sources.title: Havatec Twister bouquet line | Agro-Technology
sources.claim: On the Twister line the combination of flowers is a human-entered recipe: operators fill the turntables by recipe and the machine then picks and assembles; the machine does not originate the combination.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (automated bouquet composition); the quote establishes the division of labour between human recipe design and machine assembly, which is what this task turns on.

sources.title: Bouquet making - HAVATEC
sources.claim: Havatec also sells a gerbera bunching machine that automatically composes bunches combining up to five colours, i.e. machine selection of stems by specified colour mix on a processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated colour-mix bunching. It shows machines can pick stems of specified varieties/colours into a defined combination in a purpose-built line, the mechanical core of 'selecting flora for arrangements'.

sources.title: Placing flower bunches in buckets with robots - DERO GROEP
sources.claim: DERO's FlowerCollector is a deployed robotic cell that picks up bunches of flowers, including mixed bouquets, and places them into buckets at up to 5,000 bunches per ... inside flower processing lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of finished bunches. Establishes that delicate cut-flower material can be grasped and moved by robots at production quality in a purpose-built line, supporting E1 handling but not design selection.

sources.title: Robots Arranging Flowers — QuickFlora
sources.claim: QuickFlora's FloraBot venture built a robotic arm system that assembles a standard dozen-rose arrangement in about four minutes; the design executed is a preset product, not a newly synthesized composition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of a florist arrangement. Same objects and output format as this task, so it bounds what a robot can do: recipe execution rather than origination of new combinations.

sources.title: Using robotic arms to make floral arrangements | FloralDaily
sources.claim: A FloraBot kiosk shown at MassRobotics/TechCrunch used a robotic arm to place individual stems into a bouquet on demand from a stocked, purpose-built cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand robotic bouquet assembly from stocked stems in a machine-built cabinet; relevant because it is the closest demonstrated system to a robot 'choosing' stems, and it works only from preset catalog designs.

sources.title: RoboChallenge/Table30 · Datasets at Hugging Face
sources.claim: In the RoboChallenge Table30 real-robot benchmark, flower handling appears only as a lab tabletop task of inserting three flowers into a vase one by one — the state of general-purpose robot flower manipulation, with no design component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: generalist-robot flower placement. It shows that for non-purpose-built arms, flower work is still a benchmark insertion exercise, so no general system substantiates composing arrangements in a shop or venue.

tasks.label: Perform general cleaning duties in the store to ensure the shop is clean and tidy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail flower shop: sweeping/vacuuming and mopping the sales floor, entry and back design room throughout the day — clipped stems, leaf litter, petals, bits of soil and moss, plus water tracked from buckets and the sink. Floor is partly obstructed by buckets, boxes and display fixtures.

Wiping down and sanitizing hard work surfaces between jobs: the design bench, wrap station, checkout counter and utility sink — brushing clipped stems and leaf litter off the surface into the waste bin, mopping up standing water, spraying and wiping the surface dry.
Washing and sanitizing flower buckets, vases, liners and tools at the back sink — scrubbing out slime/bacterial film, rinsing with bleach solution, drying and re-shelving the containers.
Cleaning the walk-in display cooler: pulling spent/wilted stems, dumping and refilling bucket water, wiping down shelves and interior glass doors, sanitizing, and mopping the cooler floor.

Emptying the green-waste and trash bins at the bench and register, replacing liners, hauling bags and stem waste out to the dumpster in the back lot, and breaking down flower and hardgoods delivery boxes.

Dusting and tidying retail displays — shelved vases, giftware, silk arrangements and card racks — straightening merchandise, cleaning storefront and cooler glass, and cleaning the small customer/staff restroom.

sources.title: Pudu CC1 At QT: How A 4-in-1 Floor Cleaning Robot Delivers Real ROI In Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Pudu CC1, a compact four-in-one autonomous floor cleaning robot (sweep, scrub, vacuum, dust-mop), is deployed in QuikTrip convenience stores running scheduled sweeping and mopping rounds among customers — a small retail sales floor comparable to a flower shop.

sources.title: Gausium: Autonomous Cleaning & Service Robot / Phantas product page
sources.claim: Gausium's compact Phantas robot (vacuum, sweep, scrub, dust-mop) is sold for small, furniture-dense spaces and fleets of Phantas/Omnie robots have been deployed for autonomous store cleaning by a supermarket chain.

sources.title: Avidbots announces launch of Kas autonomous cleaning robot
sources.claim: Avidbots' Kas is a fully autonomous floor scrubber launched specifically for retail and other people-occupied facilities, sized to navigate tight spaces and clean around people and objects; Avidbots robots adapt to moved end caps and seasonal layout changes without manual intervention.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's Bathroom Cleaning Robot is a mobile manipulator deployed in hospitals and airports that autonomously cleans fixtures and counters (spray/wipe chemicals), cleans floors, and picks up trash during normal facility operating hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restroom fixture/counter wiping. Transfer to wiping a florist's bench and checkout counter is close — the same act of spraying and wiping fixed, hard, waist-height surfaces plus picking up loose litter, inside an institution-controlled facility with a learned static layout.

sources.title: Autonomous SOMATIC Robot Demonstrates its Bathroom Cleaning Skills
sources.claim: The Somatic robot is taught a space once in VR (where to spray, wipe, vacuum, blow-dry) and thereafter cleans all bathroom surfaces using onboard LiDAR and sensors without direct supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the surface-wiping cited above is autonomous after a one-time teaching phase rather than teleoperated.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fielded a commercially deployed mobile manipulator that autonomously navigates rooms and wipes surfaces with a cloth in hotels, corporate buildings and commercial outlets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hotel bathroom surface cleaning with a cloth. The wiping of fixed hard surfaces in a human-occupied commercial facility transfers to wiping a florist counter/bench of comparable size and rigidity.

sources.system: Automatic crate/container washing and stacking line
sources.developer: LONKIA Machinery / industrial crate washer vendors
sources.title: Industrial Continuous Crate Washing Machine Automatic Tunnel Crate Washer
sources.claim: Automated tunnel crate-washing lines wash, sanitize and stack plastic containers — crates, trays, pallets, deep harvesting baskets — that are conveyed through the machine, in purpose-built food-industry wash rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sanitizing plastic containers. Florist buckets and liners are plastic containers of the same size class as harvesting baskets/crates; the line delivers the same accepted output (scrubbed, sanitized, stacked) once containers are presented to it.

sources.title: Dishcraft Robotics Automatically Cleans Dishes and Utensils
sources.claim: Dishcraft Robotics operated a machine-vision robotic dish-cleaning system for commercial food service in which humans pre-sort and pre-stack dirty dishware into carts/fixtures and the machine picks, scrubs and cleans them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scrubbing food-service ware. Shows a purpose-built cell where fixtured, pre-presented vessels are robotically scrubbed clean — the E1 counterpart of washing florist vases and buckets.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots move waste in hospitals at scale — over 6 million lbs of trash hauled at one hospital in 2024 — but they transport carts that people load and unload rather than emptying bins themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: waste haulage in a facility. Cited to show the limit — autonomous transport of loaded carts is deployed, but bagging, liner replacement and tipping waste into a dumpster are not covered.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 vision-language-action model controls a mobile manipulator to tidy and clean kitchens and bedrooms in entirely new homes not seen in training, performing multi-stage cleanup behaviors autonomously; results are research demonstrations rather than reliability-rated deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general tidying/clutter clearing. Cited as the frontier for unstructured cleanup; demo-level success rates do not meet employer-accepted reliability, so it does not by itself lift any instance's tier.

tasks.label: Decorate, or supervise the decoration of, buildings, halls, churches, or other facilities for parties, weddings and other occasions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wedding install in a hotel ballroom or banquet hall: unload van, carry in vases/mechanics, place and level 15-30 centerpieces on linened round tables among chairs and other vendors, set aisle and head-table florals, top off water, remove packaging, and adjust to the room's actual layout before guests arrive on a hard deadline.

Statement installation at an event venue: build a floral arch/chuppah, floral wall, or suspended ceiling/chandelier installation on site — lashing greenery and stems to a metal or wooden frame with wire, zip ties and floral foam, working from ladders or lifts, balancing and securing the structure, then fluffing and correcting the composition by eye.

Church or house-of-worship ceremony: altar and chancel arrangements, pew/aisle markers, candelabra and greenery on fixed architecture, working around clergy rules, tight aisles, carpeted steps, and time windows between services.

Corporate party, gala, or holiday decorating in a hotel, convention center, restaurant, or office lobby: entrance and stage florals, buffet and cocktail-table pieces, garlands on railings and mantels, coordination with AV and catering crews already working the room.

Private residence, garden, or tent event (backyard wedding, shower, dinner party): decorating a home's mantel, staircase, porch, or a rented tent on uneven ground, with no fixed layout, pets and family present, improvised power/water, and weather exposure.

Supervising the decoration: directing a crew of assistants and freelancers on a large install — assigning placement, checking sightlines and heights, physically spot-correcting arrangements, and walking the room with the planner for final sign-off.

sources.system: Bercomex Flora BunchMaster / Furora bunching lines
sources.title: Automatic bunching with efficient Bercomex bunching machines
sources.claim: Commercial flower automation is confined to purpose-built processing lines that bunch and assemble bouquets from flowers presented by conveyors; nothing in the product line installs decor at an event venue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized assembly of cut-flower bunches/bouquets. It shows flower handling is automated only where stems arrive fixtured on a conveyor in a factory; it provides no capability to transport, mount, hang, or place decor inside a hall, church, or hotel ballroom, which is what this task requires.

sources.system: QuickFlora-powered floral kiosk robotic arm (MassRobotics startup)
sources.title: Using robotic arms to make floral arrangements
sources.claim: A robotic arm at an on-demand kiosk was shown arranging individual flowers into a bouquet, i.e. bench-scale arrangement making rather than venue decoration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: building a floral arrangement. Even taken at face value it is a fixed-station arm making one vase piece from pre-sorted stems; it does not travel to a facility, mount florals on architecture, or dress a room, so it cannot substantiate completing a venue decoration instance.

sources.title: Robots decorate trees, perform carols in store's holiday display
sources.claim: The closest robotic 'decorating' demonstration is a retail window display in which arms repeatedly place ornaments onto stands pre-positioned in a tree — a purpose-built, fixed-cycle exhibit, not a venue install.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing decorative objects on a display. Transfer fails because the ornaments are presented and received by fixed stands in a known pose and the same 30-minute cycle repeats; event decoration requires novel venues, varied mechanics, and aesthetic on-site judgment.

sources.system: Fraunhofer IOSB autonomous robotic system (quadrupeds plus autonomous crane)
sources.title: Holiday prep goes robotic as Christmas machines tackle decor and meals
sources.claim: A research holiday demonstration showed legged robots and a crane dressing a large outdoor Christmas tree with decorations and lights; it is a promotional research video, not a service delivered to a customer's venue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: draping decorations onto a single large object outdoors. Autonomy is not established and the scope is one staged tree at a research site; it does not show a full facility decorated to a client's accepted standard on a deadline.

sources.system: Bear Robotics Servi / Keenon servers; Aethon hospitality AMRs
sources.title: Hospitality Robots | Aethon
sources.claim: Robots actually deployed in hotels, banquet halls, and event operations are transport platforms that move food, beverages, and supply carts; they perform no manipulation of decor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobility inside event venues. It establishes that navigation in ballrooms is solved, but these machines have no arms and cannot place, mount, or arrange decor, so the decoration instance itself remains unsupported.

sources.title: Welcome, Dyna Robotics! | Salesforce Ventures
sources.claim: The commercial frontier of autonomous dexterity is a fixed-station arm performing one repetitive, high-precision manipulation for long stretches without supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained autonomous fine manipulation of limp materials in a hospitality setting. It marks the ceiling of deployed dexterous autonomy — one station, one repeated motion — far short of a multi-hour, multi-element decoration install across a whole venue.

tasks.label: Inform customers about the care, maintenance, and handling of various flowers and foliage, indoor plants, and other items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Unpack stock as it comes into the shop.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent retail flower shop, routine wholesale delivery (2-3x/week): cut open/strap taped cardboard flower boxes in a cramped workroom, pull out sleeved bunches, cut binders and sleeves, strip lower foliage, recut stems, place into water buckets with preservative, check against invoice and move buckets into the cooler.

Supermarket/mass-market floral department: cases and cart racks of pre-made consumer bouquets and mono bunches arrive; worker cuts open cases, removes sleeved bouquets, trims stems, sets them into water-filled buckets on the sales-floor display and back cooler, breaks down cartons.

Hard-goods/supplies shipment: cartons of vases, containers, ribbon, floral foam, wire, chemicals and packaging arrive; worker slits cartons, removes padding/wrap, verifies items against the packing slip, and shelves them in the stockroom.

Potted and blooming plants, greens and other perishables: plants shipped in sleeves, trays or boxes are unboxed, sleeves removed, watered, inspected for damage, and set out on display or in the cooler.

Holiday peak (Valentine's Day / Mother's Day): a truck drops dozens of flower boxes at the curb or back alley; the designer hauls them in through an unstructured outdoor drop point and unpacks and hydrates them under time pressure amid clutter.

Small parcel deliveries during business hours: boxes of dried/silk stems, artificial greenery, balloons and event supplies arriving by UPS/FedEx into the shop front amid customer traffic; unwrap, uncrush/fluff, inventory and store.

sources.title: Placing flower bunches in buckets with robots - DERO GROEP
sources.claim: DERO GROEP's FlowerCollector is a commercial robotic cell that autonomously collects bunches of fresh flowers and places them into buckets on a flower-processing line, handling many flower types and mixed bouquets at up to 5,000 bunches/hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line bunch handling at growers/bouquet packers. Transfer: identical objects (sleeved/bound fresh flower bunches) and identical end state as shop unpacking (bunch placed upright into a bucket), at comparable delicacy and precision, in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Discover our latest innovations - DERO GROEP
sources.claim: The FlowerCollector has been run in production at growers: a full-season test at a tulip grower processing ~4,600 bunches/hour, and later versions extended from tulips to roses, chrysanthemums and spray flowers.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: substantiates that the bunch-into-bucket robot runs a whole season in real production, not only as a demo.

sources.date: c. 2023-2024 article; robot in use 3+ years
sources.title: Automatisering met robot - Gijsbert Verboom: Glastuinbouw Nederland
sources.claim: At Gerbera United's Nootdorp site a fully automatic robot in the processing room receives incoming carts of freshly cut flowers, lifts the racks of flower buckets off the cart, weighs them, moves them to a cutting machine that trims the raw stem ends so the flowers take up water, then sets the flowers into water-filled buckets that go into the storage wall; it has been in use over three years and saves 15-20% of labour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intake and storage of harvested flowers at a grower. Transfer: the same physical sequence as shop unpacking of a delivery - take flower containers off an arriving cart, trim the stem ends, and place the stems into water buckets for cold storage - with the same delicate cut-flower objects.

sources.system: DAC Robotics ABOT + precision decanting system with OSARO SightWorks depalletizer
sources.title: Depalletizing, box opening and decanting combined in one system | Control Design
sources.claim: DAC Robotics' integrated warehouse receiving system combines OSARO-guided mixed-case depalletizing, the ABOT automatic box-opening robot, and a precision decant robot that transfers carton contents into totes, covering everything from pallet to tote.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse receiving/decant. Transfer: it is the same physical act as unpacking stock into a shop - slitting and opening a sealed shipping carton without damaging contents and transferring the contents into their storage container - on comparable retail cartons and goods.

sources.title: Warehouse Replenishment Automation for Fulfillment | FANUC America
sources.claim: Robotica's ABOT M1 automated box-opening and ePack decant units are production products built on FANUC industrial robots, opening shipping boxes without damaging inner contents and placing the contents into tote sub-compartments for grocery replenishment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grocery decant of inbound cases. Transfer: opening sealed cartons and unpacking their contents into storage containers is the core of unpacking hard goods and packaged floral supplies; cartons and items are of comparable size and fragility.

sources.title: Harvey - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 'Harvey' mobile robots autonomously locate, transport and place potted plants in greenhouses and outdoor nursery fields, and were bought and used in production by container-crop growers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursery pot logistics. Transfer: same objects (potted plants of shop-delivery size and weight) being picked up and set down in position, the manipulation step of putting delivered plants out on display.

sources.title: Super Trooper: Autonomous robot helps gardeners transport potted plants | SICK
sources.claim: Instar Robotics' Trooper is an autonomous handling robot used in horticultural nurseries to transport potted plants weighing up to 10 kg, navigating with 3D LiDAR.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursery plant transport. Transfer: same objects (potted plants) and same handling of delivered plant stock within a facility.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment - DHL Group
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is a fully autonomous mobile robot deployed in DHL warehouses that unloads floor-loaded cases from trailers and containers at up to 700 cases per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trailer case unloading. Transfer: covers only the receiving/moving-cases-inside portion of unpacking stock, in an as-found dock/trailer of a structured facility; it does not open cartons or handle the contents, so it cannot by itself complete this task.

tasks.label: Create and change in-store and window displays, designs, and looks to enhance a shop's image.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Independent retail flower shop, seasonal/holiday window display changeover: strip out the previous display, install backdrop fabric/paper, hang garlands, ribbon and suspended elements from a rod or ceiling, position risers, urns and props, build and place large focal arrangements, adjust spotlights, clean glass and sweep debris. Ladder and step-stool work in a shallow, awkward window bay with power cords, novel props and no fixed layout.

Daily/weekly restaging of the shop-floor and cooler displays in a small florist: cull wilted stems and dead heads, swap in fresh ready-made bouquets and vase arrangements, change water, reposition vases, potted plants, giftware, cards and signage on shelves, tables and inside the glass-door cooler, and re-face the whole look after customers have disturbed it. Cluttered, variable, mixed fragile objects.

Supermarket/garden-center floral department set to a corporate planogram: build the tiered bulk-bucket display and sleeved-bouquet racks, set a seasonal end-cap with props and point-of-sale signage, rotate stock forward, top up water, and tidy the wet-rack area during trading hours with customers and carts moving through.

Replenishing the sales-floor mass display of bunched flowers: making up uniform graded bunches of a few stem types and filling the display buckets so the front-of-store bulk display looks full and consistent for the day's trade.

Building a themed feature/focal display piece: a silk-flower or dried-material installation, wreath wall, or seasonal vignette assembled with foam, wire, hot glue, mechanics and mixed props, then mounted on a pedestal, wall or hung above the counter.

Storefront/sidewalk display: wheeling bucket racks, A-frame signs and potted stock out onto the public sidewalk at opening, arranging them for curb appeal around passers-by and street furniture, watering, then bringing everything back inside at close; adjusted for wind, rain and sun.

sources.title: Placing flower bunches in buckets with robots - DERO GROEP
sources.claim: Commercial robotic machine that automatically collects bunches of cut flowers and places them into display/transport buckets on a flower processing line, at up to 5,000 bunches per ..., handling many flower types and mixed bouquets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling buckets with bunched flowers on a purpose-built line. It transfers to the bulk-bucket display replenishment instance because the objects (bunched fresh stems), the placement precision, and the accepted output (evenly filled buckets of flowers) are the same; only the location differs, which the E1 counterfactual supplies.

sources.system: Bercomex Furora Compact / Furora Nova bunching machines
sources.date: 2026-07 (product pages, retrieved 2026-07; product line in commercial use for years)
sources.title: Bercomex Furora Compact | automatic bunching machine
sources.claim: Commercial automatic bunching machines that sort and bunch cut flowers fully automatically, using X-ray/vision scanning to grade each stem for length, diameter and crooked stems before making uniform bunches.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grading and assembling uniform flower bunches in a purpose-built line. It supplies the stem-quality culling and bunch-making that the bulk display replenishment instance requires, on the same objects (fresh cut stems) and to a commercially accepted presentation standard.

sources.title: Robots arranging flowers (FloralDaily)
sources.claim: Robotic arm cell/kiosk built to assemble fresh-flower arrangements; reported to build a typical dozen-rose vase arrangement in about four minutes from pre-loaded flowers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass-market arrangement assembly in a fixtured cell. Cited only as context for what fixtured floral automation reaches; autonomy is not established, so it does not by itself support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Track-mounted AI restocking robot deployed in hundreds of Japanese convenience stores, autonomously replenishing refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... from a pre-registered shelf layout; remote human teleoperation is used only to recover from errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store shelf replenishment in a live retail (E2) setting. It marks the current frontier of retail merchandising robots - rigid, fixed-SKU bottles into a purpose-built fridge fixture on a fixed rail - and shows why nothing cited reaches free-form floral display staging with novel props, ladders and design judgment.

tasks.label: Conduct classes or demonstrations, or train other workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail flower shop workroom: a senior designer trains a new hire at the bench — demonstrating stem processing and conditioning, wiring/taping, spiral hand-tied technique, foam mechanics for a sympathy piece — then watches the trainee work, corrects hand position and stem placement, critiques and reworks faulty arrangements until the trainee's output meets shop standard.

Supermarket floral department or wholesale bouquet operation: lead designer trains seasonal/part-time staff at a production table on standardized bouquet recipes, care-and-handling, pricing and quality checks; demonstrates the recipe once, then audits and corrects each trainee's bunches during a shift.

Paid public workshop for 8-15 adult customers at the shop's classroom or an event space: the designer demonstrates a project (wreath, hand-tied bouquet, holiday centerpiece) at the front, distributes and manages materials, then circulates to coach individuals, answer questions, fix wobbling arrangements, and pace the class to time.

Off-site live demonstration/talk at a garden club, church hall, county fair tent, or bridal-industry event: designer hauls buckets and containers in, sets up on a borrowed table with whatever space and lighting exists, designs three to five arrangements live while narrating technique and fielding audience questions, then breaks down and gives pieces away.

Floral design school, community college lab, or certification (AIFD-track) course: instructor teaches a scheduled lesson at a bench of students, demonstrates technique under an overhead camera, supervises hands-on practice, then grades and critiques each student's arrangement against design principles.

sources.title: Robots Arranging Flowers - Florists' Review
sources.claim: FloraBot (QuickFlora/MassRobotics) built a robotic-arm kiosk that assembles individual flowers into a standard dozen-roses arrangement from fixtured, pre-sorted stems in roughly four minutes; it produces product, it does not instruct people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically building a floral arrangement. It is the closest robotic capability to the physical content of a floral demonstration, but it works only on identical fixtured roses in a purpose-built kiosk and contains no instruction, narration, or correction of a learner's work, so it does not carry over to conducting classes or training workers.

sources.title: TeachBot: Towards teaching robotics fundamentals for human-robot collaboration at work - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: TeachBot is a research prototype autonomous robotic instructor that delivers a fixed spoken-plus-touch curriculum teaching manufacturing workers robot-arm fundamentals; the subject matter is the robot itself and it does not manipulate craft materials or critique a trainee's handmade output.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot conducting a hands-on training session for human workers. It fails to transfer because the taught content is operation of the robot arm itself on a scripted curriculum, with no dexterous demonstration of a craft (cutting, wiring, spiraling stems) and no individualized assessment or rework of a trainee's physical product.

sources.title: US firm to deploy humanoid robot teaching assistant in New York schools
sources.claim: Realbotix's Optio AI teaching assistant with an M-Series humanoid was launched in a New York school ... as a conversational tutor and avatar; the deployed teaching robot provides talk-based tutoring only, with no manipulation of physical materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered classroom instruction. It substantiates only verbal/avatar tutoring in a school; it has no arms performing floral technique and cannot demonstrate, inspect, or correct students' physical arrangements, so it cannot complete a floral class or bench training.

sources.title: Flora BouquetMaster - Automatically bunch uniform bouquets | Bercomex
sources.claim: Commercial floral 'automatic' bouquet lines such as Bercomex's Flora BouquetMaster still rely on human operators to compose bouquets, with the machine binding and cutting and a display instructing each employee.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial bouquet production. Shows that even in the most purpose-built floral setting the composition step is performed by human workers guided by machines — the reverse of a robot training workers — so it supports no positive judgment here.

tasks.label: Photograph layouts, using camera, to make layout prints for supervisors or clients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the design studio, the designer lays a flat comp, printed proof or hand-drawn layout sheet on a desk or copy stand, shoots it straight-on with a DSLR or phone under room/copy lighting, then outputs a hard-copy print for the supervisor's review file.

Tabletop capture of a three-dimensional layout artifact - folded package dummy, mounted display comp, bound presentation mock-up - in a studio corner with a light tent or strobes; several angles shot, best frames printed as a client presentation sheet.

Large flat layout: a full-size poster comp, mounted board, or storyboard wall photographed square-on in the studio or conference room (keystone controlled, whole board in frame), then reduced-size prints run for supervisor/client review.

Capture away from the designer's own desk but still indoors on portable material: press-check proofs at the print vendor, or layout boards at a client's office, photographed handheld under mixed lighting, with prints produced for sign-off.

In-situ capture of an installed layout - retail display, trade-show booth panel, exterior sign, vehicle wrap or mural - under found lighting, weather and clutter, then prints made for the client's records.

sources.title: Large Format Printers and Scanners | Canon U.S.A., Inc.
sources.claim: Large-format multifunction printer/scanner systems image a flat original up to 36 in wide and produce a printed copy as a machine-executed scan-to-copy workflow, i.e. capture plus print of a flat layout without a human operating a camera.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wide-format document copying. Same object class (flat sheet layouts and posters up to poster size), same output (a print for review), and the machine performs capture and printing itself once the original is presented.

sources.title: Automatic Book Scanner | Treventus
sources.claim: A camera-based imaging robot photographs flat originals at reproduction quality and handles the originals itself (automatic page turning at up to 2,500 pages/h), running in library digitization rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: camera-based digitization of flat paper originals. Comparable objects (flat sheets of artwork/text), higher precision than a review print requires, and the machine both presents and photographs each page itself.

sources.title: An eye for detail: Zoom through 1,000 artworks thanks to the new Art Camera from the Google Cultural Institute
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic camera rig, once placed before a flat artwork, autonomously steers itself over the surface and captures hundreds of high-resolution frames stitched into a reproduction-grade image; supplied to museums worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: photographing flat artwork mounted for capture. A painting and a mounted layout board are the same object class (large flat 2D artwork); focus, framing and colour fidelity demands exceed those of a layout review print.

sources.title: 3D PhotoBench 180 - Product Photography Studio
sources.claim: An enclosed automated photography bench holds a 3D object on a turntable while software drives camera, lighting and rotation through a stored capture workflow, producing e-commerce-grade stills and 360 sets after the object is placed inside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated product photography. A package dummy or display comp is the same object class and size as the products these benches shoot, and the deliverable (well-lit multi-angle images for presentation) is the same.

sources.title: This Automated Photo Studio Shoots Video and Stills Without a Photographer
sources.claim: A 'robotic studio' machine automates lighting, camera and capture so that finished stills and video are produced on set without a photographer; the vendor's machines are used by hundreds of retail brands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated studio photography of physical goods. Same skill being replaced (exposure, lighting and framing decisions of a studio photographer) on objects presented to a purpose-built capture machine.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot navigates a working grocery store on its own and photographs shelf displays aisle by aisle; deployed across 17 store locations after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-facility image capture of merchandising displays - comparable to photographing an installed retail display, though the imagery is analytics-grade rather than composed for a client.

sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A legged robot runs autonomous inspection rounds through human industrial facilities, positioning itself at recorded waypoints and capturing visual imagery of specified flat targets such as gauges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation to a target inside a human facility and capture of an in-focus, correctly exposed image of a flat target good enough for machine reading - the capture half of photographing an installed graphic.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan Autonomous Drone Inspection
sources.claim: A commercial drone autonomously plans and flies its own capture pattern over a structure, delivering complete high-resolution imagery of its surfaces in outdoor, unstructured settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous documentation photography of large installed structures outdoors. A billboard, mural or building sign is the same class of large flat installed surface, and sub-millimetre-per-pixel coverage exceeds what a client record print needs.
