tasks.label: Inspect construction work on site to ensure its adherence to the design plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-construction site visit on a commercial fit-out (office, retail, clinic, restaurant) at the framing/rough-in stage: walk the floor with drawings, verify partition locations, door and opening positions, soffit and ceiling heights, niche/blocking and device locations against the design plans, measure with tape/laser, photograph, and issue a field observation report listing deviations. Active site with trades working, dust, temporary lighting, changing obstacles.

Finish-stage walkthrough and punch list on a commercial project: check paint color/sheen and workmanship, tile layout and grout lines, flooring transitions, millwork reveals and joinery, hardware and fixture alignment, lighting trim and lamp color, comparing installed work against drawings and approved samples; open doors/drawers, sight down surfaces, tag defects and produce a punch list for the contractor.

Residential renovation or custom-home site visit in a private house (partly occupied or gutted): confirm the built work matches the design drawings — cabinetry and appliance clearances, trim profiles, tile setting, plumbing/lighting locations — over cluttered floors, stairs, and unfinished spaces, and communicate corrections to the builder.

FF&E delivery and installation inspection near project close-out: verify furniture, casegoods, window treatments and accessories are the specified items, placed and oriented per the furniture plan, correctly assembled, and free of damage; log discrepancies and damaged pieces for replacement.

On-site mock-up or material sample review: inspect a mock-up room, wall assembly or finish sample installed at the jobsite (tile setting pattern, paint drawdown, stone slab, wallcovering seam) against the approved sample and specification under site lighting, then approve or reject.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous lidar-equipped ground robots scan active construction sites daily and check whether elements have been installed correctly relative to the design.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: verifying that work built on an active site conforms to the design model, which is the core of the interior designer's rough-in adherence check (positions, dimensions, presence of specified elements).

sources.title: NEWS: Doxel uses reality capture and AI to boost construction productivity - AEC Magazine
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous robots monitor sites indoors and outdoors with lidar ... and the system assesses the quality of installed work ... how much has been installed correctly.
sources.transferJustification: Automated as-built-versus-design conformance assessment indoors on live sites transfers to the designer's inspection of whether construction adheres to the plans.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Trimble X7 laser scanner (Autowalk, Enhanced Autonomy Package)
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot carrying a Trimble X7 scanner runs unattended Autowalk missions on live jobsites; the scans are superimposed on the BIM model and assessed for deviations from design.
sources.transferJustification: Scan-to-BIM deviation checking on an occupied construction site is the mechanized equivalent of walking the job with drawings to confirm the built geometry matches the design.

sources.system: DroneDeploy Robotics with Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Turner Uses Robots to Cut Inspection Time Over 95 Percent | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Turner Construction runs Spot autonomously overnight on active data-center jobsites for daily inspection captures and 360 walkthroughs, cutting inspection time by over 95%.
sources.transferJustification: Production deployment of autonomous inspection walkthroughs on real construction sites establishes that the E3 site environment itself is navigable and the inspection round can be completed unattended.

sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: FieldAI foundation models let Spot execute inspection and monitoring missions on constantly changing construction sites without prior maps or predefined routes, without frequent resets.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates autonomous mobility and inspection-round execution in the unstructured, changing jobsite conditions that an interior designer's site inspection occurs in.

sources.system: ZEISS ScanBox (ATOS sensors, Virtual Measuring Room)
sources.title: ZEISS ScanBox | Optical 3D Measuring & Inspection Technology
sources.claim: ZEISS ScanBox is a commercial robot-controlled optical inspection cell that automatically measures fixtured parts and assemblies and flags deviations by full-field 3D comparison to the CAD model, with automated part loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated conformance inspection of a workpiece against its design model. When the built element (casework, panel, pod, furniture piece) is fixtured and presented to the cell, the geometric adherence-to-design judgment the designer makes is performed automatically at finer precision.

sources.system: ISRA VISION robot-guided paint inspection (paint shop solutions)
sources.title: INSPECTION SOLUTIONS FOR THE PAINT SHOP | ISRA VISION
sources.claim: ISRA VISION's paint-shop systems use robot-guided sensors to inspect painted parts fully automatically, detecting fine surface defects and judging them objectively against OEM appearance specifications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated appearance/finish-defect inspection of coated surfaces against a specification, i.e. the same class of judgment (color, sheen, blemishes, surface flaws) the designer makes on finishes — but only with the workpiece fixtured and presented in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Arrange properties, furniture, merchandise, backdrops, or other accessories, as shown in prepared sketches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Packaged/rigid merchandise sets on a retail sales floor: displayer works from a planogram or sketch to build or refresh a shelf set, endcap or promotional display — opens cartons, assembles the display unit, positions multiple SKUs, faces product and adds header cards, price signage and props, working around shoppers and staff.

Apparel and soft-goods interior presentation in a specialty or department store: per the visual sketch, folds and stacks garments on tables, sizes and faces hanging garments on racks, layers accessories and props into a table vignette, adjusting drape and alignment to brand standard.

Window display installation: works inside a store window platform to install backdrop panels and floor covering, dress and pose mannequins with garments and accessories, hang props, signage and suspended elements, and aim lighting to match the prepared sketch.

Trade show / exhibition booth setup on a convention hall floor during move-in: erects backwall and fabric graphics, places furniture, counters and shelving to the design drawing, unpacks crates and arranges product samples and literature, amid forklifts, crates and other crews.

Large seasonal/holiday installations in malls and department stores (heavy props, tree and scenic elements, ladder work and overhead rigging) and furniture/home showroom room settings styled with rugs, lamps, cushions and accessories per sketch.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks beverage display shelves to the store planogram in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, running on a rail with remote operators taking over only on failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: planogram-driven placement of merchandise into a display case in a store. It shows autonomous placement of packaged goods into prescribed display positions, but only for bottles and cans on a fixed rail, with no cartons, fixtures, props or signage.

sources.system: Six-axis robotic display building/filling cell (five-robot installation at Number1)

sources.claim: Robotic cells commercially build, fill and stack retail promotional displays (box pallets and tray displays) to a defined pattern inside a fenced end-of-line packaging cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and filling retail promotional display units to a prescribed pattern. Same objects (packaged retail merchandise) and same output (a merchandising display arranged to a specified layout), performed with the work fixtured and conveyed to the robot.

sources.system: PKR Gantry Robotic Packer / modular pick-and-place case packing cell
sources.title: Tray Packer | Top Load Robotic Case & Tray Packing
sources.claim: Commercial gantry/delta pick-and-place cells load retail merchandise into retail display trays and cases in a prescribed arrangement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing retail merchandise into display trays to a set pattern; comparable objects and placement precision to arranging packaged product in a display, with product presented by conveyor in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Galbot brings in $300M to scale mobile manipulator deployments - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Galbot's G1 wheeled mobile manipulator operates autonomously in unmanned retail stores and pharmacies in China, locating, grasping and placing packaged goods on store shelving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store grasping and placing of varied retail packaged goods. It establishes store-floor manipulation of merchandise, but the demonstrated work is retrieval/replenishment of individual items, not composing a display from a sketch.

sources.title: Accenture Invests in Sanctuary AI to Bring AI-Powered, Humanoid Robotics to Work Alongside Humans
sources.claim: Sanctuary AI's Phoenix humanoid performed retail merchandising-adjacent tasks (picking, packing, tagging, folding) during a week-long pilot in a Mark's clothing store, in a piloted deployment whose autonomy is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store apparel handling and folding. Autonomy is not established (Sanctuary's trials rely on human pilots), so it cannot support a positive judgment for apparel display work.

sources.title: Helix Learns to Fold Laundry
sources.claim: Figure's Helix model folded towels fully autonomously, an in-house demonstration of deformable-textile manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating deformable textiles, the core difficulty in apparel display and mannequin dressing. It is a company-facility demonstration on plain towels, well short of building a garment presentation to visual-merchandising standard.

sources.developer: Personal Robotics Laboratory, Imperial College London
sources.title: A robot that can put a surgical gown on a supine mannequin
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing of a mannequin remains laboratory research, achieving only partial dressing with a gown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dressing a mannequin. It shows the state of the art is a lab demonstration of partial gowning, not styled dressing and posing of display mannequins at worker quality.

tasks.label: Change or rotate window displays, interior display areas, or signage to reflect changes in inventory or promotion.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/department store window changeover: strip the outgoing window (remove mannequins, props, backdrop, vinyl lettering), install new backdrop and flooring, dress and pose 2-6 mannequins in the new season's garments (pinning, steaming, accessorizing), place props, aim lights, add window graphics; done partly on ladders in a raised, glazed window box, often overnight before store opening.

Full interior feature/end-cap/table reset in a chain retailer: pull the outgoing promotion off the fixture, move or re-pitch shelves, risers and grid/slatwall hardware, unpack and build the new arrangement of mixed merchandise (boxed goods, hanging garments, folded stacks, seasonal items) to a planogram or visual guide, then mount the header sign and shelf strips.

Merchandise refresh on existing standard shelving or a cooler/gondola to reflect new inventory: the fixture stays as-is and the worker swaps which uniform packaged products fill it, replenishes and faces the rows to the planogram in a convenience, grocery or club store during trading hours.

Promotional signage and graphics swap across a store: pull expired sign faces from shelf-edge holders, sign arms, easels and framed light boxes; insert new printed cards and posters; hang ceiling/wall banners on hardware; apply and squeegee window clings and floor decals; verify signs match current promotional pricing.

Trade show booth or wholesale showroom rotation: reconfigure product on booth shelving/pedestals between show days or market cycles, swap graphics panels and product samples, restage samples for new lines in an exhibit hall or showroom during move-in hours.

Independent boutique, pop-up or small specialty shop display change: freelance or owner-run visual work in a space taken as found — improvised fixtures, tight cluttered floor and back room, one-off props, seasonal decor, sidewalk sandwich boards and sidewalk merchandise racks, no two sites alike.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: TX SCARA is a rail-mounted robot deployed in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores that autonomously replenishes and faces bottled and canned beverages on the refrigerated display shelves, operating almost entirely on its own AI with rare remote intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf replenishment. It transfers to the narrow display-refresh variant of this task — same objects (uniform packaged goods), same precision requirement (planogram facings on standard store shelving), same environment (a retail sales-floor display case). It does not transfer to prop, mannequin, fixture or signage work, which TX SCARA never touches.

sources.title: Galbot brings in $300M to scale mobile manipulator deployments
sources.claim: Galbot's G1 wheeled mobile manipulator runs autonomous retail stores in over 30 Chinese cities, picking packaged goods from shelves and handling inventory/replenishment without remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store pick-and-place and shelf replenishment of packaged retail goods. Transfers to keeping a standard product display filled and faced; the store shelving and product types match. It does not evidence restaging a display, moving fixtures, dressing mannequins or changing signage.

sources.system: "From Pixels to Shelf" autonomous stocking system (Hello Robot Stretch 3)
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: An integrated mobile-manipulator system (Hello Robot Stretch 3 with ROS2 perception and behavior-tree planning) autonomously stocked supermarket shelves in replicated supermarket conditions with over 98% pick-and-place success across 724 events, though the authors state performance remains inferior to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supermarket shelf stocking. Supports placing standard packaged products onto store shelving in a replicated (purpose-arranged) supermarket setting; the same paper reports the system is still below human workers, and it demonstrates nothing about fixtures, props, garments or signage.

sources.title: Tesco sends shelf-scanning robots into supermarket aisles
sources.claim: The retail-floor robots actually deployed at scale in supermarkets are sensing-only: Simbe's Tally autonomously roams aisles detecting empty shelves, misplaced products and ..., but performs no manipulation of merchandise or signage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store shelf and price-sign auditing. It establishes that the mainstream deployed retail-floor robot class only inspects; it flags wrong signage rather than changing it, so it cannot substantiate completion of display or signage changes.

sources.title: Sanctuary AI deploys first humanoid general-purpose robot commercially
sources.claim: A general-purpose humanoid was piloted in a real Mark's (Canadian Tire) store performing 110 retail tasks including picking, packing, tagging, labeling and folding, but only in a week-long piloted trial whose control mode is not established as autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general retail store floor work (tagging, folding, picking). It is the closest thing to in-store visual-merchandising manipulation, but autonomy is unestablished, so it is treated as teleoperated and supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Place prices or descriptive signs on backdrops, fixtures, merchandise, or floor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Grocery/big-box sales floor: inserting printed price and promo signs into shelf-edge rails, clip-on holders and channel strips down a set of aisles, matching each sign to the right facing while shoppers pass by.

Apparel/department store: affixing price and descriptive signage to floor fixtures — sign holders on four-way racks, table-top card frames, mannequin platform placards, hanging sign frames above fixtures — with varied clips, stems, frames and adhesive.

Window or feature display: adhering price cards, vinyl lettering, or printed graphics to backdrops, glass and props inside a cramped window box or on an elevated display platform, aligning to the display composition.
Sales floor flooring: applying adhesive floor decals/aisle direction and promo graphics to tile, polished concrete or carpet, squeegeeing out bubbles and aligning to aisle geometry.
Trade-show or exhibition booth: placing descriptive placards, spec cards and price signs on booth fixtures, pedestals and product samples during build-out in a convention hall.
Small-format/specialty retail: placing small price cards, tent cards and tags directly on individual merchandise in glass cases and tabletop displays (jewelry, bakery, gift).

sources.title: Robot Labeler | TOPPAN Infomedia Inc.
sources.claim: TOPPAN's Robot Labeler is a commercial in-line cell in which a multi-axis robot arm, guided by five cameras, prints and applies labels to taught surfaces and positions of products/packages moving on a conveyor, with automatic inspection of placement and printing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: printed price/identification label application to merchandise and packaging. Same physical act as placing a price sign on merchandise — pick a printed sign and place it at a designated position — with camera-verified placement accuracy exceeding retail sign-placement tolerance, in a fixtured conveyor cell (E1).

sources.title: Robotic Label Applicator | Signode
sources.claim: Signode's robotic label applicator picks printed labels from a label printer and applies them to the correct position on the workpiece, deciding placement per part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pick-and-place of a freshly printed sign onto a presented surface. This is the core motion of placing a price/descriptive sign on a fixture or backdrop, performed unattended in a guarded industrial cell.

sources.system: REA LABEL DS print-and-apply with robot arm
sources.title: Automatic labeling: easier, faster, more reliable
sources.claim: REA JET's print-and-apply system prints a label and a robot arm picks it with a vacuum plate and places it on the waiting pallet, operating unattended alongside logistics traffic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated placement of a printed paper sign onto a large presented object. Comparable object (printed label/sign), comparable precision, and it establishes that printing the right sign and affixing it is fully automated at E1.

sources.system: Automated Leaflet Inserter with Batch Data Printer & Vision Inspection
sources.title: Automated Leaflet Inserter with Vision Inspection | Tekpak
sources.claim: Tekpak's automated leaflet inserter takes pre-folded printed leaflets from a vertical magazine and inserts them into cartons at high speed, with camera vision verifying leaflet presence and printed content and rejecting faulty units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine insertion of a printed card/sheet from a magazine into a slot. This matches inserting a printed price card into a shelf-edge rail or acrylic sign holder when holder and card are presented fixtured (E1), including vision verification that the right card is present.

sources.title: Lionel: Autonomous Floor Marking Robot | August Robotics
sources.claim: August Robotics' Lionel autonomously sprays layout marks on exhibition hall floors, including booth corner marks and booth labels/numbers, at ±5 mm precision, navigating around people and working on concrete, carpet and tile.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing descriptive markings (booth numbers/labels) on the floor of a human work facility. Shows autonomous floor text marking at E2, but the output is sprayed temporary paint, not the adhesive vinyl decals/signs the retail floor instance requires.

sources.title: Messukeskus Cuts Marking Time with Lionel — August Robotics case study
sources.claim: Messukeskus, Finland's largest exhibition and ... used Lionel since 2023 to mark event floor layouts; three robots complete the hall with no staff on site during operation, monitored remotely.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor layout/marking work in an institution-controlled exhibition hall (E2), establishing that mobile robots operate unattended in such venues; it does not, however, place physical signs on fixtures or merchandise.

sources.title: The Robot That Solves the Wrong Price Label Problem on Store Shelves | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: ERIS (branded MARCEL in Carrefour stores) is an in-store retail robot that scans every shelf label, compares prices with the correct ones ...; it has no manipulator and does not affix labels to the shelf.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art for shelf-price signage robots inside stores: they scan and print, while a human still places the sign. Supports the negative E2 judgments, not a positive one.

tasks.label: Maintain props, products, or mannequins, inspecting them for imperfections, doing touch-ups, cleaning up after customers, or applying preservative coatings as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine walk-through of the sales floor and window displays in an open retail store: visually inspecting mannequins, props, risers and display fixtures for chips, scuffs, fingerprints and dust; wiping and dusting them and the glass of display cases; flagging items needing repair. Store is open, shoppers and fixtures present, layout changes with each promotion.

Cleaning up after customers: restoring displays disturbed by shoppers - refolding and restacking garments on tables, re-hanging items, straightening shoes/handbags/product stacks, retrieving stray hangers, tags and trash, returning items to their display positions on the open floor during or after business hours.

Maintaining the styled look of dressed mannequins and forms: re-pinning and re-tucking garments that have shifted, straightening wigs, hats, scarves and jewellery, swapping out soiled, faded or torn garments and accessories on in-store or window mannequins.

Back-of-house / prop-shop repair and touch-up of damaged mannequins and props: sanding out scuffs and chips on fiberglass or plastic mannequin bodies, filling, spot-priming and repainting to match, blending and polishing the repair, retouching painted props, signage and set pieces before they go back on the floor.

Applying preservative and protective coatings and polish to props, set pieces and display fixtures: clear-coating or sealing painted and wood props, waxing or oiling wood display elements, applying anti-tarnish/protective coating to metal fixtures, spraying protectant on foliage or paper props, done in a back room, workshop or vendor booth staging area.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics autonomous finishing cells (ScanNSand / ScanNSpray family)
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics Unveils 100,000-Square-Foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics builds and commercially deploys autonomous robotic finishing cells whose AI plans the toolpaths and that sand, grind, polish, buff, spray, ... of diverse materials and geometries - the same operations required to inspect, sand, touch up, coat and polish a fiberglass mannequin or painted prop, but with the part brought into the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix surface finishing of manufactured parts. Mannequins and props are painted fiberglass/plastic shells of comparable size and curvature to the composite parts these cells finish, and the required operations (defect sanding, blending, polishing, coating) are the same, at cosmetic-finish precision.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics dual-arm autonomous sanding cell at BetterWay Products

It is the same activity as inspecting a mannequin or prop for imperfections and doing touch-ups - vision-based defect location plus abrasive spot repair and polish on a painted shell, to a customer-visible cosmetic standard.

Public sidewalk outside a street-front store: the trimmer steps outside to photograph the finished window display through the glass, dealing with reflections, daylight or night lighting, passersby, parked cars, and choosing a viewpoint across the street or from an angle.

Trade show or exhibition hall: after erecting the booth/exhibit, the displayer photographs the completed stand, graphics and product vignettes from several angles for the client's record and post-show report, during setup day in a convention center.

tasks.label: Dress mannequins for displays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-size standing mannequin in an apparel/department store window or floor display: undress the previous look, then dress the form in a complete outfit — bottoms pulled over legs and hips, top threaded over torso and arms (often requiring detaching/reattaching arms, hands, or splitting the torso), jacket layered, shoes and belt fitted — then clip or pin excess fabric at the back, steam out wrinkles, straighten collars/cuffs and set the pose to the visual directive.

Torso/bust and partial forms on the sales floor: pull a knit top, tee, dress or blouse over the form, work the neck/shoulder openings down, align seams and buttons to the front, tuck and pin the hem or back for a tailored look, and dress lower-body forms with jeans or shorts.

Back-of-house prep in the stockroom or visual merchandising workroom: assemble the mannequin on its stand, steam or de-tag garments, dress the fully-accessible form on a table or bench, then carry the dressed mannequin out to the floor. Space is controlled and the worker can lay the mannequin down or remove limbs freely.

Difficult garments and finishing effects: bridal/formalwear or gowns with trains and boning, layered outerwear, tailored suiting, swimwear/lingerie or delicate vintage pieces — requiring taping, pinning, padding, back-clipping and fabric shaping so the garment reads as a perfect fit on a non-standard body form.

On-site install at a trade show booth, seasonal pop-up, or window install for an outside client: mannequins dressed amid crates, tools and partially built fixtures, in a hall or space whose layout differs at every site, on a tight move-in schedule with other trades working around the display.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a manikin. It is the nearest analogue to dressing a display mannequin (same object class — a manikin — and deformable apparel), but the garment is a single loose back-opening gown on a supine manikin in a lab rig, with no undressing, layering, limb removal, pinning or wrinkle-free finishing, so it does not carry over to a merchandising-quality outfit.

sources.title: A robot that can put a surgical gown on a supine mannequin

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing. Cited to establish the boundary of the demonstration — partial dressing of one loose garment in a purpose-built lab scene — which is short of the whole instance of dressing a display mannequin in a complete, finished look.

It establishes the ceiling of general deformable-clothing skill — flat manipulation on a table — and contains no demonstration of threading garments onto a body form or finishing them for display.

Transfers to 'store... and maintain inventory records of props, products or display items' because the objects (cartons of merchandise and display goods), precision and record-keeping (WMS-tracked locations) are the same.

sources.system: Symbotic system at Walmart regional distribution centers
sources.title: Walmart plans to automate 25 distribution centers with Symbotic | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: In Walmart's Symbotic-equipped regional distribution centers, robotic arms depalletize cases, the warehouse management system assigns storage locations, and autonomous mobile robots deliver cases to those locations — a full receive-to-store-with-records loop inside a purpose-built structure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inbound receiving and put-away of retail merchandise cases. Same object class (boxed store merchandise and display stock) and same output (items stored in a known location with an inventory record).

sources.title: AutoStore ASRS | High-Density Storage & Retrieval by Kardex
sources.claim: AutoStore grids store goods in bins handled by autonomous robots, with every bin tracked in real time by software, providing automated storage plus continuously maintained inventory records.

sources.system: Sparck CVP Everest / CVP Impack automated packaging
sources.title: Sparck Technologies: CVP Everest Automated Packaging Solution - Material Handling 24/7
sources.claim: Sparck CVP auto-boxing machines automatically measure, construct, seal, weigh and ... a right-sized box around hard or soft single- or ... orders presented to the machine, integrating with the warehouse management system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fit-to-size packing of goods for shipment. Transfers to 'pack ... display items' for boxable props and merchandise: same object sizes, same accepted output (a sealed, labelled, record-generating carton).

sources.title: CMC Packaging Automation Unveils Revolutionary Solution: the CartonWrap-DUO ... | Logistics Management
sources.claim: CMC CartonWrap machines build right-sized cartons in-line around a wide range of item types, including apparel, electronics and books, without human packing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated e-commerce packing. Transfers to packing display merchandise and small props because the item mix (soft goods, rigid goods, mixed shapes) and the required output (protected, sealed, labelled package) match.

sources.system: KNAPP Pick-it-Easy Robot with Covariant Brain
sources.title: KNAPP and Covariant Partnership Advances AI Robotics for more Efficient Warehouses
sources.claim: The KNAPP Pick-it-Easy Robot running the Covariant Brain autonomously picks items of widely varying size, weight, shape and packaging out of storage totes and places them gently into target totes/order boxes in production warehouses (Obeta, McKesson).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-robot piece picking of heterogeneous SKUs. Transfers to handling assorted small props and merchandise into totes/boxes: comparable object variety, comparable gentleness/precision, items presented fixtured at a station.

sources.title: Reducing Inventory Cycle Counting Time with a Drone-Powered Monitoring Solution | SupplyChainBrain
sources.claim: Gather AI drones fly autonomously through existing, unmodified warehouses to scan pallet locations and maintain inventory records, deployed at GEODIS, NFI, Barrett, AAFES and others with reported large accuracy gains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Transfers to 'maintain inventory records of props, products or display items' — same activity (locate, count, reconcile stock against the record system) on racked stock in a human-run facility.

sources.title: BJ's to roll out inventory robots chainwide | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously scans store aisles chainwide (e.g., BJ's Wholesale, 244 clubs; Schnucks) capturing shelf images to track stock levels and reconcile them with the inventory system inside ordinary retail stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-store stock auditing. Transfers to maintaining inventory records of products and display stock in a retail setting: same items, same record output, same institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch operates autonomously in existing DHL warehouses and trailers, unloading roughly 700 cases per hour; 10 units across three countries as of June 2025 with a 1,000-unit expansion agreement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: case handling in unmodified warehouses. Shows E2-tier autonomous box handling exists, but only for uniform cases at a trailer/conveyor interface — a sub-step, not whole pack-store-record work.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading/unloading long limp-to-rigid workpieces onto carriers and racks in a fixtured cell. It transfers to the E1 counterfactual of this task — mounting and hanging decorative elements onto a fixtured structure presented to the robot — because the objects are comparable in size and weight and the placement tolerances are similar.

sources.system: Robotic pick-and-place preforming cells (hand-like grippers with robot-mounted cameras)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and precise placement of large limp fabric sheets onto fixtured tooling. sources.system: FulcrumAir LineFly / Mini LineFly with heavy-lift drone
sources.developer: FulcrumAir (with PLP); deployed for American Transmission Co.

sources.claim: A fully autonomous LineFly robot carried by a heavy-lift drone installed more than 450 bird-flight diverters on live high-voltage transmission lines in Wisconsin — autonomous installation of devices onto overhead infrastructure in an uncontrolled outdoor setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a hanging visual device to overhead outdoor infrastructure. sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot performs semi-autonomous overhead ceiling drilling for MEP and interior finishing on commercial construction sites: an operator drives it between positions by remote control, after which it drills and marks holes automatically from BIM data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: creating overhead mounting points in occupied buildings. It covers only the drilling sub-step (no anchor setting, no hanging of a decoration) and requires an operator to reposition it, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion at E2 or E3.

Small independent store with basic tools: improvised, largely freehand cutting of decorative shapes from scrap/reclaimed cartons and offcuts on a back-office table or the sales floor, no drawings or standard stock.

Finished presentation model of a play, musical or film/TV set built in a design studio or art-department model shop: painted and textured walls, scale furniture, translucent windows, figures, mounted in a scaled stage frame, delivered to director, DP and technical director.

Exhibit designer builds a scale model of a museum gallery or trade-show booth in the firm's model shop: partition walls, vitrines, graphic panels, scale figures, showing circulation and sightlines for client approval.

Miniature set built to be filmed for backgrounds or special effects: a 1:12-1:24 (or larger 'bigature') building, street or environment with weathered paint, scale texture, mixed materials, practical lighting and mechanical/pyro rigs, built over weeks in a VFX model shop and shot on camera.

Technical/working scale model for the production shop: shows scenery mechanics - tracked wagons, turntable, flown units, deck traps - with parts that actually move, used to check practicality in production meetings at the scene shop or design office.

Set and exhibit presentation models are the same class of object at the same scales (painted wall surfaces, furniture, transparent glazing, figures), so colour-and-texture printing that removes hand painting carries over to painted set and booth models.

tasks.label: Inspect installed exhibits for conformance to specifications and satisfactory operation of special-effects components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Museum/science-center exhibit designer walks a newly installed permanent gallery near completion: compares casework, mounts, graphic panels, finishes, colors, label placement and lighting focus/levels against approved drawings and specs; activates each interactive, AV/media and motion element to confirm it runs correctly; dictates a punch list for the fabricator/AV integrator. Institution-controlled building, but ladders, clutter and trades still present.

Trade-show/corporate exhibit designer inspects a booth erected on a convention-center floor hours before opening: verifies structure, graphics, hanging sign, product mounts and finishes match the design package; tests lighting, video walls, kinetic/atmospheric effects and demo devices; flags and directs fixes under severe time pressure amid other crews.

Theatre set designer attends load-in/technical rehearsal: checks built scenery, paint treatments, textures and sightlines from the house against the design and paint elevations; watches automated scenery moves, traps, fly cues, fog/haze and pyro/practical effects run through cues; notes deficiencies for the shop and technical director.

Film/TV set designer or art director inspects a set on a soundstage or backlot before shooting: confirms the build matches drafting and construction specs (wall positions, wild walls, breakaways, dressing, aging) and verifies practical/special-effects rigs (rain, smoke, gags, practical lighting) operate safely and read correctly on camera.

Themed-entertainment/immersive attraction designer inspects a show set during installation and testing: animatronics, show-control cues, projection-mapping alignment, scenic finish under show lighting, timed effect sequences; rides or walks the scene repeatedly with programmers to verify the installed work matches design intent.

Focused re-inspection of one delivered or installed component or effect device after fabrication or repair: dimensional and finish check of the unit against CAD/spec plus a functional run-through of its controls (buttons, sensors, motor cycle, timing) to confirm it operates per specification before sign-off.

sources.system: Spot (Spot CAM+IR, FLIR MUVE C360 payloads) with Orbit
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous, dock-based inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream gas plant, reading gauges, capturing thermal images and detecting anomalies including a combustible-gas leak — routine condition checks of standardized industrial assets in a structured facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine inspection verifying installed equipment is in satisfactory operating condition. Transfer is only partial — checks are pre-scripted checkpoints on standardized industrial assets with numeric thresholds, not open-ended conformance judgment on one-off exhibit builds or theatrical effects.

sources.system: Spot with Trimble X7 laser scanner payload
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot runs programmed Autowalk scanning missions on live construction sites without operator intervention; customers superimpose the laser scans on the BIM model to compare as-built work with the design and spot deviations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying installed construction work conforms to the design model. Transfer is partial: it captures geometry for human review of deviations and covers none of the finish/colour/graphic conformance or functional testing of special-effects components that exhibit inspection requires.

sources.title: Top 10: AI Tools in Construction | Construction Digital
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous robot scans live construction sites and compares LiDAR data against the BIM ... between installed components and the design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built versus as-designed conformance checking of installed work. It substantiates geometric deviation reporting only; it does not exercise or evaluate powered show components, finishes or design intent.

sources.title: Simbe Robotics Unveils Tally
sources.claim: Tally autonomously scans store shelves during normal trading hours to audit merchandise against the store's planogram, reporting out-of-stocks, misplaced items and pricing errors; deployed at scale in grocery, big-box and hardware chains through 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously auditing a physical installation against a specification document (the planogram) inside a structured human facility. Transfer is limited to catalogued, repeating products and 2D placement rules, not bespoke one-off objects, finishes or powered effects.

sources.system: SPEA push button and keyboard automatic test equipment
sources.title: Push Button and Keyboard Automatic Test | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA automatic test equipment uses robotic actuators that press every key or button at programmed force and speed to verify correct operation, with vision units checking correct key positioning, in a fixtured purpose-built test station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: functional verification that a delivered device's controls operate to specification, with comparable actuation and pass/fail criteria to bench-checking an interactive or special-effects module presented in a fixture.

sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT automates touch, button and ... of smart devices and appliances at 0.05 mm precision, verifying device functions against a test specification in a fixtured desktop cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional acceptance testing of a delivered unit's controls and responses — equivalent to confirming an interactive or effect component operates satisfactorily when presented fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: VisionGauge Digital Optical Comparator (CAD Auto-Align, CAD Auto Pass/Fail)
sources.title: Digital Optical Comparators | Automated Optical Inspection Tools | VISIONx
sources.claim: VisionGauge digital optical comparators automatically compare manufactured parts to their CAD ... and issue pass/fail conformance results without operator input, in an enclosed bench measurement station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dimensional conformance-to-specification inspection of a fabricated part against its design file — the geometric half of checking a delivered exhibit component against spec when the work is brought to the machine.

instances.label: Seasonal or promotional retail window display for a department store or boutique: designer takes a merchandising brief, develops a concept, sources and fabricates props, backdrops and signage, then dresses the storefront window on site — positioning mannequins and garments, hanging elements from the ceiling grid, aiming spotlights, working around glass, existing fixtures and store hours.

Trade show / corporate event exhibit: designer produces booth graphics, modular walls, custom hero props and product plinths, ships them, then installs and dresses the stand on a convention-center show floor during a short move-in window, adjusting fit to the actual booth footprint, rigging, power and neighboring stands.

Interior exhibit or display in a museum, visitor center or corporate lobby: design and produce display cases, object mounts, wall graphics and text panels; install in the gallery, level and align casework, mount fragile artifacts, and adjust lighting to curatorial approval.

Outdoor event decoration on streets or fairgrounds: design and produce banners, themed archways, entrance features, stage dressing and directional signage for a festival, parade or county fair; install outdoors on varied ground and street furniture, weather-proof and ballast elements, with public traffic present.

Themed interior décor package for a hospitality or entertainment venue (hotel lobby, casino, restaurant chain, seasonal theme-park overlay): design the scheme, fabricate scenic elements in a shop, then install and finish on site over a few nights.

Bespoke shop production of display elements to the designer's own drawings: cutting, carving, printing, assembling, painting and finishing props, letters, panels and signage in a scenic/display fabrication shop for delivery to a client, including touch-up and quality sign-off.

sources.system: KUKA KR QUANTEC ultra (KR 210 R3100) milling robot at Art Department Studio Babelsberg
sources.title: Automated CNC milling of sculptures in the film studio | KUKA Global
sources.claim: A KUKA KR 210 R3100 milling robot at Art Department Studio Babelsberg autonomously mills large hard-foam sculptures and props from human-made CAD/CAM models inside a dedicated robotic milling cell, switching tools by itself; the design, finishing, coating and installation of the props remain human work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scenic/prop fabrication. It carves the same rigid-foam display and scenic elements a designer would have made, so it substantiates one production sub-step at E1, but the robot receives a finished human CAD model and does not conceive the design, assemble multi-material displays, or install them on site.

sources.system: Agfa Max Bots / Durst P5 Robotics / Zund robotic loading systems
sources.title: The Rise of Robotics: Automating Wide Format Print Production | FESPA
sources.claim: Cobots from Agfa (Max Bots), Durst (P5 Robotics) and Zund are commercially used in wide-format print factories to load and unload flatbed presses and cutting tables that produce signage, POP and display graphics; the robots handle repetitive board handling inside fixed cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production of printed display graphics. It covers the flat-graphics production step of window/exhibit display materials in a purpose-built print cell, but only material handling around a press — not designing the display, building three-dimensional elements, or installing them in a window, booth or street.

sources.title: Large-format 3D printing for visual communications | Massivit
sources.claim: Massivit large-format gel-dispensing 3D printers are used commercially by print service providers such as Colorzenith to produce three-dimensional retail POP, window-display and dimensional billboard elements from supplied digital files.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabrication of three-dimensional display props. The printer outputs the same class of window-display and event props this task produces, substantiating an E1 fabrication sub-step, but it prints a supplied model and performs no concept design, finishing/painting decisions, assembly or on-site installation.

tasks.label: Attend auditions and casting calls to audition for roles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-person on-camera audition at a casting office or studio for a film/TV role: actor checks in, slates, performs prepared sides opposite a reader, takes one or two live adjustments from the casting director, and may return for a callback with producers.

Self-tape audition: actor sets up backdrop, lighting and phone/camera at home or a rented self-tape space, performs sides with an off-camera reader over multiple takes, and submits the best take by a same-day or next-day deadline.

Theatre audition or callback: actor performs a monologue or cold read on stage or in a rehearsal hall before a director and stage manager; for musicals, sings 16-32 bars with an accompanist and participates in a dance/movement call.

Commercial, print, or background casting call at a casting facility: large open call, slate to camera, improvised business with a product, physical comedy or group movement, wardrobe/look check, minimal or no script.

Voiceover, animation, or audiobook audition recorded in a professional or home booth: actor reads supplied copy in character, offers variations, and takes direction from an engineer or casting director over multiple takes.

sources.developer: Hiroshi Ishiguro Laboratories / Osaka University; producers Sam Khoze, Bondit Capital Media
sources.title: Hollywood just cast a robot actress in a $70 million movie
sources.claim: The best-known 'robot actor' case is Erica, an android cast in the sci-fi film 'b'; she was cast by producers rather than through any audition process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing a role on camera. It is the closest documented case of a robot receiving an acting role; it shows the machine did not audition, so it cannot substantiate autonomous auditioning.

sources.developer: Hiroshi Ishiguro / Kohei Ogawa, with producer Sam Khoze
sources.title: AI robot 'Erica' will star in $70 million sci-fi movie 'b'
sources.claim: Erica's screen 'acting' was produced by human operators coaching and hand-tuning her motions and simulated emotions in one-on-one sessions, not by the robot autonomously interpreting a script.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering a dramatic performance. An audition requires generating an interpretation on the spot and adjusting to live redirection; this shows the performance was human-authored offline, so it does not transfer.

sources.developer: Oriza Hirata (Seinendan) and Hiroshi Ishiguro Laboratory, Osaka University / ATR
sources.title: Creation and Staging of Android Theatre "Sayonara" towards Developing Highly Human-Like Robots
sources.claim: In android theatre productions such as 'Sayonara', the robot's stage performance is pre-recorded human motion data replayed by an operator during the show, i.e., scripted playback rather than autonomous acting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live stage performance of a scripted role, the skill an audition samples. Because motion is authored by human actors and replayed by an operator, it cannot support autonomous audition performance.

tasks.label: Work closely with directors, other actors, and playwrights to find the interpretation most suited to the role.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Table work / read-through early in a stage production: the actor sits with the director, fellow cast, and sometimes the playwright, discusses the character's objectives, backstory, and line intentions, asks and answers questions about the text, and annotates the script with agreed interpretive choices.

Rehearsal-room scene work in a theater: the actor proposes and tries interpretive choices, receives and discusses the director's notes and scene partners' reactions, and negotiates a shared reading of the scene's tone, relationships, and beats.

Film or television set between takes: the actor confers briefly with the director (and sometimes the writer or showrunner) about tone, pacing, subtext, and adjustments, agreeing what to change for the next take.

New-play or new-script development workshop: the actor works with the playwright on how lines land, flags text that does not play, and discusses rewrites and interpretive intent with the writer and director.

Pre-production or remote conferences: callbacks, character meetings, and video calls with the director, casting, or writers to discuss the role's interpretation, accent, arc, and relationship to other characters before rehearsal begins.

tasks.label: Portray and interpret roles, using speech, gestures, and body movements, to entertain, inform, or instruct radio, film, television, or live audiences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-camera scene work for film or scripted television, on a soundstage or a production-controlled location: the actor delivers scripted dialogue in character, hits marks, sustains emotional beats and continuity across many takes, reacts to scene partners, handles props and wardrobe, and adjusts the interpretation on the director's notes.

A role in a live stage play or musical before a paying audience (regional theatre, touring house, or Broadway/Off-Broadway), performed eight times a week: two hours in character, projected voice, blocking and timing coordinated with a live cast, and real-time adaptation to audience response, missed cues and technical mishaps.

Studio voice work: animation, radio drama, audiobook narration, ADR/looping, and radio spots recorded in a booth, where the whole role is carried by vocal interpretation — accent, character voice, emotional shading — reshaped take by take on a director's or engineer's notes.

Commercial, corporate and instructional on-camera work: TV/web commercials, training and safety videos, industrials, and role-play scenarios (playing a customer, patient, employee) shot in studios, offices or rented locations, with simple naturalistic performance delivered fast to a client's approval.

Live interactive character work with the public: theme-park character and costumed meet-and-greet, immersive/interactive theatre, murder-mystery dinners, historical interpretation at museums and heritage sites, brand-ambassador character work at events — staying in character while improvising responses to unpredictable guests moving through the space.

A fixed, repeated, fully pre-scripted performance in a dedicated show venue: an attraction theatre show or pre-show character presentation delivered identically several times an hour, or a choreographed set piece in a variety/live-broadcast show, with no improvisation and no direct contact with the audience.

sources.developer: Hiroshi Ishiguro Laboratory, Osaka University / ATR
sources.title: Creation and Staging of Android Theatre "Sayonara" towards Developing Highly Human-Like Robots
sources.claim: Geminoid F, an android, was billed as an actress and played a leading role in the 2015 Japanese feature film 'Sayonara' and in the stage play of the same name; its stage/film performance is generated by tele-operation relaying a human professional actor's performance.

sources.title: Robot actor stuns London audiences in new play | GMA News Online
sources.claim: In the professional touring stage production 'Spillikin', an Engineered Arts RoboThespian played a role opposite human actors, but every line and movement was pre-programmed and triggered as cues from a laptop in the theatre control room.

sources.title: Robots at Exhibitions | Centrum Nauki Kopernik
sources.claim: A RoboThespian has been installed at the Copernicus Science Centre for over a decade, where it entertains visitors by reciting literary works and film ... and singing; its behaviour is selected and programmed through a touch panel rather than generated by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live presentational/character performance to museum visitors. Shows the deployed state of robot 'acting' — canned, operator-programmed routines rather than interpreted role portrayal.

sources.title: BDX Droids: Disney's Perfect Marriage of Creativity and Technological Achievement - D23
sources.claim: Disney's free-roaming BDX droids, which interact with guests in Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge, are driven by a backstage puppeteer; only balance and gait are learned autonomously.

sources.claim: Disney Research is still developing, at the research stage, a learned system that would let its character robots recreate operator-driven guest interactions autonomously; today the interaction data is collected by a human operating the robot.

sources.title: 'Walt Disney – A Magical Life' Audio Animatronic | blooloop

sources.title: Kung fu, somersaults and scale: Unitree eyes 20,000-robot output in 2026 after gala | SCMP
sources.claim: At the 2026 Spring Festival Gala, Unitree's G1 humanoids performed a martial-arts routine on the live broadcast stage that Unitree and press describe as fully autonomous (no teleoperation), alongside H2 robots doing somersaults and high-speed running.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering a choreographed physical performance to entertain a live and broadcast audience. Transfers to the movement/staging component of a fixed set-piece performance, though it involves no spoken role portrayal.
