sources.system: Shibuya-lab violin-playing robot (RL bowing motion generation)
sources.title: Motion-generation system for violin-playing robot using reinforcement learning...
sources.claim: Violin-playing robots remain a research goal: work as of late 2024 is still learning bowing parameters and target sound pressure, with expressive automatic performance stated as an aim rather than an achievement.

sources.title: Live Hong Kong Concert Highlights How Creepy Humanoid Robots Really Are - SlashGear
sources.claim: The most prominent robot 'singer' appearance, Hanson Robotics' Sophia performing three songs with an orchestra at a Hong Kong Baptist University gala, produced synthesized audio rather than mechanically generated vocal sound and was received as a novelty, not as a substitute for a vocalist.

tasks.label: Sight-read musical parts during rehearsals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Orchestral, pit, or concert-band instrumentalist (violin, cello, clarinet, trumpet, percussion, etc.) sight-reading newly distributed printed parts at a first rehearsal in a rehearsal hall, theater pit, or church sanctuary: playing at professional tone and intonation on first pass, following the conductor's beat, dynamics and cutoffs, and restarting from called rehearsal letters.

Choral or ensemble singer (church choir, community chorus, session backing vocalist) sight-reading a new vocal line at a weekly rehearsal room: finding pitches from the printed part, matching vowels, blend and dynamics with the section, and following the director's stops and verbal corrections.

Keyboardist/accompanist reading a straightforward new notated keyboard part straight through at a rehearsal (church anthem accompaniment, orchestral keyboard/continuo part, band chart), where the job is to render the written notes in time with the ensemble.

Rehearsal pianist/repetiteur for musical theater, opera, ballet or choir reading a new score at sight while making live adaptations: reducing an orchestral score, transposing on request, vamping, taking cuts and repeats, and responding to the director's spoken instructions.

Commercial/session musician (guitar, bass, horn section, strings) sight-reading charts on a recording date or run-through in a studio: unfamiliar notation and chord symbols read down once or twice, with style, feel, and immediate response to the contractor's or producer's changes.

Rock/pop/jazz gig band rehearsing in a garage, basement, or member's home from lead sheets and chord charts: reading down an unfamiliar tune once with the group, comping, and adjusting arrangement on the fly.

sources.system: Yamaha AI Music Ensemble Technology + Disklavier reproducing piano
sources.title: Yamaha's AI Technology Makes Possible Joint Performance of Sviatoslav Richter and Today's Members of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra
sources.claim: Yamaha's AI Music Ensemble Technology drives a Disklavier reproducing piano to play a piano part in real time with human chamber musicians; the professional ensemble rehearsed with the system before the concert at Sogakudo Concert Hall, Tokyo University of the Arts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing a supplied piano part in real time within a human ensemble, including rehearsals. A machine given the part in machine-readable form needs no practice, so first-pass rendering (the essence of sight-reading a keyboard part) reduces to this demonstrated real-time ensemble playing.

sources.title: Making the Impossible Possible - Yamaha Music Blog
sources.claim: The same Yamaha system autonomously analyzes a human player's gestures and sound ... predict upcoming notes and instructs the player piano accordingly, i.e., it follows the humans rather than being triggered step by step.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy (real-time score following of live human players) for the piano-part evidence above, which is the tempo-following demand of rehearsal sight-reading.

sources.system: 32-DoF humanoid piano-performance robot with vision-based music sheet reader
sources.title: Design and Control of a 32-DoF Robot for Music Performance Using AI and Motion Planning
sources.claim: A 32-DoF anthropomorphic piano-playing robot reads printed music notation with a camera and YOLOv8 symbol detection and plays the detected notes autonomously; the authors note limits in dynamic expressiveness and symbol generalization.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the reading half of sight-reading (notation to keystrokes without prior training on the piece) on a real keyboard, in a laboratory rig rather than a human rehearsal room.

sources.title: Musical-based interaction system for the Waseda Flutist Robot | Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: The most developed autonomous wind-instrument robot, Waseda's anthropomorphic flutist, plays at roughly intermediate human level and interacts with human musicians through audio-visual cues.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published capability for autonomously playing a notated wind part; cited to show the ceiling (intermediate level, laboratory setting) falls short of professional orchestral sight-reading.

sources.developer: Jacob Muhlrad / s-projects with Malmo Live Concert Hall
sources.title: Watch as a robot performs the cello with a symphony orchestra in a world first - Classic FM
sources.claim: A robot arm played a cello alongside a symphony orchestra in a concert hall in a piece written specifically for it; coverage describes a composed showcase, with no indication the robot read or followed parts autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest instance of a robot playing a bowed string part in a professional orchestral setting; cited to show it is a purpose-composed showcase, not first-pass reading of assigned parts.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Shimon | Center for Music Technology - Georgia Tech
sources.claim: Shimon is an autonomous improvising marimba robot that listens to human musicians and plays along with them in real time, including live shows with human jazz bands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing live with human musicians in a jam/rehearsal. It improvises on its own marimba rather than reading an assigned part on a band member's instrument, so it does not carry over to reading charts at a band rehearsal.

sources.system: Polaris and Oscar (Snobots humanoid band, unified ROS framework)
sources.developer: Lau, Anderson & Baltes, National Taiwan Normal University
sources.title: Integrating humanoid robots with human musicians for synchronized musical performances (PeerJ Computer Science)
sources.claim: A humanoid robot band (Polaris on a Wii Rock Band drum set, Robotis-OP3 keyboardist Oscar) synchronizes with human musicians in real time, with the drummer reading note symbols from a screen via a vision module.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robots reading notes and playing in time with human musicians; the instruments are toy/game controllers driven by small hobby servos, so the quality does not transfer to professional rehearsal parts.

tasks.label: Seek out and learn new music suitable for live performance or recording.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gigging cover/wedding/bar-band instrumentalist (guitar, keys, bass or drums) hunts for songs that will work for an upcoming setlist (streaming, client requests, other bands' sets), then woodsheds 5-15 new tunes at home or in a home studio: transcribing by ear or from charts, working out parts, form, key and endings until they can be played reliably at a gig.

Vocalist searches out new songs suited to their voice and audience (new releases, songbooks, demos sent by writers) and learns them at home or with an accompanist/coach: lyrics, melody, phrasing, key/arrangement changes, memorization, until performance- or session-ready.

Classical/orchestral or chamber instrumentalist receives newly programmed repertoire, obtains the parts/scores and reference recordings, and learns them in a practice room at the orchestra hall, conservatory or church before sectionals and rehearsals: fingerings, bowings, intonation, difficult passages, interpretive decisions.

Worship-team or school/community-ensemble musician receives a weekly setlist of new songs from the music director, sources charts/tracks, and learns their part on standard equipment in the church or school rehearsal room, adjusting keys and arrangements to the group.

Session or touring musician prepares unfamiliar material fast for a booked date: charts, demos or stems arrive from a producer/MD, and the player learns the parts to spec in a professional studio or rehearsal facility, ready to track or run the show within days.

sources.developer: USC Viterbi School of Engineering (Valero-Cuevas lab)
sources.title: A Robot Hand That Taught Itself to Play Piano Could Change the Future of Machines - USC Viterbi
sources.claim: USC's 'Musician Hand', a four-fingered tendon-driven robotic hand on a lab bench keyboard, autonomously learns to reproduce a short (~30-note) monophonic melody it has heard once, after two minutes of self-directed 'motor babbling'; it is a research prototype limited to simple single-line tunes rather than full performance repertoire.
sources.transferJustification: Learning a previously unheard tune by ear on a keyboard is the closest robotic analog to 'learn new music'; it does not transfer to the full task because the hand plays only short single-note melodies with four fingers on a fixtured keyboard, does not choose its own material, and cannot deliver a chorded, dynamically shaped, gig-ready song.

sources.developer: Purdue University (Sudhoff, Velmurugan, Liu, Zhao, Lu, Yun)
sources.title: From Score to Sound: An End-to-End MIDI-to-Motion Pipeline for Robotic Cello Performance
sources.claim: A UR5e arm fitted with a custom bow gripper and a cello on a fixed stand autonomously converts a MIDI score into bowing motions and performs previously unseen pieces, but only open-string (no left-hand fingering) renditions of beginner Suzuki-level repertoire in a lab rig.
sources.transferJustification: Sight-reading and rendering an unseen score is the acquisition step of 'learn new music'; it falls short of the task because the system plays open strings only (left-hand fingering explicitly excluded), covers beginner Suzuki pieces, and is evaluated against an intermediate amateur, not a working professional.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Four-Armed Marimba Robot Uses Deep Learning to Compose Its Own Music - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Shimon, a four-armed marimba robot, autonomously analyzes music and improvises with human performers on stage and has used deep learning to generate original melodies, but it generates or improvises material rather than seeking out and rehearsing assigned new repertoire to performance standard.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the most advanced autonomous robotic musician performing live; relevant because it shows machine music-making is limited to improvisation/generation on one percussion instrument, not to acquiring and rehearsing a named new piece to a bandleader's or conductor's standard.

sources.title: Robot Drummer: Learning Rhythmic Skills for Humanoid Drumming
sources.claim: Robot Drummer learns over thirty rock, metal and jazz songs on a humanoid drum kit with reinforcement learning, but the results are in simulation on a Unitree G1 model; transfer to real hardware is described as future work requiring sim-to-real training and a compliant stick interface.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task of learning new songs on an instrument, but simulation-only: no physical robot has performed these learned songs, so it cannot substantiate completion in any physical environment.

tasks.label: Listen to recordings to master pieces or to maintain and improve skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classical or orchestral musician studies reference recordings of a work before rehearsals — listening with score in hand at home or in a practice room, comparing tempi, phrasing, bowing/breathing and articulation choices across interpretations to prepare their part.

Popular, jazz, or commercial musician learns a set list by ear from streamed or downloaded tracks — looping and slowing passages, identifying chord changes and licks, and internalizing the arrangement before a gig or rehearsal.

Musician or singer reviews an audio/video recording of their own rehearsal or performance to diagnose intonation, rhythm, blend, diction, dynamics, or technical faults and decide what to work on next.

Student or continuing performer listens to a teacher's or coach's demonstration recording, or to rehearsal/accompaniment tracks supplied by a director, between lessons or calls to maintain technique and repertoire.
Session/recording artist auditions playback of takes in a studio control room or on headphones to judge which pass is usable and what to correct on the next pass.

tasks.label: Make or participate in recordings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vocalist records lead and backing vocals for a song in a professional recording studio: sings take after take into a large-diaphragm mic in an isolation booth, adjusting phrasing, pitch, dynamics and emotional delivery on the producer's direction, doubling and comping parts until an accepted vocal is captured.

Session instrumentalist (electric guitar, bass, drum kit, or horn) tracks parts in a commercial studio: reads a chart or learns the part by ear, plays to a click with the band or to a backing track, adjusts tone, feel and dynamics on verbal direction from the producer, and delivers usable takes within the booked session.

Pianist/keyboardist records a piano part on an acoustic grand in a studio or on a scoring stage: performs written repertoire or a scored cue with expressive phrasing, pedaling and dynamics, repeating takes to match the tempo map and interpretation notes.

Self-releasing musician records their own material in a home or project studio: sets up mics and interface in a spare room, sings and plays several instruments across overdubbed layers, punches in fixes, and iterates until satisfied with the tracks.

Orchestral, chamber, or choral musician participates in a group recording session on a film scoring stage, in a concert hall, or in a church: plays or sings a section part on strings, winds, brass, or voice while following a conductor and click, blending with the section over repeated takes.

A band or solo act's live performance at a club, theater, or festival is multitrack-recorded or broadcast for a live album or video: the musicians perform the full set on stage, singing and playing amplified instruments before an audience with no chance to redo takes.

sources.title: Singer-songwriter robot is heading out on tour - Futurity
sources.claim: Shimon, an autonomous four-armed marimba robot that improvises in real time with human musicians using deep learning, physically played on tracks released as the album 'Shimon Sings' alongside a band of human musicians.

sources.title: Shimon | Center for Music Technology - Georgia Tech

sources.title: Into Your Mind, by Shimon The Robot (Bandcamp)
sources.claim: On the released single 'Into Your Mind' from the album Shimon Sings, the robot improvised a response to a human guitarist's solo, i.e. an autonomous machine performance captured on a commercially released recording.

sources.system: Dear Glenn AI piano system (Disklavier-based player piano)

sources.claim: Yamaha's 'Dear Glenn' is an acoustic player piano whose keys are driven by machine actuation, with AI software generating the expressive performance data (touch, timing) for any score in Glenn Gould's style rather than replaying a human-entered sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live concert performance of complete piano repertoire on an acoustic grand, including a duet with pianist Francesco Tristano and a wind trio. Recording a piano part is the same physical act on the same instrument, captured by microphone, with retakes available.

sources.title: AI piano plays Bach just like legendary pianist Glenn Gould - Classic FM
sources.claim: The AI-driven acoustic piano gave full public concert performances of demanding repertoire (Bach's Goldberg Variations) in an ordinary concert setting at the Ars Electronica Festival, alongside human musicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: concert performance rather than a studio take; the physical act (expressive playing of a scored piece on an acoustic piano) and the acoustic output captured are the same as in a piano tracking session.

sources.claim: The Z-Machines robot band (robotic guitarist, bassist and drummer with fixtured instruments) physically performed and recorded a commercially released EP on Warp Records, but every note came from a human-composed MIDI sequence, i.e. step-by-step command rather than autonomous performance.

sources.title: Compressorhead - Party Machine - CD (Album, Stereo), 2017 | Discogs
sources.claim: Compressorhead, the first robotic band to release an album, plays real electric and acoustic instruments but is driven note-by-note by a MIDI sequencer, with human musical directors, songwriters and vocalists supplying the performance.

sources.developer: Shahid, Braghin & Roveda (Politecnico di Milano / CNR-STIIMA)
sources.title: Meet the Robot Drummer That Can Play Linkin Park (and Bon Jovi) Like a Human - ZME Science
sources.claim: The state-of-the-art learned humanoid drummer (Robot Drummer, 2025) achieves human-like drumming behaviours only for a Unitree G1 humanoid in ..., not on real hardware in a studio.

sources.title: Hear and See the Robotic Orchestra, Musica Automata - Labroots
sources.claim: Robotic-instrument records that do exist are performances of a human's composition executed by machines under the artist's direct control, e.g. the Musica Automata robotic orchestra album played by 19 robots driven from the composer's laptop.

tasks.label: Make or participate in recordings in music studios.

instances.label: Lead/backing vocal tracking in a professional or commercial recording studio: singer stands at a mic in a treated booth, sings multiple takes of a song to a click/backing track, responds to producer/engineer direction over talkback (pitch, phrasing, emotion, diction), punches in fixes and stacks harmonies until an accepted comp is captured.

Session instrumentalist (guitar, bass, keyboard/piano) tracking parts in a commercial studio: reads a chart or learns the demo, chooses voicings/tone/amp settings, plays the part with the requested feel, adapts across takes to producer direction, delivers a usable take within a booked session block.

Drummer/percussionist tracking in a studio live room: plays a full drum kit or hand/tuned percussion to a click for several minutes at a time, tunes and adjusts the kit, delivers the dynamics, fills and groove the producer accepts, over multiple takes.

Ensemble/orchestral session at a scoring stage or large studio (strings, horns, choir, backing-vocal group): sight-reads unfamiliar written parts under a conductor or click, blends and matches intonation/articulation with the section, re-takes bars on the fly at the composer's request.

Singer-songwriter or artist self-recording in a home/project studio: sets up mics and interface in a bedroom, garage or spare room, plays and sings their own parts into a DAW, re-records and layers until satisfied, in a space with no fixed layout or standard equipment.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Shimon | Center for Music Technology - Georgia Tech
sources.claim: Shimon, a four-armed robotic marimba player, autonomously listens to human players and improvises with them; its marimba playing appears on released recordings (the 'Shimon Sings' project).
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: autonomous instrumental performance captured in a recording. Limited to one purpose-built marimba rig, so it does not transfer to vocals, guitar/bass/keys, drum kit or orchestral sight-reading sessions.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology
sources.title: Into Your Mind, by Shimon The Robot

sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (robots playing real instruments recorded in a studio), but the musical performance was authored note-by-note by a human, i.e. scripted step-by-step control rather than the musician's own accepted take.

sources.title: Robot called the 'Musician Hand' can hear a melody one time and teach itself to play the tune in just two minutes
sources.claim: The state of the art in autonomously learned robotic keyboard performance is a four-fingered tendon-driven hand that learns by motor babbling and plays back roughly 30-note melodies by ear, compared in blind tests with human pianists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

Member of a vocal ensemble — church choir, chorus, backup vocal group, or a cappella group — singing an assigned part in rehearsal and in scheduled services or concerts, blending and tuning with other singers under a director.

Studio recording session: singing lead or harmony/backing takes to a click and headphone mix for a record, jingle, or media soundtrack, repeating takes and punch-ins to a producer's direction until an accepted vocal is captured.
Lead singer in a band or touring stage/theater show, singing while moving on stage and coordinating with the band, monitors, and audience over a full-length set.
Broadcast or streamed performance: singing live on radio, television, or an online stream, hitting exact cues and time constraints with no chance to retake.

tasks.label: Interpret or modify music, applying knowledge of harmony, melody, rhythm, and voice production to individualize presentations and maintain audience interest.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vocalist (often singer-guitarist/keyboardist) fronting a 2-4 hour cover set at a bar, club, wedding or private event: transposing songs to fit the voice, re-phrasing melodies, ad-libbing and stretching or cutting sections, taking requests, and shaping the set to the crowd's response.

Improvising instrumentalist in a jazz/pop/rock ensemble on a club or festival stage: comping behind others, taking solos, trading with bandmates, varying harmony and rhythm from night to night in response to the band and the audience.

Solo keyboard/piano interpretive performance from a score or lead sheet - recital in a concert hall, church service, hotel lounge or restaurant background set - shaping tempo rubato, dynamics, voicing and ornamentation to make the reading individual.

Section player on strings, winds or brass in an orchestra, pit band or chamber group in a concert hall or theater: realizing the conductor's or ensemble's interpretation through bowing, breath, vibrato, intonation and dynamic blend.

Studio or broadcast session: cutting multiple takes of a vocal or instrumental part in a control-room-directed session, altering feel, phrasing, harmony parts and ornament choices between takes on the producer's direction.
Outdoor or street performance - busking on a sidewalk, park or street festival, parade, outdoor ceremony - adapting repertoire, volume and delivery to passersby, weather and uncontrolled acoustics.

tasks.label: Practice singing exercises and study with vocal coaches to develop voice and skills and to rehearse for upcoming roles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solo daily vocal practice at home or in a private practice room: breath-support and posture work, scales, arpeggios, vowel and register exercises, self-monitoring with a keyboard or tuner app, roughly 30-90 minutes, adjusting technique to the day's vocal condition.

One-on-one lesson or coaching session in a vocal coach's or repetiteur's studio with piano: the singer sings repertoire, the coach diagnoses tone, breath, diction and intonation, and the singer immediately re-sings passages applying the corrections.

Staged rehearsal for an upcoming role in an opera/musical-theatre rehearsal hall or on stage: singing the part from memory while executing blocking and stage movement with a director, conductor and other cast members, marking or full-voicing depending on vocal load.

Band, choir or session-prep rehearsal in a rehearsal studio: running the set list or charts on mic through a PA, blending and tuning with other vocalists/instruments, fixing entrances, keys and harmonies for an upcoming gig or recording date.

Pre-performance or on-the-road preparation: warming up the voice in a dressing room, backstage or a car before a call, quietly marking through difficult passages and doing humming/lip-trill exercises under time pressure and variable conditions.

Cited to show the ceiling of embodied vocal production; it does not transfer to this task because the accepted output here is a human singer's developed technique and role-readiness, which a sound-producing machine cannot deliver.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: stage performance by humanoid robots. Cited as the closest embodied analogue; it does not transfer because these are pre-choreographed entertainment appearances, not vocal-technique practice or coached rehearsal producing a role-ready voice.

Worship-service singing (cantor, soloist, choir member, or worship-band vocalist) in a church or synagogue, singing with organ, piano, or praise band, following a liturgical order and blending with other voices.

Studio recording session: singer tracks lead or backing vocals in an isolation booth against a click and pre-recorded accompaniment, taking producer direction and repeating takes/punch-ins until the performance is accepted.

Staged theatrical or classical vocal performance — musical theater, opera, or concert work with orchestra — singing memorized material in character, on pitch and in tempo with a conductor, over multiple acts.

Contracted event singing at weddings, funerals, memorials, corporate parties, and civic ceremonies (e.g., national anthem), often a cappella or with a single accompanist, in venues the singer has not rehearsed in.

Rehearsals, auditions, and a cappella ensemble work: sight-singing parts, tuning to other unaccompanied voices, taking direction from a director, and repeating passages until blend and intonation are acceptable.

tasks.label: Teach music for specific instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: One-on-one private lesson in the musician's home studio: hearing the student play prepared material, diagnosing intonation/rhythm/technique problems, demonstrating passages on the instrument or by voice, explaining fingering, breath, bowing or embouchure, and assigning practice for the coming week.

Studio lesson at a music school, community music program, conservatory prep division, or church/music-store teaching studio: scheduled 30-60 minute lessons through a method book or graded repertoire, technical exercises, sight-reading, and preparation for juries, recitals or exams, with progress reported to parents or the institution.

Traveling teacher giving the lesson at the student's home or at the student's K-12 school (pull-out lesson or private coaching in a band/orchestra room), adapting to whatever instrument condition, space and interruptions are present.

Remote lesson delivered by video call: the student plays into a camera/microphone, the teacher listens, comments, demonstrates on their own instrument, marks up scanned music and sends practice notes and recordings afterward.

Group instruction — beginner group class, instrumental sectional, chamber coaching, or a masterclass/workshop at a summer program — where the teacher must listen to several players at once, isolate individual problems, and model correct playing for the group.

tasks.label: Transpose music to alternate keys, or to fit individual styles or purposes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Accompanist or singer transposes a song (art song, standard, audition cut) into a key that fits a particular vocalist's range, producing a re-keyed lead sheet or piano part by hand or in notation software before a rehearsal or gig.

Worship or gigging band musician transposes hymns, chord charts, or Nashville-number charts into a new key for the vocalist or congregation, often marking the chart or reading it at sight in the new key during the service or set.

Ensemble leader or arranger adapts a cover or existing chart to the group's instrumentation and style — shifting key and adjusting voicings, ranges, and feel — using notation/DAW software to output new parts.

Player of a transposing instrument (trumpet, clarinet, horn, alto sax) reads a concert-pitch, C, or wrong-key part and transposes it mentally in real time during rehearsal, pit work, or a broadcast session.

Studio/recording session: singer or session player re-keys a backing track, guide chart, or instrumental part to suit the vocalist or the production's final key, coordinating the change with the producer.
Teaching or coaching setting: musician transposes exercises, scales, or a student's repertoire piece on the fly into other keys to suit the student's level, instrument, or voice.

tasks.label: Memorize musical selections and routines, or sing following printed text, musical notation, or customer instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gigging vocalist for a bar, club, or cover band: learns and memorizes a set list of 20-40 songs (lyrics, melodies, arrangements, cues) and delivers them from memory across a multi-hour live set, adjusting keys and order on the fly.

Choral, church, or opera-chorus singer performing from printed musical notation: reads the score in rehearsal and performance, follows the conductor's tempo and dynamics, and memorizes staged numbers where required.

Wedding, funeral, or private-event singer working to customer instructions: learns a client-requested song (sometimes in an unfamiliar language or a specific key/arrangement) and sings it at the requested moment in the ceremony.

Session/backing vocalist in a recording studio or broadcast setting: sings takes from a lead sheet, chart, or scratch track under producer direction, revising phrasing, harmony parts, and diction between takes.

Instrumentalist or musical-theater performer memorizing selections and staging routines: commits a show's book, cues, and choreographed blocking to memory and reproduces them across a run of performances.

tasks.label: Observe choral leaders or prompters for cues or directions in vocal presentation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Church or community choir member during a weekly worship service or rehearsal: watches the choral director's beat pattern, breath cues, entrance gestures, dynamic and cutoff signals from a choir loft or chancel, and shapes their sung line accordingly while also tracking the score.

School, college, or youth choir singer in rehearsal and concert: attends to the director's verbal directions, hand signals, and modeled phrasing, adjusting vowel shape, blend, tempo, and entrances on cue.

Symphony chorus member or oratorio soloist in a concert hall with orchestra: follows the conductor's baton for tempo changes, fermatas, releases, and balance cues, often over long rests and with limited sightlines to the podium.

Opera or musical-theatre chorister/soloist performing staged blocking: takes cues from the conductor via a monitor screen or the prompter's box while facing away from the pit, coordinating entrances and recitative pacing with stage action.

Session or broadcast singer in a recording studio or television/livestream setting: watches a conductor, contractor, or floor-director hand cue (or cue light/click and talkback direction) through glass or on camera and delivers takes on the indicated cue.

tasks.label: Collaborate with a manager or agent who handles administrative details, finds work, and negotiates contracts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Arrange and edit music to fit style and purpose.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A gigging instrumentalist adapts an existing song for their own small group (e.g., a trio): transposing to a singer's key, reharmonizing or simplifying chords, deciding intro/solo/ending structure, and producing a lead sheet or chart by hand or in notation software.

A recording or session musician edits a track in a DAW: comping takes, trimming and time-aligning phrases, tuning vocals, cutting or repeating sections, and reordering the arrangement to fit a producer's stylistic brief and target length.

A church, school, or community-ensemble musician arranges a hymn, choral, or band piece for whatever instrumentation and skill levels are available that week, then engraves and prints individual parts.

A pit, cover-band, or wedding-band player edits purchased/rented charts to fit the booking: marking cuts, vamps, repeats, key changes, and dynamics on the score and parts so the ensemble can read them at the gig.

A singer arranges backing vocal harmonies and prepares backing tracks/click for a set: choosing voicings, adjusting keys and tempos of instrumental tracks in software, and assembling a set-length arrangement.

tasks.label: Improvise music during performances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-combo gig in a bar, club, brewery or restaurant: the instrumentalist (guitar, keys, sax, bass, drums) takes improvised solos, trades choruses, comps behind others, and stretches or cuts sections in real time by ear, over a 2-4 hour set on the venue's small stage.

Worship service or similar liturgical performance: keyboardist/organist/guitarist improvises preludes, fills, modulations and vamps under prayer, and follows a leader's unplanned cues to extend or end a song, supporting congregational singing in the sanctuary.

Produced show on a concert-hall, theater, festival mainstage or broadcast set: improvised solo, cadenza or free-improvised segment inside a rehearsed program, with sound crew, monitors, and a conductor or bandleader giving cues.

Recording or broadcast studio session: player improvises solos, fills or ad-lib parts over a backing track for a producer, doing multiple takes until one is accepted, in an acoustically treated room with engineers.

Vocalist improvising during a live performance: scat choruses, gospel/soul riffs and ad-libs, call-and-response with the band or congregation, spontaneous ornamentation and phrase/key adjustments, sung acoustically or into a mic.

Private event or street work taken as found: wedding reception, house party, corporate function or sidewalk busking, where the player improvises to fill time, cover a delay, honor requests or hold a passing crowd, with no stage, no tech crew, and variable acoustics and power.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech / Gil Weinberg, Guy Hoffman
sources.title: Shimon | CHI '10 Extended Abstracts on Human Factors in Computing Systems (ACM DL)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed description of Shimon as an autonomous improvising robotic marimba player that perceives music and produces acoustic melodic and harmonic responses while playing with humans.

sources.title: Robot jazz musician, Shimon, to play Aspen Ideas Fest | AspenTimes.com
sources.claim: In live jazz-band performance Shimon tracks tempo, rhythm and pitch and reads bandmates' visual cues, improvising with the band in the moment; it was booked to play a festival concert alongside human musicians.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech / Gil Weinberg with Dimitri Vassilakis
sources.title: Dimitri Vassilakis, Gil Weinberg Shimon Robot & Friends - Megaron The Athens Concert Hall
sources.claim: Shimon appeared as a credited member of a professional jazz ensemble (sax, trumpet, piano, bass, drums, guitar) in a ticketed concert at the Athens Concert Hall, accompanying and improvising on marimba.

sources.title: Musical Robot Learns to Sing, Has Album Dropping on Spotify - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Shimon has performed at major venues such as the Kennedy Center and produced a released album of material it composed and performed, i.e. studio-captured output from a robot instrumentalist.
sources.transferJustification: Studio capture of improvised/original instrumental parts is the studio variant of the same task: same instrument-striking precision and same real-time musical generation, in a controlled room.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech / Gil Weinberg, Scott Driscoll
sources.title: When robots play real musical instruments: Could they bring analog authenticity back to modern music?
sources.claim: Haile, an acoustic percussion robot, listens to live players and improvises drum parts in real time, used in call-and-response improvisatory concert pieces with human percussionists.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the drum-set improvisation variant of the task (trading fours, fills) on a real acoustic instrument with live human players.

sources.title: The Ghost in the Keys: A Disklavier Demo for Human-AI Musical Co-Creativity (arXiv)
sources.claim: Aria-Duet uses a Yamaha Disklavier as the physical instrument: a generative model listens to a pianist and, on a pedal cue, generates and acoustically performs an improvised continuation on the keys in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Keyboard-improvisation variant of the task: an acoustically actuated piano physically plays newly generated improvisation, but only turn-taking after an explicit human handover signal on a specially instrumented piano.

sources.title: Integrating humanoid robots with human musicians for synchronized musical performances (PeerJ Computer Science)
sources.claim: Humanoid robots Polaris (drums) and Oscar (keyboard) played real instruments in live performances alongside human musicians, autonomously synchronizing tempo and song-stage transitions with the band.
sources.transferJustification: Shows current humanoid robots holding a live band chair on keys and drums with autonomous tempo synchronization to human players; the parts are pre-programmed, so it supports ensemble playing rather than the improvisation itself.

tasks.label: Audition for orchestras, bands, or other musical groups.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classical instrumentalist auditions for a professional or per-service orchestra: travels to the hall, warms up, performs a prepared concerto exposition plus a list of orchestral excerpts behind a screen for a committee, may face multiple rounds, sight-reading, and instructions such as 'play the Mozart again, lighter and slower'.

Singer auditions for an opera chorus, musical-theater production, or professional choir: sings prepared arias or a 16-bar cut with a staff accompanist in a rehearsal hall or theater, sight-sings or cold-reads on request, and takes redirection from the panel.

Instrumentalist auditions for a working commercial band (cover/wedding/jazz/touring act) at a rented rehearsal studio or club with house backline: plays several prepared tunes with the band, jams on unfamiliar material, reads charts, and adapts feel and volume on the bandleader's cues.

Audition/tryout with a band in a member's home basement, garage, or improvised DIY practice space with clutter, ad hoc gear and cramped layout: runs through set material with the group and negotiates arrangements on the spot.

Self-recorded prescreening audition: musician sets up camera and mic at home or in a rented studio, performs the required repertoire list in unedited takes to a specified standard, and submits the file to the hiring panel.

Audition for an institutional ensemble — military band, cruise-line or theme-park show band, church worship team, or conservatory ensemble placement — held in a base band room, corporate audition studio, or sanctuary, with prepared repertoire, scales, and sight-reading judged against a published standard.

sources.developer: academic consortium (RP1M authors, incl. Max Planck / ETH-affiliated researchers)
sources.title: Dexterous Robotic Piano Playing at Scale (arXiv 2511.02504)
sources.claim: OmniPianist is an autonomous RL/imitation-learning agent for bimanual robotic piano playing trained at scale, but it is evaluated in simulation and reaches only F1 0.55 on unseen songs — far below the note accuracy and musical polish a professional audition demands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing prepared piano repertoire. Auditions require flawless execution of assigned repertoire on a real acoustic instrument; this simulation-only agent's 0.55 F1 on new pieces shows the note-level reliability gap.

sources.title: Robotic Arms Play The Cello For The First Time As Part of a Symphony Orchestra
sources.claim: The first robot cello soloist to appear with a symphony orchestra was two industrial arms executing a score written specifically for them; the performance was programmed rather than autonomously interpreted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing bowed-string repertoire on a concert stage (an E2 setting). It is the closest analogue to a string audition, yet it is scripted and plays only music composed for the machine.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Shimon: an interactive improvisational robotic marimba player (ACM CHI EA)
sources.claim: Shimon is an autonomous improvising marimba robot that perceives human players and performs live with them, but its demonstrated repertoire is purpose-built jazz/experimental improvisation rather than standard audition repertoire judged against human candidates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing with an ensemble in real time, the core skill an ensemble audition tests. Transfer is limited: Shimon plays a fixed mallet instrument on original material, not assigned excerpts under panel direction.

sources.title: This Robot Toots Its Own Flute - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: After decades of development, Waseda's anthropomorphic flutist robot plays by translating MIDI files into instrument control parameters with audio feedback for tuning, i.e. it renders note data rather than interpreting a score at professional wind-audition standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing a wind instrument from notated music, exactly what a woodwind audition requires. Performance is MIDI playback quality, without the tone, phrasing and sight-reading a committee evaluates.

sources.title: Robot pianist gives diners a taste of the future
sources.claim: Xiaole, a piano-playing robot deployed as an attraction in a restaurant in Hangzhou, locates keys with a vision system and plays for diners; it is an entertainment novelty in a public venue, not a performer evaluated against human musicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live keyboard performance before an audience in a human venue. It shows deployed robot piano playing exists, but at background-entertainment quality, with no evidence of assigned-repertoire accuracy or responsiveness to direction.

tasks.label: Perform in television, radio, or movie productions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Session instrumentalist on a film/TV scoring stage or recording studio: sight-reads a newly written cue on violin, horn, guitar or piano, plays to a click and conductor, delivers repeated takes with phrasing and dynamics adjusted to the composer's verbal notes, within a booked session.

Vocalist recording in a studio booth for a soundtrack song, TV theme or radio jingle: multiple takes, pitch/phrasing/emotional direction from the producer, doubles and harmonies comped into a final vocal.

Live musical performance on a TV production (late-night house band, talk-show guest spot, awards or competition show): sound check and camera rehearsal on a soundstage, then a live or live-to-tape performance hitting exact timings with audience and crew present.

On-camera musician inside a filmed scene on a soundstage or backlot: in costume and character, plays or mimes precisely to playback, hits marks, matches action across many takes and camera setups under a director's notes.
Performance for a film/TV shoot on location taken as found: street corner, bar, church, wedding scene or outdoor festival broadcast, with variable acoustics, weather, crowds and improvised staging.
Live in-studio session at a radio station: short acoustic set performed live to air in a small studio, adapting arrangement and length to the host's cues and timing to the clock.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Four-Armed Marimba Robot Uses Deep Learning to Compose Its Own Music - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Shimon is a four-armed robotic marimba player that listens to human musicians in real time and improvises with them, and later used deep learning to compose original pieces; it performs live with bands and appeared in its own music video.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (playing an instrument in performance), but confined to marimba improvisation as a novelty act; it does not read and interpret an arbitrary written cue or absorb a composer's/director's notes across takes.

sources.title: TeoTronico - The Robot Pianist - Apple TV
sources.claim: TeoTronico is a mechanical-fingered robot pianist that plays a real acoustic piano from digital score/MIDI files, has done 50+ theatre shows with pianist Roberto Prosseda and debuted with the Berliner Symphoniker; a concert with it was filmed and distributed. Its playing is described as literal.
sources.transferJustification: Closest case of a robot performing an instrument within a filmed production; it substantiates note execution on a real piano, but the source describes literal playback rather than the interpretive performance a scoring session or broadcast spot requires.

sources.title: Compressorhead rocks the crowd to find new robot band member - New Atlas
sources.claim: Compressorhead is a robot band whose members play real electric guitars, bass and drums on stage across 100+ live shows, but each member is driven over MIDI by human-authored sequences rather than by its own musical decisions.
sources.transferJustification: Live instrumental performance on real instruments is the same physical act, but control is human-programmed MIDI, i.e. scripted note-by-note, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Robotic drummer gradually acquires human-like behaviors - Tech Xplore
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid drumming result as of 2025, Robot Drummer, learns to play full songs on a kit with high rhythmic precision, but was evaluated only in simulation of the Unitree G1, not on physical hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (playing a kit for a track), but simulation-only, so no physical performance in any environment is substantiated.

sources.title: Human-Robot Cooperative Piano Playing with Learning-Based Real-Time Music Accompaniment (arXiv 2409.11952)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous cooperative instrument playing on real hardware is a collaborative robot arm generating real-time chordal accompaniment to a human pianist in a laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act (playing piano alongside a human) at the research frontier; the demonstrated output is simple chordal accompaniment in a lab, far below session or broadcast standard.

sources.title: Mechanical voice system and its singing performance - Waseda University
sources.claim: Mechanical singing/talking robots with physical vocal tracts produce only vowel and consonant sounds at controlled pitch; no robotic vocal apparatus approaches professional singing quality.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the vocal task; the demonstrated capability is syllable-level sound production, not a recordable sung performance.

sources.developer: Unitree Robotics with director Zhang Yimou
sources.title: Unitree's humanoid robots steal the show at 2025 CCTV Spring Festival Gala with AI-powered Yangge dance - TechNode
sources.claim: Humanoid robots have appeared as performers in a live national TV production, executing a choreographed folk dance alongside human dancers on the CCTV Spring Festival Gala stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing a rehearsed routine on a broadcast TV stage. It shows robots can be staged in a TV production, but the deliverable is choreographed locomotion, not instrumental or vocal music, so it does not transfer to a musician's performance.

tasks.label: Promote their own or their group's music by participating in media interviews and other activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Radio, TV, or podcast interview tied to a single/album release or tour announcement: the musician answers a host's questions about the new work, tells stories behind the songs, and plugs dates and links, either in a broadcast studio or over a remote video/phone link.

Print/online press interview with a journalist or blogger (phone, video call, or emailed questions) for a feature, review sidebar, or Q&A; the artist supplies quotes, background, and approved talking points.

Self-directed promotion on social platforms: recording and posting short promo clips, livestreaming to fans, writing captions and announcements, replying to comments and DMs, and pushing pre-save/ticket links.

In-person promotional appearance: record-store or festival signing, meet-and-greet, red-carpet or press-junket line, or a brief acoustic 'session' at a station where the artist also talks up the release.
Industry-facing promotion: pitching press kits and music to playlist curators, promoters, booking agents, and A&R by email or phone; showcase networking and follow-up conversations at conferences.

tasks.label: Research particular roles to find out more about a character, or the time and place in which a piece is set.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

roles.title: Disc Jockeys, Except Radio
roles.description: Play prerecorded music for live audiences at venues or events such as clubs, parties, or wedding receptions. May use techniques such as mixing, cutting, or sampling to manipulate recordings. May also perform as emcee (master of ceremonies).
roles.sector: Arts, design, entertainment, sports, and media

tasks.label: Operate disc jockey controller and other equipment, such as microphones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nightclub or bar set: DJ stands at the booth operating CDJs/DJ controller and mixer — loading tracks, beatmatching, adjusting EQ/filters/faders, cueing loops and effects — to deliver a continuous mixed program for a dancing crowd over 2-4 hours, with occasional short microphone shout-outs.

Wedding reception: DJ operates a laptop-plus-controller rig and a wireless microphone, cross-fading between cocktail, dinner and dance-floor music, cutting tracks for toasts and the first dance, riding mic levels and making MC announcements timed to the event schedule.

Corporate or private party at a hired venue: DJ works a portable controller and PA, keeps background/dance music running at requested volumes, takes live requests, and uses the mic for raffle draws, speeches hand-offs and announcements.

School dance, prom or community/civic event in a gym or hall: mobile DJ operates controller, mic and lighting controls, censors/edits tracks on the fly, and repeatedly hands off or uses the microphone for crowd instructions.

Turntablist / open-format festival or competition stage: performer manipulates vinyl or DVS platters and the mixer crossfader for scratching, cutting and juggling routines synchronized to a live set, plus effects units and sampler pads.

Livestream or radio-style studio set: DJ operates controller, mixer and studio microphone to produce a recorded or streamed mix, monitoring levels in headphones and talking over the intro/outro of tracks.

tasks.label: Communicate with clients or venue owners to determine event information, such as music preferences, scheduling, and anticipated attendance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assemble audio and video equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile DJ setting up for a wedding reception in a hotel ballroom or banquet hall: load-in from a van through a service door, erect two or three tripod/pole speaker stands, lift 20-40 lb powered tops onto poles, place subwoofer, set facade/table with controller or CDJs and mixer, wireless mic receivers, run and tape XLR/speakon and power cables to house outlets, hang uplights and a moving-head T-bar, sometimes a TV or projector for a photo montage, then power up and sound-check before guests arrive.

Club or bar gig with an installed house system: DJ arrives just before doors or during another set, places laptop/controller or USB media players on a cramped booth shelf, patches RCA/XLR into the installed mixer, plugs power bricks into a shared strip, connects headphones and monitor feed, checks the video-wall or projector feed if the club runs one, and line-checks with staff and patrons moving around the booth.

Corporate meeting, school dance, or civic-hall event with a video component: PA plus a projector and screen or LED panel, HDMI/SDI runs from a laptop, podium and lavalier mics, dance lighting, cable ramps across walkways, coordinating with the venue's in-house AV staff and using the room's rack, patch panel and circuits.

Private residence, backyard, tent, or park party: gear hand-carried across a lawn, gravel, or up stairs; no loading dock; limited or unknown power (household circuits, extension cords, sometimes a generator); uneven or soft ground for speaker stands and sandbags; weather covers; ad hoc placement decided on arrival with the host.

Festival stage, large club, or promoter-supplied production: the rig already exists, and the DJ sets up their own CDJs/mixer or controller on the riser during a short changeover, patches into the house console or DI box, connects timecode/link cabling and monitor sends, and hands off with the stage tech.

sources.system: HIL-SERL (Human-in-the-Loop Sample-Efficient Robotic RL) on Franka arms
sources.title: Precise and Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: Autonomous vision-based RL policies on fixed-base arms at a fixtured benchtop workcell reach 100% success on precise assembly tasks including USB grasp-insertion, RAM insertion, SSD assembly, cable clipping and furniture-panel assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: electronics/furniture assembly and cable insertion in a fixtured cell. Assembling a DJ rig is mating audio/power connectors and joining components; the objects (plugs, cables, panels) and sub-millimetre insertion tolerances are comparable, and the cited work occurs in exactly the fixtured workcell an E1 setting provides.

sources.system: Model-based connector mating framework (industrial manipulator with force/vision/tactile sensing)
sources.developer: ArtiMinds Robotics / TU Braunschweig / AICOR Bremen (Kienle, Alt et al.)
sources.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation
sources.claim: An AI framework automates mating of automotive cable connectors using force control and visuotactile learning on an industrial robot, reporting about 95% insertion success for most connectors and 88% for a laterally constrained one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating multi-pin electrical connectors in wire-harness installation. DJ setup is dominated by mating XLR/speakon/IEC/HDMI plugs into sockets; connector geometry, insertion forces and blind-search error recovery are directly comparable, and the demonstrated setting is a fixtured industrial cell.

sources.title: FANUC Robots Automate Precise Automotive Process | Case Study
sources.claim: Deployed, commercially operating fenced FANUC robot cells autonomously feed, insert and position parts for an automotive product with precise dimensional and geometric positioning; other FANUC deployments handle payloads up to two tonnes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured multi-part assembly with automated part feeding and insertion. It shows that when parts are presented in known positions inside a fenced cell, commercial robots join components at production quality and reliability — the E1 counterfactual for assembling a speaker/stand/mixer rig.

sources.system: Rocsys Steward / M1 autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M
sources.claim: Purpose-built robotic charging systems autonomously detect a vehicle, open the port, insert a bulky power connector and disconnect, with a claimed 99.9%+ plug-in success rate in ... port and depot bays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mating of a bulky power connector outside a laboratory. It shows connector insertion at production reliability, but only at a dedicated, purpose-built charging bay where the work is presented to the machine — E1-style structure, not free-form venue setup.

sources.title: Training a Humanoid Robot for Hard Work | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A humanoid using learned whole-body policies lifts and carries a mini-fridge-sized heavy object, but only as a research demonstration inside the developer's lab, with no assembly or cabling involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and carrying a bulky heavy object such as a subwoofer or road case. It bounds current capability: heavy-object handling by legged humanoids remains a lab demonstration without equipment assembly, cabling, or venue navigation, so it cannot substantiate E2/E3 completion.

tasks.label: Select and play music incorporating crowd preferences and mood.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nightclub or dance bar set: DJ reads the dance floor (how full it is, how people are moving, time of night) and chooses the next records accordingly, beatmatching and blending tracks on CDJs/controller to keep energy building.

Wedding reception: mixed-age crowd with a client must-play/do-not-play list; DJ shifts selections from cocktail/dinner background music to peak-hour dance sets, reads which age groups are on the floor, and folds in live guest requests.

Private/corporate party, school dance, or bar/bat mitzvah: DJ works to a client brief and audience age range, keeps selections appropriate, and adjusts tempo and genre as the room's mood shifts across the event timeline.

Low-key mobile gig at a restaurant, lounge, or small bar: mostly curated background playlists at controlled volume, occasional selection changes when the room's makeup or mood changes; minimal mixing.
Festival, large public event, or opening slot with a largely prepared setlist that the DJ adapts on the fly to a big crowd's reaction and to the preceding/following act's energy.

instances.label: Mobile/wedding DJ at a banquet hall or hotel ballroom: after loading in and setting up own speakers, subs, mixer and wireless mics, runs test tracks and pink noise, sets gain structure and EQ for the room, walks the floor to check coverage, tests handheld/lavalier mics for dropout and feedback before guests arrive.

Club or bar resident DJ using the installed house system: checks each deck/CDJ and mixer channel, headphone cue, booth monitor and floor levels, plays a test track before doors open, confirms limiter/DSP settings and reports any faulty channel or blown driver to management.

Private-residence, backyard or tent event: site taken as found, unknown power circuits and no institution controlling the space; DJ verifies power, checks for hum/ground loops, sets levels for open air or a small living space, tests the mic for toasts and adjusts for reflective or absorptive surroundings.

Corporate or conference event in a hotel/convention center with in-house AV: DJ coordinates with venue AV staff, patches into the house system, tests handheld and lavalier wireless mics for speeches, confirms playback levels and program routing to house zones.

Festival or large-stage event with a front-of-house engineer: DJ performs a line check of the DJ channels into the house console, verifies booth monitor levels and redundancy (backup player/cable), and confirms signal at correct level on each input with the engineer before the set.

sources.title: Automated Audio Testing in Pre-Owned Phones: Ensuring Quality | OptoFidelity

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional audio test of transducers. It covers the core of a sound check - drive the device, capture the acoustic output, compare level and quality against acceptance thresholds, and flag failing channels - on the same class of objects (loudspeakers and microphones) in a purpose-built cell where the unit is presented to the machine.

sources.title: QC – Quality Control — Klippel Manuals

sources.transferJustification: Related task: 100% end-of-line acoustic verification of audio equipment, including on-line diagnostics of loudspeaker defects. It substantiates that pass/fail judgment of whether audio gear is working correctly is executed without a human listener in an engineered cell, which is the 'ensure equipment is working' half of the sound check.

sources.title: Drone as First Responder (DFR) for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio drones launch from docks and fly autonomously to incident scenes, streaming live video to remote operators; the imagery is situational-awareness video for public-safety agencies, with a remote operator in the loop rather than a news photographer's composed coverage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rapid aerial video capture of unplanned incident scenes. Cited to test whether spot-news field shooting is automated; camera framing and shot selection remain with remote operators, so it does not substantiate completing the reporting task.

sources.system: Skydio Dock for X10 drone ports for news gathering (KDDI Smart Drone / TV Asahi)
sources.developer: TV Asahi, KDDI Smart Drone, Skydio
sources.title: TV Asahi and KDDI Smart Drone Partner for Disaster News Drone Deployment | DroneLife
sources.claim: Broadcaster TV Asahi and KDDI Smart ... announced an initiative to gather aerial disaster news footage from pre-positioned autonomous drone ports, with a Skydio Dock for X10 installed in Ishikawa Prefecture in October 2025; footage is streamed live to the newsroom under remote launch.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (aerial news videotaping), cited to test E3 spot news; autonomy of camera framing and shot selection is not established and coverage is limited to wide aerial views from fixed port locations.

instances.label: Remote over-the-phone or video consecutive interpreting: interpreter sits at a workstation or home office, hears a speaker (patient, caller, agent) and renders each turn into the other language orally, preserving content, register, and tone; no object handling.

On-site consecutive spoken interpreting at a medical appointment, social-service intake, or immigration/insurance interview: interpreter stands or sits with two parties, renders short turns in both directions orally, maintaining register and cultural context.

American Sign Language interpreting for a Deaf consumer in a classroom, workplace meeting, or clinic: interpreter renders spoken English into ASL with hands, face, and body, and voices the Deaf person's signing back into spoken English; the act is linguistic expression, not manipulation of objects.

Simultaneous interpreting in a booth or with portable equipment at a conference, court proceeding, or legislative hearing: interpreter listens through headphones and speaks the target-language rendition into a microphone in near real time.

Escort/liaison interpreting for a delegation, factory tour, or business negotiation: interpreter accompanies parties and interprets consecutively while moving between locations; the walking is incidental to conveying speech.

roles.title: Court Reporters and Simultaneous Captioners
roles.description: Use verbatim methods and equipment to capture, store, retrieve, and transcribe pretrial and trial proceedings or other information. Includes stenocaptioners who operate computerized stenographic captioning equipment to provide captions of live or prerecorded broadcasts for hearing-impaired viewers.
roles.sector: Arts, design, entertainment, sports, and media

tasks.label: Provide transcripts of proceedings upon request of judges, lawyers, or the public.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Record symbols on computer storage media and use computer aided transcription to translate and display them as text.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live courtroom proceeding (trial, motion hearing, sentencing): the reporter's stenotype writer records each stroke of steno symbols to internal memory and an SD/flash card while CAT software (e.g., Case CATalyst, Eclipse, StenoCAT) translates the steno strokes against the reporter's dictionary and displays English text on the reporter's screen in realtime.

Deposition or arbitration in a law office or conference room: strokes are written to the writer's storage media and simultaneously streamed via cable/Bluetooth/wi-fi to the CAT laptop, which translates and feeds realtime text to attorneys' laptops, iPads, or remote streaming platforms.

Live broadcast captioning or CART: the stenocaptioner writes symbols that are captured to the writer/CAT files, translated by CAT software, and routed to an encoder or captioning platform so text is displayed to viewers or a consumer within a couple of seconds.

Post-proceeding transfer and retranslation: the reporter uploads the day's steno note file from the writer's storage media (card, USB, cloud backup) to the CAT computer, runs translation with an updated job dictionary, and generates the ASCII/rough-draft text output for editing or same-day delivery.

Voice-writer variant: the reporter speaks into a stenomask, and the recorded audio/symbol stream is stored and converted to displayed text by speech-recognition-based CAT software (e.g., Dragon-driven eScription/Case CATalyst voice profiles) for realtime display.

tasks.label: Record verbatim proceedings of courts, legislative assemblies, committee meetings, and other proceedings, using computerized recording equipment, electronic stenograph machines, or stenomasks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Official court reporter seated in a trial courtroom capturing testimony, attorney argument, and judge's rulings verbatim on an electronic stenograph machine with realtime CAT software feeding the judge's and counsel's screens; must catch rapid crosstalk, unusual proper names, and sidebars.

Freelance deposition reporter in a law-office conference room (or remotely over videoconference) writing verbatim testimony of a deponent and counsel on a stenograph machine, marking exhibits and speaker identification in the record.

Digital court reporter/electronic recording monitor operating a multichannel computerized audio/video recording system in a courtroom: starting and monitoring channels, checking levels and mic pickup, and keying time-stamped log notes identifying speakers and events.

Broadcast stenocaptioner or CART provider producing live verbatim captions of news broadcasts, sports, classes, or public meetings from a remote captioning workstation, using a stenograph machine or a stenomask/voice-writing setup with speech engine.

Reporter covering a legislative session, committee meeting, or administrative/arbitration hearing in a hearing room with many rotating speakers, public testimony, roll calls, and variable audio conditions, producing the verbatim official record.

tasks.label: Record depositions and other proceedings for attorneys.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-person deposition in a law-firm conference room: the stenographic reporter administers the oath, captures every spoken word verbatim on a steno machine (multiple speakers, crosstalk, objections, technical/medical vocabulary), interrupts to clarify inaudible or overlapping speech, and delivers a certified verbatim transcript to counsel.

Remote videoconference deposition (Zoom/Teams): reporter joins the platform, swears in the witness remotely, captures verbatim testimony over variable audio, flags dropouts and asks speakers to repeat, and produces the certified transcript.

Courtroom proceeding (motion hearing, trial, sentencing): reporter makes the official verbatim record in real time, provides realtime feed to the bench and counsel, and reads back portions of testimony on request from the judge.

Digital (electronic) reporting of a deposition: reporter sets up and monitors a multi-channel audio/video recorder with microphones for each speaker, keeps a time-stamped log of speakers, exhibits, and objections, and the record is later transcribed and certified.

Proceeding at an irregular venue for attorneys — arbitration, examination under oath, administrative or public hearing, bedside/prison deposition — with unfamiliar acoustics, accents, or interpreters; reporter captures the verbatim record and certifies the transcript.

instances.label: In-person deposition in a law-firm or court-reporting-agency conference room: counsel hands the reporter paper documents (often multi-page, stapled, sometimes color photos) during questioning; the reporter affixes sequentially numbered exhibit stickers, records each in an exhibit index (number, date, brief description), collects them from the witness/counsel at the end, and packages the set with the transcript for retention or shipment.

Trial or evidentiary hearing in a courthouse: documentary exhibits (paper, photos, printouts) are marked for identification, offered and admitted; the reporter/clerk logs each on the exhibit list with its status, keeps custody during the session, and secures them in envelopes/folders in the courtroom or clerk's file room at the end of the day.

Courtroom proceeding involving tangible non-paper evidence: bagged or boxed physical items (firearm in a sealed evidence bag, clothing, narcotics packaging, tools, oversized boards/models). The reporter or clerk logs each item, preserves chain-of-custody paperwork, and returns/stores items in the evidence locker or hands them back to the offering party.

Remote or hybrid deposition: most exhibits arrive electronically through an exhibit-sharing platform or by email; the reporter labels and indexes them, assembles the certified digital exhibit set, and also stickers, scans and files any hard copies that were mailed or handed over in the room.

Post-proceeding processing at the reporting firm's office: batches of accumulated paper exhibits are scanned to PDF, indexed to the case and transcript, originals boxed and shelved for the retention period, and individual exhibits retrieved later on attorney request.

tasks.label: Diagnose and resolve media system problems.

instances.label: Live event at a venue (concert, corporate general session, conference, worship service): audio drops out or a projector/LED wall loses picture mid-show or during rehearsal. Tech traces the signal chain by ear and eye in a dark, crowded, cable-strewn stage/FOH area, swaps a mic, battery, DI or cable, reseats connectors, re-rings console/DSP settings, all within seconds to minutes.

Fixed-install room support call (corporate meeting room, classroom, courtroom, hotel breakout): no image on the display, videoconference camera or ceiling mic not detected, laptop won't connect. Tech checks source and inputs, reseats or swaps HDMI/USB-C/network cabling, power-cycles the codec/switcher/DSP, changes configuration, occasionally swaps a failed device.

Broadcast/production facility rack room: a signal path (fiber or patch-panel link) has gone bad; diagnosis reduces to testing the link and restoring service by re-patching or rerouting to a known-good spare path.

Broadcast/production facility control or rack room, device-level fault: video server, router, encoder or IP stream failure. Tech interprets error behavior on monitors and test gear, checks configuration and reference/sync, reboots, swaps an SFP, card or unit, and verifies restored signal.

Field or remote production and off-site press conferences in locations taken as found (outdoor sports field, parking lot, plant floor, street location): RF interference or wireless dropouts, damaged cable runs, generator power and ground-loop hum, weather and improvised rigging; tech isolates and fixes the fault on the spot.

Residential or small-client service call (home theater, small church, small business): heterogeneous consumer and prosumer gear, unknown or owner-modified wiring, no documentation; tech diagnoses the reported symptom and resolves it by reconfiguring, rewiring or replacing components.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical-layer signal-path fault isolation and restoration. It transfers only to the narrow AV instance where a rack-room fault is a bad link and the fix is re-patching to a spare path: comparable objects (optical connectors, tighter tolerance than XLR/SDI), comparable precision, and the machine performs both the test and the physical reconnection. It does not transfer to faults requiring device-level reasoning, configuration or component replacement outside its enclosure.

tasks.label: Perform minor repairs and routine cleaning of audio and video equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

Mixed, delicate, non-immersible gear; visual judgment about grime, corrosion, and damage.

Bench cable repair: technician tests a suspect XLR/TRS/SDI/HDMI/speakON cable or reel with a cable tester, finds the failed end, cuts off the damaged connector, strips and tins conductors, solders or crimps a new connector, fits strain relief/heat-shrink and shell, retests continuity, then coils and labels it.

Optics and display cleaning: blowing and brushing dust off camera lenses, filters, viewfinders and sensors; cleaning projector lenses and pulling/vacuuming or replacing projector air filters (often ceiling-mounted, on a ladder or lift); wiping monitors, LED panel faces and touch panels in classrooms, conference rooms and studios.

Rack and console upkeep in a control room or equipment room: vacuuming and blowing dust from racks, fan filters, amps and video servers; spraying contact cleaner into scratchy faders and pots and working them; reseating cards and connectors; replacing fuses, batteries, knobs, worn cable ties and gaffer wraps.

Field fixes during load-in or a running show: re-terminating or swapping a failed connector on a stage snake, replacing a broken mic clip or lav clip, taping and drying gear after rain/dust at an outdoor festival, sports field or client site, working around crew, cases and cabling under time pressure.

Component- or chassis-level bench repair of a device: opening a mixer, amplifier, monitor or camera housing, resoldering a broken 1/4-inch jack or ribbon connector, replacing a fuse, pot, lamp or battery contact on the board, reassembling the chassis and function-testing before it returns to inventory.
