tasks.label: Report equipment problems, ensure that repairs are made, and make emergency repairs to equipment when necessary and possible.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live master control / studio: an on-air audio or video path fails (dead mic, SDI/audio dropout, hum, dead intercom, frozen playout device). The technician triages at the console, patch bay and rack, reseats or swaps a cable/module/mic/battery or fails over to a backup path, restores the signal within seconds-to-minutes of airtime, then logs a trouble report for engineering.

Rack room, fault already localized by monitoring: replace an identified failed hot-swap module in standardized rackmount gear - a drive in a video-server RAID, a redundant power supply, a fan tray - confirm rebuild/return to service, and log the replacement.

Station engineering shop: bench-level emergency repair of a pulled unit of heterogeneous broadcast gear (camera CCU, audio console card, encoder, UPS, lens/pan-head, mic preamp). Diagnose with meter/scope and documentation, open the chassis, replace a board/PSU/connector or resolder, functionally test, reinstall.

Transmitter/tower site call-out after a remote-control alarm: drive to the site, diagnose (tripped breaker, failed exciter or PA module, cooling fan/blower failure, arcing or moisture in transmission line, generator/HVAC fault), make an emergency repair or bypass to the auxiliary transmitter at reduced power, notify management and file the report/log.

Remote/field production (ENG-SNG truck, sports venue, news scene, roadside or parking lot, weather and time pressure): a camera, mast, fiber/triax run, RF link or power feed fails before or during a live shot. The technician improvises an on-location emergency repair - reterminate a connector, swap a converter or battery, re-run a cable, reset a transmitter - to keep the feed up, then reports the failure.

Routine monitoring/inspection rounds of the station plant and transmitter building: walk the racks, read meters and transmitter parameters, check temperatures, cooling and power, look and listen for developing faults, log anomalies and report them to the chief engineer or vendor so repairs get scheduled and tracked.

instances.label: Central technical core / rack room build-out: rack-mount and cable new playout, ingest and MAM servers, network switches and routers; run and terminate copper and fiber, dress and label cables, power up, configure addressing/VLANs and test the data and signal path before hand-off to on-air use.

Day-to-day operation and administration of station computers and network: monitoring server/network health and alarms from the master-control or engineering console, running playout automation and file-transfer/ingest jobs, applying patches, restarting services, managing accounts and backups - mostly keyboard/console or remote work inside the station.

Corrective maintenance in the technical core under time pressure: diagnose a failure (dead switch port, failed drive/PSU/fan, bad patch cord, hung server), pull and reseat or replace the faulty module or cable in a dense, heterogeneous rack, re-test and restore the on-air path.

End-user and studio-side computing: set up and maintain edit-bay workstations, newsroom PCs, control-room and graphics computers, ENG laptops, printers and Wi-Fi access points; connect monitors, audio/video and network cabling at desks, install/configure station software, join the domain, pull a cable drop to a new position and verify with the user.

Field and remote-site computing/networking: set up laptops, encoders, bonded-cellular/satellite IP links and a temporary LAN/Wi-Fi for a remote broadcast at a stadium, hotel ballroom, parking lot or news scene, or service the computers/network at a rural transmitter site; troubleshoot connectivity in as-found conditions.

sources.claim: TMGcore's OTTO modular data center platform uses a robotic arm to remove a failed server from an immersion tank and insert a replacement into a plug-and-play backplane, i.e. hardware install/replacement completed in an environment engineered around the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing and replacing rack/chassis-mounted computers with power and data connections made on insertion - comparable objects (rack servers) and precision to setting up a station's playout/video servers, with blind-mate connections standing in for hand cabling, which is exactly the E1 purpose-built presentation.

sources.system: Robot-friendly cable-less server rack with lifter robot / AGF / CTU fleet
sources.title: Inside Look: How SoftBank Corp. is Creating "Robot-friendly" Environments at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank has built a cable-less, 'robot-friendly' server rack in which a lifter robot receives a server from a container robot and pushes it into a slot, making power, network and cooling connections automatically using QR-code and laser positioning; it is being tested with robots at the Hokkaido Tomakomai AI data center.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing servers into racks and making their power/network connections, the physical core of setting up station computers. It shows such installation is achieved by rebuilding the rack around the machine (E1), not in ordinary human-cabled equipment rooms.

sources.system: DE-CIX patch robots (gantry-based optical distribution frame robots)
sources.title: DE-CIX migrates Frankfurt data center without disruption using patch robot - DCD
sources.claim: DE-CIX operates automated 'patch robots' (Patchy McPatchbot, Sir Patchalot, Margaret Patcher) that locate a socket on an optical distribution frame and plug fiber patch cords, provisioning and migrating live customer network connections without a technician physically intervening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making and changing physical network connections (patching) - the cabling half of 'set up and maintain station networks'. It runs only on a purpose-built optical distribution frame that replaces the standard rack and patch panel.

sources.system: Telescent G4/G5 Network Topology Manager robotic fiber cross-connect
sources.title: MOX Signs Agreement to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform on its Next-Generation Long-Haul Route
sources.claim: Telescent's G4/G5 robotic patch-panel systems are commercially deployed by network operators (e.g., MOX Networks, Quantum Loophole) to make, break and diagnose fiber cross-connects under software control, replacing manual patch-panel operations in data centers and long-haul networks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical-layer network provisioning, fault isolation and service restoration - the same acts a broadcast technician performs when patching and re-patching station fiber. The capability exists only inside the robot's own purpose-built cross-connect chassis.

sources.system: Data center robotics programs (Google, Meta, Switch, Alibaba, DE-CIX)
sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Industry survey of data center robotics: Google's data center VP notes that tests in data centers are far more complicated than in industries with large-scale robotic deployment, and the robots actually in use are confined to narrow, specific jobs (disk destruction, disk swaps, patching, monitoring).
sources.transferJustification: Context for negative judgments: the closest analogue to a broadcast technical core - a structured, institution-run machine room - still has no general robotic hardware technician; the cited deployments are single-purpose.

tasks.label: Control audio equipment to regulate volume and sound quality during radio and television broadcasts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Radio on-air board operation during a live music or talk show: the operator rides levels on a studio console to balance host mics, music playout, phone/remote callers, and station imaging, keeping the program within target loudness and free of clipping or dead air.

Live television newscast audio mixing (A1) in a station control room: opening and closing anchor and guest mics, mixing in field packages, voiceovers, music beds and live remotes on the director's cues, and holding program loudness to the CALM Act / ATSC A/85 target.

Master control / playout monitoring at a TV station or network hub: watching meters on incoming network, satellite and file-based feeds, correcting gain and loudness mismatches between programs and commercial breaks, and switching or muting bad audio sources.

Remote/sports or event broadcast mixing from a production truck or flypack: blending commentator mics, crowd and effects mics, replay audio, IFB and program feeds under changing live conditions, and delivering a clean mix to the transmission path.

Studio production and recorded-segment work: setting gain structure and monitoring levels while recording interviews, promos, podcasts or voice tracks, then adjusting EQ, compression and levels so the finished audio meets house sound-quality standards.

tasks.label: Regulate the fidelity, brightness, and contrast of video transmissions, using video console control panels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live studio production (news, talk, morning show): a video operator/shader sits at a CCU or remote control panel row, watching waveform monitors, vectorscopes and picture monitors, riding iris, master black, gamma and white balance to match 3-6 studio cameras as talent moves between sets and lighting states, for the duration of a live show.

Remote/OB truck or REMI sports and event coverage: shading 8-20 cameras (hard, handheld, robotic, specialty/POV) through changing daylight, stadium lighting, shadow lines and mixed camera types, matching them to a reference and keeping levels legal throughout a multi-hour live event.

Master control / transmission: monitoring outgoing program and backup feeds on waveform/vectorscope and QC displays, adjusting proc-amp video gain, pedestal, chroma and applying legalizer settings so brightness, contrast and gamut of the transmitted signal meet station and regulatory standards.

Incoming remote contributions: correcting brightness, contrast and color of satellite, bonded-cellular, IP or videoconference-quality feeds from field crews and remote guests so they intercut acceptably with studio sources, often under time pressure just before or during air.

Pre-production setup and alignment: lining cameras up on grayscale chip charts and white cards, setting black/white balance and detail, calibrating picture monitors, generating and checking bars, and building/recalling scene files before rehearsal or air.

tasks.label: Select sources from which programming will be received or through which programming will be transmitted.

tasks.label: Install broadcast equipment, troubleshoot equipment problems, and perform maintenance or minor repairs, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Install new gear in a station's technical core / rack room: rack-mount frames, routers, encoders and amplifiers on rails with hand tools; cut, route, dress, terminate and label coax/BNC, XLR, CAT6, fiber and power cables; power up and verify signal. Bespoke one-off layout per project.

Troubleshoot an equipment fault affecting production or on-air: trace the signal path across the facility, isolate whether it is a cable, connector, card, setting or upstream device, meter/scope the path, swap the suspect item and confirm restoration, often under live time pressure.

Bench maintenance and minor repairs in the engineering shop: open a chassis, replace a fan, power supply, lamp or card; re-terminate/solder a broken XLR, BNC or mic cable; clean connectors and filters; reassemble and bench-test.

Transmitter/tower site maintenance visit: inside the transmitter building swap a PA module, check line pressure, clean air filters and heat exchangers, torque RF connections, check the generator; outdoor checks of the tower base, feedline and antenna hardware in whatever weather.

Field/remote setup and teardown for a live shot or venue broadcast: rig cameras, tripods, mics and IFB, run and coil cable over uneven ground, raise a mast or align a satellite/microwave dish from an ENG truck, fix problems on site, then strike everything.

sources.title: Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing (arXiv 2604.22235)
sources.claim: A learning-augmented industrial robot cell autonomously performed deformable cable insertion into tight-tolerance PCB holes and soldered the connections on a live electric-motor production line, running over five hours unattended with a 99.4% quality pass rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting flexible cables into 0.3-0.6 mm clearance PCB holes and soldering them. This is the same class of manual act a broadcast technician performs when terminating and connecting signal cables, at comparable or finer precision, but only inside a fixtured production cell.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 assembly cell (ASG, a Division of Jergens Inc.)
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Commercial tabletop robotic screwdriving assembly cells with automatic screw feeders drive and torque fasteners on fixtured assemblies without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving screws to specified torque on a fixtured assembly. Rack-mounting broadcast frames and reassembling repaired chassis is the same fastener-driving act with comparable hardware, demonstrated only inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Telescent Introduces New G5 Robotic Patch Panel System - Silicon UK
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic patch panel autonomously grips, transports, cleans and mates fiber-optic connectors to reconfigure thousands of cross-connects inside its own enclosure, deployed in data centers and networks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making and breaking optical connections by physically mating connectors. Broadcast installation involves the same connector-mating act on fiber and coax, but the robot only achieves it inside a machine built around it.

sources.system: Komax Alpha 530 fully automatic crimping machine
sources.title: Automatic Crimping | Komax
sources.claim: Fully automatic wire-processing machines cut, strip, crimp terminals and insert seals on both cable ends to production quality, and integrated systems output labeled, ready-to-install cables from digital drawings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminating cable ends. Re-terminating a damaged mic or video cable is the same strip-and-terminate operation; the machine does it only with wire fed into a purpose-built station, not on a cable already installed in a rack.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic disassembly line takes in used consumer electronics and autonomously separates them into components, handling 23 different device models at 200 units per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening an electronic enclosure and extracting internal modules. Bench repair of broadcast gear begins with the same teardown of a fixtured chassis; Daisy shows it is done autonomously only on a dedicated line with the device presented to the machine.

sources.system: SoftBank robot-friendly cable-less server rack with lifter robot / CTU
sources.title: Inside Look: How SoftBank Corp. is Creating "Robot-friendly" Environments at Data Centers
sources.claim: A cableless, robot-designed server rack lets a lifter robot install or replace a server by pushing it into a slot, using camera QR-code recognition and laser positioning; the rack had to be redesigned because standard racks and their cabling defeat robotic servicing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing and replacing rack-mounted electronic equipment. It substantiates rack installation only when the rack itself is rebuilt around the machine (blind-mate cableless connectors), i.e. a purpose-built robotic environment, not a station's existing rack room.

tasks.label: Record sound onto tape or film for radio or television, checking its quality and making adjustments where necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Radio station studio: technician records a host's voice tracks or an in-studio guest interview to the DAW/console — arms channels, sets mic gain for each voice, positions the boom-mounted studio mic for the guest, hits record, watches meters for clipping/low level, listens for plosives, hum or headphone bleed, and re-records or corrects gain/EQ before the file goes to air.

TV studio production: technician records program audio for a taped show or newscast segment with several sources (lavs on talent, podium/desk mics, playback), rides faders live to the recording, monitors for mic hits, rustle and level swings, then plays back the recorded track to confirm quality and re-records or patches around a faulty channel.

Voiceover/narration/promo recording in a booth or edit suite: technician sets the talent at the booth mic, sets gain and pop filter, records the read, punches in retakes, checks the recorded track for noise, distortion and loudness compliance, and delivers a clean file.

Field/ENG or location recording: technician rigs a lav on an interviewee or handles a shotgun/handheld mic outdoors or in a borrowed room, fights wind, traffic, HVAC and RF hits, sets levels on a portable recorder, records the interview or event, checks the take on headphones and re-does or re-positions the mic as needed.

Live event/remote broadcast (sports venue, concert hall, city council chamber) recorded from a truck or flypack: technician takes pre-rigged venue and commentary mics, mixes and records the program feed, monitors the recording for level, phase and dropout problems, and adjusts during the event.

sources.system: Sound Devices 688 / 888 mixer-recorder with Dugan Automixing
sources.developer: Sound Devices / Dan Dugan Sound Design
sources.title: Dugan Automixing Debuts for the 688 Mixer/Recorder at NAB - Sound Devices
sources.claim: Sound Devices 8-Series/6-Series portable mixer-recorders record multitrack broadcast audio to media while an on-board Dugan automixer automatically and continuously manages the gains of multiple open microphones; the feature is used in broadcast television and production dialogue recording.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'record sound ... making adjustments' step: the same machine writes the recording to media and performs the moment-to-moment level adjustment across the same broadcast microphones the technician would ride by hand.

sources.title: News - Calrec
sources.claim: Calrec broadcast consoles include an automixer that automatically and dynamically adjusts individual microphone levels during live news programs to maintain a consistent program mix without an operator touching those faders.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element as 'checking its quality and making adjustments where necessary' for multi-microphone studio recording, on the identical broadcast console/mic chain.

sources.system: Interra Systems BATON with BCC (Baton Content Corrector)
sources.title: Mediacorp Elevates Broadcast Quality With Interra Systems' BATON QC Solution
sources.claim: Automated file-based QC systems deployed at broadcasters analyze recorded media for audio faults and loudness compliance and automatically correct loudness errors before the material is used on air. This is a software system, cited only for the file-verification step of the automated recording chain.
sources.transferJustification: Corresponds to 'checking its quality' on the finished recording; broadcasters accept these automated checks in place of a technician's listen-back for technical faults.

sources.system: Robotic-arm microphone array ('Lend me an Ear')
sources.title: Lend me an Ear: Speech Enhancement Using a Robotic Arm with a Microphone Array (arXiv:2602.17818)
sources.claim: A sixteen-microphone array mounted on a seven-DoF robot arm autonomously repositions itself based on the acoustic scene to improve the quality of captured speech in noisy conditions, demonstrating machine-controlled physical microphone placement driven by measured audio quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically moving a microphone to improve captured sound. It is the robotic counterpart of the technician's 'make adjustments' step, with the same objects (microphones, speech capture) but demonstrated only in a controlled lab rig.

sources.system: ARTSRAM (Autonomous Robot Twin System for Room Acoustic Measurements)
sources.title: Autonomous Robot Twin System for Room Acoustic Measurements (ARTSRAM)
sources.claim: Two mobile robots, one carrying a loudspeaker and one a microphone array, move autonomously inside a room to capture large sets of room ... response recordings, showing autonomous robotic microphone positioning and audio capture in a controlled indoor space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of a microphone and capture of audio. Transfers only to controlled rooms with a known layout; it does not judge program audio quality.

sources.system: DynaMount V1 / V2-R / X1-R robotic microphone mounts
sources.title: DynaMount Robotic Microphone Mount | Guitar Center
sources.claim: Commercially available robotic microphone mounts move a studio microphone's position and orientation, but they are driven by a human engineer over Wi-Fi from a phone or computer while listening, i.e. teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the mic-adjustment element of this task, but human-in-the-loop; cited to show that commercial microphone-positioning robotics remain operator-driven.

sources.title: KESQ-TV automates with Telemetrics | TV Tech
sources.claim: Robotic camera systems installed in television studios are unmanned on the studio floor but are commanded by an operator in the ... recalling presets, showing that the physically embodied robots deployed in broadcast facilities are camera platforms under human/preset control, not autonomous audio workers.
sources.transferJustification: Not the same task; cited as the state of physically embodied robotics inside real broadcast studios (E2), which is camera motion under operator/preset control and includes no sound-recording work.

tasks.label: Align antennae with receiving dishes to obtain the clearest signal for transmission of broadcasts from field locations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Satellite news gathering (Ku/Ka) uplink truck at a breaking-news field location — roadside shoulder, strip-mall parking lot, farm field. Technician deploys the roof-mounted 1.0–2.4 m dish, drives azimuth/elevation/polarization onto the assigned satellite, peaks on the beacon/carrier and sets cross-pol before the live window.

ENG microwave live truck at an ordinary street/neighborhood scene with a usable path: mast raised, mast-head directional antenna panned/tilted onto the station's central receive site or hilltop repeater, peaked on reported signal level/MER, held through the live shot.

ENG microwave live shot with a difficult path — urban canyon, terrain or foliage blockage, no direct line of sight. Technician hunts a bounce shot off a building face, tries alternate receive sites/repeaters, or repositions the truck until an acceptable link is found.

Scheduled remote/outside broadcast inside an institution-controlled venue (stadium, arena, convention center, fairground compound, campus lot): truck-mounted dish or tripod-mounted microwave/satellite antenna set in a pre-surveyed spot with a known clear shot, aligned and peaked before the event.

Portable flyaway / case-based terminal at a remote or awkward field site (building rooftop, mountaintop, disaster area, out-of-market assignment): technician hauls cases, assembles and levels the reflector and mount, then acquires the satellite and peaks the signal.

Receive-end work: aligning or re-aligning the directional receive antenna at the station's central receive site / tower site, or a temporary receive point set up for the event, so it is boresighted on the field truck and delivers the cleanest signal.

sources.system: AvL Model 2088 2.0m Auto-Acquisition Drive-Away Antenna with AAQ Antenna Controller
sources.date: 2026-06 (page published; auto-acquire product line long commercial)
sources.title: AvL Model 2088 2.0m Auto-Acquisition Multi-Band Drive Away Antenna - AvL Technologies
sources.claim: AvL's AAQ antenna controller on vehicle-mounted drive-away SNG/SATCOM antennas performs one-button deploy and fully automatic acquisition, including automated azimuth, elevation and cross-polarization ... using GPS, electronic compass, attitude sensors and a built-in beacon/carrier receiver.

sources.date: 2025-06 (product page); product family shipping for two decades
sources.title: 1200+ – Driveaway – C-COM Satellite Systems
sources.claim: C-COM's iNetVu 1200+ roof-mounted drive-away antenna acquires any Ku-band satellite from a parked vehicle in under two minutes with a single button press, with high-precision automated pointing.

sources.system: Frontline Communications Ford Transit SNG vans with AvL 1.2m Ka-Ku antennas (Brighthouse Networks)
sources.title: ENG Trucks Evolve With Changing Wireless Landscape | TV Tech
sources.claim: US television stations field satellite news vans built around AvL vehicle-mount Ka/Ku antennas operated from inside the truck at arbitrary field locations, confirming these motorized antennas are the working tool for this task.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment context for the same alignment act; cited only alongside the autonomous auto-acquire evidence, never as independent support.

sources.system: Troll AX3000 BAS tracking antenna with S8000 controller / DMR8000 diversity receiver
sources.title: Master and Remote Controlled Receive Site Infrastructure for Wireless ENG / XNG Contribution
sources.claim: Troll Systems' AX3000 broadcast-band (2 GHz BAS) receive antennas provide automated alignment, acquisition and tracking of ENG field transmitters, with automated calibration and push-button signal lock; Troll gear is installed in broadcast news facilities across the top 50 US markets.

sources.system: Troll MTX Series auto-tracking ground antennas
sources.title: Auto-Tracking Antenna MTX Series - Troll Systems
sources.claim: Troll MTX ground tracking antennas self-establish location, orientation and three-dimensional alignment with no operator input and then hold boresight automatically, tracking COFDM/DVB-T and other broadcast-class waveforms across UHF through Ku.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as ENG link alignment: a motorized directional antenna is boresighted on a distant counterpart and held on the peak, in the same frequency bands and waveforms (COFDM/DVB-T) used for ENG contribution.

sources.system: Troll Mini GS vehicle-mounted tracking antenna
sources.title: Vehicle mounted c2isr auto-tracking antenna system - Troll Systems
sources.claim: The vehicle-mounted Mini GS auto-tracking antenna automatically aligns itself to north to 0.15 degrees using dual-GPS and an onboard INS on stationary and moving vehicles, then acquires and holds a directional RF link autonomously in rugged, unimproved terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is auto-tracking a moving air/ground asset from a vehicle in the field; pointing a parked ENG truck's mast antenna at a fixed receive site is the strictly easier static case, using the same vehicle-mounted positioner, the same bands and the same RF peaking loop.

sources.system: C-COM iNetVu FLY-1202 1.2 m motorized flyaway with 7710 controller
sources.title: C-Com iNetVu FLY-1202 (Ku-Band) Motorized 1.2M Auto-Acquire Flyaway Antenna
sources.claim: Motorized flyaway satellite terminals auto-point and auto-acquire once erected, but the terminal itself must be hand-assembled on site by a person in roughly 15 minutes.

tasks.label: Design and modify equipment to employer specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Station engineering shop bench: fabricate custom cables, adapters and patch leads to a written spec — XLR mic/line cords, BNC coax video jumpers, D-sub/multipin breakouts, Ethernet patch cords. Tech picks wire and connectors, cuts to length, strips, solders/crimps, assembles shells and strain relief, tests continuity/return loss, labels.

Machine room / control room: design and build or rewire a 19-inch rack subsystem to employer spec — draw the signal flow, select and mount frames, patch panels and processing gear, run and dress power, coax, fiber, audio and network, terminate and label, configure devices and prove every path before air.

Bench or in-situ modification of existing equipment so it meets station requirements: install option cards or modules, change jumpers/straps and internal settings, replace or re-pin connectors, add pads, GPI/tally or level-matching interfaces, build a small interface box in a project enclosure, then verify against spec.

Shop metalwork: modify a blank rack panel, chassis or enclosure to a drawing — lay out and cut/drill/punch holes and cutouts for connectors, switches, meters and ventilation, deburr and finish, so the hardware fits the station's standard.

Design and fabricate custom mounts, brackets, camera rigs or cases and fit them to equipment in the field — a stadium camera position, a studio pedestal, an ENG vehicle interior — where fixings and clearances differ at every site.

On-site adaptation at a transmitter/tower site, remote production truck or venue: modify racks and gear to fit the space, rework RF plumbing and grounding, weatherproof an outdoor enclosure, build interface wiring for a one-off remote, with hand tools and limited access.

sources.system: Komax Omega 750 S wire assembly machine
sources.title: Komax Introduces the Omega 750 S: Revolutionizing Fully Automated Wire Harness Assembly - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Komax Omega 750 S is a ... wire-assembly machine that produces finished harnesses/leads including double-sided insertion of terminated wires into connector housings, running without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial cable/harness fabrication. A broadcast technician's custom cable job is the same physical operation set — cut to length, strip, terminate both ends into a connector body, test — on comparable wire gauges and connector housings, performed on a fixtured machine.

sources.title: Fully automatic crimping machines - Schleuniger
sources.claim: Schleuniger CrimpCenter machines perform cutting, stripping, crimping, sealing, twisting ... of wires fully automatically in a purpose-built enclosed cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wire processing. It covers the preparation and termination steps of the technician's cable-making instance (cut, strip, tin, crimp) at equal or better precision, but only with wire presented from reels inside the machine.

sources.title: Automated Enclosure Machining & Wire Processing | Rittal
sources.claim: Rittal's Wire Terminal WT C fully automatically cuts, strips, crimps and project-labels up to 36 different wires without changeover, i.e. it produces the small, job-specific wire sets used in panel and enclosure builds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: project-specific (non-mass-production) wire fabrication for control panels. It shows automatic machines can make one-off, spec-driven leads with labeling, which is what a broadcast tech does for a rack or patch job.

sources.title: Soldering Robot Lineup | Japan Unix - Automated Soldering Robot Manufacturer
sources.claim: Japan Unix supplies automated soldering robots used in production for repeatable soldered joints, including wire-to-connector and through-hole work held in fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic soldering of connectors and leads. Broadcast cable terminations (XLR solder cups, coax centre pins) are the same joint type and scale; the robots achieve it only with the connector fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Perforex machining centres | Rittal Kiesling
sources.claim: Rittal/Kiesling Perforex machining centres automatically drill, thread and mill holes and cutouts in standard enclosures and panels directly from imported CAD data — automated mechanical modification of sheet-metal hardware to a drawing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated enclosure/panel modification. A broadcast tech punching a 19-inch rack panel or chassis for connectors and switches is the same operation on the same materials and tolerances, done with the panel clamped in the machine.

sources.title: Rittal Kiesling Product portfolio
sources.claim: The Kiesling Averex wiring centre automates wiring of switchgear mounting plates — cutting, stripping, ferrule crimping, routing wires through ducts and connecting them to components — but works from a complete ECAD dataset on flat mounting plates with standard terminal components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cabinet wiring. It is the closest system to a broadcast rack build, but handles only ferruled single wires to screw terminals on flat plates — not mounting 19-inch gear, coax/fiber terminations, configuration or signal proving.

tasks.label: Organize recording sessions and prepare areas, such as radio booths and television stations, for recording.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Radio/podcast booth prep at a station for an interview or voice session: adjust boom mic arms and pop filters for 1-4 guests of differing heights, connect and route XLR and headphone cables, position chairs, set out scripts/water, seat and coach guests, ride a level check, arm the recorder, then reset and tidy the booth for the next booking.

TV studio prep for a daily newscast or taped segment: verify camera positions and floor marks, check and adjust studio lighting on the set areas, dress the set/desk with props and monitors, fit anchors and guests with lav mics and IFB earpieces, load and test the prompter, and run comms/mic checks with the control room before record.

Control-room / technical prep for a scheduled recording: patch audio and video on the patchbay, route sources, verify record paths and media, set tone/bars and slates, confirm levels and monitoring, coordinate record start with the studio floor, and label/log the session.

Preparing a recording area at an institution-controlled venue away from the studio (press-conference room, arena press box, council chamber, house of worship, auditorium): place mics on lectern/table or tie into a mult box, run and dress cable, set up tripods and cameras, adjust supplemental lighting, and test levels and feeds before the session.

Field/ENG remote setup at an uncontrolled outdoor location (sidewalk, parking lot, storm scene): pick and clear a spot, set tripod and camera, deploy light kit and battery/power, mic the reporter, run cabling, raise the mast or point the satellite/cellular uplink, and adapt to weather, ambient noise and passersby before the live shot or record.

sources.system: Autonomous robot capability assessment (covering Gemini Robotics 1.5 cable insertion, CATL connector-insertion humanoids)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: Independent 2026 capability assessment of autonomous robots finds cable/connector insertion and multi-step assembly still have significant limits outside the lab, and that demonstrations depend on controlled setups and heavy resets — i.e., no general-purpose autonomous robot performs the varied manipulation (cable plugging, mic and stand adjustment, object arranging) that studio prep requires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = connecting cables/connectors and multi-step assembly, the manipulation core of preparing a booth or studio (XLR/patch cords, mic mounts). The assessment places these at 'significant limits in lab', so they do not transfer to whole-session studio prep.

sources.system: Furio Robo / Furio+ robotic camera systems
sources.title: Ross Video Acquires FX-Motion Robotic Camera Systems — Ross Video
sources.claim: Robotic camera pedestals and dollies are commercially deployed in TV news studios, but they position cameras via operator-commanded preset shot and motion-path recalls — a single sub-step of studio preparation, under human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = pre-setting camera positions in the studio before a show, part of TV studio prep; it covers only camera placement and is operator-driven, so it does not carry over to the rest of the prep.

sources.system: Vinten FH-188+ robotic pedestals / FH-155 heads with Startracker, HD-VRC control
sources.title: Case Study: Nine Network installs Vinten robotics in Sydney studio - NewscastStudio
sources.claim: A major broadcaster equipped a new studio with robotic pedestals and heads that map the studio floor once and are then remotely controlled with precise repeatable positioning — deployed studio floor robotics, still commanded by operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = positioning studio cameras for a show. Shows the state of in-studio robotics: motion of installed camera mounts only, no handling of mics, cables, set pieces or talent.

sources.title: Sponsored: Robotic Deployments Are Transforming Local News | TV Tech
sources.claim: A large-market US news station deployed a robotic camera arm in its news studio ... operator with an automated, repeatable alternative — again limited to camera motion within an installed studio.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = studio camera movement. Demonstrates that installed broadcast robotics handle camera trajectories, not the physical preparation of a recording area.

sources.system: AW-SF100 auto tracking software with Panasonic PTZ cameras
sources.title: PTZ Camera Auto Tracking Software | Panasonic North America
sources.claim: Auto-tracking software drives PTZ cameras to frame presenters autonomously in classrooms, lecture halls, auditoriums and conference rooms — autonomous camera framing during a recording, not preparation of the space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = unattended camera operation in institution-controlled rooms. It removes an operator during recording but performs none of the mic placement, cabling, lighting or room setup that this task requires.

sources.system: G4NG / G5 robotic patch-panel (automated optical cross-connect)
sources.title: SBIR Success Story – Telescent Inc.
sources.claim: Robotic fiber patch panels autonomously make and break connectorized links in purpose-built racks and have been deployed commercially for years — the closest machine analogue to patching a signal chain, but confined to a fixture-built rack of standardized connectors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = physically reconfiguring signal-path connections. Comparable objects (connectorized cords) and precision, but only inside a purpose-built rack; it does not cover record-path verification, level/mic checks or floor coordination.

tasks.label: Determine the number, type, and approximate location of microphones needed for best sound recording or transmission quality, and position them appropriately.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: TV/streaming studio show setup (news set, talk show, sportscast): technician decides how many mics and which types for anchors, guests and panel, fits wireless lavalier or earset mics on people's clothing/hair, dresses and hides cables, adds desk or hanging mics, and checks each before air in a station studio.

Radio/podcast studio show prep: technician sets the host's and guests' dynamic or large-diaphragm broadcast mics on boom arms at a fixed on-air desk, chooses count and type for the number of participants, sets distance/angle/pop filters, and adjusts placement during a level check.

ENG/field remote: technician arrives at an on-location interview or live standup (street, office, home, storm scene), decides between handheld stick mic, wireless lav on the subject, and shotgun on stand or pole, adds windscreens, positions to reject traffic/HVAC/wind noise, then rigs and checks.

Live remote event or sports broadcast in a venue: technician plans and deploys a multi-mic plot across an arena, stadium, church or auditorium - announcer headsets, lectern mics, crowd/effects mics, parabolic or field mics, stage mics - clamping, taping, hanging and cabling each into place before the show.

In-studio production session with several sources: technician selects and places multiple mics on an ensemble, instruments, or a round-table discussion in a station production studio, iterating placement by ear to get the desired blend and to control bleed and room reflections.

Single-voice close-mic setup in a fixed announce/voice-over booth: one known mic type on a fixed stand or boom in a treated booth, placed at the standard distance and angle from the talent's mouth for a promo, voice track, or transmitter announce.

sources.title: Near Field Scanner System (NFS)
sources.claim: Klippel's Near Field Scanner is a commercial system that robotically moves a measurement microphone to computed positions around a stationary sound source and runs the whole measurement automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loudspeaker measurement. The physical act is identical in kind to this task's core act - placing a microphone at a determined location and angle relative to a fixed sound source - and the NFS does it unattended with far tighter precision (<1 deg angular resolution) than broadcast mic placement requires, inside a purpose-built scanning rig.

sources.title: A New Approach to Loudspeaker Measurements | audioXpress
sources.claim: The NFS scanning process uses robotics to carry the microphone around the loudspeaker while the source stays fixed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loudspeaker directivity measurement; establishes that the microphone positioning itself is machine-executed by a robotic mechanism around a fixtured source rather than done by hand.

sources.system: Multi-robotic acoustic measurement setup (two Staubli TX2-60L arms with microphone and speaker end-effectors)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Digital Building Technologies / Robotic Fabrication Lab)
sources.title: A data acquisition setup for data driven acoustic design (arXiv:2109.12014)
sources.claim: Two industrial robot arms, one carrying a microphone and one a loudspeaker, autonomously position the microphone at many locations over a fixtured test panel inside an acoustically shielded room to acquire impulse responses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: architectural-acoustics measurement. It demonstrates repeated, unattended robotic placement of a microphone at a programmed set of positions relative to a fixtured source in a purpose-built robotic cell - the same manipulation and precision class as setting a mic on a stand relative to a source.

sources.system: Robotic-arm reconfigurable microphone array ("Lend me an Ear")
sources.title: Lend me an Ear: Speech Enhancement Using a Robotic Arm with a Microphone Array (arXiv:2602.17818)
sources.claim: A 16-microphone array on a 7-DoF manipulator localizes a talker by sound and vision and then autonomously moves into the pose that best captures that talker's voice in noise, outperforming fixed arrays and a static shotgun mic on SI-SDR and word error rate.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous: the system decides the approximate best microphone location for capturing a speaking source and physically moves the mics there; experiments ran in a controlled lab with a fixtured loudspeaker-plus-printed-face standing in for the talker.

sources.system: DynaMount V2-R / X1-R robotic mic mounts
sources.title: Dynamount V2-R robotic microphone mount - KMR Audio
sources.claim: Commercially available robotic microphone mounts used in recording studios are remote-controlled by the engineer with recallable presets; they do not choose placement themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (studio mic placement), but control is continuous remote operation by the engineer, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it documents the commercial state of mic-positioning robotics.

sources.system: Ross Video Furio / CamBot studio robotics with Vision[Ai]ry tracking
sources.title: Studio Robotic Control | Centralized Camera Automation - Ross Video
sources.claim: Robotic camera pedestals, dollies and heads with AI face/body tracking are routinely deployed in working TV news studios to move capture devices to shot positions under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning a capture device inside a broadcast studio (E2). Transfer is only partial - these platforms move cameras on pedestals and tracks, never place a microphone inches from a mouth or instrument, fit body mics, or choose mic types - so it does not substantiate the mic task at E2.

tasks.label: Set up and operate portable field transmission equipment outside the studio.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: TV news ENG live shot from a marked news van at a spot-news scene (street, roadside, parking lot near a fire/crash/standoff): pick a spot clear of wires, level/stabilize the van, raise the pneumatic mast with microwave dish or deploy the vehicle-mounted Ku/Ka dish, aim/acquire the path to the receive site or satellite, run camera/audio/IFB cables to the reporter, set levels, and monitor and adjust the signal through the live hits.

Portable IP/bonded-cellular live shot (LiveU/TVU backpack, portable satellite terminal or Starlink-fed kit) from a field location, often one-person-band: mount the transmitter to the camera, power it, bring up the link, register with the station receiver, set the encoder profile, and babysit bitrate/latency and audio during the hit.

Scheduled remote at a controlled venue (city hall press conference, courthouse, convention center, stadium media position): position the truck in the assigned media area, run cable into the building, patch audio from the press mult box, set a camera position, raise the mast or deploy the dish, book the space segment/receive path, and hold the feed for the scheduled window.

Multi-camera sports or major-event remote at a stadium/arena: hours-long build of a fly-pack or OB compound - camera positions, cable and fiber runs, RF cameras and comms, audio - then establishing the transmission path (uplink truck, fiber or bonded/IP backhaul) and operating and troubleshooting it through the event.

Radio station remote broadcast from a car dealership, store or county fair: unload and assemble the remote kit (tent/table, mixer, mics, headphones, monitor receiver, wireless IP codec or cellular STL and antenna), establish and verify the link back to the station, and run the audio through the live breaks.

tasks.label: Regulate volume level and sound quality during recording sessions, using control consoles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Music recording studio session: engineer sets input gain/trim per mic and DI, rides fader levels and monitors headroom, adjusts EQ/compression and monitor mix for a tracking band over a multi-hour session on an analog or digital console.

Podcast, audiobook, or voiceover session in a small studio: engineer sets and rides levels for one to four talkers, watches for clipping, sibilance and room noise, and applies corrective EQ/compression on a small mixer or interface control surface.

Live broadcast or sports remote from a production truck/OB van: engineer balances announcer mics, effects mics, and playback sources in real time on a large-format broadcast console, meeting loudness specs while conditions change unpredictably.

Film/TV production sound or ADR/Foley recording: mixer regulates levels on a location mixer or dubbing console across dialogue tracks and boom/lav channels while the scene runs, adapting to actor dynamics and ambient noise.

Live event, house-of-worship, or theater performance recorded to multitrack: engineer regulates the record-feed levels and tone on the FOH/monitor console during the performance, correcting for feedback, unexpected sources and varying performer dynamics.

tasks.label: Record speech, music, and other sounds on recording media, using recording equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Music tracking session in a commercial recording studio: engineer chooses and physically positions mics on a drum kit, guitar amps and a vocalist in the live room, plugs XLR lines into the wall panel, sets preamp gain, then runs the DAW/console to capture multitrack takes, punch-ins and overdubs over a multi-hour session while talking back to performers.

Spoken-word capture in a studio booth (voiceover, audiobook, podcast, ADR): talent seated at a fixed large-diaphragm mic with pop filter; engineer adjusts mic height/distance for the talent, sets gain, arms and records takes, listens for clipping, plosives, HVAC and mouth noise, punches in fixes, slates and delivers the recorded files.

Location production sound for film/TV/documentary/ENG: mixer rigs lavalier mics and transmitters on talent, coordinates a boom, sets a plant mic, and records multitrack to a field recorder with timecode in varying uncontrolled locations (homes, offices, streets), fighting wind, traffic and HVAC noise.

Live event capture in a venue (concert, theater, house of worship, sports): engineer places and patches stage/instrument/ambience/crowd mics via stage boxes, sets gains at soundcheck, then records a multitrack of the live performance to a recorder or DAW while an audience and performers occupy the space.

Recording speech in a fixed-installation facility studio (TV/radio broadcast booth, corporate or campus studio): permanently installed mics and console; engineer fits/positions the presenter's mic, sets levels, arms tracks, records the segment to server/media and monitors for faults during the take.

Sound-effects and Foley capture on a studio Foley stage or dedicated SFX room: engineer positions mics close to props and pits, sets high-headroom gain for transients, records numerous short takes of footsteps, cloth and prop sounds performed by a Foley artist, naming and logging each file.

sources.title: Near Field Scanner System (NFS) — Klippel
sources.claim: Klippel's Near Field Scanner is a commercial robotic system that positions a measurement microphone around a fixtured sound source and captures the radiated sound automatically and unattended, in a room used as a purpose-built measurement setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated acoustic measurement. It performs the same physical act as the core of this task - placing a microphone at chosen positions relative to a source and capturing the resulting audio to media with automatic gain/delay handling - at sub-degree positioning precision, but on test stimuli rather than production performances.

sources.title: A New Approach to Loudspeaker Measurements | audioXpress
sources.claim: Trade-press description confirming the NFS uses robotics to move the microphone around the source while measuring sound: autonomous microphone placement plus audio capture.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Klippel product page: robotic microphone positioning and audio capture in a fixtured cell corresponds to the placement-and-capture core of recording, though the captured content is a test signal.

sources.title: Robot-controlled acoustic holography | Brüel & Kjær - HBK
sources.claim: Bruel & Kjaer (HBK) supplies robot-controlled acoustic measurement systems in which a robot moves a microphone array over a device under test in a laboratory cell and records the sound field; deployed at GN ReSound.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated near-field acoustic measurement. Transfers to the physical portion of recording - a machine moving a microphone to specified positions relative to a source and capturing audio to media - inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: HEAD acoustics end-of-line test systems (AQuire V4 / conTEST)
sources.title: End-of-Line Testing - Versatile, precise, cost-effective with HEAD acoustics
sources.claim: End-of-line acoustic test installations run fully automated capture and evaluation of speech and tone signals through devices under test on production lines: unattended audio recording plus automatic detection of level/noise/distortion faults in purpose-built cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line acoustic testing. It shows machine-controlled capture of speech and tone signals to media together with automatic detection of audio faults - the monitoring judgement a recordist applies - but only for fixtured devices presented on a line.

sources.system: Ross Furio / CamBot robotic camera systems with Vision[Ai]ry tracking
sources.title: Ross Video robotic camera systems elevate sports broadcasting to new heights — Ross Video
sources.claim: Ross Video robotic camera systems with Vision[Ai]ry automatically track and follow on-air talent and players in broadcast studios and sports venues; the same catalogue's audio automation (Lama AutoMix) is software mixing, and no robotic microphone placement or boom-operating product is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated aiming of a capture device at talent inside a structured broadcast facility. It shows what exists at E2 for video capture and, by contrast, that no equivalent robotic microphone-placement or boom-operating capability exists for audio.

sources.title: Helix-02 humanoid robot handles full 8-hour factory work shifts
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 humanoids ran multi-hour fully autonomous shifts of package handling and label scanning in a warehouse, showing general autonomous manipulation in a structured facility, but no audio-engineering work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse package handling. Bears only on generic manipulation (grasping, placing, operating simple controls) in a facility; it does not substantiate microphone selection or placement, gain staging by ear, or take monitoring, so it cannot lift any instance above E1.

tasks.label: Set up, test, and adjust recording equipment for recording sessions and live performances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial recording studio session setup: engineer carries and places mic stands, mounts and aims multiple mics on a drum kit, guitar cabs and vocal position, runs and plugs XLR cables into wall panels/stagebox, patches to preamps at the patchbay, sets gain, builds headphone cue mixes, checks each channel for signal/phase/noise, and repositions mics by ear until the tone is right.

Live music venue (club, theater, house of worship) show setup: reading a stage plot, placing wedges/IEM packs, mic stands, DI boxes, drum mics, running snake/stagebox lines and power, ringing out monitors, line check and soundcheck adjustments, then fast changeovers between acts on a crowded stage.

Corporate/conference event audio in a hotel ballroom or convention center: setting lectern and table mics, distributing and testing wireless handhelds/lavaliers on presenters, coordinating RF frequencies, cabling to a mixer and to the PA/record feed, and running level checks during rehearsal.

Broadcast/sports remote setup at a stadium or arena: placing effects and parabolic mics around the field, rigging commentary positions with headsets and talkback, running long cable pulls and fiber to the production truck, testing every line and adjusting levels before air.

Location/field recording at an uncontrolled site (documentary interview in a private home, podcast at a client's office, film location): rigging lavaliers on talent, setting a boom, placing a portable recorder/mixer, working around furniture, HVAC noise and unknown power, testing wireless links and setting levels.

Pre-show check of a permanently installed system (podcast studio, church booth, campus lecture hall): powering up the rack, swapping batteries, verifying each installed mic and line with test tones/talkback, checking playback and record paths, and trimming levels before the session starts.

sources.system: DynaMount X1-R / V2-R robotic mic mount
sources.title: DynaMount X1-R Robotic Microphone Mount - Vintage King
sources.claim: The nearest commercial automation of microphone setup, DynaMount robotic mic mounts, are motorized mounts that a human engineer drives remotely from the control room; they do not decide or execute placement autonomously and do not handle stands, cabling or gain.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the 'adjust microphone position' sub-step of this task, but it is remote-controlled by the engineer, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Self-deploying robotic microphone swarm (smart-speaker mic swarm)
sources.title: Robotic Mic Swarm Helps Pull Voices Out Of Crowded Room Of Multiple Speakers | Hackaday
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous microphone-placing robots demonstrated are a research swarm of seven tabletop robots that self-deploy to form a mic array for speech separation; scope is limited to positioning tiny built-in mics on a table, with no stands, cabling, patching or level setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous microphone deployment for capture. Transfer fails because the robots only place their own miniature onboard mics on a flat table; they cannot mount studio mics on stands, run and plug cables, patch, or verify and adjust gain.

sources.system: Robotized acoustic measurement arm for sound field estimation
sources.title: Automated Sound Field Estimation combining robotized acoustic measurements and the boundary elements method | Acta Acustica
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic audio work in labs is confined to acoustic measurement: a robotic arm moves a microphone to programmed 3D coordinates and captures responses, producing measurement data rather than a session-ready recording setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated microphone positioning plus signal capture/test. Transfer fails: the arm follows pre-programmed coordinates in a fixed rig, does no cabling, gain staging, or tonal judgment for a live source, and its output is a measurement, not accepted session setup.

sources.system: Skill-based robotic connector installation (force-controlled search and insertion)
sources.title: Automotive Wire Harness Connector Installation Using Skill-Based Robotic Programming
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic connector insertion, the closest analogue to plugging up a signal chain, remains a fixtured industrial research capability with success rates well below what a working engineer must achieve.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating electrical connectors, as when plugging XLR/TRS lines. Even in a fixtured automotive cell success is 76.7%, far below the near-perfect signal-path reliability an engineer must deliver, and it covers none of the mic placement or testing steps.

sources.system: Telescent G5 Robotic Patch Panel / Network Topology Manager
sources.title: G5 Network Topology Manager (NTM) Product Data Sheet
sources.claim: Robotic patching of signal cables is automated only inside purpose-built machines: Telescent's robotic patch panel re-routes fiber connections within its own enclosure in data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous re-patching of connectors. Transfer fails: the machine only manipulates its own captive fiber jumpers inside a sealed rack; it cannot place microphones, run cable in a room, or test and adjust audio levels.

sources.title: Helix-02 humanoid robot handles full 8-hour factory work shifts
sources.claim: State-of-the-art general-purpose humanoids running long autonomous shifts are demonstrated on parcel sorting in warehouse-style facilities, not on multi-step equipment setup, cabling or acoustic judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-duration autonomous manipulation in a structured facility. Transfer fails: demonstrated objects are packages on a conveyor, not mic stands, fragile microphones, deformable XLR cables, or console controls requiring auditory verification.

instances.label: Small-format PA strike in a club, bar, school gym or house of worship after a show: unplug and coil 20-40 XLR/Speakon/powercon cables (over-under, velcro'd), break down two tops on poles plus subs, collapse mic and speaker stands, pack mixer, wireless racks and mics into padded bags/road cases, pull gaff tape and cable ramps, wheel/carry gear out to a van, often late at night with patrons and other crew still in the room.

Corporate/conference AV strike in a hotel ballroom or convention center: power down and pack DSP/amp racks and wireless mic systems, pull taped-down cable runs and snakes from under carpet, break down powered speakers on sticks and lectern mics, inventory and case everything, stack carts and load at the loading dock inside a fixed strike window under venue/union rules.

Arena/large concert load-out: de-rig flown line arrays lowered on motor hoists, disconnect and stack subs and amp racks, strike monitor world and stage boxes, coil hundreds of feet of multicore, fiber and power cable, close and latch heavy road cases, and push and stack them into semi trailers under intense time pressure with a large crew working simultaneously.

Theatre, recording studio or broadcast-remote strike in a controlled facility: pull mics, booms and DI boxes off a set, field or stage; de-cable triax/fiber and audio snakes back to the truck or control room; wipe and case delicate microphones per inventory; restore the room or compound to its normal state for the next production.

Outdoor festival, street fair, wedding tent or on-location shoot: teardown on grass, gravel or mud in wind or rain, uneven ground and improvised layouts that differ every site; unplug and coil weather-exposed cable, break down stands and tented FOH, hand-carry or dolly gear across unpaved ground to trucks parked wherever access allows.

sources.title: F.02 Contributed to the Production of 30,000 Cars at BMW
sources.claim: Figure 02 humanoids ran an 11-month production deployment at BMW Spartanburg doing sheet-metal pick-and-place into welding fixtures, with a target of zero human interventions per shift — the state of the art for factory humanoid manipulation is a single repetitive rigid-part step in a fixtured cell, not multi-object teardown, cable coiling, or case packing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive rigid-part loading into fixtures. It shows what a deployed humanoid can do in a purpose-built cell (one known part, one known pose, 5 mm tolerance), and by contrast does not cover disconnecting connectors, coiling flexible cable, latching cases, or carrying heterogeneous gear out of a venue.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cardboard boxes from trailers and containers onto a flexible conveyor in DHL warehouses, handling mixed stacks and fallen boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving cases in and out of a trailer, the truck-loading step of a load-out. Transfer is limited: Stretch handles only vacuum-grippable uniform cardboard cartons in a warehouse dock, not wheeled road cases, speaker cabinets, stands, or any cable work, so it cannot deliver the whole teardown instance.

sources.title: Rocsys and ICT Group roll out hands-free EV charging for ports
sources.claim: Rocsys' vision-guided robotic charging arms autonomously open a charge port, plug in a heavy charging cable, and unplug it without human intervention at ports and vehicle depots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous disconnection of a cable connector, the first step of any teardown. Transfer is narrow: one known connector type at a roughly known pose on a purpose-built stall, versus dozens of heterogeneous XLR/Speakon/powercon/fiber connections plus coiling and packing.

sources.developer: academic (Cao et al., Advanced Intelligent Systems)
sources.title: Shape Control of Elastic Deformable Linear Objects for Robotic Cable Assembly
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation of cables (deformable linear objects) — the core of AV teardown, where every cable must be unplugged, coiled over-under and secured — remains a laboratory research problem of shape control with dual arms, with no deployed system that coils and stows working cable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cable handling. It substantiates the negative: as of 2026 autonomous cable manipulation is demonstrated only as lab shape-control on fixtured benches, far short of coiling, velcro-strapping and casing dozens of production cables at crew speed.

sources.title: New Helix Video Shows Robot Loading and Unloading Dishwasher Pretty Damn Well
sources.claim: Figure's most advanced general-purpose home manipulation as of early 2026 is a four-minute autonomous dishwasher loading/unloading sequence in a staged kitchen — a single-scene demo, not sustained multi-object breakdown and load-out work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose household object manipulation. Shows the 2026 frontier of humanoid autonomy in human spaces is minutes-long, single-appliance work with rigid dishware, which does not reach an hours-long strike involving cables, stands, heavy cabinets and truck loading.

tasks.label: Convert video and audio recordings into digital formats for editing or archiving.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: File-based ingest and conversion in a studio/post facility: engineer receives camera cards, recorder SSDs or client file deliveries, mounts the media or pulls files from a server, verifies checksums, transcodes to house editing codecs and archival masters (WAV/BWF, ProRes/DNx, JPEG2000/MXF), and parks results on shared storage or LTO. Handling is limited to inserting removable media; the conversion itself is software.

Small-batch transfer of cassette- and disc-based carriers in a studio or dub room: a client brings a handful of DATs, compact cassettes, VHS/Betacam/U-matic cassettes, MiniDiscs, CDs or DVDs; the engineer picks the right deck, cleans/checks the carrier, sets levels, captures in real time while monitoring, then trims, labels and exports files for editing or archive.

Mass migration project at an archive, library or broadcast facility: hundreds to thousands of barcoded videocassettes or audio carriers pulled from vaults, transferred on parallel stations around the clock, with automated signal/quality analysis, checksums, technical metadata and delivery to a digital repository.

Fragile or obsolete non-cassette carriers: 1/4-inch and 2-inch open-reel tape (threading, sticky-shed baking, splice repair, azimuth/EQ/speed decisions), lacquer discs, 78s and LPs (cleaning, stylus and playback-curve selection), wire and cylinder recordings, optical film soundtracks. Each item is inspected and transferred by hand with conservation judgment.

On-location digitization: engineer travels to a client's office, church, school or event venue with a portable A/D rig, patches into whatever legacy machines or console outputs are there, sets levels under uncontrolled conditions, captures to a laptop/recorder, and delivers files.

tasks.label: Assess safety of wiring or equipment set-up to determine the risk of fire or electrical shock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Film/TV soundstage: before power-up, the electrician walks the temporary lighting power system — company-switch or distro tie-in, feeder and extension runs, cam-lok/Bates/Socapex connections, ground path, per-phase load balance — handling cables, checking for nicked jackets, pinch points, loose or hot connectors, and metering voltage/polarity to judge fire and shock risk.

Location shoot at a practical (house, warehouse, street, exterior): assess generator bonding or house-power tie-in, capacity of residential circuits being tapped, ungrounded two-prong outlets, GFCI need, cables run through damp ground or doorways, and hot fixtures near drapes/combustibles; conditions differ at every site and change with weather.

Theatre or live-music venue: pre-show electrical check of dimmer racks and feeders, multicable and breakouts, moving-light and LED fixture power, verifying ground continuity on metal fixture bodies overhead, feeling/scanning for heating connectors and checking that nothing is overloaded before the house opens.

Corporate event, trade show, or outdoor festival stage: temporary distro fed by generator or venue power in a tent/field/parking lot; assess weather exposure and wet conditions, ground-fault protection, cable ramps and crowd exposure, daisy-chained power on truss, and judge whether the rig is safe to energize with the public present.

Shop / rental-house or staging-area prep: bench check of the gear before it ships or is hung — inspect and test cables, adapters, Socapex looms, fixtures and dimmer modules for insulation faults, missing or open ground, broken strain relief and damaged connectors, tagging out anything that fails.

sources.system: Intec Automation automated HiPot/resistance testing machine cell
sources.title: Automated Resistance and HiPot Testing to Detect Conductive Failures in Circuits
sources.claim: Intec Automation builds automated machine cells that perform HiPot (dielectric withstand) and resistance testing on circuits/panels with vacuum conveyor transport, vision registration and a multi-axis gantry, recording results and automatically rejecting failing units without operators performing the validation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line electrical safety verification. Dielectric-withstand and resistance testing is the standard machine determination of shock/fire risk in wiring; it transfers to bench testing of lighting cables and fixtures presented in a fixture, though the DUTs are boards/panels rather than heavy entertainment cable, and the cell does not judge jacket damage that is still electrically sound.

sources.system: Vitrek 95X / V7X electrical safety test systems
sources.title: Advancing Electrical Safety Testing for Automated Production Environments
sources.claim: Programmable electrical-safety testers (Vitrek 95X/V7X) combine insulation resistance, ground bond and AC/DC hipot into single automated routines integrated with production line control, giving pass/fail safety verdicts at line rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical safety qualification of assembled electrical products. Ground-bond and insulation tests are exactly the measurements a technician's shock/fire judgment rests on, and can be executed under machine control when the item is fixtured in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: Modular automated cable harness testing system (Purdue Fort Wayne)
sources.developer: Bi et al., Purdue University Fort Wayne
sources.title: Automation of Electrical Cable Harnesses Testing (Robotics 2018, 7(1), 1)
sources.claim: A fixtured automated cable-harness test system with an actuated spring-pin array and PLC control tested continuity, insulation and dielectric breakdown across many harness variants on actual production parts, flagging defects automatically; operators mount the plugs in the fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pass/fail testing of cable assemblies. Objects (multi-conductor cables with varied plug types) closely match lighting cable stock; the machine's test execution and defect classification are automatic, with fixtured presentation supplied by the cell, matching the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: How Spot Helps the Energy & Natural Resources Sector
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous thermal-scan and gauge-reading inspection rounds at Consumers Energy electrical substations, with anomaly detection flagging high-heat conditions so a human is dispatched to remediate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ thermal inspection of electrical equipment for overheating (a fire-risk indicator). It covers only one slice of the technician's assessment on fixed, pre-mapped assets in a fenced substation; it does not inspect newly built temporary wiring, verify grounding or connector integrity, or judge load and routing, and a human is still dispatched to act.

sources.title: ANYbotics Total Funding at $150 Million after Climate Investments Joins to Scale Autonomous Inspection in Hazardous Sites
sources.claim: ANYbotics reports over 200 ANYmal robots conducting thousands of weekly autonomous inspections at energy and industrial sites, navigating complex facility layouts to detect overheating and other anomalies on plant assets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds detecting overheating equipment. Deployments are on permanent, pre-mapped plant assets along taught routes; nothing in the evidence shows assessment of a newly erected temporary power distribution and cable rig, so it does not carry over to this task.
