tasks.label: Disassemble and store equipment after performances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-show strike at a regional theater or performing arts center: after the final performance the crew lowers electrics or works from catwalks/personnel lifts, unclamps 40-100 conventional and LED fixtures from pipes and truss with wrenches, pulls color frames and gobos, disconnects and coils stage-pin/Edison and DMX cable, packs fixtures into carts and road cases, and shelves them in the venue's lighting storage room, usually overnight under time pressure.

Arena or amphitheater concert load-out on tour: motorized hoists bring truss to the deck, crew unclamp moving heads and strip them into dollies and foam-lined road cases, coil socapex/powerCON/data lines, break down ground-support towers and side fills, then roll cases through a crowded loading dock and pack semi-trailers on a 3-5 hour overnight clock in low light with a mixed local/tour crew.

Film/TV location wrap: at a house, street, office or practical location the electrics crew strikes HMIs, LED panels and softboxes, collapses C-stands, combo stands and speed-rail, folds silks, flags and frames, wraps distro, banded cable and stingers, and carts everything back into the lighting truck; layout, terrain and access differ at every site.

TV studio or soundstage wrap: fixtures are pulled from the grid or pipe from catwalks or via pantographs in a controlled studio, cables are coiled and hung, and fixtures are returned to labeled racks, carts and shelves in the studio's lighting store.

Small event, corporate AV, house-of-worship or school gig: pack up battery uplights, tripod and crank-up stands, short trussing, a console and DMX runs into a handful of cases and totes and roll them into the venue's storage closet or a van.

sources.title: Apple adds Earth Day donations to trade-in and recycling program - Apple
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy is a purpose-built, commercially operating automated disassembly line that takes apart whole consumer devices at high rate, removing fasteners and separating and sorting modules into bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-life product disassembly. It is the same operation class as striking a lighting rig brought to a machine - unfasten, separate a known set of models into components, and sort them into containers - performed in a purpose-built cell, though on far smaller workpieces.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly platform (dual-arm cell with unscrewing system and vision localisation)
sources.title: Robotic Disassembly Platform for Disassembly of a Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicle Battery: A Case Study
sources.claim: A robotic disassembly platform for a plug-in hybrid EV battery pack autonomously locates and unscrews threaded fasteners under positional uncertainty, changes nutrunner adapters, and handles heavy modules, though full pack-to-module autonomy was not achieved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolting and removing heavy modules from a frame in a fixtured cell. Fixture strike is the same motion class - loosening a clamp bolt with a wrench and lifting a 10-30 kg rigid unit clear - at comparable scale and precision.

sources.system: Rocsys Steward / M1 automatic connection device
sources.title: Rocsys launches integrated platform to enable hands-free charging for autonomous mobility - Charged EVs
sources.claim: Rocsys Steward autonomously mates and un-mates high-power charging connectors on vehicles in commercial port and robotaxi-depot deployments, including opening the port, plugging in, and unplugging without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided mating/unmating of a bulky power connector. Striking a rig requires unplugging power and data connectors of similar size and force; this shows a named system doing that reliably in service, when connector geometry is known in advance.

sources.system: Ramatech ring coiling machines / FHOPE automatic cable coiling and tying machine
sources.date: product pages accessed 2026-07 (machines in commercial sale for years)
sources.title: winding and tying cable rings - Ramatech
sources.claim: Commercial ring-coiling machines automatically wind cut lengths of cable into compact coils and tie them, unattended, in purpose-built production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coiling and tying cable. Coiling stage power and DMX runs is the same deformable-object operation at similar diameters; these purpose-built machines do it unattended when the cable is fed to them, which is exactly the E1 presentation assumption.

sources.system: survey of robotic disassembly systems for electrical cable connectors
sources.title: Robotic Disassembly of Electrical Cable Connectors: A Critical Review
sources.claim: A 2026 review finds that non-destructive removal of arbitrary electrical cable connectors and harnesses is still an unresolved problem for automated disassembly, limiting fully autonomous teardown of varied, unknown assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/limiting evidence for the cable-handling portion of strike work: it shows autonomy holds only where connector type and pose are known and presented, not for arbitrary tangled cable found in the field.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Robots deployed in structured human work facilities today handle uniform cases and totes - Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed by DHL for container and trailer unloading of boxes, and Agility's Digit moves totes at GXO - but neither performs equipment disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving cases inside an institution-controlled facility (E2). It covers only the transport-and-stow fraction of strike work; no cited E2-deployed system unclamps fixtures overhead, coils cable, or packs road cases.

tasks.label: Install color effects or image patterns, such as color filters, onto lighting fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Theatre/venue conventional rig: technician slides pre-cut color gels mounted in metal color frames into the accessory slot on the front of ERS, Fresnel and PAR fixtures and closes the retaining/safety clip; dozens to hundreds of units per hang, done on a prep table or on the pipe from a ladder or personnel lift, with fixtures at varying angles and sometimes hot.

Gobo/image-pattern installation: seat a steel or glass gobo in the correct gobo holder in the correct orientation (pattern reversed, coated side out), slide the holder into the ERS gate slot, rotate it to the required angle and add accessories (donut, top hat, iris); typically done at height during or after focus on a hung fixture.

Film/TV soundstage: gaffer/lighting tech adds color correction and diffusion to lamp heads - sliding gel frames into the filter holders of Fresnels/HMIs, clipping cut diffusion to barn doors with C-47 clothespins, taping or snapping gel/diffusion onto LED panel frames; heads on stands, on the greenbed or on the perms, changed repeatedly between setups.

Touring/corporate arena or ballroom load-in: gel frames and gobos installed in conventional fixtures pre-rigged on trusses lying on the deck (and some after the truss is flown), plus loading color-scroller strings into scrollers; crowded deck, tight load-in schedule, mixed inventory of fixture types.

On-location shoot: gelling practicals and small heads inside a found house/office and taping CTO/ND/diffusion over window glass; gel cut to size on the spot with scissors, then clipped, taped or frame-mounted in whatever position the location allows.

Lighting shop / prep bench: cutting gel sheets from stock to frame size, loading gel into frames and labeling them, assembling scroller strings, and prepping gobo holders for a show or rental order at a bench in the shop.

sources.system: ABB FlexPicker pick-and-place cell with Cognex In-Sight vision (integrator QComp) at Ruud Lighting
sources.developer: ABB Robotics / QComp Technologies (user: Ruud Lighting)
sources.title: Robots Light the Way to Faster Assembly | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: An automated ABB FlexPicker cell with Cognex vision at Ruud Lighting identifies, picks, orients and places plastic optical lenses into LED light-engine (fixture) assemblies, where lens type and orientation determine the emitted light distribution - the same kind of 'install the right optical element, correctly oriented, onto a luminaire' operation as installing a gel or gobo, performed in a purpose-built cell with parts fed by bowl feeder and air track.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing optical elements onto a lighting fixture assembly. Comparable objects (small optical parts whose orientation changes the beam), comparable precision (right compartment at the right angle), and an E1 environment (fenced cell with fed parts).

sources.system: Mecademic Meca500 optical alignment/assembly station at XVP photonics
sources.title: How XVP photonics automates optical alignment assembly with the Meca500 | Mecademic Industrial Robotics
sources.claim: XVP photonics runs an automated optical assembly station in which a Meca500 six-axis industrial robot picks a lens from a tray, dispenses glue, moves it to the camera insertion site, optimizes placement from live image feedback and releases it - precision pick-and-insert of a thin optical element into a receiving holder from a fixed station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting an optical element into a holder. A gel frame or gobo holder entering a fixture's accessory slot is a looser-tolerance version of the same autonomous pick-and-insert.

sources.system: FANUC LR Mate 200iD/7L with FS-iA force sensor and iRVision
sources.title: Force Sensor | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC force-sensor-equipped robots perform tight-clearance insertion and fitting in production: LR Mate 200iD/7L robots with force sensing and vision assemble over-molded connectors, and FANUC documents insertion at H7/g7-class clearances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact-rich part insertion. Sliding a color frame or gobo holder into a fixture slot and seating its retaining clip is a low-precision instance of the force-controlled insertion these deployed cells perform.

sources.system: Festo smartphone assembly film-application station (DSBC cylinder, vacuum draw-in, ESG suction gripper, SBSI vision)
sources.title: Smartphone Assembly | Festo USA
sources.claim: Festo's smartphone assembly automation applies a thin protective film to a display: the film strip is clamped, drawn in by vacuum and precisely applied to the device - handling and accurate placement of limp thin film in a purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a thin flexible film to a device face. Color gel and diffusion are thin polyester films of comparable limpness; the cited station picks and lays them down accurately in a machine-built setting.

sources.title: Glass & window laminating machines manufactured in Europe and the USA | WALCO
sources.claim: WALCO vertical glass laminating machines automatically apply protective film ... faces of flat and insulating glass panels fed through the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laminating film to glass. Window gelling (CTO/ND film on a pane) is the same operation on the same material class when the pane is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Zund S3/G3 digital cutting systems with kiss-cut tool and automatic sheet feeder
sources.title: S3 digital cutter | Cutting System | Zund
sources.claim: Zund flatbed digital cutters cut vinyl and film sheet stock to shape with automatic sheet feeding and electronically controlled cutting pressure, kiss-cutting or through-cutting commonly used films.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting thin plastic sheet to size. Cutting color gel to frame size is the same material and tolerance class as the vinyl/film these cutters process unattended.

tasks.label: Install electrical cables or wire fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Location shoot (private home, storefront, street, exterior): run stingers and heavy feeder from a tow generator or a tie-in to distro boxes, snake cable through doors/windows/stairs, dress and secure runs with tape, mats and sandbags, plug up fixtures and practicals in occupied, cluttered, weather-exposed spaces.

Soundstage or TV studio: pull feeder from the company switch to distro, run cable up perms/greenbeds and across the grid to hanging fixtures, drop stingers to floor units, dress and tie off runs, plug up and label; the layout is re-struck for every production.

Concert/tour or theatrical load-in: pre-rig moving lights and conventionals onto truss on the deck, daisy-chain power (powerCON/Edison) and DMX/network cable between fixtures, plug socapex/multicable breakouts, run feeder to dimmer/power racks, then fly the rig.

Rental-house or shop bench prep: build and repair small-gauge cable assemblies and fixture wiring - terminate Edison/stage-pin/XLR-DMX connectors, replace pigtails, lamp sockets and internal fixture leads, crimp/solder and label, then continuity-test.
Shop repair of heavy-gauge gear: re-head damaged 4/0 feeder with cam-lok connectors, rebuild 100A Bates/socapex tails and distro whips, torque lugs on large conductors and test.

Small-format corporate, event or ENG job in a hotel ballroom, black box or conference room: run a handful of extension cords and DMX lines from house power to a few fixtures, tape down or ramp the runs, verify circuit loading.

sources.title: Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing (arXiv:2604.22235)
sources.claim: A bimanual collaborative-robot workstation autonomously inserts deformable power cables into a jig-held motor and solders them on a live production line, at near-human takt time and a 99.4% product QC pass rate over a 5-hour run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiring a component's power leads. Transfers to a lighting tech's bench wiring of small-gauge fixture leads and connectors - same object class (flexible insulated conductors), sub-millimetre insertion tolerance, and terminate-then-test workflow - but only with the workpiece jigged and cables presented in a holder.

sources.title: Fully automated wire cabling machine Wire Terminal WT C10 | Rittal
sources.claim: Commercial machine produces terminated wires (cut, strip, crimp/ferrule, label) fully automatically without manual intervention, for cross-sections 0.5-6 mm2.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up cable ends. Same operation a lighting tech performs when building small-gauge cable assemblies (cut to length, strip, crimp, label), at equal or better precision, but only inside a purpose-built wire-processing machine fed from spools.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (Springer)
sources.claim: A portal robot performs fully automated wiring of control-cabinet mounting plates: cutting, crimping, connecting wires to devices and routing them inside the enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiring devices inside an electrical enclosure. Comparable to wiring a fixture's internal leads to sockets and terminals - same conductor gauges, screw/clamp terminations and routing - but performed on a mounting plate fixtured in a portal-robot cell.

sources.title: Komax Introduces the Omega 750 S: Revolutionizing Fully Automated Wire Harness Assembly - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Fully automatic wire-harness machine assembles double-sided connector blocks, inserting terminated leads into connector housings without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading terminated conductors into multi-pin connector housings, the same act as assembling a multipin stage connector; demonstrated only in a fixtured production machine with pre-sorted wires and housings.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: The closest jobsite electrical-installation robot is a BIM-guided, operator-steered ceiling drilling machine; it marks and drills holes for MEP trades but does not install cable or wire fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the nearest jobsite electrical-installation robot; its scope is drilling only, so it does not substantiate cable installation in any environment.

sources.system: stage automation robotic arms and motorized hoists
sources.title: Behind the Scenes: How Robotics Are Being Used for Stage Automation - TLC Creative Technology
sources.claim: Robotics in live production is limited to show automation - motorized hoists and robotic arms that move already-rigged lighting and LED elements during performances; the rigging and cabling itself is done by crews.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the live-production instances: these systems move fixtures on pre-programmed show paths and neither install cable nor terminate connectors.

tasks.label: Load, unload, or position lighting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Arena/theater concert load-in and load-out: rolling 100-600 lb wheeled road cases off semi-trailers down ramps, spotting them on the deck, opening cases and hanging moving lights on pre-rigged truss with half-couplers, setting floor packages and lifting fixtures into position under time pressure on a crowded stage floor shared with audio, video and rigging crews.

TV/broadcast or film soundstage: pulling fixtures and stands from carts and the equipment room, setting LED panels and tungsten heads on rolling and C-stands, sandbagging, clamping fixtures to the pipe grid with safety cables, and repositioning fixtures between camera setups during the shoot day.

Location film/video shoot at a private home, street or office: unloading the grip/electric truck at the curb, carrying heads, stands and ballasts through doorways and stairs, positioning lights in cramped rooms, on ladders or outside windows, and striking and reloading between setups in variable weather and layouts.

Rental shop / prep warehouse: pulling fixtures off shelves for a show order, packing them into road cases and carts, staging on the dock, loading the truck in show order by weight and access, and unloading and unpacking returns.

Corporate event or house-of-worship ballroom: wheeling cases in over carpet and ramps, positioning ground-supported truss and pipe-and-base, placing uplights and tripod stands to the plot around tables and staging, then striking after the event.

Theatre hang: moving fixtures up to electrics and box booms from a personnel lift or ladder, positioning heavy followspots in the spot booth, and repositioning units on battens during the hang and focus call.

sources.title: Robotic Palletizing Systems | FANUC America
sources.claim: Heavy-payload industrial palletizing robots autonomously pick, stack and unstack cases in flexible patterns in fenced end-of-line cells, running continuously at commercial rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: case palletizing/depalletizing. With the work presented as a purpose-built cell would present it, loading and unloading heavy cases onto and off of a load is the same physical operation as loading/unloading lighting road cases, at comparable weights (185-700 kg payload class) and placement precision.

sources.title: FANUC Palletizing Robots: Applications and Integration
sources.claim: FANUC's palletizing line covers payloads well above typical road-case weights, with pattern changes routine in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy case handling. Establishes that the payload and reach needed to lift and place road cases and large fixtures exists in commercially deployed fenced cells.

sources.system: ABB robot cell (QComp Technologies integration) at Ruud Lighting
sources.title: Robots Light the Way to Faster Assembly | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A vision-guided ABB robot in a lighting-fixture production cell identifies, picks, orients and places light-fixture lenses into the fixture assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembly of lighting fixtures. Shows autonomous grasping and accurate positioning of lighting-fixture hardware presented in a fixtured production cell - the E1 form of 'position lighting equipment'.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 / AX-40 robotic screwdriving assembly cells
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Turnkey robotic assembly cells drive screws and bolts autonomously on fixtured parts behind light curtains, integrated with conveyors and screw feeders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastening in a fixtured cell. Mounting a fixture to a presented bar, yoke or plate requires clamping and tightening hardware, which these cells perform autonomously.

sources.title: Automated Trailer Unloading | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Stretch autonomously detects, grasps and places boxes when unloading trailers and containers, and is in commercial deployment unloading cases in DHL warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading a truck. Demonstrates autonomous truck unloading, but only of suction-graspable cardboard cases onto a conveyor at a warehouse dock - it does not handle wheeled road cases, stands or fixtures, so it substantiates the presented-case (E1) form of unloading rather than a venue load-in.

sources.title: Mobile Industrial Robots Adds Autonomous Mobile Robot For 1,000 Kg Loads
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots pick up, transport and deliver ... loads up to 1,000 kg through facilities shared with people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy load transport inside a facility. Covers only the horizontal move of a palletized load; it does not lift gear out of a trailer or mount fixtures, so it cannot complete a load-in instance on its own.

sources.title: Motor Stage Automation relies on Kinesys for Untold Festival - TPi
sources.claim: Positioning of lighting trusses in live venues is done by chain-hoist automation rigged by crews and driven from a control console by an operator, not by autonomous machines.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (moving lighting trusses in venues), but the hoists are rigged by human crews and driven by an automation operator, so this cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

tasks.label: Match light fixture settings, such as brightness and color, to lighting design plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live venue (theatre, concert hall, corporate stage): technician sets intensity and color on networked LED washes, profiles and moving heads from the console to match the designer's plot, magic sheet and cue list — building color palettes, matching color across mixed fixture brands, and eyeballing/verifying the result on stage with the designer.

Conventional (non-color-mixing) rig in a venue: cutting and loading color filter and diffusion frames per the color codes on the plot, dropping them into hung fixtures from a ladder/genie, patching to dimmers and setting levels/curves so intensities match the plan.

Film/TV soundstage: setting CCT, intensity and plus/minus-green on LED fixtures (SkyPanel/Orbiter/Vortex class) via onboard menu, wireless app or console to the gaffer's/DP's lighting plan; adding diffusion or CTO/CTB, matching several units to each other, checking with a color meter and on the monitor.

Location shoot (practical house, office, exterior): dialing fixture brightness and color to match practicals and shifting daylight per the plan, gelling fixtures and windows, adjusting dimmers on stands amid crew, cable and clutter, with conditions changing shot to shot.

Broadcast news or corporate studio with a fixed rig: recalling stored looks and then trimming individual fixture levels and color temperature for the talent and camera, verifying skin tone and consistency on monitors/waveform against the studio lighting plan.

sources.title: Brompton Hydra Calibration Breathes New Life into Rentex's LED Panel Inventory | PLSN
sources.claim: Brompton's Hydra is a purpose-built industrial measurement station that measures LED panels and generates calibration data so panel brightness and color match a target and stay uniform across an inventory; it is deployed commercially by rental houses (Rentex, ETS) via partner Red Rock OPS.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: matching the brightness and color output of light-emitting devices to a specified target. The machine measures emitted light and computes the drive settings that make output match the spec — the same measure-adjust-verify loop a technician performs when matching fixture settings to a lighting plan, on comparable entertainment-industry light sources.

sources.title: Brompton's New Hydra System – Brompton Technology
sources.claim: Hydra is described by its developer as an all-in-one industrial measurement solution containing the instruments and processing needed for panel measurement, i.e. a purpose-built station that work is brought to.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the environment class (purpose-built measurement/calibration station) in which automated light-output matching is performed.

sources.title: Ketra S30 Lamp - Full Spectrum PAR30 LED Light Bulb | Lutron
sources.claim: Lutron Ketra luminaires contain an onboard optical/thermal feedback loop that continuously measures the fixture's own light output and automatically adjusts drive to hold the commanded color point and intensity to within one MacAdam step over life — a deployed, autonomous closed loop that keeps a fixture's output matched to a specified target.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: holding a luminaire's brightness and color to a specified design value. This is the verification-and-correction core of 'matching fixture settings to the plan', performed by machine on the same class of object (an LED luminaire), though for architectural rather than production lighting specs.

sources.system: LISUN LPCE-2 integrating-sphere spectroradiometer test system
sources.title: Understanding Integrating Sphere Detectors: A Guide
sources.claim: Production-line photometric test systems automatically drive and measure luminaires/LED sources for luminous flux, correlated color temperature and CRI and sort them against user-defined tolerances, with SCPI/LabVIEW control for inline automation — automated verification that a fixture's brightness and color hit a specified target.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measuring a light source's brightness and color against a numeric specification and accepting/rejecting it. Supplies the objective 'does the output match the plan' check at a purpose-built station, on light fixtures presented to the machine.

sources.title: FANUC Robots Automate Precise Automotive Process | Case Study
sources.claim: FANUC M-20iD/25 industrial robots in four production cells autonomously feed, insert and weld plastic ... with precise dimensional positioning — established autonomous insertion of small parts into fixtured workpieces in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of a flat/rigid part into a slot on a fixtured object. Sliding a pre-cut color-filter or diffusion frame into a luminaire's accessory slot presented in a jig requires comparable object handling and far looser precision.

sources.title: BlackTrax Creates Aesthetics for Magic Mike Live - CAST Software
sources.claim: BlackTrax, deployed on live productions in theatres and arenas, autonomously computes and drives moving-light parameters in real time — locking beam diameter by automating zoom and iris and triggering douse-and-flip at pan stops — after an on-site calibration of fixtures and sensors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine computation and continuous application of fixture parameter values inside a working venue. It shows what venue-deployed automation covers today — tracking-derived pan/tilt, beam size and douse — not reading a lighting design plan and setting brightness and color to it.

sources.title: Maestro DMX Autonomous Lighting Designer, Automated AI Lighting Control
sources.claim: MaestroDMX is a commercial controller that autonomously sets color, dimmer and movement on DMX fixtures in venues from live music analysis, but it generates its own looks rather than reproducing a designer's specified plan.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous machine setting of brightness and color on physical fixtures in venues, but with no design plan as input; it therefore cannot deliver the accepted output of this task (fidelity to the designer's plan).

tasks.label: Operate manual or automated systems to control lighting throughout productions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Theatre performance (regional, touring, university, Broadway house): the board operator runs the programmed cue stack on a lighting console through a play, musical, opera or dance piece, taking each GO from the stage manager's live calls, adjusting for variable actor timing, holds and miscues, and restoring after any fault.

Large-scale concert, festival headliner, arena tour or residency show that is pre-programmed and locked to SMPTE/MIDI timecode: the console plays the cue list back against the band's click/playback track for the whole set while the LD monitors and adds occasional busked accents.

Live-operated ('busked') show with no timecode: club or mid-size concert, festival support act, corporate general session, house of worship service or awards show, where the operator makes real-time judgement calls on submasters, intensity, color and effects as the event unfolds.

Follow spot / spotlight operation during a live performance: picking up performers on cue, tracking them around the stage, sizing the iris, fading in and out and changing color throughout the show from a spot booth or truss position.

Live television studio broadcast (news, talk, sports desk): recalling and riding lighting states per rundown item and camera area throughout the broadcast, correcting levels for on-air look, handling breaking-news deviations.

Film, commercial or streaming shoot on a soundstage or studio: the board/dimmer operator controls fixtures through rehearsals and takes at the gaffer's and DP's spoken direction, riding practicals and effects cues in sync with action across many takes.

Shoot or event in an unstructured space taken as found - a practical location such as a private home, street or warehouse, a tented outdoor event or a non-standard venue - where the tech runs a portable console or wireless DMX control through the production as conditions and layout vary.

sources.developer: zactrack Lighting Technologies GmbH (distributed by ACT Entertainment)
sources.title: zactrack SMART Gives a Big Followspot Look to Premiere of "Run Bambi Run" at Milwaukee Rep (USITT)
sources.claim: zactrack SMART, a UWB-tag automated follow system, drove moving heads as front and back follow spots tracking eight characters through the full run of a musical at Milwaukee Repertory Theater, doing the work of several human spot operators.

sources.title: zactrack PRO System (developer product page)
sources.claim: The zactrack system automatically controls the pan/tilt of ordinary moving lights to follow tracked performers, with position-triggered auto functions such as relative iris, and is sold and deployed across theatres, arenas, cruise ships and touring productions.

sources.developer: zactrack Lighting Technologies GmbH / Illumity AB
sources.title: Illumity AB Taps zactrack SMART & grandMA3 For Swedish Band Avatar's World Tour (Live Design)
sources.claim: On a 2026 world arena tour, zactrack SMART tracked the band members and aimed the follow-spot fixtures automatically, replacing error-prone human spot operators while the LD retained dimmer control.

sources.system: SMPTE/MIDI timecode show playback on grandMA-class lighting consoles with automated moving-light rigs
sources.developer: MA Lighting / production lighting industry (reported by PLSN)
sources.title: Timecoding a Rock Show | PLSN
sources.claim: Timecode-locked concert productions have the lighting console execute the programmed cue list automatically for the length of the show, with automated moving lights as the standard fixtures; the operator monitors rather than triggers each cue.

sources.title: Themed Attractions - Pharos Controls
sources.claim: Pharos show controllers run complete timeline-driven lighting shows in themed attractions and installations automatically and continuously, without an operator at a desk.

sources.system: Viz Mosart studio automation at Suzhou Broadcasting System
sources.title: China's SBS Empowers News Production With Advanced Graphics and Studio Automation Technology From Vizrt
sources.claim: Broadcast studio automation systems place studio lighting under machine control alongside cameras, audio and graphics, so that no separate lighting operator runs the newscast; however the rundown is still advanced item-by-item by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: broadcast studio lighting operation. Cited only as context - the trigger for each rundown item is human, so autonomy of the lighting control across a whole broadcast is not established.

sources.system: StyleShoots Vertical / Live automated studio machines
sources.title: Profoto Acquires Automated, Robotic Photo Studio Company StyleShoots | PetaPixel
sources.claim: StyleShoots machines are self-contained robotic photo/video studios whose built-in lights are controlled by the machine's own software throughout each capture; they are sold commercially and used for e-commerce production at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: controlling lighting throughout a photographic/video production. The machine drives its own studio luminaires (intensity, which sources fire, per-shot states) through every capture in a purpose-built enclosure, the same control function a lighting tech performs on a stage shoot, with comparable fixtures and repeatability requirements.

sources.system: Ortery PhotoBench / Photosimile automated lightbox studios
sources.title: The Best Product Photography Automation Solutions - Ortery
sources.claim: Ortery's automated photography systems give software control of up to eight lighting sources inside a purpose-built lightbox and run the capture sequence automatically; the company reports thousands of commercial users.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating lighting control systems through a photographic production. The system sets and changes its integrated lighting per shot automatically, matching the control function of the task with studio-grade luminaires in a machine-built setting.

tasks.label: Patch or wire lights to dimmers or other electronic consoles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live theater / performing-arts venue hang-and-plug: after fixtures are hung on electrics and booms, the tech plugs each unit's pigtail into stage-pin or Edison circuits, adds two-fers and jumpers, dresses and ties cable to the pipe, and runs the DMX line from the console position to the dimmer racks or nodes. Work is done from an A-frame ladder, personnel lift or catwalk over a stage cluttered with scenery, checking each circuit against the plot and hookup.

Concert / touring / corporate event load-in: building truss with moving lights and LED units, plugging Socapex multicable breakouts and powerCON/true1 daisy chains, running DMX/ArtNet lines back to distro, dimmer beach and console, all under a few-hour load-in clock in an arena floor, ballroom or festival stage with heavy cable, tight schedules and crew traffic.

TV/broadcast studio: patching grid-hung fixtures on a standard studio lighting grid to numbered circuits at a hard-patch bay or dimmer rack room, connecting dimmer racks and DMX/Ethernet nodes to the lighting console, and verifying channels; fixed layout, standardized connectors and documented circuit numbering.

Film/video location shoot: pulling feeder from a generator or tie-in to distro boxes, running stingers and cable to fixtures, wiring practicals and lamps through dimmer boards or DMX dimmer packs and wireless nodes, inside a private house, warehouse, street or field location whose layout, power and clutter differ site to site.

Addressing, verification and troubleshooting at patch time: setting DMX addresses on each fixture via its menu or DIP switches, soft-patching in the console, ringing out circuits channel by channel with the board, then finding and fixing a dead or mis-patched channel by reseating or swapping a cable, moving a plug to another circuit, or replacing a dimmer module.

sources.system: Telescent G4/G5 Network Topology Manager (robotic patch panel / optical cross-connect)
sources.title: Telescent to Showcase Largest Capacity Optical Circuit Switch at OFC 2025
sources.claim: Telescent's G4/G5 Network Topology Manager is a commercially deployed robotic patch panel that physically makes and breaks fiber patch-cord connections between ports under software command, inside its own purpose-built enclosure, and is being deployed by network operators such as MOX Networks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically patching cords between ports of a patch panel per a routing schedule, with automated verification. This is the same act as hard-patching lighting circuits at a dimmer/patch bay - mating latched connectors at labelled ports and managing the cord between them - performed by a machine in a purpose-built enclosure at production reliability.

sources.system: Rocsys hands-free robotic charging platform (RCS-1 / M1)
sources.title: At APM Terminals, the Rocsys platform soon powers a critical link in the largest port of Europe
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic charging systems autonomously locate a vehicle's charging port, open it, insert and remove a heavy high-power charging connector; six robotic bays serve 30 autonomous terminal trucks 24/7 at APM Terminals Maasvlakte II, with remote operators only monitoring/assisting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided mating of a bulky, high-current power connector into a receptacle, with a flexible cable to manage. Lighting patching is the same class of act (stage-pin, Edison, twist-lock, powerCON plugs into circuit outlets); the demonstrated plug-in reliability (99.9%+ claimed for the successor M1) is comparable to worker quality for connector mating.

sources.system: Komax Omega 745/755 and 840/850 automatic insertion machines
sources.title: Harness Manufacturing | Komax
sources.claim: Komax harness manufacturing machines (Omega 745/755, 840/850) perform fully automatic wire-harness production in a purpose-built machine cell, covering cutting, crimping, insertion of leads into connector housings and cable routing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiring - terminating conductors and seating them in connector housings and routing the resulting flexible cable. This is the 'wire lights to dimmers' half of the task, done at production volume and quality by machines when the wire and housings are fixtured and presented, i.e. exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: FANUC SCARA connector-assembly cells with FANUC force sensor
sources.title: Assembly Robots | Assembly Line Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC SCARA robot cells perform high-speed automotive connector assembly in production, with automated changeover and in-line inspection; FANUC force-torque sensing supports precise fitting/insertion under contact force.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated mating/assembly of electrical connectors in a fenced industrial cell with in-line verification. Transfers to plugging lamp tails into circuits when the plug and receptacle are fixtured and presented, with comparable precision and force requirements.

sources.system: MATT smart device test automation robot
sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: Adapta Robotics MATT is a commercial test-automation robot that operates a device's physical controls in a fixtured rig - pressing buttons, switches and control knobs and verifying the device's response with a camera.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine operation of a small device UI (buttons, DIP switches) with camera-based verification of the display. This matches setting DMX addresses on a fixture and confirming the readout when the fixture is presented in a jig.

sources.title: Microsoft Research details early-stage modular robotics for data centers
sources.claim: Microsoft Research has prototype (not deployed) data-center robots, including a transceiver manipulation robot that uses vision to navigate cluttered cabling in a rack and reseat, plug or unplug a transceiver; the work is described by the team as at the very start of the journey.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plugging/unplugging a connector at a port inside a human-built facility (data center hall) rather than in a fixtured cell. It is the closest E2-style cable-plugging system found, but it is an early-stage prototype covering only a single sub-step, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion at E2.

tasks.label: Perform minor repairs or routine maintenance on lighting equipment, such as replacing lamps or damaged color filters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Theatre or TV studio: during a pre-show/pre-shoot check the tech finds several dead or dim fixtures hung on the grid, pipe or catwalk, and relamps them and swaps burnt or torn color filters/gel frames in place, working from an A-frame ladder, personnel lift or catwalk, often one-handed and overhead, with the fixture still hung and cabled.

Shop/rental-house bench: routine maintenance of a batch of like fixtures before a hang or after a return — relamp conventional units (e.g., ellipsoidals, fresnels, PARs), replace damaged gel and cut/load new gel into frames, clean lenses, check safety cables and connectors, and bench-test each unit.

Shop/rental-house bench: a fixture is reported faulty with the cause unknown (moving head, LED wash, dimmer pack, cable). The tech meters it, opens the housing, isolates the fault, and replaces or repairs the failed part — fuse, lamp socket, driver board, DMX card, pigtail, solder joint — then reassembles and verifies operation.

Live event/touring: between shows in an arena or at a festival, the tech swaps failed lamps in moving heads and replaces damaged gel frames, fuses and short cables on a lowered truss or at height, under time pressure before doors.

Film/TV location shoot: on-location fixes in a found space (private home, street, warehouse) — swap a blown bulb in a fixture on a stand or clamp, replace burnt diffusion/gel, repair or replace a damaged cable — while the crew waits and other departments work around the tech.

sources.title: Sims Lifecycle Services and MOLG Forge Strategic Relationship to Drive Innovation
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory autonomously assembles and disassembles complex electronic products (laptops, servers, battery packs) in a fixtured robotic cell, and units have been installed at Sims Lifecycle Services ITAD facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly/reassembly of used, screwed-together electronic housings and extraction/insertion of internal modules. Transfers to relamping a luminaire presented in a jig — comparable objects (screwed housing, plug-in component), comparable precision, same fixtured-cell environment.

sources.title: Molg Raises $5.5 Million in Seed Funding to Tackle Electronics Waste Through Circular Manufacturing
sources.claim: Molg's disassembly microfactories are installed at an e-waste processing facility, i.e. running in production rather than only as a lab demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: substantiates that the fixtured-cell disassembly/component-swap capability is deployed, not merely demonstrated.

sources.system: Robooptic Systems courtesy-light assembly and inspection cell
sources.title: Boosting Automotive Courtesy Light Production with Machine Vision and Robotics
sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic cell built by Robooptic Systems assembles and functionally inspects automotive courtesy light fixtures (housing, optics, LED) in under seven seconds per part.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of a light fixture — precise seating of a lamp/optic in a housing plus a functional light-output check. Transfers to installing a lamp or filter in a fixture held in a jig and verifying it lights correctly.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 / AX-40 automatic screwdriving cells
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Commercial off-the-shelf robotic screwdriving cells (ASG AX-10 tabletop Cartesian cell, AX-40 cell with conveyor, screw feeder and light curtain) automate opening/closing screwed assemblies in fenced or light-curtained cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving/removing the fasteners that hold a housing or lamp cap closed. Same class of fasteners and torque as stage-fixture covers, performed on a workpiece fixtured in a cell.

sources.date: 2023-04-03 (listing); product in field service for years
sources.title: Ship signalling light - TF-3B - Tideland Signal
sources.claim: Tideland Signal's TF-3B is a deployed, fully automatic six-place lampchanger: a stepper-driven turret that rotates a fresh lamp into the focal position of a signal lantern when the in-service lamp fails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled replacement of a failed lamp inside a lighting fixture. It shows the core action — detecting a dead lamp and putting a good lamp into service — is achievable by machine when lamps are presented in a purpose-built holder.

sources.title: How are LED car lamps built? Lamp assembly lines from ELPLC
sources.claim: ELPLC builds robotized automotive lamp assembly lines in which multiple industrial robots handle lens/optic application, gluing and assembly of luminaire housings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and precise placement of thin optical elements (lenses/covers) into luminaire housings — comparable to seating a color filter or filter frame in a fixture held in a jig.

tasks.label: Program lighting consoles or load automated lighting control systems onto consoles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Set up and focus light fixtures to meet requirements of television, theater, concerts, or other productions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Theatrical hang-and-focus in a performing arts venue (regional theatre, road house, university theatre): crew works from personnel lifts, ladders and catwalks to clamp 60-200 ellipsoidals, PARs, LED washes and a few moving heads onto electrics and booms, attach safety cables, circuit and cable them, then run a focus session where each unit is panned/tilted to the designer's call, the barrel is racked for beam edge, four shutter blades are cut off the proscenium and walls, and gel/gobo/top hats are added.

Concert / touring / festival load-in in an arena, amphitheatre or club: pre-rig trusses are laid out on the deck, moving heads and strobes are clamped and safetied, power and data are run through truss-integrated distribution, trusses are motored to trim, then the rig is powered up, addressed, position-calibrated and focused (movers from the console, conventional specials by hand) under tight load-in time pressure.

Broadcast/TV studio lighting setup (news, talk, game show, sitcom stage): fixtures on a fixed grid or motorized pantographs are moved, added or swapped for a new set or camera blocking; key/fill/back and cyc lights are aimed for each position, barn doors, diffusion, egg crates and gel are fitted, intensities balanced to camera, cabling and DMX patched.

Film/TV/commercial or stills shoot, largely on location (houses, offices, streets, practical interiors) and sometimes on a soundstage: the electric crew flies in HMIs/LED panels on stands, condors, wall spreaders or overhead frames, runs distro cable, and sets and re-sets 3-8 sources with flags, silks, bounce and diffusion for each camera setup, resetting quickly between shots.

Corporate/live event in a hotel ballroom or convention center: ground-supported truss towers and pipe-and-drape, uplights around the perimeter, moving heads and washes for stage and podium, gobo/logo projections aimed on walls; fixtures are clamped, safetied, cabled and focused during a same-day install around venue staff and other trades.

sources.title: zactrack PRO System
sources.claim: zactrack is a commercially deployed tracking system that automatically calibrates the 3D positions of already-rigged moving lights and continuously aims them at tracked performers in theatres, arenas and studios — i.e. it automates the aiming/'focus' portion for automated fixtures, but performs no rigging, clamping or cabling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aiming/pointing production light fixtures. It substantiates automated fixture aiming on real stages, but the fixtures must already be hung, powered and data-connected by human technicians, so it covers only part of 'set up and focus'.

sources.title: Zactrack PRO | Zactrack | Ambersphere
sources.claim: zactrack's alignment algorithm determines fixture positions and calibrates the rig automatically without prior stage geometry, using a puck placed on stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: focus calibration of a hung rig. Shows automated determination of fixture aim in real venues; it does not mount, cable, shutter or gel fixtures, so it cannot complete the whole hang-and-focus instance.

sources.title: Meet KIRA The Lightning Quick Programmable 6-axis Camera and Lighting Robot
sources.claim: Motorized Precision's KIRA is a commercially available six-axis cinema robot marketed for both camera and lighting moves, executing pre-programmed, repeatable motion (±0.05 mm) while carrying a light or camera on purpose-built motion-control stages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning and aiming a production light fixture for a shot. The luminaire is mounted on the robot's tool plate (the way a purpose-built cell would present the work) and the machine places and points it to the DP's specification, which is the 'focus' output for a camera setup.

sources.title: Motorized Precision | Cinema Motion Control Robots
sources.claim: Motorized Precision sells its cinema robots (KIRA, MIA, VIGO, COLOSSUS) as production equipment with stated payloads and repeatability, confirming commercial availability and precision of the arms used to carry cameras and lights.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the KIRA item: repeatable placement/aiming of a payload (light head) in a purpose-built motion-control stage.

sources.title: Robe RoboSpot System | Equipment | Version 2
sources.claim: Robe's RoboSpot, the standard system for remote fixture aiming in arenas, theatres and TV, is operated by a human at a base station with hand controls for pan, tilt, focus and intensity — remote aiming of fixtures in venues is teleoperated, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aiming fixtures in live venues. Recorded as teleoperated evidence; it shows the state of the art for venue fixture aiming still keeps a human in the control loop.

sources.title: Martin Professional and Verity Studios Redefine Drone Shows with Integrated Lighting — DroneXL
sources.claim: Verity Studios' Lucie micro-drones are autonomous flying light sources deployed commercially in arenas and theatres (Céline Dion, Cirque du Soleil, TV galas), self-positioning as show elements rather than rigging or focusing a production's fixture inventory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous positioning of light sources inside performance venues. It shows self-positioning luminaires exist, but the drones are choreographed show effects; humans still hang, cable and focus the conventional and automated rig.

sources.title: Drone lighting – Robotics @ MIT
sources.claim: A research prototype quadrotor carrying a light source autonomously flies to the position that produces a photographer-specified lighting effect (rim width), using feedback from the photographer's camera; demonstrated indoors as a lab prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a light to meet a stated lighting requirement for photography. Single-source lab prototype; no mounting hardware, cabling, shuttering or multi-fixture rig, so it does not establish worker-quality completion.

sources.title: Headlamp aiming system for commercial vehicles - Dürr
sources.claim: Fully automatic headlamp setting (aiming) stations are installed at the end ... automotive production lines, mechanically adjusting a lamp's beam to a measured specification inside a purpose-built line station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically aiming a light fixture to a beam specification in an E1 line station. The object (vehicle headlamp already installed on a car) and the absence of any mounting, cabling or shaping work limit the transfer to the aiming step alone.

sources.title: The StudioBot LT | Compact Robotic Arm System
sources.claim: Robotic arms deployed in broadcast studios (MRMC StudioBot family) carry cameras, not lighting fixtures; no comparable product line exists for rigging or focusing studio luminaires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable robotic positioning in a broadcast studio. Payload is a box camera (≤10 kg) on a fixed base; it does not clamp fixtures to a grid, cable them, or fit barn doors and diffusion.

tasks.label: Set up scaffolding or cranes to assist with setting up of lighting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Soundstage or TV studio: technician and a partner wheel in and erect a rolling scaffold tower (Baker/Perry tower) — base frames, casters, cross braces, decks, guardrails — and/or drive a personnel/scissor lift into position under the grid so fixtures can be hung, cabled and focused. Flat sealed floor, institution-controlled stage, moving cable runs and set pieces to clear.

Theater, arena or ballroom load-in: assemble/position scaffold towers or an articulating lift on a raked or obstacle-rich house floor (seating rows, orchestra pit, stage edges, carpeted floors requiring plywood protection), level with screw jacks, lock casters, add outriggers, then hold the tower in place while lighting positions are hung and focused.

Outdoor location shoot: spot a condor/telescoping boom lift or truck-mounted crane on a street, parking lot, dirt lot or lawn to fly a large HMI or balloon light — chock/level on uneven ground with cribbing and outrigger pads, check clearance from overhead power lines and trees, set sandbags/ballast, and position the basket where the lamp will hang.

Large multi-tier scaffold build for a big lighting array (backlot exterior set, festival field, exterior night shoot): a crew erects several bays and levels of tube-and-clamp or system scaffold, planks and guardrails, ties/ballasts the structure, and builds out a top platform to carry lighting fixtures and their cabling on ground taken as found.

sources.title: KEWAZO raises funding to accelerate LIFTBOT deployment in heavy industry - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced commercially deployed scaffolding robot automates only vertical transport of scaffold parts on scaffolding already erected by humans; erection itself remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial system to the task: it works on scaffolding assembly, but only moves material to height (a sub-step). It does not erect frames, deck, or guardrail a tower, so it cannot complete the instance.

sources.title: Meet the robot that transports scaffolding
sources.claim: Kewazo's robot carries scaffold components to human erectors, who perform the assembly; component transport was targeted because it accounts for most of erection time.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (scaffolding erection) but the robot's role is delivery of parts to human erectors, confirming that no cited system performs the scaffold assembly itself.

sources.title: GITAI Successfully Demonstrates Robotics Construction Capabilities for Lunar Communications Towers
sources.claim: Multi-robot autonomous assembly of a 5-meter tower from purpose-designed modules with robot grapple interfaces was demonstrated once on a lunar-analog desert site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous erection of a tower structure. Transfer fails for this task — the modules were bespoke, fitted with grapple interfaces, lightweight, and the one-off result is an antenna mast, not a human-occupiable, load-rated scaffold with decks and guardrails erected in a venue.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Fully autonomous heavy construction machinery exists commercially for outdoor sites, but for surveying and driving solar piles, not for erecting access structures or setting up cranes and lifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous positioning and operation of a heavy machine on an outdoor site. It shows the frontier of outdoor construction autonomy but performs no scaffold erection, lift spotting, outrigger/cribbing setup, or crane rigging, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

tasks.label: Test lighting equipment function and desired lighting effects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-show channel check / dimmer check in a theatre or performing-arts venue: with the rig already hung and patched, the tech brings up each channel from the console and confirms every conventional and LED unit strikes at the right intensity, colour and gobo and hits its assigned stage area, logging dead lamps, bad dimmer curves and non-responding units for repair.

Film/TV soundstage: after the units are set for a shot, power up and test each lamp, ballast and dimmer, check for flicker against the camera's frame rate and shutter, take incident/spot and colour-meter readings at the subject, and evaluate the look on the monitor with the DP/gaffer, tweaking output, diffusion and colour until the intended effect is achieved.

Arena / touring / corporate ballroom technical line check: verify every moving head and LED batten on the trusses responds on its DMX address, homes and pans/tilts correctly, runs colour, gobo, prism, zoom and strobe channels, and that hazers, strobes and practicals fire; flag units to be swapped before doors.

Rehearsal / cue-check pass in the same arena or ballroom: run the programmed cues and effects with the lighting designer present and confirm the looks read as intended on the stage, on the IMAG cameras and from the audience positions, adjusting fixtures and cue levels to get the desired effect.

Location shoot (practical interior, exterior street, event site): test lighting run off distro, generator or batteries in the found space, confirm HMIs strike and LEDs dim without flicker under the available power, and verify the light does what is wanted on camera against changing daylight and ambient practicals.

Shop / prep bench testing at a rental house or venue electrics shop: each fixture placed on a bench or test stand, powered up and run through lamp output, dimming, DMX/RDM channel response and mechanical functions; cables, dimmer packs and control gear tested; faults tagged and units cleared for the job.

sources.title: KUKA Case study at opsira GmbH | KUKA Germany
sources.claim: opsira's robogonio is a commercially sold KUKA-robot-based goniophotometer that automatically positions a lamp or luminaire and measures its angle-dependent luminous intensity distribution, colour distribution and luminance (glare) in a light-measurement laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: photometric qualification of a luminaire. It is the fixtured-bench form of 'test lighting equipment function' — the same objects (luminaires, including entertainment fixtures) are energised and their output verified against spec, at precision exceeding a technician's meter check.

sources.title: Opsira will demonstrate light measurement equipment live at Light+Building 2016 | LEDs Magazine
sources.claim: The robogonio product range is explicitly sized for large luminaires including stage lights, so the robot goniophotometer is applied to the same class of fixtures a lighting technician tests.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (photometric bench qualification of luminaires); this item establishes that the robotic test cell handles stage lighting fixtures, i.e. the very equipment in this task.

sources.system: SEETECH DRAGON X15 headlamp aiming machine
sources.title: Advanced Headlamp Aiming Machines with ±1 mm Proven Accuracy
sources.claim: SEETECH's headlamp aiming machines are end-of-line stations that automatically measure a lamp's beam cut-off, hot-spot and photometric distribution and, in the robotic configuration, have a cobot locate the adjustment screws and re-aim the lamp fully automatically in lights-out production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying a luminaire's beam pattern and aim against a specification and correcting it. Comparable objects (high-output LED/matrix luminaires), comparable acceptance criteria (beam position, intensity distribution), in a fixtured cell — the E1 analogue of confirming a fixture lights correctly and points where it should.

sources.system: Averna Headlamp Test Platform (photometric EOLT stations)
sources.title: Headlamp Test Platform | Automated Automotive Test | Averna
sources.claim: Averna supplies automated photometric end-of-line test stations for headlamps that run electrical and control-communication tests and measure beam patterns for low-, high-, corner and designer lighting elements without an operator judging the output.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional plus photometric test of a controllable luminaire. It covers both halves of a bench check a lighting tech performs — does the unit respond to control signalling, and is its light output within spec — in a purpose-built fixtured station.

sources.system: LISUN LPCE-3 integrating sphere spectroradiometer system
sources.title: Master Light Measurement: LISUN Optical Integrating Spheres
sources.claim: Inline integrating-sphere spectroradiometer systems perform full spectral and luminous-flux measurement fast enough for 100% inline inspection of luminaires on LED production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pass/fail testing of every luminaire's output and colour on a line. Same measurable quantities a technician verifies on a bench (output, colour temperature), with the work presented to the machine.

sources.developer: University of Angers (Guyonneau et al.), Journal of Building Engineering
sources.title: Robotic system for indoor illuminance map generation - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Romulux is a research mobile robot with 3D LiDAR and an illuminance meter that autonomously drives a sports hall or ice rink to build an illuminance map; it measures light levels only and does not verify fixture function, colour, focus or programmed looks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ measurement of lighting levels inside a human facility. It marks the limit of what mobile robots do in venues today — illuminance mapping, not fixture-by-fixture function or effect verification — so it does not substantiate E2 completion of this task.

sources.title: Development of a multi-robot system for illuminance measurement | CiNii Research
sources.claim: A multi-robot system for autonomous illuminance measurement in buildings reported measurement error of about 1.36% versus human measurement, but remains a laboratory/field research system limited to illuminance readings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated light-level verification inside a facility under construction. Shown only as a research demo restricted to illuminance readings, so it cannot stand in for a technician's in-venue functional and effects check.

tasks.label: Visit and assess structural and electrical layout of locations before setting up lighting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Film/TV/commercial tech scout at a practical location (private home, storefront, small office): the technician walks the space with the gaffer/DP, judges ceiling structure and height for rigging, window size/orientation for daylight control, locates the breaker panel, counts usable circuits and amperage, identifies tie-in or generator placement and cable runs, and flags hazards; reports back so the lighting package can be specified.

Advance/site survey for a live event, concert or theatrical production at a venue (theatre, arena, club, ballroom): confirm rigging/hang point locations and rated capacity with house staff, verify trim heights and throw distances, locate the company switch/three-phase tie-in, dimmer and distro rooms, cable paths, and note obstructions and sightlines.

Corporate/broadcast shoot survey in a hotel ballroom or convention center: walk the room, count and test wall circuits and their breakers, check ceiling grid or truss-hang possibilities, evaluate house lighting and control, load-in path and staging area, and dimming/blackout capability.

Pre-rig assessment on a soundstage, studio or broadcast facility: check pipe/greenbed grid capacity and available hanging positions, inventory existing distro, stage boxes and dimmer channels, verify service capacity for the planned load and plan cable runs.

Exterior/outdoor location survey (city street, parking lot, park, industrial yard, field): assess terrain and access for stands, lifts and condors, plan generator placement and long cable runs since no house power exists, note overhead hazards such as power lines and tree cover, sun path, weather exposure and permits/neighboring structures.

sources.system: Spot (with Trimble X7 / FARO / 360 camera payloads)
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot, carrying laser scanners or 360 cameras, autonomously executes recorded Autowalk missions on active construction sites to capture reality-capture data (point clouds, 360 photos) for as-built documentation; the interpretation of that data against a BIM model is done by software and human engineers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite reality capture. It shares locomotion through a cluttered building and sensing of structure, but the robot only records geometry along a route a human first taught; it does not open panels, evaluate circuit capacity or rigging load ratings, or produce the technician's suitability assessment.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Trimble (deployed by Hensel Phelps)
sources.title: See Spot Scan: Robots in Your Workplace - xyHt
sources.claim: Spot with a Trimble X7 scanner was used on a Denver International Airport terminal reconstruction project to capture scans and 360-degree images; the team used both manual and autonomous modes and humans compared the point cloud to the BIM model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built scanning inside a structured human facility (airport terminal). It shows data capture in an E2-type setting, but the assessment step—comparing to design intent and drawing conclusions—was performed by people and software, not the robot.

sources.title: Exyn Brings Level 4 Autonomy to Drones - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Exyn's ExynAero drones exhibit Autonomy Level 4: an operator defines a volume and the drone explores an unknown, unmapped, GPS-denied space on its own and returns a high-resolution 3D map; used for mine and tunnel surveying.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exploration and 3D mapping of a previously unseen space. It substantiates that geometry of a novel location can be captured without a pilot, but a point cloud is not an assessment of electrical service, rigging capacity, or lighting positions, and the drone performs no manipulation (panel doors, meters, measurements of load ratings).

sources.title: ANYmal Monitors High-Voltage Transmission at RTE - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs scheduled autonomous inspection missions at electrical transmission installations, acquiring thermal, visual, acoustic and frequency ... on predefined assets in substation environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous electrical asset inspection. It is the closest robotic analogue to 'assessing electrical layout', but it runs pre-taught routes over already-mapped, catalogued assets in a controlled industrial plant; it does not survey an unfamiliar location, read panel schedules, verify spare circuit capacity, or judge where power can be tapped for a lighting rig.

roles.title: Photographers
roles.description: Photograph people, landscapes, merchandise, or other subjects. May use lighting equipment to enhance a subject's appearance. May use editing software to produce finished images and prints. Includes commercial and industrial photographers, scientific photographers, and photojournalists.
roles.sector: Arts, design, entertainment, sports, and media

tasks.label: Adjust apertures, shutter speeds, and camera focus according to a combination of factors, such as lighting, field depth, subject motion, film type, and film speed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Posed portrait session with controlled lighting: studio, school gym/library picture day, or a corporate headshot day in an office conference room. Subject seated or standing at a known distance under strobes/continuous lights; photographer picks aperture for depth of field, a sync-safe shutter speed, and focuses on the eyes, adjusting as subjects and poses change.

Wedding and event coverage: candid documentary shooting through ceremony, reception and dancing in churches, banquet halls, backyards and outdoor venues. Rapidly changing mixed light (window, tungsten, DJ lighting, flash), moving subjects, shallow depth of field, constant re-setting of aperture/shutter/ISO and continuous tracking focus.

Commercial product / e-commerce / catalog tabletop shoot in a studio: packshots, apparel, jewelry or food on a table or sweep with strobes. Small apertures or focus stacking for depth of field, sync shutter speeds, precise focus placement on a static subject that can be positioned by the photographer.

Real-estate, architectural and interior capture on location in as-found homes and buildings: bracketed/HDR exposures balancing bright windows against dim interiors, wide depth of field, focus set for room-scale scenes, camera on a tripod moved room to room.

Photojournalism, sports and editorial field assignments: news scenes, games, street and outdoor locations under available light. Long lenses, panning and motion-freezing shutter speeds, wide apertures for subject isolation, continuous autofocus on unpredictable action, settings changed shot to shot.

Scientific, industrial and aerial/technical documentation: photographing assets, equipment, construction progress, infrastructure and site conditions for records or inspection. Exposure and focus set for the lighting at hand and for the detail size that must be resolved; repeatable, documentation-grade output rather than creative interpretation.

sources.title: Announcing the General Availability of Skydio 3D Scan | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan turns the drone into an autonomous scanning system that plans its own flight in real time and captures photographic datasets of assets and scenes; generally available after trials with construction, DOT and police organizations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial inspection/scan photography. It is the same act as this task — the machine sets capture parameters for the lighting and subject distance it finds and must return in-focus, correctly exposed frames of the structure being documented.

sources.title: SKYDIO X10 OPERATOR'S MANUAL (ManualsLib)
sources.claim: The Skydio X10 sets shutter speed itself from the available light in Auto mode, i.e. the machine performs the exposure adjustment named in this task.

sources.title: Understanding camera focus with Skydio X10 – Skydio
sources.claim: The X10's cameras autofocus, with several focus modes, and Skydio documents depth-of-field behaviour as a function of aperture, focal length and subject distance for its capture settings.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases Spot and Orbit 5.1 with new Spot Cam - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Spot runs autonomous patrol/inspection missions inside industrial facilities and captures PTZ, panoramic and thermal imagery on its own, including reacting to what it sees.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection imaging. Same act as this task for documentation photography — the robot must aim, zoom, focus and expose repeatable images of plant equipment under fixed facility lighting.

sources.claim: The Matterport Pro3 determines its own exposure: each capture is a five-exposure HDR image with automatic white balance, and Matterport notes the Pro3 handles challenging interior lighting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior/architectural capture for real-estate digital twins. Same act — the machine must choose exposure for window-versus-room contrast in as-found homes, the core judgement a real-estate photographer makes.

sources.title: Matterport Pro3 Review – Camera Jabber
sources.claim: Once triggered on its tripod the Pro3 rotates itself through a full 360 degrees and captures the scene automatically, indoors or outdoors, in homes and commercial buildings used by real-estate and AEC professionals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated interior capture. The motorized camera performs the physical capture and its own exposure setting; the photographer only places the tripod, which belongs to a different task.

sources.title: New robotic capability lets retailers remotely monitor store shelves | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously drives grocery aisles and photographs merchandise on shelves under ordinary store lighting, in long-running retail deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous merchandise documentation imaging in a retail facility. Comparable to documentation photography of merchandise — the robot must expose and focus usable images of shelf goods under uncontrolled ambient store lighting.

sources.title: Live Sports Solutions by Pixellot - What is Automated Production?
sources.claim: Pixellot's operator-free AI camera systems are installed at thousands of indoor and outdoor sports venues and produce game coverage automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated camera coverage of moving subjects in venue lighting. It shows autonomous exposure/framing for sports, but the deliverable is streaming video, not the publishable stills a sports photographer's employer accepts.

sources.title: Want to know what a Getty Images photographer takes to the Paris 2024 Olympic Games?

tasks.label: Create artificial light, using flashes and reflectors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wedding or social-event coverage at a venue (banquet room, church, hotel ballroom): photographer works an on-camera bounce flash and places two or three off-camera speedlights/strobes on stands around the room, re-aims and re-powers them as the crowd, decor and ambient light change, and lights both candids and formal group portraits on the move.

On-location portrait session outdoors or at a client's site (park, city street, farm, office exterior): assistant or stand holds a collapsible reflector to bounce sun onto the subject, a battery-powered strobe in a softbox is balanced against changing ambient light and wind, and everything is repositioned each time the subject or sun moves.

Standardized portrait work with many sitters in a room set up as a studio or in a permanent portrait studio: corporate headshots, ID/passport and badge photos, school and volume portraits — a fixed key/fill/hair/background strobe setup plus a reflector under the chin, repeated identically over dozens or hundreds of subjects.

Product and tabletop still-life shooting in a commercial studio: strobes with softboxes, light tents, white/silver reflector cards and black flags arranged around small merchandise, exposure metered and ratios tuned, then the same lighting held consistent across many SKUs.

Bespoke editorial/advertising studio shoot: a multi-light rig built for a specific concept (gridded key, gels, scrims, hard modifiers, hair and rim lights, bounce boards), refined iteratively while tethered with an art director on a fashion, beverage or hero-product set.

Architectural, interior or industrial location lighting: several flashes bounced off ceilings or hidden behind furniture across the rooms of a house, a restaurant or a plant floor, fired in sequence and blended/composited to balance window light and mixed ambient.

sources.system: Orbitvu Alphashot XL G2 / Alphashot XL Pro
sources.title: Alphashot XL G2 | Automated Product Photography & Measurement | Orbitvu
sources.claim: Orbitvu Alphashot automated photo studios are enclosed machines in which the product is placed and the machine itself drives the lighting: software-controlled light panels (including sliding/rotating strip lights) with automatic lighting control per shooting template.

sources.title: Iris Photo Booth | Ohio State Software Directory
sources.claim: The Iris Booth is a self-serve automated headshot booth whose hardware supplies the artificial lighting: a DSLR plus a custom array of roughly 800 white-balanced LEDs giving consistent studio-grade illumination without a photographer present.
