sources.claim: Autonomous positioning of a photographic light by a free-flying robot exists only as a research demonstration: MIT/Cornell quadrotors that hold a specified rim-lighting effect on a subject, published in 2014 and never productized.

tasks.label: Determine desired images and picture composition, selecting and adjusting subjects, equipment, and lighting to achieve desired effects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Art-directed shoot in a photographer's studio or rented studio space: a portrait client (family, senior, executive, editorial subject) or a styled set (food, lifestyle, hero product). The photographer decides the look, builds a multi-light setup (key/fill/rim, modifiers, flags, gels), chooses backdrop and lens, poses/directs the subject or arranges props and stylist input, and adjusts through several looks in one session.

High-volume standardized portrait work at a fixed station: corporate headshot programs, ID/badge, credentialing and passport-style photos. One approved look, fixed background, one seated or standing subject at a time, minimal posing, hundreds of subjects per day, output must match a template exactly.

Catalog and e-commerce photography of merchandise in a studio: packshots on white, 360-degree spins, apparel on mannequin/flat-lay, jewelry and small goods. Repeatable framing and lighting templates across hundreds or thousands of SKUs; subject is a movable object placed by the photographer.

Weddings, parties, corporate events and other on-location people photography: venues, homes and outdoors taken as found, mixed and changing ambient light, on-camera or portable flash, candid coverage plus posed group and couple portraits, subjects moved and directed by the photographer around unpredictable backgrounds and crowds.

On-location documentation of places and events for publication or listings: real estate and architectural interiors/exteriors (window-balanced exposures, room composition, supplemental lighting), plus photojournalism, editorial and sports assignments where the photographer chooses vantage point, moment and framing in an uncontrolled scene.

Technical, scientific and industrial documentation on site: complete photographic coverage of infrastructure, facilities and assets (bridge/tower/roof inspection imagery, aerial surveys, construction progress capture) where the requirement is systematic, repeatable coverage of every surface at a specified resolution rather than an aesthetic single image.

sources.title: Alphashot XL G2 | Automated Product Photography & Measurement | Orbitvu
sources.claim: Orbitvu's Alphashot XL G2 is a commercially sold enclosed automated photo studio: after the operator places a product on the turntable and selects a lighting template, the machine controls 170 LED panels, turntable rotation ..., up to ~250 products/day.

Scientific, industrial, macro, or copy work: measuring lamp-to-subject distances, applying inverse-square and bellows-extension/filter-factor formulas, and computing exposure counts for repeatable documentation series.

Photographer field-tests new equipment or a new shooting technique on location (new body/lens, drone, flash, filters, tilt-shift or long-exposure method) under uncontrolled outdoor light and weather, shooting real subjects and deriving practical settings and a working procedure.

Photographer runs controlled technical tests in the studio/office: shoots standardized charts and test targets to compare sensors, lenses, ISO/dynamic range and light sources, and builds color-managed output procedures by printing profiling targets and measuring them with a spectrophotometer to create ICC profiles for new paper/ink combinations.

Photographer experiments with photographic chemistry and print materials in a darkroom/print lab: mixing developers or alternative-process sensitizers, hand-coating papers, varying exposure and processing times, and evaluating density, tone and permanence of the resulting prints.

Scientific/industrial photographer develops a new imaging procedure in a lab or plant: rigging illumination and optics for photomicrography, high-speed, macro, infrared/UV or multispectral capture of a novel specimen or process, running trials, validating results and writing up the protocol.

sources.system: Tecno DXOMARK Joint Imaging Laboratory (DXOMARK Camera V6 automated lab solution)
sources.title: DxOMark Teams With Tecno to Launch World's First Automated Imaging Lab | PetaPixel
sources.claim: Tecno/DXOMARK joint imaging laboratory is a purpose-built, fully automated camera-testing lab in which robotic positioning rigs, automatic chart switching and controlled lighting execute an entire imaging-quality test protocol and produce the report without a human in the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: controlled characterization of cameras and lenses against standardized charts and lighting. A photographer's controlled comparison testing uses the same objects (cameras, charts, studio lights) and the same measured outputs, so lab performance carries over to that portion of photographic procedure research.

sources.system: X-Rite i1iSis 2 / i1iSis 2 XL automated chart reader with i1Profiler
sources.title: i1iSis 2 XL Automated Chart Reader for Profiling and Calibration | X-Rite
sources.claim: The X-Rite i1iSis 2 automated chart reader is a commercial motorized spectrophotometer that scans printed test targets and automates creation of printer/ICC profiles used in photographic print workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: building a color-managed printing procedure. Establishing a procedure for a new paper/ink requires printing targets and measuring them; the instrument physically transports and measures the chart and produces the profile, the accepted output of that research step, in a purpose-built device.

sources.developer: Argonne National Laboratory, Center for Nanoscale Materials

sources.transferJustification: Related task: developing a new coating formulation and process. Photographic materials research (emulsions, sensitizers, coated papers and inks) involves the same physical operations — dispensing and mixing liquids, coating a substrate, drying/curing, optical read-out and iteration — at comparable precision inside an enclosed robotic lab.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop optimization of a coated optical film. The steps mirror photographic materials research (mix chemistry, coat substrate, process, image and measure optical response), so the demonstrated loop transfers to formulation-and-characterization research on photographic coatings in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials (Journal Article) | OSTI.GOV

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous materials-development experimentation. It shows closed-loop synthesis and characterization research running unattended in a purpose-built robotic cell, supporting the materials side of this task at E1.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scientific imaging experiments. Cited to bound capability: autonomy exists only within a single pre-configured instrument's parameter space, not in assembling and validating a new imaging procedure with new illumination and optics.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated studio capture. Cited only to bound capability — these rigs replay human-specified lighting and camera recipes and provide no autonomous exploration or aesthetic evaluation, which developing a new lighting procedure requires.

instances.label: Portrait/wedding/school photographer in the studio workroom finishes a client order: dry-mounts 5x7-16x20 prints on foam or mat board and fits the mounted prints, with mat and backing, into stock frames or presentation mounts, then inspects for dust and alignment and packs. Small mixed batches, standard sizes, workbench and hand press.

Photographer or in-house lab tech laminates/encapsulates a run of finished prints (display prints, menu boards, trade-show graphics) on a roller or flatbed laminator and mounts them to rigid board, trimming to size. Standard repeated sizes, production print-finishing area.

Fine-art or commercial photographer applies a protective lacquer/spray coating to finished prints in a spray area or booth, racks them to cure, and inspects the coated surface for runs, dust and even gloss.

Bespoke custom framing of an exhibition or gallery print: mat and backing cut to a one-off size and opening, glass or acrylic cut, moulding mitred and joined, print positioned and fitted, dust cover sealed and hanging hardware attached.

On-location event/school/sports photographer at the venue mounts on-site prints into cardboard folder frames, easel mounts or slip-in frames on a folding table amid crowds and a shifting layout, and hands them to customers.

tasks.label: Send film to photofinishing laboratories for processing.

instances.label: Studio/office after a film shoot: photographer gathers 5-30 exposed 35mm/120 rolls from a table or camera bag, matches them to a completed lab order form (dev/scan/push-pull notes), slips them into a padded mailer or small box with padding, seals it, prints and affixes a prepaid carrier label, and puts it in the outgoing-mail bin for USPS/FedEx pickup.

Hand-delivery to a local pro lab or retail photofinishing counter: photographer drives or walks several blocks/miles through public streets with rolls in a bag, enters the shop, hands film across the counter, fills out the drop-off envelope/ticket and discusses processing instructions with the technician, and takes a receipt.

Taking an already-sealed film mailer out to the mail stream: walking or driving to a post office counter, UPS Store, or street drop box, waiting in line if needed, paying/scanning, and depositing the parcel.

On assignment away from the studio (photojournalist, destination wedding, travel): packing exposed rolls in a hotel room or vehicle with improvised materials, keeping them out of X-ray/heat, and getting them to a shipping counter, hotel front desk, or a courier/runner for transport to the lab.

High-volume studio with a lab courier account: photographer bags each job's rolls separately, writes job numbers/instructions on lab envelopes, logs them in a job sheet, and leaves the batch in the designated pickup box or hands it to the lab courier at the studio door on the daily run.

instances.label: Loading a fresh 35mm cassette into a film camera and unloading it on assignment (portrait/wedding/editorial, studio or client location): open the back, seat the cassette, pull the leader across to the take-up spool, close and advance to frame 1, then rewind and pocket/label the exposed cassette, often quickly between shots.

Loading a 120 roll into a medium-format camera or interchangeable back: seat the fresh spool, thread the paper leader across to the empty take-up spool, wind to the start arrow/frame 1; at the end, wind off, remove the exposed roll and seal it with its tape. Done in a studio or on location.

Loading 4x5 or 8x10 sheet film into film holders in a darkroom or a changing tent/bag in total darkness (film seated under the guide rails, correct emulsion side, dark slide reinserted), and unloading exposed sheets back into a light-tight box for processing.

In a darkroom or changing bag, unloading exposed roll film from its cassette/backing paper, cutting/trimming the leader, spooling it onto a developing reel and sealing it in a processing tank (or attaching it to a leader card and feeding a lab processor).

Specialized/industrial film handling in a lab or facility: loading and unloading film magazines for aerial, scientific, high-speed or copy cameras, loading instant/sheet film packs, and bulk-loading reusable 35mm cassettes from a bulk roll in the darkroom.

sources.title: Harman Makes Largest Investment in Film Manufacturing Since the 1990s

sources.transferJustification: Related task: spooling/attaching 35mm film onto a spool inside a light-tight cassette. Same material, same darkness constraint, same thread-and-wind manipulation as threading a leader onto a camera take-up spool, at far higher throughput and tolerance.

sources.title: The best things in life are analog | ADOX PHOTO FACTORIES

sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine spooling of roll film. The manipulations (aligning, winding a film web onto a spool in darkness) are the same class as loading a roll into a camera or reusable cassette.

sources.title: The best things in life are analog | ADOX news
sources.claim: ADOX's 120 finishing machine aligns film to the paper backing, cuts it, attaches film to the backing paper and spools the roll — the exact operations a photographer performs when threading a 120 paper leader onto a spool, done by machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching 120 film to backing paper and winding the assembly onto a spool in darkness — the same objects (120 film, paper leader, spool) and the same threading/winding precision required to load a 120 back.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: the complete load-and-unload cycle for sheet film in a light-tight holder, performed by one machine — directly parallel to a photographer unloading exposed sheets from holders and reloading them with fresh film.

instances.label: Solo or group show install at a commercial gallery, co-op, or arts center: photographer transports crated framed prints, lays out the wall plan, measures and marks, drives hooks/nails or sets rail-and-cable hardware, hangs and levels 20-40 frames at 57-58 in. centerline, cleans glass, applies vinyl wall text and title cards, aims track lights, and sets out price lists and cards.

Outdoor art festival / craft-fair booth: photographer erects a 10x10 pop-up canopy with fabric top on grass or asphalt, adds weights and sidewalls in wind, assembles mesh/ProPanel walls, hangs 30-60 matted and framed prints with hooks, sets print browse bins, table, signage, and card reader, then breaks it down at day's end.

Small hanging show in a cafe, restaurant, library, clinic, or office lobby: 8-20 framed prints hung on whatever hardware the venue has (rail, existing nails, uneven or plaster walls), worked around patrons and furniture, with price/title labels and a contact card holder placed.

Booth at an indoor photo expo, hotel-ballroom art show, or convention-center trade show where the venue supplies pipe-and-drape or modular hardwall panels: photographer mounts prints and large-format canvases on the provided panels, arranges a table with portfolio and print bins, clips on booth lighting, and posts signage.

Open-studio or pop-up show in the photographer's home studio or a short-term rented raw space: furniture cleared, prints hung on residential drywall and improvised panels, portable lights and stands positioned, sales table and payment setup arranged in an idiosyncratic, non-standard room.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging painted parts on conveyor hooks. It transfers to hanging framed prints in an E1 counterfactual because the objects are rigid, gripper-compatible items presented in known poses and the placement is onto a hook fixture at a known height — the same pick-and-hang primitive, with lighter loads than steel beams.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial print-and-apply labeling. Applying an adhesive title/price card at a set offset beside a hung print is the same pick-and-apply operation on a planar surface at known coordinates.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans

sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying in a home. Cited to bound E3/E2 capability: even the frontier home humanoid demo covers soft-goods handling in a staged room, not wall-fixing hardware, measured layout, or leveled hanging of glazed frames.

tasks.label: Produce computer-readable, digital images from film, using flatbed scanners and photofinishing laboratories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial studio/office workstation: photographer scans small batches of 35mm or 120 negatives and mounted slides on a desktop flatbed (e.g., Epson V850) or dedicated film scanner — slides strips out of glassine sleeves, blows off dust, snaps them into holder tabs, places the holder on the platen, runs the scan software, crops/spots, and exports files.

Home workspace of a freelance/self-employed photographer: multi-session digitization of a personal or client film archive on a kitchen table or spare-room desk, mixed and sometimes degraded originals, no institutional standard for the room.

Photofinishing lab / minilab: high-volume develop-and-scan of whole rolls on production equipment (Noritsu HS-1800, Fuji Frontier SP-3000, Pakon F135) — uncut rolls fed into the film carrier, hundreds of frames per day, batch color/density rendering and file delivery.

High-end / archival digitization in a pro lab or studio: medium- and large-format sheet film, delicate or damaged originals, wet mounting or Flextight/drum scanning, individual tonal and color correction to a fine-art or reproduction standard.

Outsourcing route from the studio/office: sorting and labeling exposed or processed rolls, packing and shipping them to a photofinishing laboratory, then reviewing the returned digital files, accepting them, and requesting rescans of bad frames.

On-site digitization at a client's premises or a family's home: portable scanner or camera-scanning rig set up on whatever surface is available to digitize negatives, slides or transparencies that cannot leave the site; variable lighting, dust and layout.

instances.label: Black-and-white roll film (35mm/120): photographer loads exposed rolls onto spiral reels in a changing bag or blacked-out room in their own home/studio darkroom, mixes and tempers developer/stop/fixer, times and agitates the tank, washes, adds wetting agent, hangs the negatives to dry, then sleeves them. Chemistry, dilution and times vary by film stock and push/pull needs.

Color negative or slide roll film (C-41/E-6): photographer runs the process at home or in a small studio darkroom with a kit and a tabletop/rotary processor, holding 38-39 C temperature tightly through developer, blix/bleach-fix, stabilizer, wash and dry.

Production develop-and-print run inside a commercial photo lab or studio lab: rolls are attached to leader cards and fed to a roller-transport minilab film processor, then negatives are printed/scanned in volume on a minilab printer with automatic color and density correction; operator monitors control strips, replenishment and output quality.

Routine enlargements and proof/work prints from negatives in a wet darkroom: set the enlarger and easel, make a test strip, expose onto RC or RA-4 paper, run trays or a roller-transport paper processor, wash, dry and trim a batch of standard-size prints for a client or contact sheet.

Custom/exhibition printing: the photographer interprets a negative on fiber paper with split-grade contrast control, extensive dodging and burning, bleaching or toning, then dries, flattens and hand-spots dust marks with spotting dyes and a fine brush before mounting.

Large-format sheet film (4x5 to 8x10) and specialty negatives: development in trays, hangers, or a rotary drum, often individually push/pulled per exposure and processed a few sheets at a time in a home or small studio darkroom.

tasks.label: Observe sets or locations for potential problems and to determine filming and lighting requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-camera TV studio production (news, talk show, live entertainment): before and during the show the camera operator walks/looks over the studio set, checking for problems — cable runs and trip hazards in camera paths, boom or lighting stands creeping into frame, monitor glare, hot spots and shadows on the set, sightline conflicts with other cameras and talent marks — and determines camera positions, lens choices and what lighting adjustments the gaffer/LD must make.

Soundstage or built-set film/episodic shoot: operator walks the set with the DP and gaffer, observing for rigging, grip stands, reflections in windows/glass, continuity and shadow problems, floor marks and dolly-track clearance, and determines shooting requirements (camera position, lens, height, movement) and lighting requirements (key/fill placement, flags, level and color-temperature changes) for each setup.

Shoot at an institutional venue or event site (arena/stadium, corporate conference hall, house of worship, hotel ballroom, courtroom pool feed): operator surveys the venue in advance or on arrival for problems — restricted camera positions, obstructed sightlines, mixed/flickering house lighting, color temperature and level, power and cable routing, crowd and safety issues — and determines camera placement and supplemental lighting needs.

Location shoot at premises taken as found (private home, small business, restaurant, warehouse, wedding venue, street exterior) for commercial, corporate, documentary or event work: operator observes the space for problems — clutter and unattractive backgrounds, mixed daylight/tungsten/fluorescent sources, windows blowing out, low ceilings, noise, power limits, sun path over the shoot day — and determines framing, camera positions and the lighting package to bring in.

ENG / breaking-news or run-and-gun documentary field work: operator arrives at an uncontrolled outdoor or interior scene, rapidly assesses hazards (traffic, emergency operations, crowds, weather), picks a background and shooting position, judges available light, sun direction and contrast, and decides whether an on-camera or LED panel light, ND or reflector is required — often within minutes and while conditions change.

tasks.label: Test, clean, maintain, and repair broadcast equipment, including testing microphones, to ensure proper working condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-show/pre-record equipment check in a TV studio or remote (OB) truck: power up each camera chain, verify image (back focus, shading, colour match between cameras), check viewfinder and monitors, blow/wipe dust off the lens front element, confirm camera cables, tally and intercom, and hand off to air. Institution-controlled premises, fixed layout, standard gear.

Testing microphones and the audio chain before/between takes: plugging in and level-checking boom, lav, handheld and camera-top mics, verifying phantom power and wireless RF channels/batteries, monitoring on headphones, and swapping out a mic or cable that reads dead or noisy. Occurs in studio or on a controlled set/stage.

On-location ENG/field upkeep while the shoot is running: wiping rain, sea spray, dust or fingerprints off the lens and filter between shots, swapping a failing battery or media card, re-seating a loose BNC/XLR, re-taping a lav, and drying/protecting the rig — done on found ground (street, arena, remote location) under weather and time pressure.

Bench diagnostics and minor repair in the station gear room or shop: using a cable tester/tone generator to isolate which cable, adapter or mic is faulty, re-terminating or soldering an XLR/BNC connector, replacing a worn cable or lens-mount screw, tightening a slipping tripod head, cleaning oxidised contacts, and tagging out what must go to engineering.

Routine cleaning and preventive maintenance of the kit at the facility gear cage/prep bay: blowing and wiping lens elements, filters and sensor, cleaning camera bodies and mattes, inspecting and coiling cables, charging and load-testing battery packs, checking rigs/mounts and repacking cases after a shoot.

sources.title: IQLaR | Imatest
sources.claim: Imatest/Sofica IQLaR is a commercial image-quality laboratory automation product in which a 6-axis robot arm on a track positions and aligns a camera against test targets, controls lighting, triggers capture and runs automated analysis — i.e. an automated functional/quality test of a camera in a purpose-built test cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line / lab image-quality testing of cameras. It transfers to 'test broadcast equipment to ensure proper working condition' because the objects are cameras and lenses, the checks (focus/back focus, resolution, colour, uniformity) are the same ones a camera operator verifies before a show, and the pass/fail precision exceeds a human eyeball check.

sources.title: iQ-Automator | Image Engineering
sources.claim: Image Engineering's iQ-Automator pairs workflow software with a UR3 robot arm that automatically positions and aligns the camera under test and executes image-quality test sequences in a test lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated camera testing in a lab cell. Same transfer as IQLaR — the system verifies that a camera is imaging correctly, which is the substance of the operator's 'test camera' check, in a fixtured purpose-built setting.

sources.title: LCU modulo - Lens Cleaning - Modulo - SCHNEIDER Optical Machines
sources.claim: Schneider Optical Machines' LCU Modulo is a fully ... inline machine that brush-cleans both sides of lenses scratch-free, removing fingerprints and residues, in an optics production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production cleaning of optical lenses. It transfers to 'clean broadcast equipment' because the workpiece is the same class of object (precision glass optics), the contaminant (fingerprints, residue, dust) is the same, and the scratch-free standard is at least as strict as a camera operator's lens cleaning.

sources.title: Automated Testing for Bluetooth Earbuds at the Limits of Range
sources.claim: Nextgen's ATAM Connect is a commercial automated audio-device test platform that uses a collaborative robot to physically manipulate the device under test while running audio quality, pairing and functional test sequences.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-handled functional and audio testing of small audio transducer devices. It transfers to 'testing microphones' because the cell physically presents the device, plays/records acoustic stimuli and returns pass/fail on audio performance, which is what a mic check establishes.

sources.title: Microphones / Loudspeakers & Microspeakers - Listen, Inc.
sources.claim: Listen Inc's SoundCheck is used for microphone testing on production lines, integrated with automated line control so that measurement is automatic and failed units are removed ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line acoustic test of microphones. It transfers to 'testing microphones to ensure proper working condition' because the measured parameters (frequency response, self-noise, distortion) are the fault modes a mic check is looking for, and the line physically sorts out failures.

sources.system: G4 NTM robotic patch panel (with EXFO diagnostics)

sources.claim: Telescent's G4 NTM robotic patch panel is a deployed automated fiber cross-connect that makes and breaks optical connections and performs physical-layer diagnostics inside a purpose-built enclosure at network operator sites.

tasks.label: Set up and operate electric news gathering (ENG) microwave vehicles to gather and edit raw footage on location to send to television affiliates for broadcast.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Breaking/spot news: photographer drives the ENG live truck to a street scene (fire, crash, police standoff), finds a parking spot with clear sky path and no overhead power lines, sets the brake/levelers, raises the pneumatic mast, aims/peaks the microwave dish to a mountaintop or tower receive site while coordinating with the station's receive-site operator, runs camera/audio cable, shoots the scene and interviews handheld, cuts a quick VOSOT/package in the truck's edit bay, and feeds it plus a live shot to the station for network/affiliate distribution. Crowds, weather, deadline pressure, changing scene.

Scheduled live shot from an institution-controlled venue or media compound (courthouse plaza, city hall, campus, arena/stadium media lot): truck parks in the designated live-truck position, mast up, path to a known receive site, tripod/camera/light/mic set for a reporter standup, b-roll of the event shot, package edited in the truck and fed to the station and affiliates.

Straight event feed from a controlled venue: truck positioned at a fixed, pre-surveyed spot to provide a clean, largely locked-off camera feed of a scheduled proceeding or game (press conference, ceremony, sporting event) plus recorded raw footage sent back for the newscast; little roving camera work, minimal on-site editing.

Remote/rural or severe-weather deployment: truck sent to a rural crash, wildfire, flood or storm-coverage position at the fringe of microwave coverage; operator must hunt for a workable line-of-sight position (sometimes relaying via another truck or helicopter), run the generator, deploy the mast in wind/rain, shoot in poor light, and feed footage back on deadline.

In-truck ingest and edit: photographer offloads camera cards/wireless media in the truck's edit bay at the scene, logs and cuts the reporter's package with track and nat sound, checks audio/video levels, and transmits the finished piece plus raw feed via microwave or bonded cellular to the station for affiliate/network use.

Pre-/post-assignment truck work at the station lot: pre-shift inspection of the ENG microwave vehicle (fuel, generator, tires, mast air pressure, safety interlocks), loading and cabling camera gear, deploying the mast to test the link to the receive site and confirm channel assignment, then stowing and returning the truck.

tasks.label: Perform a series of manual adjustments to the spine or other articulations of the body to correct the musculoskeletal system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine high-velocity, low-amplitude manual adjustment in the chiropractor's own clinic: patient positioned prone, supine or side-posture on a treatment table, practitioner palpates the spine for restricted/tender segments, sets a hand contact on a spinous or transverse process (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacroiliac), takes the joint to end-range and delivers 3-8 short thrusts over a 5-10 minute visit, monitoring patient tolerance throughout.

Low-force or mechanically assisted adjustment in the clinic: Activator/Impulse instrument thrusts, drop-piece table adjusting, or flexion-distraction, chosen for patients in acute pain, with disc involvement, or who cannot tolerate a manual thrust. Practitioner still selects the segment, angle, force setting and pre-load by hand.

Extremity and non-spinal articulation adjustment in the clinic: shoulder, elbow, wrist/carpals, hip, knee, ankle/foot, ribs, or TMJ; practitioner stabilizes the proximal segment, positions the limb, and applies a graded manipulative thrust or mobilization, typically alongside spinal work.

Adjustment of special populations in the clinic: pregnant patients (side-posture/Webster technique on a modified table), elderly patients with osteoporosis, spinal stenosis or fused segments, and pediatric/infant patients; force, vector and positioning must be heavily modified and contraindications continuously screened.

Off-site adjustment: sideline or training-room work at sporting events, corporate wellness or event booths, and home/assisted-living visits, using a portable table or drop-chair in a space taken as found, with variable lighting, surfaces and patient positioning.

sources.system: Cervical spine rotation-traction manipulation robotic training system (Wangjing Hospital / Beijing Institute of Technology)
sources.developer: Liguo Zhu, Wangjing Hospital, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences with Beijing Institute of Technology
sources.title: Robot trainer helps perfect orthopaedic technique (Nature partner content)
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic system in spinal manipulation is a training simulator that emulates the patient's cervical spine so human physicians can practice rotation-traction manipulation; it is used in eight Chinese TCM universities to train physicians, and its developer says a treatment-delivering version remains a distant goal. This is direct evidence that no robot performs the adjustment itself.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (spinal manipulation/rotation-traction thrust). It is cited to establish that the robot occupies the patient role in training, not the practitioner role delivering the thrust.

sources.title: AI Massage Startup Raises $83 Million, Brings Robots to Equinox - Bloomberg
sources.claim: Aescape is a commercially deployed, autonomous two-arm robotic massage table installed in gyms and massage studios; it delivers soft-tissue pressure to a fully clothed client lying prone, covering back through calves. It does not position patients or perform joint manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Massage is the closest deployed robotic task involving force-controlled contact with a patient's back. Cited to bound the frontier: it applies distributed soft-tissue pressure, not a segment-specific high-velocity thrust to a joint, so it does not transfer to chiropractic adjustment.

sources.title: Aescape Robotic Massage - Safe by design, built for you (Massage Envy)
sources.claim: Aescape's commercial service is limited to soft-tissue coverage from the upper back to the calves on a fully clothed client, with no work on the neck, no patient repositioning, and no joint manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (therapeutic bodywork on the back). Cited to show the deployed system's scope excludes the cervical spine, patient positioning and articular thrusting that define a chiropractic adjustment.

sources.title: Can a robot give a decent massage? We tested one at a luxury hotel in New York City - CNBC
sources.claim: Independent hands-on trade reporting confirms Aescape operates without a therapist present and works only on the back region, scanning the body then applying pressure with its arms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (back bodywork). Establishes autonomy and the narrow, soft-tissue-only scope of the most capable deployed patient-contact therapy robot.

sources.title: A New Option: Tui Na Massage by a Robot Masseuse - Parkway Shenton
sources.claim: EMMA is a deployed clinical massage robot in Singapore, but it is explicitly a soft-tissue treatment system replicating Tui Na kneading/pressing, not joint manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (TCM manual therapy). Tui Na delivered by EMMA is soft-tissue pressure with a single arm on a prone patient; it does not include the spinal thrust/joint cavitation component of chiropractic adjustment.

sources.system: Robot-assisted massage systems (systematic review of the field)
sources.developer: Mayo Clinic authors (Yang, Lim, Mohabbat, et al.)
sources.title: Robotics in Massage: A Systematic Review (Health Services Research and Managerial Epidemiology)
sources.claim: A 2024 systematic review of robot-assisted massage finds the technology is still not in wide clinical use and identifies no robotic system performing joint manipulation; reviewed systems replicate soft-tissue massage techniques.
sources.transferJustification: Field-level review of the closest robotic task (manual therapy on patients). Cited as corroborating absence of any system performing manipulative thrusts; it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Diagnose health problems by reviewing patients' health and medical histories, questioning, observing, and examining patients and interpreting x-rays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-patient initial evaluation in a chiropractic office: take/review intake history and questionnaires, question the patient about complaint and red flags, observe posture and gait, palpate spine and paraspinal soft tissue (static and motion palpation), measure range of motion, run orthopedic and basic neurological tests (reflexes, myotomes, dermatomes), and interpret an in-office plain-film spinal series to reach a working diagnosis.

Routine follow-up visit re-assessment in the clinic: brief questioning about response to prior care and current pain, quick observation, static and motion palpation of the spine and pelvis to locate restricted/tender segments, a short ROM or provocative test, forming the assessment that guides that day's adjustment.

Complex or red-flag presentation in the clinic: radiating leg/arm pain, post-trauma, prior spinal surgery, or systemic comorbidities; deeper review of outside records and prior MRI/CT/x-ray reports, extended neurological and orthopedic examination, interpretation of radiographs for fracture, instability, spondylolisthesis or destructive lesions, and a decision to treat, co-manage, or refer out.

Off-site evaluation: sideline assessment at a sports event, corporate/health-fair spinal screening, or a home visit to a homebound patient; history and questioning plus hands-on palpation and orthopedic testing performed on a portable table, chair, or floor, with no imaging and variable space, lighting and clothing.

Special-population examination in the clinic: infant/pediatric, pregnant, or frail elderly patient; modified positioning (side-lying, seated, on a caregiver's lap), gentle palpation, adapted orthopedic/neurologic screening, careful decision about whether imaging is appropriate.

sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: The closest system to a whole clinical examination (interview, inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation) is ProteCT, a robotic tele-examination cabin evaluated on emergency-department patients, but it is driven by a remote physician rather than operating autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general physical examination of emergency patients, which shares the palpation and inspection steps of a chiropractic exam. Transfer fails because the system is continuously teleoperated by a remote physician, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: South China University of Technology (Su, Liu, Ren et al.)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound can scan a body region and flag findings without a human operator, but it covers only a narrow imaging sub-step under laboratory/clinical-study conditions, not history-taking, hands-on musculoskeletal examination, or a chiropractic diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sonographic examination of a patient. It shows robots can position a probe on a body surface with force control, but it does not include patient history, orthopedic/neurologic testing, radiograph interpretation, or rendering a diagnosis, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage table scans a clothed body and delivers pressure-controlled bodywork in commercial gyms and massage franchises, demonstrating autonomous robot contact with a human body in a structured facility, but it performs no assessment, palpatory diagnosis, or clinical decision-making.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic soft-tissue bodywork on a human, comparable in contact and body-mapping to palpation. Transfer fails for diagnosis: the robot applies pre-selected massage programs to a user-chosen area and produces no clinical findings, examination tests, or diagnostic conclusion.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation (and TRINA-based auscultation robot)
sources.developer: University research groups (Zhu et al.; INESC/Portuguese team)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic auscultation of heart ... lungs has been demonstrated only at research-platform level, indicating that even single diagnostic maneuvers on a patient remain laboratory demonstrations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical diagnostic maneuver on a patient. It supports only placement of a sensor on the torso in a lab; it does not cover musculoskeletal palpation, orthopedic testing, or diagnostic synthesis, so it cannot substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Evaluate the functioning of the neuromuscularskeletal system and the spine using systems of chiropractic diagnosis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-patient initial evaluation in a private chiropractic clinic: takes history, observes gait and posture, measures cervical/lumbar range of motion, performs static and motion palpation along the whole spine and pelvis to locate restricted, tender, or hypermobile segments, runs orthopedic tests (e.g., Kemp's, straight-leg raise) and a neurological screen (deep tendon reflexes, myotome strength, dermatome sensation), and integrates the findings into a working diagnosis and care plan. Draped, partially clothed patient of unknown anatomy and pain tolerance, on a treatment table.

Pre-adjustment assessment at a routine follow-up visit (the highest-volume case): 2-5 minutes of hands-on re-check before treating — motion palpation of the region of complaint, tenderness and muscle-tone check, quick active range-of-motion screen, leg-length/pelvic check, sometimes an instrument scan (paraspinal thermography or surface EMG) — to decide which segments to adjust that day. Clinic treatment room, patient prone/seated, interactive verbal feedback about pain throughout.

Periodic re-examination / progress exam in the clinic: repeat objective measures (inclinometer range of motion, orthopedic tests, muscle testing, posture photos), repeat outcome questionnaires, compare with baseline and with X-ray or MRI findings, and document whether care is working and should continue, change, or stop.

Complex or atypical clinic patient: older adult with osteoporosis/prior surgery, a patient with radicular or suspected non-mechanical pain, a pediatric or pregnant patient. Requires cautious graded palpation, thorough neurological and vascular screening, red-flag differential reasoning, and a judgment about contraindication or referral out.

Off-site evaluation in an improvised setting: sideline or training-room assessment at a sports event, corporate wellness or health-fair spinal screening, or a house call for a homebound patient — evaluation done on a portable table, mat, chair, or bed, with variable lighting, space, clothing, and no clinic equipment.

sources.system: Robotic ultrasound scoliosis scanning system (UR5 + force sensor + US probe, HK PolyU / TUM groups)
sources.developer: Hong Kong Polytechnic University / Technical University of Munich research groups
sources.title: Reliability of Robotic Ultrasound Scanning for Scoliosis Assessment in Comparison with Manual Scanning (arXiv:2205.03566)
sources.claim: A robotic arm with force control and deep-learning guidance autonomously scanned the backs of 23 scoliosis patients with an ultrasound probe, yielding deformity angles comparable to manual scanning; the measurements themselves were then made by two human raters. This is spinal imaging acquisition in a research setting, not a chiropractic functional evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ultrasound imaging of the human spine for deformity assessment. It shows a robot can safely contact and track a human back, but it acquires one static image measure, does not palpate joint motion, does not perform orthopedic or neurological testing, and the clinical interpretation was done by human raters — so it does not carry over to completing a chiropractic diagnostic evaluation.

sources.title: AI and Robotic Massage, Delivered On-Demand - ASME
sources.claim: A commercially deployed robotic massage table scans the client's body with overhead depth sensors and delivers a full autonomous massage without a human therapist; it plans strokes from a 3D surface model but produces no clinical assessment of joint function, tenderness, or neurological status.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hands-on bodywork on a client's back and shoulders in a facility. It establishes safe force-controlled robot contact with human backs, but the system executes preset massage programs from surface geometry and preference input; it does not motion-palpate spinal segments, test reflexes or muscle strength, or generate a diagnosis, so it cannot carry the evaluative task.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous massage robots are being installed in commercial fitness facilities (Equinox clubs) and hotels — a structured human work facility deployment of a body-contact robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial deployment of an autonomous table-based body-contact robot in an E2 facility. Establishes environment and safety maturity for touching clients, but the deployed function is massage delivery, not neuromusculoskeletal evaluation.

sources.system: Unitree H1 / bimanual humanoid teleoperation surrogate for clinical tasks
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions (arXiv:2503.12725)
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstration of a humanoid robot performing clinical physical examinations was carried out entirely by human teleoperation, not autonomously, and only in a laboratory feasibility study.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-performed physical examination manoeuvres on patients. Because control is continuous teleoperation by a clinician, it cannot support a positive autonomous-capability judgment for chiropractic evaluation.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Tissue Palpation and Abnormalities Characterisation via Ergodic Exploration (arXiv:2602.14287)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic palpation for detecting tissue abnormalities remains at the level of silicone phantoms with embedded inclusions in the laboratory; no human-patient diagnostic palpation deployment is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous palpation to characterise tissue stiffness, the closest robotic analogue to chiropractic palpation. Validation is on phantoms, not living patients, and it maps stiffness only rather than assessing joint play, tenderness response, or neurological function, so it does not transfer to the chiropractic exam.

sources.title: Test–retest reliability of KINARM robot sensorimotor and cognitive assessment: in pediatric ice hockey players
sources.claim: Commercial robotic assessment of neuromuscular function exists (KINARM), but it works by having a cooperative subject grasp robot handles and perform automated upper-limb reaching tasks; it measures limb sensorimotor performance and does not examine the spine or perform manual palpation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic quantitative assessment of neuromuscular/sensorimotor function. Transfer fails because the robot only administers standardised limb-movement tasks to a cooperative seated subject; it performs no spinal palpation, orthopedic provocation testing, or clinical differential reasoning.
