tasks.label: Suggest and apply the use of supports such as straps, tapes, bandages, or braces if necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Kinesiology taping in a chiropractic treatment room: after an adjustment, the DC selects tape strips, tears/cuts them, peels the paper backing, anchors on a bony landmark, applies with a prescribed 25–75% stretch along paraspinal, shoulder, or knee musculature over hair and moist skin, rubs to activate the adhesive, and checks skin tolerance and comfort while the patient is prone or seated.

Fitting an off-the-shelf orthopedic support (lumbosacral corset, sacroiliac belt, wrist cock-up splint, or thumb spica) on a clothed patient: measuring/sizing, positioning the device at the correct anatomical level, threading and tensioning Velcro straps, checking circulation and fit while the patient stands or sits, then coaching self-donning.

Rigid athletic taping/strapping of an ankle, wrist, or thumb in-office: applying pre-wrap, anchors, stirrups and heel locks with non-elastic tape at controlled tension around a moving, compliant joint held in a corrected position, then verifying range of motion and comfort.

Applying an elastic compression bandage or wrap (ACE-type, cohesive wrap, or cold-pack compression) around an acutely swollen ankle, knee, or elbow with graduated tension and securing it, on a patient who may guard or wince from pain.

Fitting a cervical collar, posture brace/clavicle strap, or elastic slip-on knee/elbow sleeve: sliding or wrapping the device onto the patient's neck, torso, or limb, adjusting height/tension, and verifying alignment and tolerance before the patient leaves.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing (force-feedback imitation learning + trajectory optimization, UR/Axia80 force-torque setup)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) with Cornell
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv:2510.06127)
sources.claim: UCSD/Cornell researchers built an autonomous framework for adhesive medical tape handling (initial detachment and placement) with a robot arm on a lab bench; it addresses only sub-steps of wound redressing and performance degrades on real human skin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing a secondary wound dressing with medical tape. It is the closest published work to applying tape/supports to a human body, but it automates isolated sub-steps (peeling, placing a strip), not whole-task therapeutic taping at prescribed tension on anatomical landmarks, and the authors report a performance drop on out-of-distribution human skin.

sources.system: One Policy to Dress Them All (sim-to-real RL dressing policy, Sawyer/Franka arm)
sources.title: One Policy to Dress Them All: Learning to Dress People with Diverse Poses and Garments (arXiv:2306.12372)
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing research has demonstrated a learned policy autonomously pulling gown/garment sleeves onto a manikin and onto human participants' arms in a laboratory, with partial arm-dressed ratios rather than reliable completion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a garment onto a person's limb, the nearest analogue to sliding on an elastic support sleeve or brace. Transfer is limited: the demonstrated garments are loose sleeves with the arm held in a static pose, and no strap tensioning, sizing, or fit verification is performed.

sources.system: Force-Constrained Visual Policy for robot-assisted dressing
sources.title: Force-Constrained Visual Policy: Safe Robot-Assisted Dressing via Multi-Modal Sensing (arXiv:2311.04390)
sources.claim: Follow-up dressing work with force-constrained policies on ten human participants reports incomplete arm-dressed ratios and failures where the garment snags on the person, indicating lab-level rather than clinical reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: garment donning on a human limb. Cited to show that even the closest analogue to applying a support onto a patient does not reach worker-quality reliability outside the lab.

sources.title: Equinox | The World's Most Advanced Massage
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated two-arm massage table is commercially deployed in Equinox spas and gyms, showing autonomous, force-controlled robot contact with a human body inside a structured commercial facility — but it only applies pressure with rigid end effectors and does not handle tape, bandages, or braces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on soft-tissue work on a patient's body in a clinic-like facility. It establishes autonomous safe body contact but not deformable/adhesive material manipulation, sizing, or strap fastening, so it does not transfer to applying supports.

roles.title: Dentists, General
roles.description: Examine, diagnose, and treat diseases, injuries, and malformations of teeth and gums. May treat diseases of nerve, pulp, and other dental tissues affecting oral hygiene and retention of teeth. May fit dental appliances or provide preventive care.
roles.sector: Healthcare practitioners and technical

tasks.label: Use masks, gloves, and safety glasses to protect patients and self from infectious diseases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine turnover in a general-practice operatory: after hand hygiene, the dentist dons a fresh ASTM-level surgical mask (shaping the nose bar, tying/looping straps), puts on protective eyewear or loupes with side shields, and pulls on a pair of exam gloves sized to the hand, all within a minute before seating the next patient; PPE comes from wall/counter dispensers.

Placing and later removing protective eyewear on the seated patient before treatment: selecting tinted or clear glasses/shield, fitting them over the patient's own spectacles or over a child's small face, adjusting so they do not slip while the chair is reclined, and confirming comfort.

Mid-procedure PPE management with the patient in the chair: replacing a torn or visibly contaminated glove without touching the outside surface or breaking the aseptic field, re-gloving after leaving the operatory, replacing a saturated mask after an aerosol-generating step, and clearing or swapping fogged/spattered eyewear.

Doffing at the end of the appointment: peeling contaminated gloves off inside-out without self-contamination and discarding them in the correct waste stream, removing the mask by its straps, disinfecting reusable eyewear/face shield with an intermediate-level disinfectant, and performing hand hygiene.

Enhanced PPE for surgical or high-aerosol procedures (extractions, implant placement, ultrasonic scaling) in an operatory or oral-surgery suite: donning an N95 respirator with a user seal check, a face shield over eyewear, a gown, and sterile surgical gloves using aseptic technique, sometimes assisted by a dental assistant.

sources.system: Force-Constrained Visual Policy (robot-assisted dressing, Kemp/Erickson-line assistive robotics research)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / Robotics Institute (RCHI lab) and collaborators
sources.title: Force-Constrained Visual Policy: Safe Robot-Assisted Dressing via Multi-Modal Sensing
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous garment-on-person capability found is research robot-assisted dressing: a robot arm pulls a hospital-gown sleeve onto a seated participant's arm, evaluated in a laboratory human study of 10 participants and 240 trials. It handles a loose sleeve on an arm, not gloves, masks, or eyewear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing (pulling a gown sleeve onto a human arm). Transfer to this task fails: PPE donning requires everting a thin, tacky, skin-tight nitrile glove onto a hand or manipulator, seating a mask's nose bar and straps, and placing eyewear precisely on a face near the eyes — far higher precision and far more deformable, self-adhering material than a loose sleeve, and demonstrated only in a lab, not at clinical reliability.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics (British Dental Journal)
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous dental robot performed a crown-preparation procedure on a human patient, but it is a chairside cutting/scanning system that human staff set up, drape and support; no part of its demonstrated capability includes donning masks, gloves or eyewear or placing protective eyewear on the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operative dentistry in the same operatory environment. It shows what dental robotics can do in a dental setting, but the cited system does not perform PPE donning/doffing or patient eye protection, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: KHZKHC Automatic Glove Machine (disposable glove donning dispenser)
sources.title: Amazon.com: KHZKHC Automatic Glove Machine, Disposable Glove Machine
sources.claim: Commercial automatic gloving machines exist that open and apply a disposable glove in a few seconds, but they are dispensers into which a human inserts their hands; they do not don a glove onto a robot manipulator, and they do not handle masks or eyewear.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated glove donning. Transfer fails because the machine only presents an opened glove; a human hand performs the insertion and the machine covers neither masks, protective eyewear, nor doffing, so no robotic system completes the instance.

tasks.label: Administer anesthetics to limit the amount of pain experienced by patients during procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cooperative adult in a general dental operatory needing local infiltration (e.g., maxillary buccal) before a restoration: dry the mucosa, apply topical gel, retract lip/cheek, insert a 27/30-gauge needle at the mucobuccal fold, aspirate, deposit a carpule slowly while reassuring the patient, then test for profound soft-tissue and pulpal anesthesia before starting.

Adult needing an inferior alveolar nerve block (plus long buccal) for mandibular restorative, endodontic, or extraction work: palpate the coronoid notch and pterygomandibular raphe in an open, moving mouth, advance about 20-25 mm to the mandibular foramen, aspirate to avoid intravascular injection, deposit, confirm lip/tongue numbness, and re-inject or switch technique if the block fails.

Supplemental anesthesia mid-procedure on a partly anesthetized patient: painful palatal injection, intraligamentary/PDL injection with a pressure syringe, or intrapulpal injection for a 'hot tooth', judged from the patient's reported pain while the field is wet with saliva/blood and rubber dam or instruments are in place.

Pediatric or highly anxious/phobic patient: behavior guidance and distraction, topical, slow small-volume injection kept out of the child's sight, sometimes combined with nitrous oxide inhalation sedation (placing and adjusting the nasal hood, titrating flow, monitoring the patient) in a general/family practice operatory.

Medically complex or special-needs patient (cardiac disease, anticoagulants, pregnancy, anesthetic allergy, limited mouth opening, involuntary movement): choosing agent and vasoconstrictor, limiting dose, monitoring vitals, managing an unexpected reaction, and occasionally administering oral or IV moderate sedation alongside the local anesthetic.

sources.system: FZ-DISAS-I autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS)
sources.developer: Sichuan Fengzhun Robot Technology Co., Ltd
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery - The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry
sources.claim: In clinical use of an autonomous dental implant robot on 74 patients, the local anesthetic was still administered by the clinical team; the robot's autonomy covers osteotomy drilling and implant insertion, not injection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous intraoral drilling in real patients in a dental operatory). It is the closest existing capability to intraoral instrument insertion, yet the published protocol shows a human gives the anesthetic injection first, so it does not substantiate robotic completion of this task.

sources.developer: clinical case series, Chinese hospital (multiple robot vendors)
sources.title: Accuracy of robot-assisted dental implant surgery and its clinical influencing factors: a retrospective case series of 100 patients | BMC Oral Health
sources.claim: Retrospective series of 100 robot-assisted dental implant patients: infiltration anesthesia is given by the surgeon before the robotic arm is brought to the oral cavity and registered.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-assisted intraoral surgery on patients). Shows that in the most advanced intraoral robotic workflows deployed clinically, dental local anesthesia remains a human-performed step.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: The first fully automated dental procedure performed by a robot on a human patient was a crown preparation (tooth cutting); no autonomous dental robot has been reported administering the anesthetic injection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous intraoral tooth preparation on a patient). It is the frontier of autonomous intraoral robotics, but the demonstrated procedure is hard-tissue cutting, not needle placement and anesthetic deposition, so it does not transfer to administering anesthesia.

sources.developer: Hemmerling et al. / Oceanic Medical Products
sources.title: Technical communication: First robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans using the Magellan system - PubMed
sources.claim: Robotic nerve-block delivery in humans has been demonstrated only under joystick teleoperation from a remote control centre (13 patients), not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic regional anesthesia nerve block in humans). Nearest analogue to a nerve block performed by a machine, but it is teleoperated by an anesthesiologist with a joystick, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: An autonomous robot has performed a needle-free intramuscular (deltoid) injection on a human, but only as a one-off demonstration and without inserting a needle into tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous injection into a human). Transfer fails: the target is an exposed deltoid treated with a needle-free jet, whereas dental anesthesia requires needle insertion millimetres to centimetres deep into oral mucosa in a confined, moving, saliva-filled mouth, with aspiration and titration.

sources.developer: Rutgers University (Leipheimer, Balter, Yarmush et al.)
sources.title: First-in-human evaluation of a hand-held automated venipuncture device for rapid venous blood draws | TECHNOLOGY
sources.claim: Automated needle insertion into humans has reached first-in-human demonstration only for peripheral arm veins, using a hand-held device positioned by a clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous needle insertion into a patient). Anatomy and access differ fundamentally from the oral cavity, the device is hand-positioned by a clinician, and it remains a research prototype, so it does not substantiate completion of dental anesthesia.

tasks.label: Examine teeth, gums, and related tissues, using dental instruments, x-rays, or other diagnostic equipment, to evaluate dental health, diagnose diseases or abnormalities, and plan appropriate treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic recall exam in a general dental operatory: cooperative adult reclined in the chair, dentist uses mirror and explorer for visual-tactile caries and restoration checks on all quadrants, screens periodontal tissues with a probe, orders/reviews bitewing radiographs (sensor placed intraorally, tube head aligned), records findings and recommends treatment.

Comprehensive new-patient examination in the operatory: full-mouth or panoramic radiographic series, six-point periodontal charting on every tooth with bleeding/recession/mobility, occlusion and TMJ evaluation, extraoral head-and-neck palpation and intraoral soft-tissue oral cancer screening, integration with medical history, and a sequenced written treatment plan.

Emergency / problem-focused exam for pain, swelling or trauma: localize the offending tooth by percussion, palpation, bite test and pulp vitality testing (cold or electric), take a periapical radiograph, differentiate reversible vs irreversible pulpitis, cracked tooth, abscess or perio-endo lesion, and decide immediate treatment; patient is often in pain, guarded and swollen.

Pediatric examination of a young or apprehensive child: intermittent cooperation, small mouth, possible knee-to-knee or parent-lap positioning, behavior guidance, caries risk assessment, eruption and development check, and bitewings on a moving child.

Examination of a medically complex, frail elderly or special-needs patient, in the operatory or at a long-term-care facility with portable equipment: limited mouth opening, strong gag reflex, involuntary movement, dentures/partials to remove and assess, xerostomia, retained roots and mucosal lesions to evaluate.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm performed an autonomous crown preparation (drilling a tooth to a pre-computed geometry) on a live human patient; imaging is acquired with a clinician-held OCT intraoral scanner and the system was not FDA-cleared. It executes a planned restorative procedure, not a diagnostic examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation for a crown. It shares the operatory environment and intraoral precision, but the robot executes a geometry planned in advance from a clinician-acquired scan; it does not probe periodontal pockets, acquire radiographs, screen soft tissue, or generate a diagnosis and treatment plan, so capability does not transfer to the examination task.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robot (Beihang University / FMMU Stomatological Hospital)
sources.developer: Beihang University and FMMU Stomatological Hospital, Xi'an
sources.title: First-ever robot-led dental surgery performed in China
sources.claim: An autonomous robot at the Fourth Military Medical University's Stomatological Hospital placed two 3D-printed implants in a live patient's mouth in a hospital operatory, following a pre-programmed plan derived from a prior CT scan, with staff present but not intervening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral implant osteotomy and placement. It shows a robot can work inside a live patient's mouth in a clinic, but diagnosis and the surgical plan were produced by clinicians from a prior CT; nothing in the demonstration performs examination, tactile/periodontal assessment, or treatment planning.

sources.title: Yomi robotic system from Neocis gets FDA nod for full-arch dental implants
sources.claim: Yomi is the only FDA-cleared robotic system used routinely in US dental offices; it is a co-manipulated haptic guidance platform for implant surgery in which the surgeon physically drives the drill and retains control, so it is not autonomous and performs no examinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted implant placement in the same dental operatory. It is the most mature commercial dental robot, yet it is surgeon-driven haptic guidance for a planned surgical step; it performs no diagnostic examination and, being co-manipulated, cannot support an autonomous judgment.

sources.developer: research group publishing in Scientific Reports
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: SR-NOCS is an autonomous force-controlled robot that inserts a swab into the mouths and noses of live patients; it was validated in two clinical studies with 52 suspected COVID-19 patients, showing autonomous robots can safely place a slender instrument in a human oral cavity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral instrument insertion on live humans in a clinical station. It substantiates safe robotic access to the oral cavity only; the robot collects a specimen and makes no assessment of teeth, gingiva or radiographs, so it cannot substantiate an examination ending in a diagnosis and treatment plan.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: RobOralScan is the first reinforcement-learning pipeline for automatic robotic intraoral scanning; it was evaluated in simulation with real-world hardware validation, and the authors state that in-mouth / human-subject evaluation remains future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of intraoral 3D geometry, the closest robotic analogue to the visual survey portion of an exam. It has not been run in a live mouth, captures only surface geometry (no caries probing, radiographs, or soft-tissue/perio assessment), and issues no diagnosis, so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.system: PerioAI (and FDA-cleared dental imaging AI platforms)
sources.developer: Tan et al., Cell Reports Medicine; Pearl / Overjet / VideaHealth
sources.title: AI-powered digital probing improves periodontal disease diagnosis: Cell Reports Medicine
sources.claim: Automated dental diagnosis that exists today is software-only: PerioAI computes periodontal status from intraoral scans and CBCT without manual probing, and FDA-cleared platforms such as Pearl, Overjet and VideaHealth read radiographs as clinician decision support. None is physically embodied.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated interpretation of dental images. It is software running on human-acquired images, not a robotic system, so under the rules it supports no environment tier; it is cited only to show that the automated portion of this task is disembodied decision support.

tasks.label: Formulate plan of treatment for patient's teeth and mouth tissue.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Use dental air turbines, hand instruments, dental appliances, or surgical implements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operative/restorative visit in a general dental operatory: anesthetize, isolate, remove caries from a live tooth with a high-speed air-turbine handpiece and slow-speed bur, then place, contour, cure and adjust a composite or amalgam restoration with hand instruments; patient is awake, moving and salivating, and tooth hardness and caries extent are judged tactilely while drilling.

Examination and periodontal/preventive instrumentation: mirror and explorer over all surfaces, six-point periodontal probing, hand scalers/curettes and ultrasonic tips for supra- and subgingival calculus, then polishing; performed on a reclined awake patient with soft-tissue retraction and constant tactile discrimination of calculus versus root surface.

Fixed and removable prosthetic work: full-crown or onlay preparation with an air turbine to precise margins, temporization, scan/impression, and seating/cementation at a later visit with hand instruments; also delivery and chairside adjustment of dentures, night guards and retainers with acrylic burs against the patient's occlusion.

Extractions and minor oral surgery: local anesthesia, luxation with elevators, forceps delivery of erupted or broken-down teeth, surgical handpiece for bone removal or sectioning of impacted teeth, socket curettage and suturing; bleeding field, variable root anatomy, tactile force control to avoid root or bone fracture.

Endodontic treatment: access cavity cut with an air turbine, canal negotiation and shaping with hand and rotary files, irrigation, obturation and core placement; sub-millimetre work inside curved canals of a rubber-dammed but moving patient, guided by tactile feedback and radiographs.

Implant fixture placement in the operatory: after CBCT-based planning, run the sequential surgical drill protocol to prepare the osteotomy in the jawbone and insert the implant fixture to the planned position, depth and angulation with the surgical handpiece/torque driver.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic (ADIR) system (Yakebot-class autonomous implant robot)
sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co., Ltd.; clinical study by Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital / Medical University of Vienna group
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in partial edentulism: A pilot clinical study (Clinical Oral Investigations)
sources.claim: An autonomous dental implant robotic (ADIR) system carried out the drilling and implant placement for 20 implants in 13 partially edentulous patients in a clinical setting, with sub-millimetre entry/apex deviation and no adverse events.

sources.system: Yakebot / Remebot / Yomi robotic computer-aided implant surgery systems
sources.title: Accuracy and operation procedure of robotic computer-aided implant surgery (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: Active dental implant robots enter and exit the mouth, ... implants automatically; Yomi (FDA 2017) and the autonomous systems Remebot and Yakebot (NMPA 2021) are approved and increasingly used in clinical settings.

sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co., Ltd. (Beijing) with Peking University School of Stomatology researchers
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems (International Journal of Oral Science)
sources.claim: Review of dental implant robotics describes Yakebot's autonomous operation with binocular-vision tracking that compensates for patient head movement in real time during drilling, alongside the list of commercially approved dental implant robots.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotic system (OCT intraoral scanner plus robotic arm)
sources.title: Perceptive completes automated dental procedure with AI-driven robot (MassDevice)
sources.claim: Perceptive announced one company-reported fully automated robotic crown-preparation procedure on a single human patient in July 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = crown preparation with a dental handpiece, the closest robotic demonstration to restorative/prosthodontic air-turbine work; it is a single unreplicated company demonstration covering only the preparation step, so it does not establish worker-quality completion.

sources.title: DIA Backs Perceptive to Launch a New Era of Robotic Dentistry (Dentistry Today)
sources.claim: Perceptive's technology remained in human clinical trials with commercialization still a future step, as reported in January 2025 and repeated in 2026 trade coverage.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (robotic crown preparation); establishes maturity stage rather than deployed, worker-quality capability.

sources.system: Autonomous jawbone-milling dental surgical robot (Yakebot-derived platform)
sources.developer: Stomatological Hospital of Air Force Medical University, Xi'an
sources.title: Efficiency for robotic-assisted extraction of completely impacted supernumerary teeth in children: a randomized controlled trial (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: In a randomized trial of robot-assisted extraction of impacted supernumerary teeth in 10 children, the autonomous robot performed only the planned bone resection while the surgeon performed incision, flap elevation and the extraction, because the platform cannot autonomously execute all phases ....

sources.system: Autonomous dental robotic system for endodontic microsurgery
sources.developer: Chinese university stomatology group (Journal of Endodontics clinical report)
sources.title: Endodontic Microsurgery With an Autonomous Robotic System: A Clinical Report (Journal of Endodontics)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic system performed the osteotomy and root-end resection steps of endodontic microsurgery in a reported clinical case, with the remaining surgical steps left to the clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = surgical endodontics; it shows robots executing only rigid bone-cutting sub-steps, so it does not transfer to canal instrumentation or obturation in nonsurgical root canal treatment.

sources.system: Catalytic/magnetic microrobot swarms for oral biofilm removal
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (Penn Dental Medicine, Koo lab)
sources.title: Microrobots Navigate Diverse Oral Environments to Deliver Therapies (Penn Dental Medicine)
sources.claim: Penn's magnetically driven microrobot systems for removing dental biofilm remain preclinical, with animal studies still being prepared as of April 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = mechanical plaque/biofilm removal, the closest robotic analogue to hand-instrument scaling; it is preclinical and therefore cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Design, make, or fit prosthodontic appliances, such as space maintainers, bridges, or dentures, or write fabrication instructions or prescriptions for denturists or dental technicians.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed prosthodontics sent to a lab: in the operatory, the dentist anesthetizes, prepares the abutment tooth/teeth with a handpiece, retracts tissue, takes a digital scan or PVS impression plus bite record and shade, writes the lab prescription (margin design, material, pontic form), then fabricates and cements a provisional; at the seating visit removes the temp, tries in the crown/bridge, checks and adjusts contacts and occlusion with articulating paper and burs, cements, and removes excess cement. Wet field, tongue/cheek, moving patient.

Complete or removable partial denture case: preliminary and final impressions in the patient's mouth, border molding, jaw-relation records and wax rims, esthetic/wax try-in with patient feedback, written design instructions to the lab or denturist (tooth mold and shade, framework rests and clasps), then insertion, pressure-indicating paste, relief of intaglio sore spots and occlusal equilibration with acrylic burs over several adjustment visits.

Fitting, adjusting or repairing an existing appliance: chairside reline, denture repair or tooth addition at the office bench lab, clasp adjustment on a partial, recementing a loose bridge or crown, easing a sore spot, adjusting a night guard or space maintainer. Mixed intraoral work and small-scale bench work on the appliance.

Pediatric or interceptive appliance: sizing and seating an orthodontic band on a primary molar, taking an impression or scan, sending fabrication instructions, then fitting and cementing a band-and-loop or distal-shoe space maintainer in a small, often uncooperative child; checking clearance and occlusion.

In-house fabrication step of a case: from the approved digital design, the practice produces the appliance itself on office/lab CAD/CAM equipment - milling a zirconia or lithium-disilicate crown from a block, or printing a crown, night guard or denture base - then sintering/post-curing, sprue removal, staining/glazing or polishing, so a finished appliance is ready for try-in. Occurs in the office CAD/CAM area or in-house lab.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotics system (robotic arm + OCT handheld intraoral scanner)
sources.title: Perceptive completes automated dental procedure with AI-driven robot
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm performed a fully automated procedure on a human patient - autonomously preparing a tooth for a crown - but only the preparation step, and the prototype had no FDA clearance and was not for sale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation for a crown. It is one step of the fixed-prosthodontic instance (same patient, same operatory, same restoration), so it is directly relevant, but it does not cover impression/scan handling, try-in, occlusal adjustment, or cementation.

sources.title: Robot dentist can prep a tooth crown in 15 minutes | Popular Science
sources.claim: Press coverage confirms the Perceptive demonstration showed the machine autonomously preparing a patient's ... crown, done outside FDA clearance as a prototype demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: crown preparation is a sub-step of the fixed prosthodontic instance; the demonstration does not extend to fitting or cementing the finished restoration.

sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment
sources.claim: First-in-human study of Perceptive's semi-automated robotic preparation system: in six patients the robot executed a preplanned crown preparation while the dentist observed holding a deadman's switch; the five crowns were cemented during the same visit by the clinician, not the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation in a live patient. It shows the intraoral portion that is automatable today is limited to preplanned hard-tissue cutting under a splint/clamp; try-in, contact and occlusal adjustment, and cementation remained manual.

sources.system: Robotic computer-assisted implant surgery systems (review of Yomi and comparable systems)
sources.title: Contemporary Applications of Robotic Systems in Dental Implantology: A Review - PMC
sources.claim: A 2025 review of robotic systems in clinical dentistry states that no fully autonomous medical robots currently exist in ...; commercial dental robots (e.g., haptic-guided implant systems) are surgeon-controlled or task-autonomous only for drilling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted implant osteotomy, the most mature intraoral robotic application. If even this narrow, rigidly registered drilling task is not fully autonomous, the broader prosthodontic fitting workflow is not automated either.

sources.title: Fully automated milling machine - Ceramill Matik - Amann Girrbach
sources.claim: The Ceramill Matik is a commercially sold, fully automated dental milling machine with an integrated blank changer, self-cleaning and material/tool management that processes restoration orders autonomously, including unattended over weekends.

sources.system: BruxZir Factory robotic manufacturing line (custom in-house robotics)
sources.title: Robotics and Automation - Chairside Magazine Vol. 21 Issue 2
sources.claim: Glidewell's BruxZir Factory runs a deployed production line in which robotic arms select the correct zirconia block per the digital prescription and feed it to the milling center; AI software generates the restoration design, with technicians inspecting, coloring and finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine fabrication of the prosthesis a dentist prescribes. Same objects (zirconia crowns/bridges), same tolerances and same accepted output as the in-house fabrication instance, performed in a purpose-built production cell.

sources.title: Automate Dental Restoration Finishing | Zahn Dental
sources.claim: Commercially available AutoFinish machines automatically smooth, buff and polish milled zirconia crowns and printed dentures and night guards, automating the finishing step of appliance fabrication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated finishing of the same appliances (zirconia crowns, printed dentures) that this task's fabrication instance must deliver ready for try-in.

sources.system: SprintRay Midas digital press 3D printer (with NanoCure post-cure unit)
sources.title: Transforming same-day dentistry: SprintRay continues to innovate chairside solutions
sources.claim: SprintRay's Midas digital press printer is a commercial chairside unit that automatically recognizes material and shade and produces definitive crowns, inlays/onlays and veneers, with design, print and post-cure completed in under 30 minutes in the dental office.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-office machine fabrication of the restoration from the digital design - the physical 'make' content of the in-house fabrication instance, with the same objects and tolerances.

tasks.label: Advise or instruct patients regarding preventive dental care, the causes and treatment of dental problems, or oral health care services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Diagnose and treat diseases, injuries, or malformations of teeth, gums, or related oral structures and provide preventive or corrective services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic/comprehensive oral examination and diagnosis in a private-practice operatory: visual-tactile caries detection with explorer and mirror, periodontal probing and charting of six sites per tooth, soft-tissue/oral-cancer screening, occlusal and TMJ check, exposing and interpreting bitewing/PA radiographs, forming a diagnosis and treatment plan and explaining it to a patient who is awake, talking and moving.

Direct restoration of carious or fractured teeth: administer local anesthetic block/infiltration, isolate with rubber dam or cotton, excavate caries with high-speed and slow-speed handpieces judging tissue by tactile feel and color, assess pulpal exposure risk, place matrix/wedge, bond and layer composite (or amalgam), then contour, check and adjust occlusion with articulating paper. Lesion size, access and patient cooperation vary widely, including pediatric and anxious patients.

Indirect restorative / fixed prosthodontics: anesthesia, prepare a posterior full crown or onlay with defined margins and taper, retract tissue, take a digital scan or impression, fabricate/fit a provisional or same-visit milled crown, try in, verify margins and contacts, adjust occlusion and cement, on a live patient in a standard operatory.

Extractions and minor oral surgery in the operatory: anesthesia, simple forceps/elevator extraction of a mobile or decayed tooth, surgical extraction with flap and sectioning, or placement of a single dental implant (flap, osteotomy, implant insertion, healing abutment), plus hemostasis, sutures and post-operative instructions.

Endodontic therapy: anesthesia, rubber dam isolation, access cavity through crown or existing restoration, locating and negotiating curved canals with files, working-length determination, shaping, irrigation, obturation and core build-up, on molars with variable canal anatomy.

Preventive and periodontal services: scaling and root planing of subgingival calculus in periodontally involved sextants, prophylaxis and polishing, sealant placement on pediatric molars, fluoride application, and periodontal maintenance with re-evaluation of pocket depths, in the operatory.

sources.title: Perceptive | Meet Modern Dentistry
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic dentistry system performed a first-in-human automated restoration (crown preparation) outside the US; the company states this has not been verified in US patients under IRB or FDA IDE, i.e. a single demonstration rather than routine clinical use.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed dental journal commentary corroborates that in July 2024 an autonomous AI-controlled robot performed ... crown-preparation procedure on a human patient, faster than a dentist.

sources.title: Robot Performs First Ever Fully Autonomous Dental Surgery on Live Patient
sources.claim: The Perceptive milestone was a single test on one patient abroad with no peer-reviewed clinical data released and no FDA approval at the time, indicating demonstration-stage maturity rather than worker-quality reliability across patients.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic implant surgery system (ARI; Yakebot-class autonomous dental implant robot)
sources.title: In vitro and in vivo accuracy of autonomous robotic vs. fully guided static computer-assisted implant surgery - PubMed
sources.claim: Task-autonomous dental implant robots have been used clinically in patients, drilling the osteotomy and placing the implant more accurately than fully guided static templates; the clinician still performs anesthesia, flap elevation, and closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bone drilling and implant insertion in the jaw. It shows autonomous hard-tissue cutting in a live mouth, but covers only the osteotomy/placement sub-step of the surgical instance, not anesthesia, soft-tissue flap, hemostasis or suturing.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic system for endodontic microsurgery (Yakebot-class)
sources.developer: Chinese university hospital group (Journal of Endodontics clinical report)
sources.title: Endodontic Microsurgery With an Autonomous Robotic System: A Clinical Report - Journal of Endodontics
sources.claim: In endodontic microsurgery an autonomous robot performed only the osteotomy and root-end resection; the clinician then inspected the site and carried out root-end preparation and filling under ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic apical surgery, the closest robotic work to endodontic treatment. It substantiates only an autonomous bone/root cutting sub-step; canal negotiation, shaping, irrigation and obturation remain manual.

sources.title: Neocis' Yomi Robotic System Receives FDA 510(k) Clearance for Bone Reduction
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared dental surgical robot in commercial use provides interactive planning and physical (haptic) guidance of instrumentation held by the surgeon, i.e. the clinician drives the cutting; it is not autonomous.

sources.system: Collaborative tactile robot for interproximal tooth cleaning
sources.title: Interproximal tooth cleaning operated by a tactile robot. An in vitro analysis - PubMed
sources.claim: Robotic tooth cleaning has only been tested in vitro: a collaborative tactile robot programmed ... removed artificial interproximal plaque on models, with no live-patient prophylaxis or subgingival scaling demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical plaque removal from tooth surfaces, the core of a prophylaxis. Performance does not carry over: the trial used artificial plaque on models, not a live mouth with saliva, soft tissue and calculus.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: Automation of even the imaging step of a dental examination remains a research problem: a learned robotic intraoral scanning policy was evaluated as a closed-loop task in a bounded oral workspace, with the authors noting scanning is still labor-intensive with limited automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic intraoral data acquisition, a prerequisite of robotic examination. It shows only geometric scanning in a bounded workspace, not tactile caries/periodontal examination or diagnosis.

tasks.label: Remove diseased tissue, using surgical instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine caries excavation for a direct restoration: patient anesthetized and supine in an operatory chair, moderate occlusal or proximal decay in a molar/premolar, dentist uses high-speed diamond/carbide bur then slow-speed round bur and hand excavator, judging by tactile hardness, color and caries-detector dye where the infected dentin ends, leaving a cavity free of soft dentin ready for bonding, with tongue/cheek retraction, suction and patient micro-movement throughout.

Extensive or deep caries: decay under a failed amalgam/composite or beneath an existing crown margin, or a broken-down tooth needing a build-up/crown. Dentist removes the old restoration plus undermined enamel and infected dentin, performs selective removal near the pulp horn to avoid exposure, checks for pulp proximity/exposure and decides on liner, build-up or pulpotomy.

Pulpal debridement during root canal therapy: access cavity cut through enamel/dentin, inflamed or necrotic pulp extirpated with barbed broaches, canals located, negotiated with hand files and shaped with rotary NiTi under irrigation to remove infected pulp tissue and dentin to working length, rubber dam isolation, single or multi-canal molar anatomy.

Surgical removal of a diseased tooth and infected tissue: extraction of a non-restorable or periodontally hopeless tooth with elevators and forceps, sometimes with a bur osteotomy or sectioning, followed by curettage of granulation/infected tissue from the socket; occasionally periapical curettage or root-end resection in a flap procedure, with bleeding, suction and suturing.

Periodontal debridement: removal of subgingival calculus and diseased root-surface deposits with curettes/ultrasonic scalers in pockets, or excision of inflamed granulation tissue from a periodontal defect during open-flap debridement, in a bleeding, saliva-filled field with the tissue boundary judged by tactile and visual feedback.

Oral soft-tissue lesion removal: excisional biopsy of a mucocele, fibroma or suspicious mucosal lesion, operculectomy over a partially erupted molar, or gingivectomy of hyperplastic tissue, using scalpel, electrosurge or diode laser with margin judgment, hemostasis and suturing in the confined oral cavity.

sources.system: SARP (Perceptive Technologies semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system)
sources.developer: Perceptive Technologies with Harvard School of Dental Medicine
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment (preprint)
sources.claim: Perceptive's semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system (SARP) autonomously executed preplanned crown preparations on six live patients in a dental clinic; the dentist only observed, holding a deadman's-switch foot pedal, and mean deviation from the plan was 39 µm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crown preparation. It transfers partly — same objects (human tooth hard tissue in vivo), same operatory, far higher precision than caries excavation needs — but the removal volume is preplanned from a surface scan, so it does not substantiate removing tissue whose extent must be found intra-operatively.

sources.developer: Perceptive Technologies with Harvard School of Dental Medicine
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment (preprint)
sources.claim: In the same first-in-human robotic tooth-preparation trial, any caries removal or build-up needed to make the target tooth sound was performed by human dentists before the robot was used, and teeth with untreated caries in the clamped region were excluded.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point as negative evidence: the most advanced clinical dental cutting robot's own protocol assigns removal of diseased tissue to a human dentist before robotic operation.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive announced in July 2024 the first fully automated robotic dental procedure on a human — a crown preparation completed in about 15 minutes; the system remains a prototype without US marketing clearance for its OCT imaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crown preparation (cutting sound tooth structure to a planned shape), not excavation of diseased tissue; cited to establish the state of the art for autonomous intraoral cutting in a clinic.

sources.claim: An autonomous robotic (ATR) system performed the bone osteotomy and root-end resection of a maxillary second molar in a patient in a dental hospital, but the surgeon raised the flap and performed the periapical curettage, retrograde preparation and filling manually.

sources.developer: Chinese dental hospital group (autonomous oral surgery robot, DentalNavi)
sources.title: Endodontic microsurgery utilizing an autonomous robotic system for the maxillary second molar: a case report (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: In the same robot-assisted endodontic microsurgery case, removal of the periapical granulation tissue was done by the surgeon by hand after the robot's resection.

sources.developer: Chinese clinical research group (Journal of Endodontics case report)
sources.title: Endodontic Microsurgery With an Autonomous Robotic System: A Clinical Report (Journal of Endodontics)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic system performed a planned 3-mm osteotomy and root-end resection on a patient with symptomatic apical periodontitis; the clinician verified the result and completed the remaining surgical steps.

sources.system: Autonomous dental surgery robot (robot-assisted windowing extraction)
sources.developer: Chinese clinical group (BMC Oral Health clinical report)
sources.title: Robot-assisted extraction of impacted mandibular tooth: a clinical report (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic arm performed the bone-windowing osteotomy for extraction of an impacted mandibular tooth in a patient, compensating for patient micro-movement, while elevation of the bone fragment and the tooth itself was done by hand.

sources.title: Accuracy of the Yakebot dental implant robotic system versus fully guided static computer-assisted implant surgery template in edentulous jaw implantation (PubMed)
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots such as Yakebot place implants in patients in dental clinics with accuracy better than static surgical guides, showing that preplanned autonomous drilling is clinically usable in an ordinary operatory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: implant osteotomy drilling. It shows autonomous, image-planned bone/tooth drilling works in a clinic on patients, but the target volume is a preplanned geometric path, not tissue identified as diseased during the procedure.

sources.system: NIR image-guided CO2 laser ablation system (Fried lab)
sources.title: Selective Removal of Natural Occlusal Caries by Coupling Near-infrared Imaging with a CO2 Laser (PMC)
sources.claim: A computer-controlled near-infrared-image-guided CO2 laser selectively removed natural occlusal caries from extracted human molars on a bench, but removal was incomplete per pass and highly variable with lesion severity.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (caries excavation) but only on fixtured extracted teeth in a laboratory, with incomplete, variable removal — it does not reach the completeness or speed a dentist's cavity preparation requires.

sources.system: Catalytic antimicrobial robots / shapeshifting microrobot swarms
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (School of Dental Medicine and Penn Engineering)
sources.title: Scientists Have Created Microrobots That Can Automatically Brush and Floss Your Teeth (SciTechDaily)
sources.claim: Penn's magnetically actuated iron-oxide microrobot swarms removed dental plaque biofilm from mock and real human teeth in a hands-free proof-of-concept device; it has not been shown to remove subgingival calculus or inflamed tissue in patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plaque/biofilm removal. Biofilm is soft and surface-level, whereas periodontal debridement removes mineralized calculus and inflamed granulation tissue from pockets, so the demonstration does not carry over.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer) on a da Vinci platform
sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: The SRT-H system autonomously executed the 17-step dissection and division phase of a gallbladder removal on ex vivo porcine specimens in a laboratory, identifying ducts and arteries, clipping and cutting them without human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection and organ removal. It was done on ex vivo porcine tissue in a lab through laparoscopic ports, not on live oral mucosa in a confined mouth with margin judgment and hemostasis, so it does not substantiate oral lesion excision.

tasks.label: Apply fluoride or sealants to teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fluoride varnish applied chairside in a private-practice operatory to a cooperative school-age child or teen after a prophy: isolate and air-dry each quadrant with cotton rolls and suction, brush a thin varnish coat over all accessible surfaces of every tooth including interproximal areas, manage tongue/cheek and saliva, give post-op instructions.

Pit-and-fissure sealants placed on newly erupted permanent molars of a 6-12 year-old in an operatory: clean the occlusal surface, isolate (cotton rolls/Isolite or rubber dam), etch 15-20 s, rinse and thoroughly dry, flow resin into pits and fissures without voids or overflow, light-cure, probe for retention, check and adjust occlusion.

Topical fluoride (varnish, gel tray, or silver diamine fluoride) for a high-caries-risk adult in an operatory: root surfaces, exposed cervical areas, crowns/bridges, orthodontic brackets or xerostomia patients; requires careful drying, targeted placement, and avoidance of soft-tissue contact or restoration staining.

Fluoride varnish or sealant applied to a very young (age 1-3, knee-to-knee), anxious, gagging, or special-needs patient in the operatory, with behavior guidance, stabilization, and frequent stops for a moving or uncooperative mouth.

Sealant/fluoride application in a school-based sealant program, community outreach event, or mobile dental van: portable chair and curing light in a gym, classroom or trailer, variable lighting and layout site to site, high throughput, children often never treated before.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-guided robotic arm autonomously prepared a tooth for a crown on a live human patient (single first-in-human case in Colombia, 2024) using OCT imaging and a stabilizing mouthpiece; the demonstration is hard-tissue cutting, not application of fluoride varnish or resin sealant.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest related task: robotic tooth preparation inside a live patient's mouth in a dental operatory. Transfer to fluoride/sealant application is NOT established: the demo was handpiece cutting on one rigidly stabilized tooth, with no etching, rinsing/drying, moisture control, resin dispensing into fissures, light-curing, occlusion checking, or brushing varnish across all surfaces of a full dentition.

sources.title: A Robot Just Performed Fully Autonomous Surgery On A Live Patient For The First Time
sources.claim: Press coverage confirms the Perceptive procedure was a one-off treatment of a single patient abroad, with no peer-reviewed study published and FDA clearance still pending.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (robotic crown preparation); cited to show maturity limits, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality completion of preventive fluoride/sealant work.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic systems (e.g., Yakebot-class r-CAIS)
sources.developer: Yakebot Technology and academic clinical groups
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems (International Journal of Oral Science)
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots (level-2 autonomy) place implants in patients in dental clinics, drilling osteotomies after rigid splint/fiducial registration; their demonstrated capability is hard-tissue drilling along a planned axis, not intraoral material application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic work inside a live patient's mouth in a dental operatory. It shows the environment is reachable, but manipulation differs fundamentally from sealant/varnish work: a rigidly splinted drill trajectory in bone versus soft-brush coating, acid etching, rinse/dry moisture control, and viscous resin placement in fissures with curing.

sources.system: Shape-shifting microrobot swarm (surface topography-adaptive robotic superstructures)
sources.title: Swarm of tiny robots scrub teeth (NIH Research Matters)
sources.claim: The most advanced automated intraoral cleaning technology, Penn's magnetically driven microrobot swarm that brushes, flosses and removes plaque, has been tested only on experimental/extracted teeth and models and still requires clinical trials; it does not place sealants or professionally applied fluoride varnish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated application of an agent to tooth surfaces. It is in vitro only and delivers cleaning/antimicrobial action, not a cured resin sealant or professionally brushed fluoride varnish, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task in any environment.

tasks.label: Eliminate irritating margins of fillings and correct occlusions, using dental instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Finishing a just-placed direct restoration (composite or amalgam) chairside: removing flash and rough/overhanging margins with finishing burs, discs and strips, checking interproximal contacts with floss, marking the bite with articulating paper on an anesthetized patient and reducing high spots, then polishing. Posterior access, tongue/cheek retraction, saliva and blood, patient may move.

Delivery of an indirect restoration (single crown, onlay, small bridge): try-in, relieving tight proximal contacts and marginal excess/cement flash, verifying occlusion in maximum intercuspation and lateral/protrusive excursions with articulating paper plus the patient's own report of the bite, intraoral grinding and repolishing of porcelain/zirconia, iterating until accepted.

Recall or emergency visit for a complaint about an existing restoration: a rough or overhanging margin that shreds floss and traps food, or a filling/crown that 'feels high' and is causing soreness. Dentist locates the fault with explorer, floss, radiograph and articulating paper, then smooths the margin or reduces the contact and repolishes.

Occlusal adjustment/equilibration of the natural dentition: selective grinding of enamel to remove premature contacts, fremitus, or excursive interferences after restorative work or in bruxism/TMD management, guided by articulating paper of two colors, manipulation of the mandible into centric relation, and patient feedback over one or more visits.

Adjusting a removable appliance chairside: relieving denture borders/sore spots marked with pressure-indicating paste and equilibrating the occlusion of a new denture or an occlusal splint, removing the appliance from the mouth to grind acrylic with burs, then reinserting and rechecking with the patient closing.

sources.system: SARP (semi-automated robotic tooth preparation), Perceptive Technologies
sources.developer: Perceptive Technologies with Harvard School of Dental Medicine
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment
sources.claim: Perceptive's SARP robot autonomously executed a pre-planned crown preparation on six live patients (Harvard clinical study, 39 µm RMS), with the robot rigidly clamped to the patient's own teeth; however, seating the crown and adjusting its margins and occlusion was done by the dentist, not the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Crown preparation is the closest related task: intraoral cutting of tooth structure with a dental handpiece at sub-50 µm accuracy in the same operatory setting. Transfer to this task fails, however, because in the same trial the crown's fit was 'assessed and adjusted as needed' by the dentist, and one crown was rejected for poor margin/occlusal contact — the marking-grinding-recheck loop against a patient's bite was never performed by the robot.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive announced the first fully automated robotic dental procedure on a human in July 2024, a crown preparation; the system targets restorative dentistry but no automated margin finishing or occlusal correction was reported.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (crown preparation) as the SARP study; cited to date and characterize the maturity of the only autonomous restorative dental robot, which as of 2026 remains in clinical trials rather than routine chairside use.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics
sources.claim: An independent review in the British Dental Journal confirms that the single first-in-history autonomous in-mouth robotic procedure was crown preparation; robotics in clinical dentistry otherwise remains guidance/navigation for implant surgery.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a state-of-the-art survey: it establishes that no fielded robotic system performs intraoral restoration finishing or occlusal adjustment, only crown preparation (demo) and implant guidance.

sources.title: Accuracy of the Yakebot dental implant robotic system versus fully guided static computer-assisted implant surgery template in edentulous jaw implantation: A preliminary clinical study
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots (Yakebot) drill osteotomies in patients' mouths in clinical practice with better accuracy than static guides, showing autonomous intraoral drilling to a CBCT-planned path is clinically feasible.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cutting inside a patient's mouth in a dental clinic. It does not transfer to this task because the target is a rigid pre-planned drill path in bone, whereas eliminating an irritating margin or a high occlusal contact requires detecting the fault (explorer, floss, articulating paper, patient report) and iterating removal against functional contact — no such closed loop is demonstrated.

sources.title: Automate Dental Restoration Finishing | Zahn Dental
sources.claim: Commercial automated finishing machines smooth, buff and polish lab-fabricated restorations, but they operate on appliances in a dental laboratory, not on fillings in a patient's mouth, and do not identify or correct occlusal contacts clinically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated surface finishing/polishing of dental restorations. It does not substantiate this task because the workpiece is a bench-held appliance before delivery; the instance's work is an in-situ restoration on a living patient whose margin fault and occlusal contacts must first be found intraorally.

tasks.label: Perform oral or periodontal surgery on the jaw or mouth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine extraction of an erupted, non-restorable or mobile tooth in a general dental operatory: local anesthetic injection, luxation with elevators, forceps delivery, socket curettage/compression, hemostasis with gauze, occasional single suture, post-op instructions. Patient awake, moving, gagging; bleeding and saliva obscure the field.

Surgical (open) extraction in the operatory: impacted or partially erupted third molar, fractured root, or retained root tip. Mucoperiosteal flap elevation, bone removal with a handpiece, tooth sectioning, elevation of fragments, socket debridement, irrigation, suturing; proximity to inferior alveolar nerve and sinus.

Implant-related surgery in the operatory: crestal incision or tissue punch, flap reflection, sequential osteotomy drilling per CBCT plan, implant insertion to torque, cover screw/healing abutment, socket preservation or small bone graft with membrane, suturing.

Periodontal surgery in the operatory: open-flap debridement/osseous recontouring, gingivectomy, crown-lengthening, or free/connective-tissue gingival graft with palatal donor site; scaling of root surfaces, flap repositioning, fine suturing, periodontal dressing.

Minor intraoral soft-tissue surgery: frenectomy, incisional/excisional biopsy of a mucosal lesion, operculectomy, incision and drainage of a localized abscess; scalpel or laser, hemostasis, sutures, specimen handling.

Other alveolar/apical surgery: apicoectomy with root-end filling, alveoloplasty, tori or exostosis removal, exposure of an impacted tooth for orthodontic bonding; flap, bone work under magnification, closure.

sources.system: Beijing Ruiyibo autonomous dental robotic system
sources.title: Robot-assisted extraction of impacted mandibular tooth: a clinical report (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: An autonomous dental robotic system (Beijing Ruiyibo) performed the bone osteotomy/windowing autonomously during extraction of an impacted mandibular tooth in a patient, but the surgeon performed anesthesia, the sulcus incision, full-thickness flap reflection, tooth removal, grafting and suturing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: surgical extraction of an impacted tooth in the jaw; shows the robot covers only the bone-cutting sub-step.

sources.system: Autonomous dental milling robotic system (r-CAIS platform, Yakebot-class)
sources.developer: Chinese hospital study using a commercial autonomous dental robot
sources.title: Efficiency for robotic-assisted extraction of completely impacted supernumerary teeth in children: a randomized controlled trial (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: In a randomized controlled trial of robot-assisted extraction of impacted supernumerary teeth in children, the robot performed only precision bone milling while a second surgeon performed incision, flap elevation and tooth ..., because the platform cannot autonomously execute all surgical phases.

sources.system: Yakebot (and Remebot, Cobot, Theta, Dcarer, Yomi)
sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co., Ltd. (Beijing) and others
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems (Int J Oral Sci)
sources.claim: Commercially approved dental implant robots (Yakebot and peers in China; Yomi in the US) autonomously execute implant bed preparation and implant placement at the planned site, i.e. the drilling/placement sub-steps of implant surgery.

sources.developer: Chinese dental implant robot manufacturer (clinical study, J Prosthet Dent)
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery (The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry)
sources.claim: In a clinical accuracy study, an autonomous dental implant robotic ... executed the preprogrammed drilling/placement steps autonomously while the surgeon monitored the system and changed the drill needles throughout the surgery.

sources.title: FDA Clears Neocis Inc.'s Robotic System for Dental Implant Procedures (Medical Product Outsourcing)
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared robotic system for dental surgery in the US, Neocis Yomi, is a haptic guidance system: the clinician holds and drives the handpiece while the robot constrains motion; it does not act autonomously.

sources.title: US-Based AI Company Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human (Oral Health Group)
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robot completed what it described as the ..., but the procedure was a restorative crown preparation, not oral or periodontal surgery, and was a single unreviewed demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hard-tissue tooth preparation in the mouth of a live patient): shows the current frontier of autonomous intraoral robotics is restorative drilling, with no soft-tissue incision, flap, extraction, or suturing.

tasks.label: Fill pulp chamber and canal with endodontic materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-rooted anterior or premolar with a straight, patent canal in a general dental operatory: after shaping and irrigation, dentist dries with paper points, fits and radiographically verifies a master gutta-percha cone, coats with sealer, seats to working length, sears off, condenses at the orifice, and seals the chamber with a temporary or bonded core; anesthetized patient under rubber dam.

Multi-rooted molar (3-4 canals, curved, varying working lengths) in general practice: master cones fitted per canal, sealer applied, warm vertical compaction/continuous-wave downpack plus thermoplastic backfill, chamber cleaned of gutta-percha and sealer, floor sealed; verified radiographically for length, density, and voids on a patient who may move, gag, or bleed.

Pediatric pulpotomy or pulpectomy on a primary molar in a general/family practice: after pulp tissue removal and hemostasis, the pulp chamber (or resorbable canals) is filled with MTA/bioceramic putty or zinc-oxide-eugenol/iodoform paste, compacted, and restored with a stainless steel crown, on a small, often uncooperative moving child under local anesthesia or nitrous oxide.

Difficult case handled in general practice: retreatment after removal of old gutta-percha, severely curved or calcified canal, internal resorption defect, or open apex requiring an MTA/bioceramic apical plug placed with a carrier and condensed with pluggers, then backfilled; requires tactile judgment and repeated radiographic checks.

Interim/emergency fill in an operatory: after emergency pulpotomy or between-visit endodontics, placing calcium hydroxide or other intracanal medicament into canals and filling the pulp chamber with a temporary sealing material (Cavit/IRM) to a good coronal seal, often on a patient in acute pain with limited opening.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic system for endodontic microsurgery (Yakebot-class dental robot)
sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co. / Chinese university dental hospital clinical team
sources.title: Endodontic Microsurgery With an Autonomous Robotic System: A Clinical Report (Journal of Endodontics)
sources.claim: Autonomous robot (Yakebot-type) performed the osteotomy and root-end resection in endodontic microsurgery on a patient, but the clinician still performed root-end preparation and filling by hand under a microscope — i.e., the filling/obturation step is not robot-performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted apicoectomy in a live patient's mouth. It shows autonomous in-mouth robotic drilling is real, but the material-placement/filling step was explicitly reserved for the human, so it does not transfer to obturation.

sources.system: PUMCH endodontic robot prototype (photoacoustic-steaming / hydramatic obturation)
sources.developer: Peking Union Medical College Hospital (Jizhi Zhao) with Beihang University (Chong Pan)
sources.title: The robot that may one day do your root canal surgery (Nature partner content)
sources.claim: An endodontic robot prototype for 'PUMCH therapy' was given a capability for automated root canal filling by vacuum/hydraulic delivery of bioceramic material, but the robot is a research prototype not approved for use and no clinical filling quality data are reported.
sources.transferJustification: This is the target task (canal obturation), but the source describes an unapproved bench prototype with no evidence of autonomous completion at clinical quality in a patient, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.developer: National Taiwan University / Taiwanese research team (Cheng, Ho, Chen)
sources.title: DentiBot: System Design and 6-DoF Hybrid Position/Force Control for Robot-Assisted Endodontic Treatment (arXiv 2310.09691)
sources.claim: DentiBot is an autonomous robot-assisted endodontic system that performs access drilling and root canal cleaning/shaping with hybrid position/force control on phantom/in-vitro models; its scope is file-based shaping, not filling the canal with obturation materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous canal cleaning and shaping with rotary files. It involves the same tooth and canal geometry, but obturation requires inserting compliant gutta-percha cones, viscous sealer and thermoplastic compaction with void control — manipulation modes the system does not perform, so capability does not transfer.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Perceptive's robot performed an entire crown-preparation procedure autonomously on a human patient in a dental operatory in July 2024, demonstrating autonomous in-mouth robotic drilling under patient movement, but only for subtractive tooth preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crown preparation (drilling external tooth structure) in a dental chair. It shares the environment and patient-motion compensation, but obturation is additive placement of soft/viscous materials into sub-millimetre curved canals with tactile length control, which the system has never performed.

sources.system: Literature-wide survey of endodontic robots (Yomi, Yakebot, DentiBot, navigation robots)
sources.title: Contemporary Applications and Future Perspectives of Robots in Endodontics: A Scoping Review (Int J Med Robot Comput Assist Surg)
sources.claim: A 2024 PRISMA-ScR scoping review of robots in endodontics found the published robotic applications concern root canal cleaning, shaping and surgical procedures; obturation is not among the demonstrated robotic applications.
sources.transferJustification: Survey evidence covering the whole family of endodontic robots; it delimits demonstrated capability (cleaning, shaping, surgery) and shows no system performs the filling/obturation step, supporting negative judgments.

tasks.label: Plan, organize, or maintain dental health programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Bleach, clean, or polish teeth to restore natural color.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult prophylaxis polish in a dental operatory: after scaling, the dentist polishes all accessible surfaces of ~28 teeth with a slow-speed handpiece, rubber cup/brush and prophy paste, working around lips, cheek and tongue, with mirror retraction, air/water and high-volume suction, then rinses and checks that plaque and light stain are gone without abrading enamel or lacerating gingiva.

Heavy extrinsic stain removal (coffee, tea, tobacco, chlorhexidine) on an adult: repeated passes with coarse paste and/or an air-polisher (sodium bicarbonate/glycine powder jet), angling the tip to avoid gingiva and restoration margins, re-checking shade against a guide, and deciding when further abrasion would harm enamel or existing composites.

In-office (chairside) bleaching: place cheek retractors and suction, apply and light-cure a resin gingival barrier precisely along the gumline of the anterior teeth, apply 25-40% hydrogen peroxide gel to each tooth, run 2-4 light/timed cycles with suction and gel replacement, remove barrier and gel, rinse, take shade photos and check for soft-tissue burns or sensitivity.

Take-home whitening delivery: polish teeth to remove surface deposits, scan/impress the arches, try in and adjust custom bleaching trays chairside (trim, check fit and gel reservoirs), demonstrate gel loading in the patient's mouth and verify seating.

Prophylaxis polish for a child, anxious adult, or special-needs patient in the operatory: patient moves, closes, gags, or must be repositioned; the operator adjusts force and timing continuously, works in short bursts, and manages behaviour while removing plaque and stain from small or crowded teeth.

Cleaning/polishing outside the fixed operatory using portable equipment: mobile school or community dental van, nursing-home bedside or wheelchair, or military/public-health clinic; limited lighting and suction, patient not in a standard dental chair.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotics system (OCT scanner + robotic handpiece)
sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven dental robot autonomously performed a complete crown preparation on a live human patient in a clinical setting - the frontier of in-mouth autonomous robotics - but the demonstrated capability is planned hard-tissue cutting for restorative work, not prophylaxis polishing, stain removal or bleaching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = crown preparation on a live patient in a dental operatory. Transfer is only partial: same objects (teeth) and environment, and it shows motion-compensated autonomous work in a live mouth, but the system removes tooth structure along a pre-planned digital path at a single site. It has no demonstrated capability for force-controlled full-arch polishing with abrasive paste, air-polishing stain judgment, or placement of a gingival barrier and bleaching gel, and it is a single-patient IRB demonstration without FDA clearance.

sources.system: Dentronics tactile collaborative robot (7-axis cobot holding manual/electric toothbrush)
sources.developer: Dentronics research group (dental robotics academic study, Int J Comput Dent)
sources.title: Dentronics: tooth cleaning with a tactile collaborative robot - an in vitro proof of concept
sources.claim: A seven-axis tactile collaborative robot programmed by ... removed surrogate plaque from typodont teeth in articulated phantom jaws in vitro, comparable to a human operator; the work was on a fixtured laboratory model, not a live patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = mechanical plaque removal (toothbrushing) on typodont teeth. It is the closest robotic analogue to prophy polishing, but it is in vitro on a rigid phantom with surrogate plaque, the trajectory was programmed by a human for that specific model (autonomy not established), and it does not address real extrinsic stain, prophy paste/rubber-cup work, saliva, soft tissue or a moving patient.

sources.system: Tactile collaborative robot with interproximal brush
