sources.title: Interproximal tooth cleaning operated by a tactile robot. An in vitro analysis
sources.claim: A tactile robot with integrated AI, programmed by a dental student, cleaned interproximal surfaces of model teeth set in phantom jaws as effectively as the student - an in vitro pilot only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = interproximal cleaning of teeth. Same object class (teeth) and a cleaning endpoint, but performed on artificial plaque on model teeth in phantom jaws with a human-programmed path; nothing establishes worker-quality stain removal or safe operation in a living mouth.

sources.system: Shape-shifting microrobotic swarm (catalytic magnetic iron-oxide nanoparticles)
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (Penn Dental Medicine / Penn Engineering, Koo, Steager, Lee)
sources.title: Shapeshifting microrobots can brush and floss teeth | Penn Today
sources.claim: Magnetically actuated iron-oxide microrobot swarms formed bristle- and floss-like structures that removed biofilm from tooth surfaces in proof-of-concept experiments on tooth-like slabs, 3D-printed models and extracted human teeth; no in-patient professional cleaning has been demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = plaque/biofilm removal from tooth surfaces. It targets the same objects, but it is a laboratory proof of concept under externally operated magnetic fields on models and extracted teeth, addresses biofilm rather than tenacious extrinsic stain, and has not been shown to deliver a chairside prophylaxis or bleaching outcome in patients.

sources.title: Yakebot Dental Implant Robotic System, Beijing Yakebot Technology Co., Ltd. | DFA Awards Online Showcase
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots (Yakebot) have been used clinically on large numbers of patients in dental hospitals, drilling osteotomies and placing implants in live mouths under a rigid registration splint - showing autonomous in-mouth work is deployed, but only for single-site planned drilling, not tooth cleaning, polishing or bleaching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic implant osteotomy in a dental operatory. Same environment and patient population, and it proves autonomous instrument motion inside a live mouth, but the task is a rigidly registered straight-line drill at one site; it demonstrates nothing about compliant full-arch surface polishing, abrasive stain judgment, or gingival-barrier and bleaching-gel handling on soft tissue.

tasks.label: Treat exposure of pulp by pulp capping, removal of pulp from pulp chamber, or root canal, using dental instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult patient in a general dental operatory: during caries excavation on a permanent posterior tooth the dentist finds a near or frank pinpoint pulp exposure, achieves hemostasis, places a direct pulp cap (calcium silicate/MTA or calcium hydroxide liner), seals with base and definitive composite restoration, and checks occlusion — all with rubber dam, suction, and a patient who may move or gag.

Adult patient, single-rooted anterior or premolar tooth with irreversible pulpitis or necrosis: local anesthesia, rubber dam, access cavity through enamel/dentin, extirpation of pulp tissue with barbed broach/files, electronic and radiographic working length, rotary shaping, NaOCl/EDTA irrigation, drying, gutta-percha/sealer obturation, temporary or core restoration.

Adult patient, molar root canal treatment in general practice: 3-4 canals including a hidden MB2 or partly calcified canal, curved roots, limited mouth opening, bleeding pulp chamber; full access, negotiation, shaping, irrigation, obturation and coronal seal, sometimes across two visits with intracanal medicament.

Emergency visit for acute irreversible pulpitis ("hot tooth"): anxious patient in pain, difficult profound anesthesia requiring supplemental intraligamentary/intraosseous injection, rapid access and pulpotomy/pulpectomy of the pulp chamber and canals for pain relief, medicament and temporary seal, patient rescheduled for completion.

Pediatric patient (age 4-9) in a general/family practice: primary molar with carious pulp exposure; behavior management of a moving, apprehensive child, rubber dam or cotton-roll isolation, coronal pulpotomy with removal of chamber pulp, hemostasis, MTA/ferric sulfate medicament, and stainless steel crown restoration.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotics system (OCT scanner + robotic arm)
sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic system autonomously performed a crown preparation (tooth drilling) on a live human patient in a clinical setting — the closest demonstrated robotic analogue to cutting tooth structure in the mouth — but it is limited to restorative crown prep, is not FDA-cleared, and does not perform pulp therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crown preparation. It shares the workpiece (a patient's tooth in the mouth), sub-millimetre precision and a dental operatory setting, so it bears on whether a robot can cut tooth structure; it does not cover pulp capping, pulp extirpation, canal shaping, irrigation or obturation, which are the substance of this task.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted apical surgery on an endodontically involved tooth in a dental clinic. It shows autonomous robotic drilling to a planned depth near a tooth root, but the published case series table lists every clinical endodontic robot application as assisting a single drilling step (osteotomy, apicoectomy, post removal, calcified-canal location), with pulp removal, canal cleaning/shaping and obturation still done manually.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted access/post removal during root canal retreatment — the same tooth, instruments and clinic as this task; it substantiates only the drilling sub-step, with the pulp-space cleaning and filling performed conventionally by the dentist.

tasks.label: Administer general and local anesthetics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Awake adult in the OMS office operatory: surgeon selects agent and dose, loads a carpule syringe, applies topical, palpates landmarks, inserts the needle intraorally (buccal infiltration or inferior alveolar/long buccal/lingual block), aspirates to rule out intravascular placement, deposits slowly while watching the patient, then tests for adequate soft-tissue/pulpal anesthesia before extraction, biopsy, or implant placement.

Office-based IV moderate/deep sedation or general anesthesia for third-molar removal or implants: preoperative airway and ASA assessment, monitor placement, peripheral IV cannulation, titration of midazolam/fentanyl/propofol/ketamine to target depth, continuous airway support (chin lift, nasal airway, suction, oxygen) alongside local anesthetic, management of events such as laryngospasm or apnea, then emergence and discharge readiness.

Hospital operating room case (orthognathic surgery, facial trauma, pathology): general anesthesia with nasoendotracheal intubation and ventilation managed through the case, plus the surgeon's regional blocks and local infiltration with vasoconstrictor for hemostasis and postoperative analgesia in the draped surgical field.

Pediatric, developmentally disabled, or severely phobic patient in the office: uncooperative or moving patient, difficult venous access, weight-based dosing, behavioral/protective stabilization, heightened airway vigilance during sedation or office general anesthesia.

Nitrous oxide/oxygen inhalational sedation or oral premedication: fitting and adjusting the nasal hood, titrating N2O concentration to patient response, monitoring, and 100% oxygen recovery, usually followed by local anesthetic injection.

Supplemental/rescue anesthesia mid-procedure: patient reports breakthrough pain, surgeon re-assesses and chooses an alternate technique (intraligamentary, intraosseous, Gow-Gates) and delivers additional anesthetic in a bloody, saliva-filled, partially operated field with limited access.

sources.title: FDA Grants Premarket Approval for SEDASYS (R) | American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA)
sources.claim: Sedasys, the only FDA-approved computer-assisted personalized sedation system, automatically delivered propofol for minimal-to-moderate sedation in healthy adults undergoing colonoscopy/EGD; it did not place the IV, manage the airway, or provide deep sedation/general anesthesia, and was withdrawn from the market in 2016.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated sedative administration. It is the closest deployed automated anesthetic-delivery system, but covers only drug titration through an already-placed IV at minimal-to-moderate depth, not the OMS anesthesia episode (injection, IV access, airway, deep sedation/GA).

sources.developer: PGIMER Chandigarh (Puri et al.) and others
sources.title: Advances in automated anesthesia: a comprehensive review
sources.claim: Review of automated anesthesia reports that closed-loop delivery systems such as CLADS automatically titrate propofol from BIS feedback in clinical trials; these are infusion controllers used under a supervising anesthesiologist who performs vascular access, airway management and rescue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated maintenance of anesthetic depth. It substantiates only the infusion sub-step; no cited system performs an induction-to-emergence anesthetic including airway care.

sources.title: Remote Control Robotic Intubation System Developed | Respiratory Therapy
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System performed tracheal intubation in 12 patients, but the robot is driven by a human operator with a joystick from a remote ... rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = airway instrumentation for general anesthesia; cited to show this sub-step exists only as teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: First Robotic Ultrasound-Guided Nerve Blocks in Humans Using the Magellan System | Semantic Scholar
sources.claim: The Magellan system performed the first robotic ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve blocks in 13 patients, with needle placement and injection commanded by an anesthesiologist through a joystick.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot-delivered regional anesthetic injection, the closest analogue to a nerve block; because it is teleoperated it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.developer: Clinical dental robotics groups (China), published in J Prosthet Dent
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robotic systems drill osteotomies and place implants inside awake patients' mouths in dental clinics under optical navigation, but the local anesthetic is administered by the human surgeon before the robot begins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous sub-millimetre intraoral instrument insertion in the same operatory setting; cited to show that even where intraoral autonomy exists in clinical use, the anesthetic injection remains a clinician step.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomously performs the complete venous blood-draw sequence (tourniquet, skin prep, ultrasound-guided vein selection, needle insertion) and is CE-marked and being deployed in European hospitals; it draws blood and does not administer anesthetic drugs or manage sedation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous percutaneous needle placement in an arm vein inside a clinical facility, the closest analogue to IV cannulation; it covers only that sub-step and provides no drug titration, airway management, or intraoral injection.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System | Business Wire
sources.claim: Perceptive's robot performed an automated crown preparation on a human patient, showing emerging autonomous intraoral hard-tissue work, but it was a single unpublished case and did not include administering anesthesia.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous work inside a patient's mouth in a dental operatory; cited to bound the state of the art, which stops short of delivering local anesthetic.

sources.title: Robotic Anesthesia: A Vision for 2050 - Anesthesia Experts
sources.claim: Analysis of Sedasys notes it could only automatically decrease propofol dosing, with any increase requiring the physician, and that it targeted lighter sedation than practitioners wanted — automated sedation never covered the deep-sedation/GA range typical of oral surgery offices.

tasks.label: Remove impacted, damaged, and non-restorable teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Removal of one to four impacted third molars in a healthy young adult, in the surgeon's office operatory under IV sedation/general anesthesia: local anesthesia, mucoperiosteal flap, bur osteotomy near the inferior alveolar nerve/lingual plate, tooth sectioning, elevation and forceps delivery, socket debridement, hemostasis and suturing.

Extraction of damaged or non-restorable teeth (deep caries, fractured crowns/roots, periodontally hopeless teeth) in the office under local anesthesia: forceps or surgical (flap/root sectioning) delivery, granulation tissue curettage, often ridge preservation grafting and closure.

Multiple or full-arch extractions with alveoloplasty in an older adult preparing for a denture or full-arch implant prosthesis, office suite under sedation: sequential extractions, bone recontouring, tuberosity/undercut reduction, hemostasis in an often anticoagulated patient, and closure.

Extractions performed in a hospital operating room under general anesthesia for medically compromised, special-needs or very young patients (e.g., full-mouth dental clearance, nasotracheal intubation, throat pack), with intraoperative coordination with anesthesia staff.

Complex/high-risk removals: deeply impacted or ankylosed canines, roots displaced toward the maxillary sinus, teeth in a cyst or fracture line, or extraction in an irradiated/antiresorptive-treated jaw, requiring intraoperative judgment, plan revision and management of complications such as sinus communication or bleeding.

sources.system: Autonomous dental surgical robot (CBCT-planned robotic arm, Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital case)
sources.developer: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine (with commercial robotic arm/handpiece)
sources.title: Robot-assisted extraction of impacted mandibular tooth: a clinical report (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: In the most advanced published clinical use of robotics for impacted tooth removal, an autonomous robotic arm performed only the planned bone osteotomy/windowing; the surgeon made the incision and flap, elevated the bone fragment, extracted the tooth, grafted and sutured.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (impacted tooth removal); cited to show the robot completes only the osteotomy sub-step while the surgeon performs flap, tooth delivery and closure.

sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co. / academic dental hospital investigators
sources.title: Efficiency for robotic-assisted extraction of completely impacted supernumerary teeth in children: a randomized controlled trial (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: Randomized controlled trial of an autonomous robotic system for extraction of completely impacted supernumerary teeth in children: the robot executed the pre-planned osteotomy (and tooth sectioning), while the surgeon luxated and delivered the tooth, irrigated and sutured.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (impacted tooth extraction); cited to show that even in the best controlled clinical trial the human surgeon performs luxation, delivery and closure.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System (Business Wire)
sources.claim: The only reported fully automated intraoral robotic procedure on a live human is a crown preparation (tooth reduction) by Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm — a restorative procedure, not an extraction, and a single reported case rather than a deployed service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated crown preparation). Transfer fails: crown prep shapes a retained tooth with no flap, no luxation or delivery, and no bleeding socket or suturing, so it does not substantiate completing an extraction.

sources.system: Dental robotics state-of-the-art review (covering Perceptive, Yomi, autonomous implant robots)
sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics (British Dental Journal)
sources.claim: A 2025 review of dental robotics confirms that the first and only autonomous full procedure on a human patient was crown preparation; no autonomous system performs surgical tooth removal.
sources.transferJustification: Field-level survey of related tasks (implantology, restorative robotics) establishing the ceiling of autonomous intraoral robotics; no extraction capability reported.

sources.title: Neocis Submits New 510(k) For Yomi Dental Robotic System (Surgical Robotics Technology)
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared dental surgical robot in routine US oral-surgery offices, Yomi, is a haptic guidance device: the surgeon physically drives the handpiece while the robot constrains its position, so it is not autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (implant osteotomy and guided bone reduction in the same operatory). Transfer fails: the surgeon manipulates the instrument throughout, so it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment for extraction.

tasks.label: Treat infections of the oral cavity, salivary glands, jaws, and neck.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/clinic incision and drainage of a localized odontogenic abscess (vestibular, buccal, palatal or submucosal space) in an awake patient in the dental chair: local anesthetic infiltration/block, scalpel incision through swollen friable mucosa, blunt hemostat dissection to loculations, evacuation and culture of pus, irrigation, Penrose drain placement and suture-fixation.

Source-control extraction of the infected offending tooth in the office (grossly carious/periapically abscessed tooth, or pericoronitis around a partially erupted third molar) under local anesthesia or IV sedation: flap if needed, elevation and forceps delivery of a frequently brittle tooth, socket curettage, irrigation, hemostasis and suturing.

Operating-room management of a severe multi-space or deep neck infection (Ludwig's angina, submandibular/masticator/parapharyngeal space) in an acutely ill patient: airway secured by awake fiberoptic intubation or tracheostomy, extraoral submandibular and intraoral incisions, blunt digital/instrument exploration of fascial planes, copious irrigation, multiple through-and-through drains, plus removal of the causative teeth.

Surgical treatment of infected/necrotic jaw bone — chronic mandibular osteomyelitis, medication-related osteonecrosis, or osteoradionecrosis: mucoperiosteal flap, sequestrectomy, saucerization and bur/rongeur debridement to bleeding bone, smoothing of margins, tension-free closure, sometimes with fixation or reconstruction.

Treatment of salivary gland infection — acute suppurative sialadenitis or obstructive sialolithiasis of the submandibular/parotid gland: ductal papilla dilation, sialendoscopy with irrigation and basket/forceps stone retrieval, transoral duct slitting and marsupialization, or transcervical drainage of a gland abscess.

Follow-up and inpatient infection care: bedside or clinic wound checks of a draining oral/neck infection, advancing or removing Penrose drains, irrigating and repacking wounds, re-culturing, and adjusting culture-directed antibiotics on a swollen, tender, sometimes trismic patient.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic osteotomy system for impacted tooth extraction (clinical report, Chinese stomatology center)
sources.developer: academic clinical group (BMC Oral Health case report)
sources.title: Robot-assisted extraction of impacted mandibular tooth: a clinical report | BMC Oral Health
sources.claim: An autonomous dental robotic arm performed the bone osteotomy ('windowing') step of an impacted mandibular tooth extraction in a live patient, but the human surgeon performed the anesthesia, gingival incision, flap reflection, elevation of the tooth and closure — i.e., the robot completes a hard-tissue sub-step, not the whole surgical procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: surgical removal of a tooth from the jaw, the same anatomy and instruments used for source-control extraction of an infected tooth. It shows the current autonomy boundary — planned rigid-bone drilling only, with all soft-tissue incision, elevation, curettage and suturing done by the surgeon.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS / Yakebot)

sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots (Yakebot-class ADIRS) execute preprogrammed drilling and implant placement autonomously in the human mouth under surgeon supervision, while the surgeon still administers local anesthesia and performs the soft-tissue steps.

It establishes that commercially deployed autonomous intraoral robots are confined to planned rigid-bone drilling along a CBCT trajectory, with no capability for soft-tissue incision, blunt fascial dissection, pus evacuation or drain placement.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robot — Dentaltown
sources.claim: An AI-driven robot autonomously performed a complete restorative dental procedure (tooth preparation for a crown) on a human patient — the furthest demonstrated intraoral autonomy — but the procedure is hard-tissue cutting on a healthy, immobilized tooth, not infection surgery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral hard-tissue cutting in a dental chair. Cited to mark the ceiling of demonstrated intraoral autonomy; it does not transfer to abscess incision and drainage, fascial-space dissection or debridement of infected soft tissue, which involve deformable, bleeding, distorted anatomy rather than a rigid planned tooth surface.

sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgical system reported autonomously executed steps of a cholecystectomy, but only on ex vivo porcine gallbladders in a laboratory, not on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection and clipping. It is the closest analogue to abscess drainage and fascial-space dissection, and it establishes that such autonomy exists only on ex vivo animal tissue in a research lab, with no clinical human deployment.

tasks.label: Perform surgery to prepare the mouth for dental implants and to aid in the regeneration of deficient bone and gum tissues.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office surgical operatory, local anesthesia ± IV sedation: extraction of one or more failing/nonrestorable teeth with alveoloplasty and socket (ridge) preservation grafting — socket debridement, packing particulate allograft, placing a collagen membrane/plug, and suturing the site closed.

Office surgical operatory: osteotomy preparation and placement of one to three implants (or second-stage uncovery with healing-abutment placement) in a healed site with adequate bone — anesthesia, crestal incision and full-thickness flap or tissue punch, sequential drilling, implant insertion to torque, cover screw/healing abutment, suturing.

Office or hospital: ridge augmentation / guided bone regeneration for a deficient ridge — flap with periosteal releasing incisions, decortication, particulate or block graft (sometimes with autogenous bone harvested from ramus/chin), membrane fixed with tacks or screws, tension-free primary closure.

Office surgical operatory: maxillary sinus floor augmentation (lateral window or crestal osteotome approach) — window osteotomy, atraumatic Schneiderian membrane elevation without perforation, graft placement, membrane coverage and closure, in a posterior maxilla with variable septa and thin bone.

Office surgical operatory: soft-tissue surgery to correct deficient gum tissue around planned or placed implants — free gingival or subepithelial connective tissue graft harvested from the palate, vestibuloplasty or apically positioned flap, graft trimmed and sutured with 5-0/6-0 suture in a bleeding, mobile field.

Hospital OR or advanced office case under general anesthesia/deep sedation: full-arch reconstruction (e.g., All-on-4, zygomatic implants) with full-arch extractions, alveoloplasty/bone reduction, multi-implant placement, grafting, and multilayer closure in a patient with atrophic or pathologic jaw anatomy.

sources.system: ADIRS (autonomous dental implant robotic system, Yakebot class)
sources.developer: Chinese dental implant robot manufacturer; clinical study by university dental hospital
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery — The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry
sources.claim: An autonomous dental implant robot system autonomously performed osteotomy drilling and implant insertion in 74 partially edentulous patients in a dental clinic, while the surgeon administered anesthesia and raised (or omitted) the soft-tissue flap.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (implant osteotomy/insertion): it is the only autonomous intraoral surgical step demonstrated, and it is a sub-step of these instances — it does not cover extraction, flap work, grafting, membranes or closure.

sources.claim: Clinical trade review from October 2025 confirms the same limits persist: robots do flapless implant placement but struggle with suturing, soft-tissue management and auxiliary regenerative surgeries such as GBR and ....

sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems (PMC)
sources.claim: Yomi, the FDA-cleared commercial dental surgery robot used in US offices, is a haptic-guidance platform in which the surgeon holds and drives the handpiece while the robot constrains the trajectory — co-manipulated, not autonomous.

sources.title: Contemporary Applications of Robotic Systems in Dental Implantology: A Review (PMC)

sources.transferJustification: Related task (implant osteotomy) — establishes the ceiling of demonstrated intraoral autonomy: hard-tissue drilling only, with the human handling access, soft tissue and closure.

sources.claim: Perceptive reported the first fully automated dental procedure ... — robotic preparation of a tooth for a crown in a dental chair — demonstrating autonomous intraoral hard-tissue cutting but not implant site surgery, bone grafting or soft-tissue work.
