automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/clinic excisional biopsy of a small benign oral soft-tissue growth (fibroma, mucocele, papilloma, epulis, pyogenic granuloma) under local anesthesia in a dental surgical operatory: infiltrate anesthetic, retract cheek/tongue in a wet, mobile, blood- and saliva-filled field, excise the lesion with scalpel/laser including a cuff of normal tissue, achieve hemostasis, place sutures, and submit the specimen for pathology.

Enucleation/curettage of an odontogenic cyst or benign jaw tumor (dentigerous cyst, odontogenic keratocyst, odontoma, small ameloblastoma) in an office or ambulatory surgery center under IV sedation or general anesthesia: mucoperiosteal flap elevation, cortical bone window with a bur, removal of the lesion and its capsule intact while sparing the inferior alveolar nerve and adjacent tooth roots, peripheral ostectomy or Carnoy's application, hemostasis, flap closure.

Excision of a facial skin or lip lesion (basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, nevus, keratoacanthoma) in clinic or ASC: mark margins, elliptical or wide local excision to appropriate depth on curved facial contours near eyelid/nose/lip, orient specimen for pathology, undermine and close with a layered closure or small local flap for a cosmetically acceptable result.

Hospital operating-room resection of a malignant oral/maxillofacial tumor under general anesthesia: composite resection, marginal or segmental mandibulectomy or maxillectomy with frozen-section margin control, often with neck dissection and free-flap or plate reconstruction, in a bleeding field with airway management over several hours.

Hospital OR or ASC removal of a larger benign head-and-neck mass — submandibular gland excision, superficial parotidectomy for pleomorphic adenoma, excision of a vascular or neurogenic lesion — with facial or lingual nerve dissection and preservation, drain placement, and layered closure.

sources.title: Precision excision of mandibular anterior compound odontoma using autonomous robotic guidance: a clinical case report
sources.claim: An in-house autonomous robotic guidance system built on the Yakebot dental platform was used clinically to enucleate a compound odontoma in an 8-year-old, but the robot autonomously executed only the planned bone-milling osteotomy; the surgeon performed the incision, flap, lesion extraction, hemostasis and suturing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-guided alveolar osteotomy for jaw-lesion enucleation. It is the closest published clinical robotic contribution to oral tumor removal, but it covers only the bone-window sub-step under surgeon foot-pedal initiation; incision, capsule dissection, hemostasis and closure remained manual, so it does not substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help – Johns Hopkins Malone Center for Engineering in Healthcare
sources.claim: The SRT-H hierarchical surgical robot transformer autonomously performed one lengthy phase of a cholecystectomy on ex vivo porcine gallbladders in a laboratory setting; it is a research demonstration, not a clinical procedure on patients, and it did not perform a complete operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection and clipping during gallbladder removal. It is the state of the art in surgical autonomy, but it is ex vivo animal tissue, a single procedure phase, and not an oral/maxillofacial excision with margin control and closure, so it does not transfer to completing tumor removal at worker quality.

sources.developer: Advanced Osteotomy Tools (AOT AG) / University Hospital Basel
sources.title: CARLO | Department of Clinical Research | University of Basel
sources.claim: The CARLO cold-ablation robot-guided laser osteotome autonomously cuts bone along a planned path and has been used in first-in-man transoral midface osteotomies in maxillofacial surgery in Basel, Vienna and ...; the robot performs the bone cut only, within an otherwise surgeon-performed operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic bone cutting inside the maxillofacial operative field. It shows a robot can execute a planned osteotomy in a hospital OR, but it does no soft-tissue lesion excision, margin judgment, hemostasis or closure, so it cannot complete tumor removal.

sources.system: da Vinci SP surgical system (transoral otolaryngology)
sources.title: U.S. FDA Clears da Vinci SP for Certain Transoral Otolaryngology Procedures
sources.claim: Transoral robotic surgery for benign and malignant oral/pharyngeal tumors is performed with the da Vinci system, which is fully surgeon-controlled from a console rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (removal of oral/oropharyngeal tumors) performed with the only widely deployed robot in this domain; it is continuous teleoperation, which by the rating rules cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: STAR (Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot) with multi-DOF electrosurgical tool
sources.title: Semi-Autonomous Electrosurgery for Tumor Resection Using a Multi-Degree of Freedom Electrosurgical Tool and Visual Servoing
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot ... only semi-autonomously resected pseudo-tumors in porcine tissue as a laboratory proof of concept, with margin accuracy still variable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous electrosurgical excision of a tumor with a planned margin. It is bench work on excised animal tissue with a single cutting step and no closure or pathology handling, so it does not substantiate completing a clinical excision.

tasks.label: Provide emergency treatment of facial injuries including facial lacerations, intra-oral lacerations, and fractured facial bones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Emergency department consult for an isolated facial soft-tissue laceration (cheek, lip/vermilion, eyelid, chin) in an adult: local anesthetic infiltration, irrigation and debridement of contaminated wound, hemostasis, layered closure with deep and skin sutures, dressing — often at the bedside with a moving, anxious or intoxicated patient.

Intra-oral laceration repair (tongue, floor of mouth, buccal mucosa, gingiva, palate), frequently in a child or agitated patient under sedation or general anesthesia: control of brisk bleeding and saliva, exploration for foreign bodies/tooth fragments, resorbable suture closure in a confined, mobile oral cavity.

Closed reduction and stabilization of fractures in ED or OR: nasal fracture reduction and splinting, dentoalveolar fracture repositioning and composite/wire splinting, application of arch bars or IMF screws with maxillomandibular fixation for a minimally displaced mandible fracture — occlusion judged by feel and inspection.

Open reduction and internal fixation of a displaced mandibular, zygomaticomaxillary or orbital floor fracture in the operating room under general anesthesia: intraoral/transcutaneous incisions, dissection with nerve preservation, anatomic reduction, plate contouring, screw fixation or orbital implant placement, layered closure.

Initial emergency management of panfacial/complex trauma in the trauma bay with a trauma team: airway assessment and securing (including surgical airway if indicated), control of severe midface/nasal hemorrhage by packing or vessel ligation, temporary stabilization and imaging-based surgical planning under time pressure.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help – Johns Hopkins Malone Center for Engineering in Healthcare
sources.claim: Johns Hopkins' SRT-H performed an autonomous laparoscopic gallbladder removal on ex vivo/cadaveric pig tissue in a laboratory setup — the most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgery demonstrated, still confined to animal tissue and a single rehearsed procedure, not human emergency trauma care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous soft-tissue dissection and clipping) cited to test transfer to facial wound repair; it does not transfer — the work was on excised animal tissue in a rigidly staged lab setup, without anesthesia, hemostasis of an open facial wound, or cosmetic layered closure on a live moving patient.

sources.title: Autonomous Robot Improves Surgical Precision Using AI | NVIDIA Technical Blog
sources.claim: STAR performed autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis suturing on pig soft tissue, but required specially marked tissue and a highly controlled setup; no human-patient autonomous suturing is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous suturing of bowel) examined for transfer to laceration repair; it does not transfer — fluorescent tissue markers, a fixed insufflated field and a single suture line differ from irrigating, debriding and cosmetically closing an irregular facial wound.

sources.title: LL-MAROCO: A Large Language Model-Assisted Robotic System for Oral and Craniomaxillofacial Osteotomy
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic craniomaxillofacial osteotomy systems execute planned bone cuts only on skull models/phantoms, with per-run completion rates of 87–92%, and authors note clinical application remains at an early stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (planned facial bone osteotomy) is the closest robotic analogue to fracture reduction and fixation; it does not transfer — work is on inanimate skull models with no soft-tissue exposure, no fracture reduction, no plate/screw fixation, and success rates far below surgical acceptance.

sources.system: oral and maxillofacial surgical robot-assisted navigation system
sources.developer: academic group, published in BMC Oral Health
sources.title: Model experiments on application of oral and maxillofacial surgical robot-assisted mandibular tumor resection and reconstruction | BMC Oral Health
sources.claim: Robot-assisted craniomaxillofacial systems in the surgical literature are navigation/assistance devices operated with the surgeon, evaluated in model experiments for tumor resection and reconstruction rather than autonomous trauma repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-assisted mandibular surgery) checked for transfer; autonomy is not established and the work is model-based assistance to a surgeon, so it cannot substantiate autonomous emergency facial trauma treatment.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive reported the first fully automated dental procedure ... — a robotic crown preparation in a dental clinic — showing autonomous intraoral hard-tissue work exists as a first-in-human demonstration only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous intraoral tooth preparation on a cooperative seated patient) tested for transfer to intra-oral laceration repair; it does not transfer — it cuts rigid tooth structure on a planned, immobilized field and involves no bleeding soft tissue, exploration, or suturing.

tasks.label: Treat problems affecting the oral mucosa, such as mouth ulcers and infections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/clinic consult for a symptomatic mucosal lesion (recurrent aphthous ulcer, candidiasis/denture stomatitis, lichen planus, herpetic or traumatic ulcer): history-taking, intraoral exam with mirror, retraction and palpation of buccal mucosa/tongue/palate, differential diagnosis, and prescription or chairside application of topical/systemic therapy plus patient instruction.

Chairside incision and drainage of a localized intraoral (vestibular/palatal) odontogenic abscess under local anesthesia: infiltrate anesthetic into inflamed tissue, scalpel incision through mucosa, blunt dissection of the space, irrigation, placement and suturing of a drain, antibiotic prescription and follow-up.

Chairside biopsy of a suspicious or non-healing mucosal lesion (leukoplakia, erythroplakia, chronic ulcer): local anesthesia, incisional or excisional biopsy of soft, mobile, bleeding mucosa, hemostasis, suturing, specimen handling, then interpretation of the pathology report and treatment planning.

Hospital operating room / emergency management of a severe spreading soft-tissue infection of odontogenic origin (Ludwig's angina, submandibular or buccal space abscess) under general anesthesia: airway assessment, intraoral and extraoral incision and drainage, blunt dissection of fascial spaces, drain placement, culture, IV antibiotics, inpatient follow-up.

Follow-up and adjunctive mucosal care in office or at the bedside: debridement of necrotic/ulcerated mucosa (e.g., MRONJ-associated ulcer, severe mucositis), laser or chemical cautery of a small persistent lesion, wound irrigation, suture removal, dressing changes, and adjustment of medication based on healing response.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive reported an AI-driven robotic arm performing a fully automated restorative dental procedure (crown preparation) on a human patient in a clinic, i.e. autonomous hard-tissue work inside the mouth; single unpublished case, not a mucosal diagnosis or soft-tissue treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest intraoral autonomous robot: same workspace (human oral cavity, patient in a dental chair). Cited to show scope limits — it prepares rigid tooth structure to a pre-planned CAD path, and does not examine, diagnose or cut deformable, bleeding mucosa.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS, e.g. Yakebot)
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery - The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robot systems execute pre-planned osteotomy and implant placement in patients under surgeon supervision; the soft-tissue steps (anesthesia, flap, suturing) are still done by the surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoral autonomous surgery in a dental clinic. Transfer fails because the robot follows a rigid pre-planned trajectory registered to teeth/bone; mucosal ulcer and infection care requires diagnostic judgment and manipulation of mobile soft tissue, which this system does not perform.

sources.title: Cold Ablation Robot-Guided Laser Osteotome (CARLO): From Bench to Bedside
sources.claim: The CARLO robot-guided Er:YAG laser performed a linear Le Fort I bone osteotomy autonomously in patients, but the mucosal incision exposing the bone was made conventionally by the surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cutting in the maxillofacial region in a hospital OR. It cuts bone along a planned line; the soft-tissue/mucosal portion of the same operation remains a manual surgeon task, so it does not substantiate robotic treatment of mucosal disease.

sources.title: Hopkins robot is first to perform laparoscopic surgery without assistance from humans
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed autonomous soft-tissue suturing/anastomosis in live pigs in a research laboratory setting; no human clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation and suturing of soft tissue. Transfer fails: it works on marked bowel in an open abdominal field in animals, not on lesion-bearing oral mucosa in the constrained human mouth, and it makes no diagnosis or therapeutic decision.

sources.developer: academic research consortium (published in a peer-reviewed journal, PMC10762007)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot contacted oropharyngeal soft tissue in human volunteers and patients for COVID-19 sampling, showing autonomous force-controlled instrument contact in the mouth for specimen collection only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument contact with oral/pharyngeal mucosa in humans. It only wipes a swab at a target site; it does not inspect lesions, incise, drain, biopsy or medicate mucosa, so it cannot complete mucosal-disease treatment.

sources.system: robot-assisted transoral surgical platforms (incl. da Vinci-based systems)
sources.title: Recent Advances in Robotic Systems for Robot-Assisted Transoral Surgical Procedures: A Systematic Review
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of robot-assisted transoral surgery finds that meaningful surgical autonomy has not yet been achieved in transoral robotic platforms, which remain surgeon-teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers robotic surgery on oral/oropharyngeal soft tissue; establishes that clinically used transoral robots are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive autonomous judgment for treating oral mucosal disease.

tasks.label: Restore form and function by moving skin, bone, nerves, and other tissues from other parts of the body to reconstruct the jaws and face.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Composite jaw reconstruction with a vascularized free tissue transfer (fibula, scapula, or anterolateral thigh flap) after segmental mandibulectomy/maxillectomy for tumor or gunshot trauma: hospital OR under general anesthesia, 8-12 hours, donor-site flap harvest with pedicle dissection, virtual-plan osteotomies and patient-specific plate fixation, microvascular arterial and venous anastomoses under the microscope, and intraoral/skin insetting.

Non-vascularized autologous bone grafting of jaw defects: iliac crest, tibial, ramus or symphysis block/particulate harvest for alveolar cleft repair, post-traumatic or post-cystectomy jaw defects, sinus augmentation and pre-implant ridge augmentation; hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center, general anesthesia or IV sedation, graft shaped and screw-fixated, membrane and tension-free mucosal closure.

Local/regional soft-tissue transfer for oral and facial defects: buccal fat pad flap, facial artery musculomucosal or nasolabial flap, palatal or preauricular full-thickness skin/mucosal graft after tumor excision, oroantral fistula closure or trauma; ASC or office-based OR, sedation/general anesthesia, 1-3 hours, layered suturing in a small, bloody, mobile field.

Autologous fat or dermal-fat grafting for facial contour restoration (post-traumatic contour deficits, hemifacial atrophy, post-ablative defects, TMJ interpositional grafts): liposuction harvest from abdomen/thigh, processing, and multi-plane micro-injection or graft insetting through small incisions; ASC or office OR under sedation.

Microneurosurgical repair of injured inferior alveolar or lingual nerve with autologous sural/great auricular nerve graft or nerve transfer: hospital OR under general anesthesia, transoral or transcervical exposure, neuroma excision, donor nerve harvest, and 8-0/9-0 epineurial coaptation under the operating microscope.

sources.developer: Medical Microinstruments (MMI), used at University Hospital RWTH Aachen
sources.title: First Series of Free Flap Reconstruction Using a Dedicated Robotic System in a Multidisciplinary Microsurgical Center
sources.claim: The Symani microsurgical robot has been used in a 23-flap free-flap series including oral and maxillofacial cases, but only for the vessel anastomosis step; all other steps (flap harvest, osteotomy, fixation, insetting) were done by surgeons, and five robotic arterial anastomoses had to be redone.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (free flap reconstruction including maxillofacial), but the robot is a surgeon-driven master-slave manipulator performing one sub-step, so it cannot support autonomous completion of any instance.

sources.title: New FDA-approved robot opens doors for microsurgery in L.A. (ASPS)
sources.claim: The Symani system, FDA de novo authorized in April 2024 for microsurgery, is fully surgeon-controlled: the surgeon drives the instruments from hand controllers and a 3D screen; there is no autonomous mode.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the only commercially available reconstructive-microsurgery robot in the US is continuously teleoperated, which by the rules cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer) on dVRK-Si
sources.title: Johns Hopkins' AI-powered, voice-controlled robot performs autonomous surgery
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgical AI, SRT-H on a da Vinci research platform, performed a 17-step gallbladder removal on ex vivo porcine specimens in a laboratory, not on patients and not involving autologous tissue transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous multi-step soft-tissue dissection. Cited to bound the state of the art: it is an ex vivo animal-organ laboratory demonstration of an ablative procedure, so it does not transfer to harvesting and insetting autologous flaps/bone in a live human face.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Interview with Axel Krieger and Justin Opfermann: autonomous robotic laparoscopic surgery for intestinal anastomosis (Robohub)
sources.claim: The STAR robot autonomously sutured small-bowel anastomoses laparoscopically in live pigs — the furthest autonomous soft-tissue suturing has reached — but only a single repetitive suturing sub-step in an animal model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous vascular/hollow-organ anastomotic suturing, the microsurgical sub-step of flap reconstruction. It is animal-model only, on 20-30 mm bowel rather than sub-millimetre facial vessels, and covers no other step of the reconstruction.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic computer-assisted implant surgery (r-CAIS; Yakebot-class systems)
sources.title: Accuracy of autonomous robotic surgery for dental implant placement in fully edentulous patients: A retrospective case series study
sources.claim: Clinically autonomous robotic surgery in the oral and maxillofacial field is limited to drilling osteotomies and placing dental implants in patients; no autonomous system harvests, shapes, or transfers autologous bone, skin, or nerve.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous rigid-bone drilling in the jaw under optical tracking. It shows autonomy is confined to registered, rigid hard-tissue trajectories; it provides no capability for soft-tissue flap raising, graft harvest, or suturing required by this task.

sources.developer: Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital and others; AOT AG (CARLO)
sources.title: LL-MAROCO: A Large Language Model-Assisted Robotic System for Oral and Craniomaxillofacial Osteotomy
sources.claim: Robotic systems reported for craniomaxillofacial bone work (CMF ROBOT, CARLO laser osteotomy, LL-MAROCO planning robot) address osteotomy cutting or planning only, and are demonstrated on skull models, animal models, or as surgeon-supervised cutting aids.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic jaw osteotomy, one sub-step of jaw reconstruction. Autonomy claimed is for planning, with model/animal-level execution, so it cannot substantiate completion of a whole tissue-transfer reconstruction.

tasks.label: Perform surgery on the mouth and jaws to treat conditions such as cleft lip, cleft palate, and jaw growth problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Orthognathic surgery for a skeletal jaw-growth discrepancy in an adolescent/adult: hospital OR under general anesthesia, nasal intubation, Le Fort I maxillary osteotomy and/or bilateral sagittal split mandibular osteotomy (± genioplasty) — intraoral mucosal incisions, subperiosteal dissection, osteotomies near nerves and tooth roots, down-fracture and mobilization, splint-guided repositioning, titanium plate/screw fixation, hemostasis, layered closure.

Primary cleft lip (± nasal) repair in an infant a few months old: hospital OR, general anesthesia, precise anthropometric markings, rotation-advancement flap design, muscle (orbicularis oris) dissection and reapproximation, cartilage repositioning, fine multi-layer suturing with aesthetic result in bleeding, deformable soft tissue.

Primary cleft palate repair in a 9–18-month-old: hospital OR, mouth gag exposure of a small deep oral cavity, two-flap or Furlow double-opposing Z-plasty, elevation of mucoperiosteal flaps, levator veli palatini muscle dissection and retropositioning, tension-free layered closure, control of bleeding from greater palatine vessels.

Secondary cleft alveolar bone grafting in mixed dentition: hospital OR or ASC; fistula closure and flap design at the alveolar cleft, harvest of cancellous bone from anterior iliac crest (second surgical site) or mandible/tibia, packing of graft into the cleft, watertight closure over graft.

Distraction/expansion and revision procedures for jaw growth problems and residual cleft deformity: mandibular distractor placement for micrognathia (e.g., Pierre Robin/hemifacial microsomia), surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion, condylectomy for condylar hyperplasia, or secondary lip/nose revision — hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center, device fitting and osteotomy plus soft-tissue closure.

sources.system: CARLO (Cold Ablation Robot-guided Laser Osteotome), Advanced Osteotomy Tools
sources.developer: Advanced Osteotomy Tools (AOT AG), with KUKA arm
sources.title: Performance and safety evaluation of a cold ablation robot-guided laser osteotome (CARLO) in 28 midface osteotomies
sources.claim: The CARLO robot-guided Er:YAG laser osteotome performed the linear portion of midface (Le Fort I) osteotomies in 28 human patients in the operating room, i.e. a single bone-cutting step; the surgeon performs incision, exposure, remaining cuts, down-fracture, repositioning, fixation and closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the bone-cutting step of Le Fort I orthognathic surgery, the same procedure and anatomy as this task. It substantiates autonomous execution of one planned linear cut only, not the whole operation (soft-tissue exposure, mobilization, splint-guided repositioning, plate fixation, closure remain manual), so it cannot support whole-instance completion.

sources.system: CARLO robot-assisted laser Le Fort I osteotomy (LLFO)
sources.developer: Advanced Osteotomy Tools / Ulm Military Hospital team (Ebeling et al.)
sources.title: First-Hand Experience and Result with New Robot-Assisted Laser LeFort-I Osteotomy in Orthognathic Surgery: A Case Report
sources.claim: First developer-independent clinical use of robot-assisted laser Le Fort I osteotomy: the planned linear osteotomy was transferred to the robot and executed by it under the surgeon's direct visual control, with the rest of the orthognathic procedure done conventionally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the maxillary osteotomy step of jaw-deformity (orthognathic) surgery. Shows autonomy is limited to a pre-planned straight bone cut in an already surgically exposed field; the surgical approach, mobilization, repositioning and fixation are surgeon-performed.

sources.system: Yakebot autonomous dental implant robotic system
sources.developer: Yakebot (Beijing) / Peking University School of Stomatology collaborators
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems
sources.claim: The Yakebot autonomous dental implant robot prepares the implant bed and places implants intraorally in human patients under surgeon supervision (foot-pedal enable), after the surgeon has performed any flap and with no soft-tissue reconstruction by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoral robotic drilling of jaw bone (dental implant osteotomy) — same anatomical region and sub-millimetre precision class. It transfers only to rigid, pre-planned drilling of exposed bone; it does not cover flap design, osteotomy of mobile segments, grafting or multilayer soft-tissue closure required here.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer–Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - PubMed
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous soft-tissue surgery is at the level of a single procedural phase on ex vivo animal tissue: SRT-H autonomously completed the dissection/clipping phase of cholecystectomy on eight ex vivo pig gallbladders, not a whole operation on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection and clip application, the closest published analogue to the flap dissection and suturing needed in cleft lip/palate repair. Performance does not carry over: it is ex vivo porcine tissue, phase-level rather than whole-procedure, and involves no aesthetic flap design, muscle reconstruction or layered closure.

sources.system: da Vinci Si/Xi (transoral robotic cleft palate repair feasibility)
sources.developer: Intuitive Surgical (system); MD Anderson/Selber et al. (study)
sources.title: Infant Robotic Cleft Palate Surgery: A Feasibility Assessment Using a Realistic Cleft Palate Simulator
sources.claim: Robotic cleft palate repair has only been shown as teleoperated feasibility work with the da Vinci system on a cleft palate simulator, with the surgeon controlling every instrument motion.

tasks.label: Evaluate and treat problems related to the temperomandibular joint (TMJ).
Treat snoring problems, using laser surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office-based laser-assisted uvulopalatoplasty (LAUP): awake patient in a surgical operatory chair, topical plus infiltrative local anesthesia of the soft palate, CO2 laser handpiece with backstop used through the mouth to make vertical trenches beside the uvula and reshape/partially amputate it; surgeon manages gag reflex, tongue retraction, smoke evacuation, bleeding and endpoint judgment, then gives post-op instructions. Often staged over 2-4 sessions weeks apart.

Non-ablative Er:YAG 'NightLase'-type palatal tightening in a dental/OMS office: no anesthesia, laser handpiece scanned over soft palate, uvula, tonsillar pillars and sometimes oral floor in timed passes, energy and coverage titrated to patient tolerance and tissue response; typically 3-4 sessions about 3 weeks apart with snoring/bed-partner outcome follow-up.

Laser-assisted palatoplasty/UPPP in a hospital OR or ASC under general anesthesia with nasotracheal intubation, mouth gag and airway-fire precautions; laser excision and reshaping of soft palate, uvula and posterior pillars, suture closure and hemostasis, frequently combined with tonsillectomy or other multilevel airway work in a snoring/OSA patient.

Adjunctive laser work at other airway levels during snoring treatment, in office or OR: diode/CO2 laser inferior turbinate reduction or lingual tonsil/tongue-base reduction under local or general anesthesia with endoscopic visualization, addressing the nasal or retrolingual contribution to snoring.

Revision or touch-up laser session for persistent or recurrent snoring, or in a medically complex patient (anticoagulated, high BMI, brisk gag reflex, prior palatal scarring): altered anatomy from earlier surgery, conservative energy settings to avoid velopharyngeal insufficiency, extra hemostasis and sedation planning.

sources.system: da Vinci Surgical System (TORS for OSA)
sources.title: Robotic Obstructive Sleep Apnea Surgery - PubMed
sources.claim: The only robotic system in routine clinical use for airway/snoring soft-tissue surgery, the da Vinci used for transoral tongue-base reduction in OSA, is a teleoperated master-slave system driven move-by-move by a surgeon at a console.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transoral robotic soft-tissue airway surgery for snoring/OSA. It is the closest clinical robotic analogue to laser snoring surgery, but it is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment of autonomous completion.

sources.title: Features and Safety | OSF HealthCare
sources.claim: Clinical da Vinci systems have no autonomous mode: the system cannot be programmed and requires direct surgeon input for every surgical maneuver.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the deployed surgical robot used for airway soft-tissue surgery has no autonomy, so its hospital-OR (E2) deployment does not substantiate autonomous completion of this task.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous soft-tissue surgery remains laboratory animal work: STAR autonomously sutured intestine in live pigs under supervision, not in human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgery. It marks the frontier of autonomy on deformable tissue but was performed on animal bowel in a research lab, not on a human oropharynx, so it does not substantiate palatal laser surgery.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - Johns Hopkins University
sources.claim: The most advanced 2025 autonomous surgical policy completed multi-step cholecystectomy only on ex vivo animal tissue in a laboratory, showing no autonomous system performs whole human soft-tissue operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-step soft-tissue dissection. Demonstrated only on excised animal organs on a lab bench, with no transoral access, anesthesia, airway safety or endpoint judgment, so it cannot substantiate this task even in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Performance and safety evaluation of a cold ablation robot-guided laser osteotome (CARLO) in 28 midface osteotomies - PMC
sources.claim: A robotic Er:YAG laser has cut human bone autonomously in the OMS operating room, but only the planned linear part of a Le Fort I osteotomy, after surgical exposure and under the surgeon's direct visual control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-guided laser cutting in oral and maxillofacial surgery. Transfer fails: it ablates rigid, navigation-registered bone along a preplanned line, whereas snoring laser surgery requires transoral access to mobile, deformable palatal soft tissue with intraoperative dosing and endpoint judgment.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: The only reported fully automated procedure inside a human mouth was a hard-tissue restorative preparation by a purpose-built dental robot; no automated intraoral soft-tissue laser procedure is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intraoral procedure on a seated human patient. It works on a rigid, splint-registered tooth in the anterior mouth and does not address oropharyngeal access, deformable palatal tissue, laser dosimetry, bleeding or airway safety, so it does not transfer.

tasks.label: Perform minor cosmetic procedures, such as chin and cheekbone enhancements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Alloplastic chin implant augmentation in an office-based OR or ambulatory surgery center under IV sedation/GA: intraoral or submental incision, subperiosteal pocket dissection while protecting the mental nerves, sizing/seating a silicone or porous-polyethylene implant on the symphysis, screw fixation, hemostasis, layered closure, dressing.

Cosmetic osseous (sliding) genioplasty in a hospital OR or ASC: intraoral degloving incision, mental nerve identification, reciprocating-saw horizontal osteotomy of the symphysis, advancement/reduction and midline setting against the planned position, plate-and-screw fixation, contour rasping, closure with mentalis resuspension.

Malar/submalar (cheekbone) implant augmentation, usually bilateral, via intraoral vestibular approach: pocket dissection over the zygoma while protecting the infraorbital nerve, symmetric implant positioning, screw fixation, symmetry check, closure.

Nonsurgical chin/cheek/jawline contouring in an office treatment room on an awake, unfixed patient: HA filler deep supraperiosteal boluses and cannula threads plus neuromodulator shaping, with aspiration, vascular-danger-zone avoidance, molding, and real-time aesthetic judgment and patient feedback.

Adjunct minor cosmetic soft-tissue contouring around the chin/cheek in office/ASC: submental liposuction or autologous fat harvesting and micro-grafting to the chin/malar region, occasional scar revision, with intraoperative symmetry assessment and closure.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help – Johns Hopkins Malone Center
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgery demonstrated is SRT-H (Johns Hopkins), which performed a phase of gallbladder removal without human help — but on an ex vivo/lifelike phantom in a research lab, not a whole procedure on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (laparoscopic cholecystectomy) is the closest published autonomous soft-tissue surgery; it bounds what autonomy exists for dissection/clipping, and it is a lab demo on non-human tissue, so it does not transfer to completing a facial implant augmentation on a patient.

sources.title: In a First, a Humanoid Robot Performed Live Surgery Under a Surgeon's Control
sources.claim: The 2026 state of the art for humanoid robots in a real operating room is teleoperation, not autonomy: a surgeon-controlled humanoid removed a pig's gallbladder with human surgeons standing by.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (live animal cholecystectomy in a standard OR) shows that even the newest general-purpose surgical humanoids require continuous teleoperation, which the task rules exclude as completion.

sources.developer: Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital / Shanghai Jiao Tong University
sources.title: The Feasibility of Robot-Assisted Chin Osteotomy on Skull Models: Comparison with Surgical Guides Technique
sources.claim: A craniofacial surgical robot performed chin osteotomies automatically, but only on ex vivo 3D-printed skull models — bone cutting alone, with no soft-tissue incision, dissection, fixation or closure, and not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related sub-step of osseous genioplasty; autonomy is shown only for the saw cut on a rigid ex vivo model, so it cannot substantiate whole-procedure completion on a live patient.

sources.developer: Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Ninth People's Hospital
sources.title: Preliminary clinical experience of robot-assisted surgery in treatment with genioplasty
sources.claim: Clinical robot use in genioplasty is assistive positioning and force-limited drilling with the surgeon operating, reported in only six patients.
sources.transferJustification: Same anatomical procedure (genioplasty); the robot supplies guidance and drill-stop control while the surgeon performs the operation, so it is assistance rather than autonomous completion.

sources.system: Yomi (and comparable robotic dental implant systems)
sources.title: From AI in the office to robot-assisted dental implant surgery – Oral Health Group
sources.claim: Commercial oral/maxillofacial implant robots such as Yomi are haptic guidance devices: the surgeon retains continuous control of the handpiece and performs site preparation and implant placement.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded robot in the oral/maxillofacial operative field (intraoral bone drilling and implant placement); it is surgeon-driven, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of implant-based chin or cheek augmentation.

sources.title: Robotic Injections: The Future in Aesthetics – MedicalExpo e-Magazine
sources.claim: The only reported facial-injection robot, LENA, is a vendor-described AI arm for toxin/filler injection that was still awaiting medical certification and shows no evidence of routine clinical deployment or of chin/cheek volumizing augmentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (facial neuromodulator/filler injection) is the non-surgical form of chin/cheek enhancement; the system is unproven, uncertified and its autonomy is unestablished, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Perform minor facial rejuvenation procedures, including the use of Botox and laser technology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cosmetic botulinum toxin session in the surgeon's office procedure room: healthy adult seated in a treatment chair, surgeon assesses dynamic glabellar/frontalis/orbicularis lines with the patient animating, reconstitutes toxin, marks and delivers ~20-40 small intramuscular/intradermal boluses with a 30-32G needle, adjusts units per site for asymmetry, applies pressure, schedules 2-week touch-up.

Hyaluronic acid filler for nasolabial folds, lips, cheeks or tear troughs in the same office room: topical/block anesthesia, needle or cannula threading in specific tissue planes, tactile depth sensing and aspiration to avoid vessels, product molded by palpation, live judgment of volume and symmetry, vascular-occlusion vigilance.

Non-ablative photorejuvenation session (Q-switched/long-pulsed Nd:YAG, IPL photofacial, pigment or vascular lesion pass) over the forehead, cheeks and periorbital region: eye shields placed, handpiece moved over the contoured face with even, non-overlapping coverage at set fluence, skin response monitored, cooling applied.

Ablative or fractional-ablative resurfacing (CO2/Er:YAG) of the full face or perioral region under topical/local anesthesia or sedation: metal corneal shields, multiple planned passes with density/depth titrated to visible tissue endpoint, wiping of ablated debris, feathering at borders, occlusive post-care instructions.

Therapeutic/functional botulinum toxin as practiced by OMS: masseter hypertrophy, bruxism/TMD or gummy smile, in the office chair; the muscle is palpated while the patient clenches or animates, 3-6 deeper intramuscular points per side are injected with landmark (sometimes ultrasound) targeting, and function is re-checked.

sources.system: ARTAS iX / iXi robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: ARTAS® Robotic Hair Transplant | Venus Treatments USA
sources.claim: ARTAS iX (Venus Concept, formerly Restoration Robotics) is an FDA-cleared robotic system that autonomously harvests follicular units from human scalp skin under physician supervision; it is sold and used commercially in hair-restoration clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic follicular-unit excision and implantation. It is needle work on the skin of a living patient's head, executed by machine at sub-millimetre accuracy against a physician-designed site map with controlled depth and angle, in an aesthetic-clinic procedure room with the treated skin held in a mechanical tensioner. The mechanical demands of placing a mapped grid of shallow facial toxin injections are of the same class and lower precision.

sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant Pros and Cons: A Clinical Trainer's Evidence-Based Verdict
sources.claim: The current ARTAS platforms execute thousands of planned needle placements per hour in head skin and perform both graft harvesting and implantation robotically, with the surgeon planning and supervising rather than driving each motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic recipient-site creation and graft implantation. Delivering material through a needle into skin at a planned coordinate, depth and angle at high throughput is the mechanical core of executing a physician's facial neuromodulator injection map.

sources.system: Robotic skin photo-rejuvenation prototype (PolyU / RODS Technology)
sources.developer: Hong Kong Polytechnic University, RODS Technology, Jinan University Institute of Dermatology
sources.title: A Split-face Study of Novel Robotic Prototype vs Human Operator in Skin Rejuvenation Using Q-switched Nd:Yag Laser: Accuracy, Efficacy and Safety
sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic laser prototype performed a Q-switched 1064 nm non-ablative facial rejuvenation session on the forehead and cheek of 17 human subjects in a split-face trial run in a university hospital dermatology department, achieving better laser coverage than the practitioner with no side effects.

sources.system: Vision-guided skin photo-rejuvenation robot (IEEE/ASME Trans. Mechatronics 2022)
sources.developer: Muddassir, Gomez, Hu, Chen, Navarro-Alarcon (Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
sources.title: Robotics Meets Cosmetic Dermatology: Development of a Novel Vision-Guided System for Skin Photo-Rejuvenation
sources.claim: The same group's peer-reviewed system models the patient's face with a depth sensor, segments it into seven regions and automatically fills them with laser shots using a manipulator carrying a cosmetic laser and thermal camera, validated on human subjects.

sources.title: Flawless Skin Boutique Introduces EON, a Revolutionary Robotic Body Contouring Treatment
sources.claim: EON is an FDA-cleared 1064 nm aesthetic laser whose treatment head is carried by an articulated robotic arm that maps the patient's body surface in 3D and moves autonomously without contacting the skin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic laser body contouring. It is autonomous delivery of a planned laser dose over a curved, moving human body surface with real-time skin-temperature monitoring in an ordinary aesthetic treatment room, the same delivery problem as a robotic facial laser pass.

sources.title: Dominion Aesthetic Technologies Receives New FDA Clearance for EON Smarter Body Contouring
sources.claim: EON is deployed commercially in aesthetic practices and medical spas across more than 18 US states.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic laser body contouring, showing that machine-guided aesthetic laser delivery is accepted in routine clinic practice; transfers to the delivery mechanics of a facial laser rejuvenation pass.

sources.title: Venus gets 510(k) clearance for fractional skin resurfacing technology
sources.claim: Venus Concept's AI.ME robotic platform received FDA 510(k) clearance for fractional skin resurfacing of wrinkles and acne scars, using machine vision and AI to act on the dermis according to a pre-planned treatment; commercial launch was projected for late 2024 and independent confirmation of autonomous operation was not found.

sources.title: Role of Robotics in Neuromodulator and Filler Injections of Face
sources.claim: The only named robot built for facial neuromodulator and filler injection, NextMotion's LENA arm, is a robot-assisted device that still depends on the injector's judgment; the peer-reviewed review describes robotic facial injection as an emerging field.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device uses AI-driven ultrasound guidance and robotic needle insertion to perform the whole blood draw on a patient without an operator; it is CE-marked and was launched into European healthcare settings in March 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture. A machine locates a subsurface target by imaging and inserts a needle into a living patient's tissue to a computed depth, with the limb presented in a purpose-built cradle, inside a clinical facility - the same class of act, at tighter tolerance, as placing planned facial toxin injections on a fixtured head.

emergingTasks.label: Read and evaluate imaging, such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), for diagnosis and treatment.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Orthodontists
roles.description: Examine, diagnose, and treat dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies. Design and fabricate appliances to realign teeth and jaws to produce and maintain normal function and to improve appearance.
roles.sector: Healthcare practitioners and technical

tasks.label: Diagnose teeth and jaw or other dental-facial abnormalities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-patient comprehensive diagnosis for an adolescent in a private orthodontic practice: the orthodontist synthesizes examination findings, intraoral scan/models, panoramic and cephalometric radiographs and facial photos into a diagnosis and problem list (Angle classification, crowding, overjet/overbite, skeletal pattern, midlines).

Early/mixed-dentition diagnosis for a 7-9 year old (interceptive screening): determining whether crossbite, ectopic eruption, arch-length deficiency, habits, or growth-timing problems constitute a diagnosable abnormality warranting Phase I treatment or observation.

Adult or complex dentofacial diagnosis: skeletal discrepancy or asymmetry possibly requiring orthognathic surgery, TMD signs, airway/CBCT interpretation, periodontal or restorative compromise; diagnosis formulated in consultation with oral surgeon, periodontist or prosthodontist.

Interim diagnostic re-evaluation of a patient in active treatment: judging from progress records and chairside findings whether root resorption, impacted/ankylosed canine, anchorage loss, arch coordination failure or an emerging asymmetry is present.

Screening or remote contexts: school-based and community-event screenings and teledentistry submissions (patient-taken photos, mailed or shop-acquired scans) where the orthodontist renders a preliminary diagnosis or referral determination on limited records.

tasks.label: Examine patients to assess abnormalities of jaw development, tooth position, and other dental-facial structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-patient comprehensive orthodontic examination of an adolescent in a private orthodontic office: extraoral facial/profile and lip analysis, TMJ palpation and mandibular opening/closing path, intraoral inspection with mirror and probe of tooth position, crowding, molar/canine classification, overjet/overbite measurement, midlines, soft tissue and hygiene, integrated with photos, intraoral scan and pano/ceph radiographs to reach a diagnosis of skeletal and dental abnormalities.

Progress examination at a routine adjustment visit during active treatment (many per day, 5-10 minutes each): checking achieved tooth movement against plan, bite changes, appliance/bracket/wire condition and fit, root and anchorage concerns, oral hygiene and decalcification, elastic wear, then directing the next adjustment.

Mixed-dentition growth-monitoring recall of a 7-11 year old ('observation' visit): assessing eruption sequence and timing, arch width and space analysis, palpation for ectopic/impacted canines, crossbite or shift, habits (thumb, tongue posture, mouth breathing), and skeletal growth pattern to decide on interceptive timing.

Adult examination with complicating factors in the office: periodontal attachment loss and recession, existing crowns/implants/missing teeth, wear facets, TMD signs with muscle and joint palpation and range-of-motion testing, prior orthodontic treatment or need for surgical-orthodontic assessment.

Examination of a poorly cooperative patient — a young or anxious child, a gagging patient, or a patient with special needs — in the office chair: limited opening, head and tongue movement, need for coaxing and adaptive positioning while still assessing tooth position and jaw relationships.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System | Business Wire
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm autonomously performed a crown preparation on a live human patient in a dental clinical setting, using a handheld 3D volumetric (OCT) imaging scanner; it remains an IRB/clinical-trial-stage prototype rather than a deployed exam system, and it performs restorative preparation, not an orthodontic diagnostic examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral instrument work on a live patient. It shows a robot can operate a tool inside a human mouth in a dental operatory, but it captures tooth-level structure for a single restorative site and produces no orthodontic assessment of jaw development, facial structures or function.

sources.developer: British Dental Journal review of the field
sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Independent peer-reviewed commentary confirms the July 2024 event: an autonomous AI-controlled robot completed a whole tooth-preparation procedure on a human patient, the only such reported case; robotics in dentistry is otherwise described as an auxiliary tool in implantology, restorative dentistry and education.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dental treatment on a human. Cited to show the current frontier of in-mouth robotic autonomy; the reviewed applications are implant/restorative execution and education, not patient examination or orthodontic diagnosis.

sources.system: RobOralScan (Franka Research 3 arm + Huvitz Lilivis SCAN intraoral scanner)
sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction (arXiv)
sources.claim: RobOralScan is a reinforcement-learning policy for automatic robotic intraoral scanning; the real-world validation was zero-shot on a bench setup with a Franka arm and an intraoral scanner scanning a jaw model (phantom), reaching ~92.6% average coverage and satisfying the scan criterion in 8 of 10 simulated episodes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquiring a 3D record of tooth position, one input to the orthodontic exam. Transfer is limited: the demonstration is on a fixtured jaw model on a lab bench, not a live moving patient, coverage is below clinical acceptance, and it yields geometry only, no diagnostic assessment.

sources.developer: Research group publishing in Scientific Reports (Lifeline-style force-controlled robot)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station (SR-NOCS) inserted swabs into the mouths and noses of live patients under force control in a hospital clinical trial with 52 suspected COVID-19 patients, showing autonomous instrument placement in the oral cavity of a cooperative human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safe autonomous entry of an instrument into a live human's oral cavity in a clinical facility. It supports contact safety only; the objects (throat mucosa vs. dentition), precision, and required perceptual judgment (malocclusion, skeletal relationships) differ entirely from an orthodontic examination.

tasks.label: Study diagnostic records, such as medical or dental histories, plaster models of the teeth, photos of a patient's face and teeth, and X-rays, to develop patient treatment plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Fit dental appliances in patients' mouths to alter the position and relationship of teeth and jaws or to realign teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bonding a full fixed appliance at treatment start in an orthodontic office: isolate and dry the arch with cheek retractors/cotton rolls, etch and prime enamel, place ~10-20 brackets and molar tubes at prescribed heights/angulations (direct placement or seating an indirect-bonding tray), light-cure, remove flash, verify each bracket's position and occlusal clearance on a seated, talking, sometimes moving teen or adult patient.

Routine adjustment appointment: remove ligatures/open self-ligating clips, take out the existing archwire, select and insert the next flexible or stainless archwire through every bracket slot, cinch or bend distal ends, add auxiliaries (power chain, coil springs, hooks, elastics), check for irritation and comfort, in a standard operatory chair.

Delivering removable appliances: seating a clear aligner series (often after bonding composite attachments through a template and doing interproximal reduction), or fitting a Hawley/Essix retainer — checking seating, pressure points and occlusion and adjusting acrylic/wires chairside until fit is acceptable.

Fitting and cementing banded/fixed auxiliary appliances in children: removing separators, sizing and seating molar bands, trial-fitting a rapid palatal expander, Herbst, transpalatal arch or lingual holding arch, loading bands with cement, seating the appliance fully against the palate/teeth, removing excess cement and confirming fit and activation.

Difficult-condition fittings: young child, strong gag reflex, special-needs or uncooperative patient, poor moisture control or a patient presenting for an emergency rebond/repair of a loose bracket or band with saliva, blood, or partially cured adhesive present in a busy multi-chair clinic.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-controlled robotic dental system autonomously performed a crown preparation (drilling) on a live human patient in a dental clinic setting — the frontier of autonomous intraoral robotic work — but it is a prototype limited to pre-planned cutting of a tooth, not placement/bonding of orthodontic attachments or wire manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crown preparation inside a live patient's mouth in a dental operatory. It shows a robot can register to a moving mouth and run a handpiece, but it removes tooth structure along a planned path; it does not grasp, adhesively bond, or seat millimetre-scale appliances, thread flexible archwires, or verify appliance fit, so it does not substantiate appliance fitting.

sources.developer: Yakebot (China); studied at Peking University School of Stomatology and others
sources.title: Accuracy of the Yakebot dental implant robotic system versus fully guided static computer-assisted implant surgery template in edentulous jaw implantation: A preliminary clinical study
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots (Yakebot and similar) place implants in patients' jaws in clinical studies using rigid splint registration; this is the most mature autonomous intraoral robotic capability, and it is confined to drilling osteotomies and inserting implant fixtures into bone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: implant placement in a patient's mouth. The workpiece is rigidly registered bone and the action is drilling/screw insertion along one axis; orthodontic appliance fitting requires adhesive handling on wet enamel, sub-millimetre placement of many small brackets, flexible-wire threading and fit verification, none of which this system performs.

sources.system: orthodontic archwire-bending robots (e.g., SureSmile/Orametrix-type wire-bending robots)
sources.developer: various (review by De La Garza-Ramos et al., Cureus)
sources.title: Application of Robotics in Orthodontics: A Systematic Review
sources.claim: A 2024 systematic review of robotics in orthodontics finds published robotic applications are confined to archwire bending and simulation of dental/mandibular movement; no robotic system is reported that fits or bonds appliances intraorally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabrication of the appliance (wire bending) in a bench-top machine, not fitting it in the patient's mouth. It is cited to establish that the deployed orthodontic robotics frontier is off-patient fabrication, so it cannot substantiate chairside fitting.

sources.system: surveyed orthodontic robotic systems (robotic dental assistants, wire-bending and aligner-production robots)
sources.developer: review by Adel et al., BioMed Research International
sources.title: Robotic Applications in Orthodontics: Changing the Face of Contemporary Clinical Care
sources.claim: A scoping review of robotic applications in orthodontics enumerates the domains where robots are used — assistants, diagnosis/simulation, education, wire bending and appliance fabrication, nano/microrobots, maxillofacial surgery and implants, aligner production — none of which is chairside fitting of appliances in the patient's mouth.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a survey of the field rather than of a single system: it maps where orthodontic robots do operate (lab fabrication, simulation, surgical guidance) and shows the absence of any system that seats or bonds appliances intraorally.

tasks.label: Adjust dental appliances to produce and maintain normal function.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine fixed-appliance adjustment visit in the orthodontic operatory: patient reclined in chair, remove elastic ligatures, withdraw and replace/upsize the archwire, place bends or stops, cinch and ligate, check occlusion and comfort, add elastics — all intraorally with pliers on a moving, salivating patient.

Removable or functional appliance adjustment chairside: activate/adjust Adams clasps and labial bow on a Hawley retainer, relieve acrylic pressure points, check and turn a palatal expander, adjust a Herbst/twin-block advancement — repeated try-in, judge fit against the tissues, re-bend with pliers.

Emergency/repair adjustment: loose or rotated bracket rebonded and repositioned, poking distal wire cut and tucked, broken ligature or spring replaced, appliance arm re-adapted — unscheduled, variable presentation, often on a young or anxious patient.

Bench/lab wire customization in the practice's in-house lab or via a lab order: form or re-form an archwire, fixed-retainer wire, or retainer wire component to a new digital or written prescription so the appliance delivers the intended forces; output is the shaped wire, ready for the clinician to place.

Clear-aligner-related adjustments in the chair: rebond or replace a lost composite attachment, perform interproximal reduction, trim or relieve an aligner edge, adjust buttons/hooks so the aligner seats and tracks properly.

sources.system: SureSmile archwire bending robot (Dentsply Sirona / OraMetrix)
sources.title: Robotic Archwire Bending in Orthodontics: A Review of the Literature (PMC)
sources.claim: SureSmile (Dentsply Sirona) commercially supplies robotically bent custom orthodontic archwires; the bending robot is a fixed-base manipulator with gripping tools that hold the wire while it is twisted to a computed shape, i.e. work brought to a purpose-built machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: shaping the appliance wire to a prescription so it delivers the intended forces. It substantiates only the bench/fixtured wire-forming instance, not intraoral adjustment.

sources.title: Custom Orthodontics | SureSmile USA
sources.claim: Robotically bent wires are an ordinary commercial product line clinicians prescribe today, confirming deployment rather than demonstration.

sources.system: YOAT BendArc / YOAT Bender II wire bending robot
sources.title: BENDARC - Orthodontic wire bender by YOAT Corp | MedicalExpo
sources.claim: YOAT sells an in-office robotic wire bender (BendArc) for finishing archwires, placing the fixtured bending machine inside the orthodontic practice; the same maker's Bender II bends retainer wires on site.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers forming/re-forming the wire component of a fixed or removable appliance to a prescription; the wire is loaded into the machine's grippers, so it is an E1 presentation.

sources.system: OG-DOS Hawley retainer wire bending robot
sources.title: AI-assisted design and robotic wire bending of Hawley retainer - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A commercially offered Hawley retainer wire bending robot automates bending of labial bows, Adams clasps, lingual bows, TPA and Nance bows for dental labs and orthodontic clinics; an associated study evaluated AI-assisted design plus robotic bending of Hawley retainers in the OG-DOS system.
sources.transferJustification: Covers forming the wire elements of a removable appliance to a digital design; it does not cover chairside re-adaptation of an existing appliance against a patient's tissues.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: The only autonomous robot reported to work inside a live patient's mouth performed a restorative crown preparation; it is a prototype demonstration on a single patient and its maker states the prototypes lack FDA 510(k) clearance and are not for sale in the US. No orthodontic wire, ligature, bracket or aligner-attachment manipulation is claimed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = intraoral crown preparation (rotary cutting along a planned path with an intraoral stabilization brace). It does NOT transfer to appliance adjustment: that requires bimanual plier work on 0.016-inch superelastic wire, ligation, bracket rebonding and tactile fit judgement, none demonstrated; the system is also an unclear-quality single-patient prototype without clearance.

tasks.label: Provide patients with proposed treatment plans and cost estimates.

tasks.label: Advise patients to comply with treatment plans.

tasks.label: Instruct dental officers and technical assistants in orthodontic procedures and techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chairside coaching during patient appointments: the orthodontist verbally directs and corrects an orthodontic/dental assistant on tasks such as placing separators, seating bands, changing ligatures or archwires, taking intraoral scans and photos, explaining what to do and why while the assistant performs the work in the operatory.

Scheduled in-office staff training sessions: reviewing office clinical protocols, infection control and bonding sequences with assistants and technicians, sometimes demonstrating a technique on a typodont or model while explaining the rationale and answering questions.

Case-specific direction to lab technicians and assistants: conveying appliance design and fabrication instructions (retainer type, expander design, wire dimensions, adjustments to a returned appliance) through written prescriptions, annotated photos/scans, and verbal explanation of the technique to be used.

Teaching residents, dental students or general dental officers (hospital/military/academic or CE settings): lectures, case seminars, and supervised clinic instruction where the orthodontist explains diagnosis, mechanics and technique and critiques trainees' work.

Remote or asynchronous instruction: video calls, recorded technique videos, screen-shared case reviews and written protocol updates sent to assistants, technicians or affiliated dentists in other locations.

tasks.label: Coordinate orthodontic services with other dental and medical services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Design and fabricate appliances, such as space maintainers, retainers, and labial and lingual arch wires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-debond clear thermoformed retainer (Essix/Vivera-type): after an intraoral scan or impression, a model is produced, a plastic sheet is thermoformed over it, the shell is trimmed to the gingival line, edges polished and the retainer packaged; done in the practice's in-house lab or a commercial orthodontic lab.

Hawley or wraparound removable retainer: labial bow and Adams/ball clasps bent from stainless wire to a working model, wire seated and processed into an acrylic baseplate, then trimmed and polished on a lab bench.

Labial or lingual arch wires for a fixed-appliance case: forming arch form and first/second/third-order bends to the prescribed tooth positions, either bent by the doctor/assistant on a bench or ordered as a patient-specific custom wire from a digital wire service.
Fixed bonded lingual retainer wire: a multistranded or CAD/CAM wire contoured to the lingual surfaces of the anterior teeth on a model (or chairside), delivered ready to bond.

Space maintainers and other fixed appliances (band-and-loop, lingual holding arch, Nance, transpalatal arch, palatal expander): band/abutment fitted or scanned, framework wires formed and joined to bands (soldered/welded) or the appliance produced as one CAD/CAM piece, then finished and polished in the lab.

Same-day chairside fabrication, modification or repair in the operatory/in-office lab: adding a finger spring or adjustment bend to an existing appliance, re-adapting a distorted retainer wire, patching a cracked acrylic baseplate with self-cure resin while the patient waits.
