sources.title: SureSmile » suresmile archwires
sources.claim: SureSmile's wire-bending machine in the SureSmile digital lab bends patient-specific archwires with first-, second- and third-order bends from the doctor's digital plan, and the wires are shipped to the practice for insertion.

sources.system: SureSmile Advanced Wire / robotically bent wires
sources.title: Dentsply Sirona's SureSmile Solutions to be Highlighted at AAO 2025
sources.claim: SureSmile's commercially offered platform includes robotically bent labial and lingual custom wires, confirming current commercial availability of robot-fabricated arch wires.

sources.system: SureSmile archwire bending robot; Bending Art System
sources.title: Robotic Archwire Bending in Orthodontics: A Review of the Literature (Cureus)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed 2024 review identifies SureSmile as the leading archwire-bending robot, and describes CAD/CAM bending systems producing custom wires for both labial and lingual applications.

sources.system: OG-DOS Bender MAX / Bender S Hawley Retainer Wire Bending Robot
sources.title: Hawley Retainer Wire Bending Robot – Dental Mates
sources.claim: A commercially sold benchtop wire-bending robot automates production of Hawley retainer wires and other orthodontic wire components (Adams clasp, labial bow, lingual ..., TPA, Nance bow) from digital designs for labs and clinics.

sources.system: OG-DOS AI-assisted design and robotic wire bending system
sources.title: AI-assisted design and robotic wire bending of Hawley retainer (Journal of Dentistry / ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed study evaluated AI-assisted digital design plus robotic wire bending of complete Hawley retainers (labial bow plus two Adams clasps) against manual 3D design.

sources.system: Align Technology aligner/retainer manufacturing line (3D printer farms, automated thermoforming, automated trimming and laser marking)
sources.title: DEEP DIVES | Inside the race to launch a direct 3D printed clear aligner solution (TCT Magazine)
sources.claim: Align Technology runs an automated production chain that 3D prints patient-specific thermoforming moulds, thermoforms the plastic appliance over them, then trims and laser-marks automatically, at over a million unique custom appliances per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass fabrication of thermoformed clear aligners. Vacuum/pressure-formed clear retainers (Essix, Vivera) are made by exactly this process — thermoforming a sheet over a patient-specific printed model, then trimming and finishing — with the same materials, tolerances and factory setting, so performance carries over to retainer fabrication.

sources.system: Invisalign Palatal Expander System (direct 3D printed device)
sources.title: FDA Clears Invisalign Palatal Expander System (Orthodontic Products)
sources.claim: Align's Invisalign Palatal Expander is a direct 3D printed orthodontic appliance cleared by FDA for commercial use, i.e. a fixed/removable expansion appliance whose body is fabricated entirely by machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabrication of an arch-expansion appliance. Palatal expanders belong to the same appliance class as space maintainers and holding arches (rigid intraoral appliance built to a scanned arch), showing machine fabrication of appliance bodies at clinical quality.

sources.system: Niryo Ned3 Pro + LAC laser aligner cutter automated cell
sources.title: Automated production of orthodontic aligners – Niryo
sources.claim: A turnkey robot cell combining a 6-axis arm, laser aligner cutter and storage magazine trims up to 96 thermoformed appliances per day without human intervention and is in use by orthodontic practices/labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic trimming of thermoformed aligners. Trimming and finishing a thermoformed clear retainer is the identical operation on the identical workpiece (a formed plastic shell on/off a printed model), so the demonstrated capability transfers to retainer fabrication.

sources.system: DHR Engineering automated resin model production cell (Formlabs Form 4L/BL, Wash L, Cure L, robotic arm)
sources.title: Fully Automated Resin Model Production for Clear Aligner Manufacturing by DHR Engineering
sources.claim: A fully automated print cell with a robotic arm serving SLA printers, wash and cure stations produced 7,280 dental models in 24 hours with no operator input, covering the model-production step of appliance fabrication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated production of dental working models. Retainer and appliance fabrication begins with a patient-specific model; this cell shows the printing, washing, curing and handling steps run unattended, supplying the fixtured input for downstream retainer forming.

sources.title: CAD/CAM nitinol bonded retainer versus a chairside rectangular-chain bonded retainer: A multicentre randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: Memotain CAD/CAM bonded lingual retainers are designed from a digital scan and laser-cut from nitinol with no wire bending, and were tested against chairside-fabricated bonded retainers in a multicentre randomised controlled trial.

sources.system: 3D-printed band-and-loop space maintainer (CAD design, additive metal/resin printing)
sources.developer: University clinical研究 group (Kapoor et al., IJCPD)
sources.title: Efficacy of 3D-printed Space Maintainers in Comparison to Conventional and Prefabricated Space Maintainers: A Randomized Control Trial
sources.claim: A randomised controlled trial found 3D-printed band-and-loop space maintainers clinically successful for survival, gingival health and satisfaction, comparable to conventional soldered band-and-loop appliances.

roles.title: Prosthodontists
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, rehabilitate, design, and fit prostheses that maintain oral function, health, and appearance for patients with clinical conditions associated with teeth, oral and maxillofacial tissues, or the jaw.
roles.sector: Healthcare practitioners and technical

tasks.label: Examine patients to diagnose oral health conditions and diseases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Comprehensive initial prosthodontic examination of a new adult patient in a private-practice operatory: takes/updates history, palpates head, neck, lymph nodes and TMJ, retracts and inspects all oral soft tissues for lesions (oral cancer screening), charts caries and existing restorations with mirror and explorer, probes periodontal pockets at six sites per tooth, tests mobility/percussion/vitality, evaluates occlusion and interarch space, interprets radiographs or CBCT, and records diagnoses.

Recall/maintenance examination of an existing prosthetic patient in the operatory: inspects and probes around crowns, fixed partial dentures and implants for peri-implant mucositis/peri-implantitis, checks abutment and prosthesis mobility, screw loosening, cement excess, ceramic chipping, caries at margins, occlusal wear, soft-tissue health, and issues diagnoses.

Problem-focused/emergency examination in the operatory: patient presents with pain, swelling, a loose or fractured crown, debonded veneer, or a denture sore spot; clinician palpates, percusses, tests with cold/electric pulp tester, inspects the failed restoration and mucosa, orders and reads a periapical film, and reaches a working diagnosis the same visit.

Examination of an edentulous or partially edentulous patient being assessed for removable prostheses: evaluates residual ridge form and resorption, palpates for flabby/displaceable tissue, tori, undercuts and sharp spicules, assesses saliva, mucosal health (denture stomatitis, hyperplasia), vertical dimension and existing denture fit, often in an elderly patient with limited tolerance.

Examination in an institutional setting — hospital dental clinic or maxillofacial prosthetics unit — of a medically complex or post-oncologic patient (obturator or facial prosthesis wearer): assesses defect margins, radiation-affected mucosa, trismus/limited opening, screens for tumor recurrence and osteoradionecrosis, sometimes chairside on a ward or with limited portable equipment.

sources.system: Perceptive autonomous dental robot (with hand-held OCT intraoral scanner)
sources.title: A Robot Just Performed Fully Autonomous Surgery On A Live Patient For The First Time - BGR
sources.claim: Perceptive's dental robot performed what the company describes as the first fully automated dental procedure (crown preparation) on a human patient; diagnosis/planning input came from a hand-held OCT intraoral scanner operated by a person, not from robotic examination of the patient, and the demonstration was a single unapproved case abroad.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation inside a live patient's mouth. It is the closest evidence to robotic oral examination — it shows autonomous intraoral instrument control plus AI caries detection from OCT — but the imaging is acquired by a human holding the scanner and the output is a crown prep, not a clinician-grade diagnostic examination of soft tissue, periodontium, TMJ or prostheses.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: The same July 2024 milestone is described in the peer-reviewed dental literature; the system relies on a hand-held 3D volumetric (OCT) scanner to model the mouth, i.e. the data-gathering step of the examination is still performed by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic crown preparation. Cited to establish that even the most advanced autonomous dental robot depends on human-performed intraoral scanning, so it does not substantiate robotic completion of a patient examination.

sources.developer: DLR / clinical partners (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous force-controlled swab robot station performed naso- and oropharyngeal swab sampling on 52 suspected COVID-19 patients in clinical studies, showing autonomous instrument insertion into a cooperative patient's mouth in a clinical facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of an instrument in the oral cavity of a seated patient in a clinic. It shows physical access to the mouth is achievable autonomously, but the robot only collects a specimen at one site; it performs no inspection, palpation, probing, or diagnostic interpretation of oral disease.

sources.title: Accuracy of autonomous robotic surgery for dental implant placement in fully edentulous patients: A retrospective case series study - PubMed
sources.claim: The Yakebot autonomous dental implant robot places implants in patients in dental clinics, but operates from a clinician-made plan built on CBCT/intraoral scan data — the examination, diagnosis, and planning remain human work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic drilling in the jaws of patients in a dental operatory. Shows the state of clinical dental robotics — narrow, pre-planned surgical execution — and provides no capability for examining a patient to diagnose oral conditions.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction (arXiv)
sources.claim: Automated robotic intraoral scanning — the mere data-acquisition step of an oral examination — is still a research problem, with the first reinforcement-learning pipeline for automatic intraoral scanning reported in 2026 and validated on reconstruction coverage rather than on patients or diagnoses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of intraoral 3D geometry. Cited to show that even automating the sensing sub-step of an oral examination is at prototype stage on dental models, well short of a patient examination yielding accepted diagnoses.

tasks.label: Fit prostheses to patients, making any necessary adjustments and modifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Delivery appointment for a fixed prosthesis (single crown, onlay, or 3-unit bridge) in a dental operatory: remove provisional, clean the prep, try in the restoration, check margins and proximal contacts with floss/explorer, adjust interproximal and occlusal contacts with a handpiece and articulating paper while the seated patient taps and grinds, polish the adjusted porcelain, then cement/bond and clean excess cement.

Complete denture insertion and follow-up adjustments in the operatory: seat the processed denture, evaluate border extensions and tissue blanching with pressure-indicating paste, relieve sore spots with acrylic burs, equilibrate occlusion at centric and in excursions, adjust retention/fit, instruct the patient - relying on the patient's spoken comfort feedback across one or more recall visits.

Implant-supported prosthesis delivery (single implant crown or screw-retained full-arch hybrid): verify passive fit clinically and radiographically, seat abutments, torque screws to specification, adjust the occlusal scheme, seal access channels with composite, confirm hygiene access - in a private-practice or dental-school operatory.

Removable partial denture insertion: adjust framework, rest seats and internal fit with disclosing medium and burs, tune clasp retention by bending or relieving, seat and check occlusion, relieve tissue-contacting acrylic causing soreness, and re-check at follow-up visits.

Complex / maxillofacial prosthesis fitting: obturators for maxillectomy defects, attachment-retained overdentures, implant-retained facial or ocular prostheses, chairside relines and repairs - highly individual anatomy, sometimes performed for medically compromised patients at hospital chairside or bedside rather than a standard operatory.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Perceptive's autonomous dental robot performed the first fully automated dental procedure ..., but the demonstrated procedure was drilling/preparing a tooth for a crown - not seating, adjusting, or cementing the prosthesis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tooth preparation is the step immediately preceding prosthesis fitting, in the same intraoral workspace. It shows autonomous intraoral cutting is possible, but does not transfer to fitting - no handling, try-in, contact/occlusal adjustment against patient feedback, polishing or cementation of a prosthesis was demonstrated.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Perceptive's own announcement frames 15-minute crown placement as an aim of the system rather than a completed capability; a single in-house automated procedure was performed on one patient.
sources.transferJustification: Stated aim/roadmap rather than a demonstrated prosthesis-fitting capability; recorded to document the frontier claim and its limits.

sources.title: Practical applications of robots in prosthodontics for tooth preparation and denture tooth arrangement: A scoping review (J Prosthet Dent)
sources.claim: A PRISMA scoping review of robots in prosthodontics found robotic work confined to tooth preparation (mostly in vitro on phantom models) and denture tooth arrangement in the laboratory; no studies of robotic chairside prosthesis insertion or adjustment on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Field-scope evidence: it establishes that the robotic prosthodontic literature covers tooth preparation and laboratory denture tooth arrangement, not fitting a finished prosthesis to a patient.

sources.system: Yakebot autonomous dental implant robotic system
sources.title: Learning curve of autonomous computer-assisted implant surgery systems for postgraduate dental trainees: an in vitro study (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: The Yakebot autonomous dental implant robot autonomously enters the mouth, prepares the implant site and places the implant, under surgeon supervision; its scope ends at osteotomy and fixture placement, not prosthesis try-in or adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted implant surgery in the same intraoral workspace at sub-millimetre accuracy. It does not transfer to prosthesis fitting, which requires grasping and seating a small restoration, verifying margins and contacts, iterative occlusal grinding and polishing, and cementation or screw torquing guided by patient feedback.

sources.title: Implant placement with an autonomous dental implant robot: A clinical report (J Prosthet Dent)
sources.claim: Clinical reports of an autonomous dental implant robot in patients cover implant placement accuracy only; the prosthetic delivery phase is still carried out by clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral surgical drilling and implant insertion in a dental clinic. It marks the ceiling of demonstrated autonomous intraoral robotics; prosthesis delivery, occlusal adjustment and cementation remain clinician-performed in these reports.

sources.title: Robotics in Prosthodontics: Current Applications, Challenges and Future Directions (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: A 2026 review of robotics in prosthodontics reports the field is moving from proof-of-concept and ... human-supervised systems, with evidence mostly in vitro or early clinical ....
sources.transferJustification: Field-level scope evidence establishing that no commercially available robot performs chairside prosthesis fitting and adjustment on patients.

tasks.label: Replace missing teeth and associated oral structures with permanent fixtures, such as implant-supported prostheses, crowns and bridges, or removable fixtures, such as dentures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-tooth implant restoration in a private prosthodontic office operatory: local anesthesia, flap or flapless osteotomy and fixture placement in the jawbone, suturing, healing period, then abutment connection, intraoral scan/impression, and try-in, occlusal adjustment and screw-retention or cementation of the definitive implant crown on a conscious, moving patient.

Fixed crown or 3-unit bridge on natural abutment teeth (replacing one missing tooth): anesthesia, isolation and retraction, handpiece preparation of abutments with subgingival margins and gingival management, digital scan or impression, provisional fabrication and cementation, then seating the definitive restoration, checking contacts/occlusion, adjusting and cementing.

Complete denture for an edentulous patient in a clinic operatory: preliminary and border-molded final impressions, jaw relation records and facebow, wax try-in with esthetic/phonetic evaluation, delivery of the processed denture, pressure-spot relief and multiple chairside adjustment visits based on patient-reported sore spots.

Removable partial denture for a partially edentulous patient: mouth preparation (rest seats, guide planes cut with a handpiece), impressions, framework try-in and intraoral adjustment of clasps/rests, altered-cast or tooth arrangement try-in, insertion, occlusal equilibration and follow-up adjustments.

Full-arch implant-supported fixed prosthesis (All-on-X) in a surgical suite/operatory of a dental practice or hospital dental department: extractions and alveoloplasty, placement of 4-6 implants including tilted posterior implants, multi-unit abutments, immediate conversion of an interim prosthesis chairside, then definitive prosthesis pick-up, fit verification and occlusal refinement.

Complex or maxillofacial prosthetic rehabilitation in a hospital or academic clinic: obturator for a maxillectomy defect, implant-retained overdenture for a medically compromised or irradiated patient, or remake/reline/repair of an existing prosthesis with heavily irregular tissue beds and limited mouth opening.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS, Chinese NMPA-marketed class)
sources.developer: reported by Chinese university dental hospital investigators; commercial ADIRS vendors
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery — The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: An autonomous dental implant robotic ... (ADIRS) placed implants in 74 partially edentulous patients: the clinician gave anesthesia, disinfected and registered the patient, and the robot then autonomously drilled the osteotomy and inserted the implant. Only the surgical sub-step is robotic; the prosthetic phase (abutment, scan, crown delivery) remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic osteotomy and implant fixture insertion. It is one sub-step of 'replace missing teeth with implant-supported prostheses'; it does not cover soft-tissue flap/suturing, impressions, or prosthesis fitting, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.system: Yakebot, Remebot, Cobot, Theta, Dcarer, Yomi
sources.developer: Yakebot Technology; Baihui Weikang; Shecheng; Hangzhou Jianjia; Dcarer Medical; Neocis
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems — International Journal of Oral Science
sources.claim: Review of dental implant robotic systems: Yakebot autonomously reaches the implant site and performs implant bed preparation and placement; several such systems are regulatory-approved and used in dental clinics (Yomi in the US, Yakebot/Remebot/Cobot/Theta/Dcarer in China).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted implant surgery in a dental operatory. Establishes only the drilling/fixture-placement portion of implant-supported tooth replacement; prosthesis fabrication, try-in and delivery are performed by clinicians.

sources.system: dental implant robots used in full-arch clinical trials (incl. Yakebot-class systems)
sources.developer: multiple academic groups (Bolding, Li, Jia, Xie et al.)
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems — PMC
sources.claim: Full-arch robotic implant clinical trials have placed five or six implants per jaw, but the associated prostheses (including immediate complete dentures) are delivered by clinicians, not the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-implant surgical placement for full-arch prostheses. Covers only the osteotomy/fixture stage of an All-on-X case; conversion prosthesis fabrication, pick-up and occlusal refinement remain manual.

sources.system: autonomous zygomatic implant robot (Chinese research system)
sources.developer: Li C., Wang M., Deng H. et al.
sources.title: Autonomous robotic surgery for zygomatic implant placement and immediately loaded implant-supported full-arch prosthesis: a preliminary research — Int J Implant Dent (PMC)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic placement of zygomatic implants followed by an immediately loaded implant-supported full-arch prosthesis was carried out in a single clinical case; robot performed drilling/placement, clinicians did the prosthetic loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic zygomatic implant placement in a complex atrophic maxilla. Substantiates only the surgical fixture step of a complex prosthetic rehabilitation, not impression-making, prosthesis fit or adjustment.

sources.system: SARP (semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system, Perceptive)
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment (preprint listing, Sciety)
sources.claim: First-in-human study of a semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system (Perceptive's SARP) prepared crowns in six patients with 39 µm RMS deviation; the five crowns were cemented during the same visit by the clinical team, not the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation of a natural tooth, the abutment-preparation sub-step of crown-and-bridge work. The system is described as semi-automated and does not perform anesthesia, isolation, seating or cementation, so it cannot complete a whole crown/bridge instance.

sources.title: Perceptive completes automated dental procedure with AI-driven robot — MassDevice
sources.claim: Perceptive announced the first fully automated robotic dental procedure on a human (tooth cutting for a crown) in July 2024, an in-house first-in-human demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tooth preparation for a crown. It is the cutting sub-step only; the demonstration involved a human dentist for diagnosis, decision-making and the remainder of the restorative visit.

sources.title: Perceptive | Meet Modern Dentistry
sources.claim: Perceptive states its robotic prototypes lack FDA 510(k) clearance and are not for sale in the US, with only in-house and out-of-US first-in-human testing completed.

sources.title: Neocis brings in $20M for robotic dental surgeries — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Yomi, the only FDA-cleared dental implant robot in US practices, is explicitly not autonomous: it provides haptic constraint while the surgeon holds and controls the drill.

tasks.label: Measure and take impressions of patients' jaws and teeth to determine the shape and size of dental prostheses, using face bows, dental articulators, recording devices, and other materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dentate patient in a dental operatory: prosthodontist captures a digital optical impression (intraoral scan) of prepared teeth, opposing arch and bite for a crown, bridge or implant restoration — retracting cheek/tongue, managing saliva and gingival tissue, verifying margin capture and re-scanning gaps.

Conventional physical impression for fixed prosthodontics: select/adapt a stock or custom tray, place retraction cord, mix and load alginate or PVS, seat the loaded tray on the patient's arch, hold during set, remove, inspect margins, take an opposing impression and a bite registration.

Edentulous/removable prosthesis records: preliminary impression, custom tray border molding with compound/PVS, final impression of denture-bearing mucosa, wax occlusion rims adjusted for lip support and vertical dimension, and a centric-relation jaw registration on a live, often elderly patient.

Face bow transfer at chairside (bite fork on maxillary teeth, ear pieces/nasion positioning, transfer to articulator) plus interocclusal records, then mounting maxillary and mandibular casts on a semi-adjustable articulator with plaster at the office bench and setting condylar guidance.

Complex cases: full-arch implant-level impression with splinted transfer copings or scan bodies and verification jig, maxillofacial/obturator impressions of surgical defects, or patients with severe gag reflex, limited mouth opening, tremor, or dementia requiring adaptation and repeat attempts.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotics system + hand-held OCT intraoral scanner
sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robot performed an autonomous crown preparation on a live patient in 2024, but the 3D imaging/impression step of that workflow is performed with a hand-held intraoral OCT scanner operated by a person, not by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic crown preparation) in the same operatory environment; cited to show that even in the most advanced autonomous dental robot the impression/measurement step remains human-performed, so it does not substantiate robotic impression taking.

sources.developer: DGIST (Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology)
sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction (arXiv 2606.26955)
sources.claim: RobOralScan is described by its authors as the first reinforcement-learning pipeline for robotic automatic intraoral ...; it is evaluated in simulation with only zero-shot sim-to-real feasibility trials on a bench robot-scanner setup (92.58% average coverage, scan criterion met in 8 of 10 episodes), not on live patients.

sources.system: Yakebot autonomous dental implant robotic system
sources.developer: Yakebot (Beijing) / Peking University School of Stomatology
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems
sources.claim: The Yakebot autonomous dental implant robot works inside live patients' mouths in dental clinics and drills implant osteotomies autonomously, but it executes a trajectory pre-planned from CBCT and human-acquired intraoral scans with a marker splint; it does not acquire impressions or jaw records.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (implant osteotomy) in the same setting (dental clinic) and same anatomy, cited as the strongest in-mouth autonomous dental robot; it does not transfer to impression taking because it removes bone along a pre-planned path from human-supplied scans rather than acquiring full-arch surface geometry while retracting soft tissue.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / partners (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: Autonomous swab robots have inserted swabs into the mouths/throats of live human subjects in clinical studies, showing force-compliant autonomous instrument insertion in the oral cavity, but they perform a coarse contact-sampling motion, not high-precision capture of dental surface geometry or jaw relations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-mouth swab sampling on live patients) shares the environment and the moving, compliant human subject, but the required precision is orders of magnitude lower (touching a mucosal area vs. capturing complete-arch geometry to tens of microns), so it cannot substantiate impression taking.

tasks.label: Collaborate with general dentists, specialists, and other health professionals to develop solutions to dental and oral health concerns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Design and fabricate dental prostheses, or supervise dental technicians and laboratory bench workers who construct the devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-unit or short-span fixed restoration (crown, inlay/onlay, veneer, up to a 3-unit bridge) for a routine restorative patient: prep scan or model in hand, restoration designed in CAD to the opposing/adjacent anatomy, then milled or printed in the office mill or by the commercial lab, sintered/glazed and polished to a seatable unit.

Implant-supported single-unit restoration: from an implant scan-body scan, design and fabricate a patient-specific abutment and/or screw-retained crown with correct emergence profile and screw-channel angulation, milled from zirconia or titanium and finished for delivery.

Digital complete denture or implant overdenture prosthesis: from digital records/scans, tooth arrangement and base design in CAD, then monolithic milling or 3D printing of base and teeth, finishing and polishing to a deliverable denture.

Conventional or hand-finished removable work: cast or SLM partial denture framework with clasp adjustment plus acrylic saddles and tooth setting, immediate or characterized dentures, wax try-ins, and bench relines/repairs performed in the office lab.

Complex full-arch implant-supported fixed prosthesis, full-mouth rehabilitation, or maxillofacial prosthesis (obturator, facial/ocular prosthesis): framework design from implant positions and clinical records, milling, layering/characterization or silicone coloring, and passive-fit/esthetic verification.

Supervising dental technicians and bench workers: writing and clarifying the lab prescription, reviewing wax-ups, frameworks and try-ins returned from the in-house or commercial lab, checking fit and shade on the model, and directing corrections and remakes.

sources.title: Digitizing Dentistry: How Glidewell Automation Empowers Mass Customization
sources.claim: Glidewell's dental laboratory runs automated 'BruxZir Factory' lines containing robotics, material handling, milling machines, vision systems, automatic finishers and QC scanners that produce patient-specific zirconia crowns and bridges with minimal human intervention.

sources.title: Glidewell and Beckhoff | Automated BruxZir Manufacturing
sources.claim: On Glidewell's monolithic crown manufacturing lines a robot selects and transfers the zirconia blank to ... anatomical shaping and the restoration is then glazed, with barcode and vision tracking and optical comparison to the design file (50 µm tolerance).

sources.system: Glidewell CloudPoint AI design + Intelligent Manufacturing
sources.title: Robotics and Automation (Chairside Magazine Vol. 21 Issue 2)
sources.claim: Cases arriving as digital files (or impressions scanned by an in-house CT scanner) are turned into restoration designs automatically by Glidewell's AI software, including die trim, margin marking and anatomy proposals, before automated manufacture.

sources.title: Harnessing the Power of AI in Digital Dentistry
sources.claim: 3Shape Automate returns AI-generated crown/inlay/onlay designs from an intraoral scan without human intervention, in about 90 seconds, with a reported ~92% design acceptance rate across tens of thousands of US lab cases.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the design half of this task; it is design software, not a robot, but it produces the CAD file that the cited milling systems then fabricate, so it substantiates that the design step need not be done by the prosthodontist.

sources.title: Same-Visit Screw-Retained Crowns: fastmill.io In-Office Mill
sources.claim: The fastmill.io chairside mill produces finished restorations, including screw-retained implant crowns, from fully sintered BruxZir NOW blocks inside a dental office in about 40 minutes, replacing a seven-day lab cycle.

sources.title: How Glidewell Intelligent Manufacturing Elevates Simplicity, Quality, Speed and Predictability for Dentists
sources.claim: Glidewell verifies finished units automatically: optical inspection compares milled restorations with the design file and only accepts cases within a 50 µm tolerance, evidence that machine output meets clinical acceptance criteria.

sources.title: Ivotion | Tooth & Denture Materials | Ivoclar
sources.claim: The Ivotion Denture System mills a complete removable denture, teeth and base together, from a single bi-layer disc in one uninterrupted milling cycle.

sources.system: PM7 milling unit with Ivotion discs (digital complete dentures)
sources.title: Digital vs. conventional removable complete dentures: A retrospective study on clinical effectiveness and cost-efficiency in edentulous patients
sources.claim: A retrospective clinical study of dentures milled on a 5-axis PM7 unit from Ivotion discs found machine-fabricated complete removable dentures gave the same clinical results as conventionally made ones.

sources.title: CERAMILL MATIK | AMANN GIRRBACH # 181200
sources.claim: Fully automatic dental milling machines present the work to themselves: the Ceramill Matik holds 36 blanks and 27 RFID-tracked tools, loads and changes them without an operator, and cleans itself between jobs.

sources.system: Stäubli TX40 six-axis robot at Westcam denture production
sources.title: Handling dental prosthesis | Stäubli
sources.claim: Industrial denture production cells use six-axis robots that detect, position and press artificial teeth automatically, showing robotic handling of denture components at production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (industrial denture tooth placement) transfers to denture fabrication here: same small prosthetic components, sub-millimetre placement accuracy, inside an enclosed automated cell.

sources.system: survey of prosthodontic robotic systems (49 publications, 1987–Aug 2025)
sources.title: Robotics in Prosthodontics: Current Applications, Challenges and Future Directions
sources.claim: A 2026 narrative review of robotics in prosthodontics finds current robotic use concentrated in laboratory automation (robot-assisted milling, polishing ...), with clinical applications still human-supervised.

sources.title: Fraunhofer technology revolutionises 3D printing of prosthetic eyes
sources.claim: Machine-made maxillofacial prostheses exist but only the modelling and printing steps are automated: Fraunhofer's Cuttlefish:Eye workflow 3D-printed an ocular prosthesis first fitted at Moorfields Eye Hospital in 2021, with finishing and fitting still done by an ocularist.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Removables: SLM-Printed Metal Partial Dentures
sources.claim: Selective laser melting produces cobalt-chrome partial denture frameworks directly from the design file at Glidewell, but each printed partial is still reviewed and finished by technicians in the lab.

tasks.label: Restore function and aesthetics to traumatic injury survivors, or to individuals with diseases or congenital disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult who lost multiple posterior/anterior teeth to caries or advanced periodontal disease: prosthodontist in a private practice operatory works up the case, plans and places (or restores) dental implants, takes intraoral scans/impressions, delivers provisional and then definitive implant-supported fixed prosthesis, adjusts occlusion chairside and reviews at recall.

Traumatic injury survivor (sports/motor-vehicle/fall) with one to four fractured or avulsed anterior teeth: emergency assessment, shade and contour matching to adjacent natural teeth, tooth preparation, provisional restoration, soft-tissue management, bonding/cementation of implant crown, veneer or crown, and occlusal/esthetic refinement over several visits in the dental operatory.

Partially or fully edentulous patient (disease-related tooth loss, often elderly or medically compromised): complete denture, removable partial denture, or implant overdenture — border-molded impressions, jaw relation records, wax try-in with esthetic approval, insertion, and repeated sore-spot adjustments and relines in the clinic.

Head-and-neck cancer patient after maxillectomy/mandibulectomy, or patient with a palatal defect: hospital-based maxillofacial prosthetics clinic; impression of an irregular, healing, sometimes irradiated defect, fabrication and fitting of a surgical/interim/definitive obturator or speech aid, with repeated modification as tissues change.

Adolescent or young adult with congenital condition (ectodermal dysplasia/oligodontia, cleft lip and palate, amelogenesis imperfecta): staged interdisciplinary restorative care in a clinic — transitional prostheses that accommodate growth, later definitive crowns/implants, esthetic form and speech considerations, close coordination with orthodontics and surgery.

Extraoral facial prosthesis (auricular, nasal, orbital) for trauma or tumor resection: impression/scan of the facial defect, sculpting or digital design, color matching to the patient's skin, adhesive- or implant-retained fitting on the patient, and periodic remakes/adjustments.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm performed an automated crown preparation on a human patient (outside the US) in about 15 minutes; the demonstrated procedure was tooth preparation for a crown, not the full restorative episode.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: tooth preparation is one chairside step inside a prosthodontic restoration episode; it does not cover diagnosis, shade/esthetic matching, soft-tissue handling, prosthesis try-in, cementation, or occlusal adjustment.

sources.title: Perceptive | Meet Modern Dentistry
sources.claim: The Perceptive system has not been tested in the US under IRB/IDE and has no FDA clearance or US commercial availability; testing to date is in-house and out-of-US.
sources.transferJustification: Bears on maturity/deployment of the only reported fully automated restorative dental robot; shows it is a demonstration rather than clinical practice.

sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment
sources.claim: A semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system (SARP) completed digitally pre-planned crown preparations in six patients with ~39 µm deviation; pre-manufactured crowns were seated and cemented in the same visit by the clinical team, and the robot's role was limited to the preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step (crown preparation) within the restoration of a diseased/damaged tooth; the surrounding steps (anesthesia, isolation, shade selection, cementation, occlusal adjustment) remained human-performed, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.title: Safety and performance of the first supervised automated dental robot to perform minimally invasive tooth prep for laminate veneers
sources.claim: The Lupin Robotic System performed supervised-automated minimally invasive tooth preparations for laminate veneers on 52 teeth in 12 patients in a prospective clinical (post-market) study in India; the robot performed the preparation step of the esthetic veneer workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: veneer preparation is the cutting step of an esthetic anterior restoration (relevant to trauma/congenital enamel cases); design, shade matching, try-in and adhesive bonding of the veneers remained clinician tasks.

sources.title: Robot-assisted dental implant surgery procedure: A literature review
sources.claim: Active dental implant robots such as YakeBot autonomously enter the mouth, prepare the implant osteotomy and place the implant with the operator only changing drills and monitoring; FDA-cleared Yomi is passive and must be guided by the operator's hands.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: implant placement is the surgical phase of implant-supported prosthodontic rehabilitation; the prosthetic phase (impressions, provisional, definitive prosthesis, occlusion) is not performed by these robots.

sources.title: Accuracy and operation procedure of robotic computer-aided implant surgery (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: Two autonomous dental implant robotic ..., received Chinese NMPA authorization in 2021 and are used clinically in dental hospital/clinic operatories, while Yomi received FDA clearance in 2017.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes regulatory/clinical maturity of autonomous robots for the implant-surgery sub-step only, in dental hospital operatories.

sources.system: Remebot autonomous robotic oral surgery system
sources.developer: Beijing Rui Yi Bo Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Autonomous robotic surgery for zygomatic implant placement and immediately loaded implant-supported full-arch prosthesis: a preliminary research
sources.claim: In a clinical case, the autonomous Remebot oral surgery robot placed zygomatic and alveolar implants for a severely atrophic maxilla as part of an immediately loaded full-arch implant rehabilitation; the digital planning, prosthesis fabrication and delivery were performed by the clinical team.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published analogue to full-arch rehabilitation of a disease-affected patient, but the robot executed only the osteotomy/implant placement; prosthesis design, fabrication, seating and occlusal adjustment were human.

sources.system: prosthodontic robots (tooth preparation, denture tooth arrangement)
sources.title: Practical applications of robots in prosthodontics for tooth preparation and denture tooth arrangement: A scoping review
sources.claim: A scoping review of robots in prosthodontics found the work concentrated on in vitro phantom studies of tooth preparation and denture tooth arrangement, with clinical application still at an early stage.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the task domain (prosthodontics); documents that robotic work is confined to isolated bench sub-steps rather than complete patient rehabilitation.

tasks.label: Repair, reline, or rebase dentures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chairside reline of a loose complete denture in the dental operatory: prepare/relieve the intaglio, mix and load hard reline resin or tissue conditioner, seat the denture in the seated patient's mouth, guide border molding and closure, remove at the correct set stage, trim flash, cure/polish, reseat and adjust occlusion and sore spots.

Same-day repair of a fractured denture base or a debonded/lost acrylic tooth done in the office lab: reassemble fragments and hold alignment (sticky wax/index or plaster jig), bevel and roughen fracture margins, apply autopolymerizing repair acrylic, cure under pressure/heat, trim and polish, then try in the patient's mouth and adjust.

Laboratory-processed reline or full rebase: clinician makes a closed-mouth functional impression in the existing denture; the denture is flasked, old base resin removed, new heat-cured acrylic packed and processed, deflasked, finished and polished; clinician then delivers, checks fit and occlusion, and adjusts.

Removable partial denture repair: add a replacement tooth to an existing acrylic/metal RPD, repair or add a clasp, or solder/laser-weld a fractured cast metal framework; involves an impression or index with the framework in place, bench metalwork and acrylic addition, finishing, and intraoral fit adjustment.

Digital reline/rebase or copy-denture: wash impression in the existing denture, desktop or intraoral scanning of denture and tissue surface, CAD redesign of the base, milling or 3D printing of the new base (or full monolithic denture), post-processing/bonding of teeth and polishing, then clinical delivery and occlusal adjustment.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive demonstrated an AI-controlled robotic arm performing a full crown-preparation procedure autonomously on one human patient — the closest existing autonomous intraoral robotics — but it cuts a fixed natural tooth and does not handle removable prostheses, impression/reline materials, or denture seating and adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous intraoral tooth preparation. It shares the operatory setting but not the objects or manipulations of relining/repair (flowable resin loading, border molding of a removable prosthesis, fragment reassembly, acrylic finishing), so capability does not carry over; it is also a single unpublished demonstration.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR5 cobots tending CNC crown mills at Glidewell Laboratories
sources.title: Collaborative Robots Cut Crown Production Time | Modern Machine Shop
sources.claim: Glidewell runs collaborative robot arms that autonomously tend CNC mills producing patient-specific dental crowns in its purpose-built production facility — machine-tending and milling of fixtured blanks, not repair or adaptation of an existing patient prosthesis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated fabrication of a patient-specific restoration from a stock blank in a purpose-built cell. It substantiates only blank handling and subtractive shaping of new workpieces; denture repair/reline requires handling a used, deformable, patient-worn prosthesis plus intraoral steps, which this system does not do.

sources.system: Ivotion Denture System (PM7 mill + monolithic disc)
sources.title: Monolithic Digital Dentures | Blog | Ivoclar USA
sources.claim: Ivoclar's Ivotion system mills a complete denture from a single monolithic disc in one continuous machine-controlled cycle, showing that denture-base geometry can be produced by a CNC machine, but design, tooth/base finishing, and all clinical impression and delivery steps remain manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = CAD/CAM fabrication of a new complete denture. It covers only the shaping sub-step of a possible digital rebase; the instance's start (functional impression in the patient's denture) and end (delivery, occlusal adjustment) are outside this machine's scope.

sources.system: AutoFinish DCPC250 / DCPC500 dental finishing machines
sources.title: Automate Dental Restoration Finishing | Zahn Dental
sources.claim: Commercial automated finishing machines polish printed dentures and other prosthetics in a batch chamber, automating only the finishing sub-step of denture work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated polishing of dental prostheses. Polishing is one late sub-step of a repair or reline; the machine cannot align fractured fragments, apply repair acrylic, process a new base, or fit the prosthesis, so it cannot complete the whole instance.

sources.title: Robotics in Prosthodontics: Current Applications, Challenges and Future Directions - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A 2026 narrative review of robotics in prosthodontics finds current applications limited to laboratory automation, scanning support, robotic articulators, and implant-guidance systems, with no reported robotic system for denture repair, relining, or rebasing.
sources.transferJustification: Field-level survey establishing the absence of any named robotic system performing denture repair/reline/rebase; used to support negative judgments, not a positive one.

tasks.label: Use bonding technology on the surface of the teeth to change tooth shape or to close gaps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Direct composite bonding to close a midline diastema or interdental spaces on anterior teeth in a private prosthodontic practice operatory: shade selection, isolation/retraction, enamel etch and adhesive, incremental placement of composite against Mylar/sectional matrices, sculpting proximal contours and emergence profile, light curing, occlusal check, finishing and polishing on a conscious, moving patient.

Direct composite bonding to reshape a tooth — repairing a chipped or worn incisal edge, building out a peg lateral, masking a discolored facial surface, or lengthening/recontouring an anterior tooth — freehand layering with enamel/dentin shades intraorally, cured, contoured and polished chairside.

Adhesive bonding (cementation) of indirect ceramic laminate veneers or composite veneers fabricated to change tooth shape/close spaces: try-in with pastes, rubber dam or retraction cord isolation, etch/silane of the intaglio, tooth etch and bonding agent, seating multiple thin veneers with resin cement, excess cement cleanup at margins, tack and final cure, margin finishing.

Multi-tooth additive composite rehabilitation of worn dentition (injection-molding technique with clear silicone indices or freehand full-arch composite buildups), often at an increased vertical dimension, over one or more long appointments with occlusal adjustment and polishing.

Bonded intraoral repairs and difficult-access cases: chairside composite repair of a chipped ceramic crown/fixed prosthesis or bonded closure of a space in a limitedly cooperative patient (anxious, gag-prone, pediatric or special-needs), sometimes in a hospital or institutional dental clinic under sedation.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm performed a fully automated crown preparation (subtractive tooth cutting) on a human patient in July 2024 — the state of the art for autonomous intraoral robotics; it does not perform adhesive/composite bonding buildup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation for a crown. It shows autonomous cutting inside a patient's mouth, but it is subtractive removal along a planned surface; it does not substantiate additive work — etching, adhesive application, incremental composite placement, sculpting anatomy, curing, contouring and polishing — required by this task.

sources.developer: Lupin (clinical study reported in Int J Comput Dent)
sources.title: Safety and performance of the first supervised automated dental robot to perform minimally invasive tooth prep for laminate veneers
sources.claim: A supervised automated dental robot performed minimally invasive tooth preparation for ... in 12 patients (52 teeth); the robot only cuts the tooth — the veneer bonding step is done by the clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: veneer tooth preparation in the same anterior esthetic zone. It establishes robotic precision for planned enamel reduction in vivo, but the reported robotic scope stops at preparation; adhesive cementation of the veneers and any composite shaping remain manual, so it cannot substantiate the bonding task.

sources.developer: University of Basel, Department of Biomedical Engineering
sources.title: Meet the Miniature Robot That Could Transform Crown Preparation - Dimensions of Dental Hygiene
sources.claim: A cork-sized intraoral robot prototype for scanning and preparing teeth for crowns was demonstrated by University of Basel researchers; it is a subtractive drilling prototype, not a system that places or shapes bonded composite.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoral tooth preparation. Shows miniaturized in-mouth robotic cutting at prototype stage; it does not handle viscous adhesive resins, matrix systems, layering or polishing, so it does not transfer to bonded shape change.

sources.title: Robotics and 3D Printing Products in Dentistry | Rayo 3DToothFill
sources.claim: The Rayo 3DToothFill robot casts and cures composite filling material into a 3D-printed mould on a benchtop; the finished restoration is then fixed (bonded) into the tooth by the dentist, showing the intraoral bonding step remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fabrication of composite restorations. The robot dispenses and cures composite in layers, but only inside a printed mould outside the mouth; the adhesive attachment to the tooth surface, contouring and polishing are performed by the clinician, so completion of this task is not substantiated even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS, e.g., Yakebot)
sources.developer: Chinese ADIRS developers; study reported in The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robotic systems have been used clinically in operatory settings (74 partially edentulous participants), demonstrating that autonomous dental robots exist but are confined to planned osteotomy/implant placement, not adhesive restorative work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling in the oral cavity of live patients. Establishes that dental robots can register to jaw motion and execute planned trajectories, but the manipulation class (rigid drilling into bone) differs entirely from handling flowable adhesives and sculpting composite to esthetic contour.

tasks.label: Treat facial pain and jaw joint problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial orofacial pain/TMD evaluation in a private prosthodontic or hospital dental operatory: history taking, bilateral palpation of masseter, temporalis and TMJ capsule for tenderness, measurement of maximal opening and excursions, palpation/auscultation of clicking or crepitus, load testing, screening of occlusion and existing prostheses, review of panoramic/CBCT or MRI images, arriving at a diagnosis (myalgia, disc displacement, arthralgia) and a plan discussed with the patient.

Records for and delivery of an occlusal stabilization splint/night guard: intraoral scan or alginate/PVS impressions and bite registration with the patient in the chair, centric relation record, lab or in-office fabrication, then a delivery visit where the appliance is seated, borders relieved with a handpiece, retention checked, and occlusal contacts marked with articulating paper and ground in to even bilateral contacts and smooth guidance, plus wear instructions.

Follow-up visits over weeks to months: re-interview about pain levels and sleep, re-measure opening, re-palpate muscles and joint, adjust the splint chairside as the bite settles, reinforce self-care (soft diet, heat, jaw exercises), modify medication or refer to physical therapy/behavioral therapy.

Occlusal correction in a TMD patient: analysis of occlusal contacts and interferences (articulating paper, T-scan, mounted casts), selective grinding of natural teeth or of crowns/dentures, or remaking/adjusting prosthetic restorations to distribute load, with iterative check-and-adjust cycles guided by the patient closing and reporting comfort.

Minimally invasive procedures for persistent pain: diagnostic local anesthetic block, trigger-point injection into masseter or temporalis, botulinum toxin injection for masticatory myalgia/bruxism, or (in some practices) TMJ arthrocentesis/intra-articular injection using palpated anatomic landmarks on a seated, awake patient.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-controlled robot autonomously performed a full crown preparation on a human patient in a dental chair, showing autonomous intraoral cutting, but nothing about diagnosing or treating jaw-joint or facial pain conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crown tooth preparation. It is the closest demonstrated autonomous intraoral procedure (handpiece cutting in a live mouth), but it executes a pre-planned tooth geometry and does not perform TMD examination, splint fitting, or occlusal equilibration decided from occlusal contacts and patient pain feedback.

sources.system: Yakebot autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS)
sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co., Ltd (Beijing) with Peking University School of Stomatology
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery
sources.claim: Yakebot, an autonomous dental implant robotic ..., performs implant osteotomy and placement autonomously on patients in dental clinics under surgeon supervision; its scope is preplanned drilling into bone, not facial pain or TMJ therapy, and the clinician still gives the local anesthetic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: implant surgery in a dental operatory. Shows autonomous robots can work intraorally in a clinic along a rigid preplanned trajectory registered to a marker, but provides no capability for palpation-based diagnosis, appliance fitting, occlusal adjustment, or injections.

sources.developer: Waseda University with Asahi Roentgen and Aichi Gakuin University (Japan)
sources.title: An oral rehabilitation robot for massaging the masseter and temporal muscles: a preliminary report (Oral Radiology)
sources.claim: The Waseda-Asahi oral rehabilitation robot (WAO-1) delivered maxillofacial massage to masseter and temporal muscles of patients with TMJ dysfunction and myofascial pain in small phase-1/phase-2 trials; it is a 2009 research prototype delivering one adjunct modality, not a system that evaluates, plans, or delivers prosthodontic TMD care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adjunct massage therapy for masticatory myofascial pain. It is the closest robotic system acting therapeutically on facial pain, but operator supervision/positioning is not established (autonomy unclear), trials involved 12 patients in 2009, and it performs no examination, splint work, or occlusal adjustment.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: Robotic intraoral scanning remains a research problem: RobOralScan learns a scan-control policy evaluated largely in simulation with zero-shot sim-to-real experiments, with the authors noting in-mouth deployment challenges, so even the record-taking step of splint therapy has no demonstrated robotic performance on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoral scanning for prosthodontic workflows. It bears on the impression/scan step of splint fabrication and shows this sub-step is only at simulation/bench stage, not patient-ready.

tasks.label: Place veneers onto teeth to conceal defects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Delivery/bonding appointment for 1-2 indirect ceramic laminate veneers on anterior teeth in a private prosthodontic operatory: remove provisionals and residual cement, try in the veneers with try-in paste, isolate the field (rubber dam/retraction cord), etch and silanate the ceramic, etch/prime enamel-dentin, seat each shell in exact position with resin cement, tack-cure, remove excess cement interproximally and subgingivally, final cure, floss, check and adjust occlusion, polish margins on a conscious, moving patient.

Tooth-preparation visit of a veneer case: local anesthesia, gingival retraction, 0.3-0.7 mm enamel reduction to a planned depth with margin placement, refinement and finishing of the prep, digital scan/impression, then fabrication and bonding of provisional veneers, all in a dental operatory with suction, water spray and soft tissue nearby.

Multi-unit esthetic case (6-10 anterior veneers, 'smile makeover') delivered in one long appointment: sequential try-in of the full set, esthetic and phonetic evaluation with patient feedback and mirror check, staged isolation and adhesive bonding of each unit, contact and midline verification, extensive cement cleanup, occlusal and excursive adjustment in a clinic operatory.

Direct composite veneers placed freehand chairside to mask discoloration, hypoplastic defects or diastemas: shade selection, enamel etch/bond, incremental layering and hand-sculpting of dentin/enamel composite shades to individual anatomy, curing, contouring with discs and burs, and polishing to a natural luster in a single visit.

Problem cases: rebonding a debonded veneer, replacing a fractured unit, or bonding onto a compromised substrate (endodontically treated/tetracycline-stained tooth, exposed dentin, subgingival margin, bruxer) - requires removal of old cement, substrate-specific adhesive protocol, moisture and hemostasis control, and often intraoral adjustment of the ceramic before final cementation.

sources.title: Safety and performance of the first supervised automated dental robot to perform minimally invasive tooth prep for laminate veneers - PubMed
sources.claim: The Lupin Robotic System is a supervised automated dental robot that performed minimally invasive tooth preparation for ... in a clinical study of 12 patients (52 teeth) at a dental college hospital; its clinical role is the enamel reduction step only, not the adhesive placement of the veneers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation for veneers, on the same teeth in the same operatory. It substantiates the cutting step of a veneer case, but the system's demonstrated scope stops before try-in, adhesive bonding, cement cleanup and occlusal adjustment, which are the placement acts of this task.

sources.title: Lupin Dental announces the world's first supervised AUTOMATED MULTI-TREATMENT DENTAL ROBOTIC SYSTEM, initially demonstrated on complex aesthetic veneer procedures.
sources.claim: Lupin's first clinical use took place inside a university dental college and hospital in Pune, India, in an ongoing post-market study of robotic minimally invasive tooth preparation for aesthetic veneers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic veneer tooth preparation in a dental clinic. Establishes the environment (a standard human dental operatory, E2) in which dental robots work, but not the veneer bonding/placement step this task requires.

sources.system: Perceptive SARP (semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system)
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment
sources.claim: Perceptive's semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system (SARP) completed the first in-human robotic restorative procedure in six patients: it preplans and executes the tooth preparation with sub-50 micron precision, while the restoration itself is pre-manufactured and delivered separately.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation on live patients. Comparable objects (anterior/posterior teeth) and precision, but the demonstrated robot scope ends at tooth cutting; seating, adhesive luting and finishing of the restoration were not robot-performed.

sources.system: review of dental robotic systems (Perceptive, implant robots)
sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: A 2025 British Dental Journal review of robotics in dentistry identifies the July 2024 milestone as an autonomous robot performing a crown-preparation procedure; the review's restorative-dentistry examples are preparation and implant surgery, with no robotic adhesive cementation of indirect restorations reported.
sources.transferJustification: Survey-level evidence delimiting the state of the art: robotic dentistry covers drilling/preparation and implant osteotomy, which bounds what can transfer to intraoral adhesive veneer placement.

sources.system: automated robotic tooth preparation system for porcelain laminate veneers (Otani et al.)
sources.title: In vitro evaluation of accuracy and precision of automated robotic tooth preparation system for porcelain laminate veneers - PubMed
sources.claim: Automated robotic tooth preparation for porcelain laminate veneers has also been evaluated in vitro on tooth models, showing robot arms can execute the planned reduction on fixtured teeth; the studies cover preparation accuracy only, not veneer cementation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: veneer preparation on fixtured tooth models, i.e. the E1 counterfactual (work brought to the machine). It shows machine-side capability for the cutting step only; no bonding, cement cleanup or finishing was performed.

tasks.label: Bleach discolored teeth to brighten and whiten them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chairside (in-office) power bleaching of vital anterior teeth in a dental operatory: place cheek retractor and suction, paint and light-cure a gingival barrier along the gingival margins, apply 25-40% hydrogen peroxide gel evenly over the labial surfaces, run 2-3 timed cycles with light activation, suction/rinse gel between cycles, remove the barrier, apply desensitizer and record the shade with a guide or digital shade device, while monitoring a conscious patient for tissue burns and sensitivity.

Custom-tray take-home bleaching: examine and record baseline shade, take an intraoral scan or alginate impression, have scalloped reservoir trays fabricated and checked for fit and gingival extension in the mouth, dispense carbamide peroxide syringes, instruct the patient on loading and wear time, and re-evaluate shade and tissue health at a follow-up visit.

Pre-prosthetic whitening within an esthetic treatment plan: bleach the natural dentition to a target shade before fabricating crowns, veneers or implant restorations, sequence chairside and tray bleaching, wait out shade rebound, verify the stabilized shade against the ceramic shade tab, and explain that existing restorations will not lighten.

Non-vital (internal/walking) bleach of a single discolored endodontically treated incisor: rubber dam isolation, lingual access through existing restoration, remove gutta-percha to below the CEJ, place a cervical barrier, seal sodium perborate/peroxide paste into the chamber with a temporary restoration, review and refresh over one to three visits, then restore.

Adjunct and problem visits: managing severe bleaching sensitivity or gingival irritation (desensitizer application, tray adjustment), touch-up appointments, extended regimens for tetracycline or fluorosis staining, and bleaching for less cooperative patients (strong gag reflex, limited opening, anxious or special-needs patients) in the operatory.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive announced that its AI-driven robotic arm completed what it called the world's first fully automated ... (crown preparation), performed in a dental clinic in Barranquilla, Colombia; a one-off milestone demonstration, not a cleared product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation. It is the closest demonstrated autonomous intraoral procedure, but it is rigid-tool cutting of hard tissue along a preplanned path; it involves no dispensing or removal of viscous bleaching gel, no gingival barrier placement on soft tissue, and no shade endpoint judgment, so it does not substantiate bleaching.

sources.developer: Perceptive Technologies / Harvard School of Dental Medicine
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed first-in-human report of Perceptive's semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system: five crown preparations executed on patients in a clinical setting, still an early feasibility study rather than routine practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation in the operatory. It shows the state of the art for autonomous work inside a live patient's mouth is preplanned bur cutting of enamel/dentin; isolation, materials handling and esthetic endpoint judgment remain with the clinician, so capability does not carry over to bleaching.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic (ATR) system with DentalNavi planning software
sources.developer: Chinese hospital / DentalNavi robotic dental platform
sources.title: Endodontic microsurgery utilizing an autonomous robotic system for the maxillary second molar: a case report
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic (ATR) dental system performed a preplanned osteotomy and root-end resection on a maxillary second molar in a hospital dental clinic; the clinician performed the remaining root freehand and handled all soft-tissue and isolation steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral/periapical drilling under optical tracking. It demonstrates precise autonomous tool placement in a patient's mouth, but only hard-tissue cutting along a CBCT-planned path; no demonstrated handling of gels, barriers, suction or soft-tissue protection needed for bleaching.

sources.title: K211466 Trade/Device Name: Yomi Robotic System (FDA 510(k) summary)
sources.claim: Yomi, the only FDA-cleared dental surgery robot in the US, is a haptic navigational system: the surgeon physically holds and drives the handpiece while the robot constrains position, i.e. it is a guidance device rather than an autonomous operator, and it addresses implant surgery only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-guided implant osteotomy in a standard dental operatory. It shows commercially deployed dental robotics is human-driven guidance limited to drilling, providing no autonomous capability transferable to bleaching.

sources.developer: British Dental Journal (review of Perceptive system)
sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: A 2025 British Dental Journal review of dental robotics identifies the July 2024 crown-preparation case as the first entire procedure performed by an autonomous robot on a human patient, indicating that autonomous robotic dentistry remains confined to isolated restorative demonstrations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: survey of autonomous dental procedures. Establishes that as of 2025 the only autonomous whole-procedure precedent is crown preparation; no robotic system is reported for whitening, isolation or soft-tissue-adjacent material application.

instances.label: Hospital foodservice: clinical nutrition/foodservice manager makes daily-to-weekly rounds through the production kitchen and patient tray line — probe-checks hot-holding and cold-holding temperatures, verifies dish-machine wash/rinse temps and sanitizer concentration with test strips, opens walk-ins to check dating/labeling and cross-contamination, watches staff handwashing and glove use, spot-checks trays against diet orders, records findings on a sanitation/HACCP audit form and directs corrections.

K-12 school nutrition: district dietitian/school nutrition director observes meal service at a school kitchen and serving line — verifies meal-pattern components and portion sizes for reimbursable meals, takes held-food temperatures, reviews HACCP production and temperature logs, inspects storage, equipment and floor sanitation, observes serving-line and point-of-service practices, and files a site review with corrective actions.

Long-term care / senior living: dietitian's periodic test-tray and sanitation audit — evaluates a test tray for temperature, taste, appearance and accuracy against the resident's diet and texture order, checks steam table and trayline temperatures, inspects unit pantry/nourishment refrigerators, and documents compliance for state survey.

Large-volume contract, correctional, military or college dining kitchen: dietitian/foodservice director inspects incoming deliveries (truck and product temperatures, case condition), runs line checks across multiple stations, completes a food-safety self-inspection audit and issues corrective actions.

Community and satellite sites: dietitian monitors meal service at Head Start or child-care centers, congregate/senior meal sites, food pantries, or a caterer's off-site event — layouts and equipment differ site to site, holding equipment is improvised, checks hot/cold holding temperatures, sanitation practices and portioning against menu specification.

Central production kitchen or contract meal manufacturer (cook-chill, home-delivered-meal or hospital off-site kitchen): the dietitian inspects trays/packages coming off the assembly line against modified-diet specifications - component presence, portion weights, appearance, sealing and labeling - with nonconforming trays removed from the run.

Foodservice director/dietitian tests new equipment in the facility kitchen (combi oven, blast chiller, rethermalization cart, tray-line conveyor, high-speed blender): runs trial loads of standard menu items, probes food temperatures and times cycles, judges output quality and consistency, assesses staff usability, cleanability and sanitation compliance, and writes a purchase recommendation.

Quick screening tastings at a vendor food show, distributor sales visit, or office conference room: small samples of many products tasted back-to-back, brief notes on flavor, texture and label/nutrient fit, shortlisting a few for full facility trial.

Product-development or research dietitian in a company R&D test kitchen / sensory lab: prepares prototype formulations, serves and participates in descriptive or consumer sensory panels, checks nutrient composition and label claims, and iterates the formula with food scientists until the prototype is accepted.

Community, WIC, or outpatient nutritionist trials a new product or small appliance in an uncontrolled setting (community-center kitchen, client's home, mobile pantry site): prepares the item with whatever equipment is on hand, tastes it, and judges palatability, safety and practicality for the client population.

roles.title: Optometrists
roles.description: Diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system. Examine eyes and visual system, diagnose problems or impairments, prescribe corrective lenses, and provide treatment. May prescribe therapeutic drugs to treat specific eye conditions.
roles.sector: Healthcare practitioners and technical

tasks.label: Examine eyes, using observation, instruments, and pharmaceutical agents, to determine visual acuity and perception, focus, and coordination and to diagnose diseases and other abnormalities, such as glaucoma or color blindness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine comprehensive eye exam of a cooperative adult in a private-practice or retail-chain exam lane: entrance testing (VA, pupils, EOMs, cover test, confrontation fields, color vision as indicated), retinoscopy/refraction at the phoropter, binocular/accommodative testing, slit-lamp biomicroscopy of lids, cornea, conjunctiva and lens, tonometry, and fundus evaluation (78D/90D or fundus imaging), ending in a documented diagnosis and plan.

Problem-focused or urgent medical eye exam in the office: red eye, corneal foreign body, contact-lens complication, flashes/floaters, or an annual diabetic eye exam. Requires instilling pharmaceutical agents (anesthetic, fluorescein, dilating drops), lid eversion, slit-lamp examination with filters, and binocular indirect ophthalmoscopy of the peripheral retina, sometimes with scleral depression.

Chronic ocular disease monitoring exam (glaucoma suspect/glaucoma, AMD, diabetic retinopathy follow-up): Goldmann applanation tonometry after anesthetic/fluorescein, gonioscopy with a contact lens on the cornea, stereoscopic optic nerve evaluation through a dilated pupil, plus OCT and threshold visual fields, interpreted together to judge progression.

Exam of a patient with limited cooperation — a preschool child, a patient with developmental disability, or an elderly patient with dementia: objective retinoscopy (often cycloplegic after drops), fixation and alignment testing (Hirschberg/cover test), Ishihara or matching color vision testing, and ophthalmoscopy performed opportunistically while the patient moves and attends inconsistently.

Refraction-focused visit for a healthy adult in an office or retail optical setting: determining visual acuity and refractive error to update or verify a spectacle prescription (glasses re-check/non-adapt, contact-lens over-refraction, post-op refraction), with no dilation or contact procedures required.

Off-site examination with a portable kit: bedside in a nursing-home resident's room, a house call, or a mobile/school clinic. Handheld retinoscope, trial frame, portable slit lamp or transilluminator, iCare tonometer and BIO used in a room with variable lighting, furniture and seating, with the patient in a wheelchair or bed.
